### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>ihor-sokoliuk/mcp-searxng (docker.io/isokoliuk/mcp-searxng)</summary>

### [`v1.12.0`](https://redirect.github.com/ihor-sokoliuk/mcp-searxng/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1120---2026-07-25)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/ihor-sokoliuk/mcp-searxng/compare/v1.11.1...v1.12.0)

##### Fixed

- **Established HTTP sessions now receive the configured session rate limit:** Each `POST /mcp` request now passes through exactly one limiter. Requests with a currently live `mcp-session-id` use the session allowance, while initialization requests and missing, malformed, unknown, or stale session identifiers retain the stricter initialization limit. ([#​179](https://redirect.github.com/ihor-sokoliuk/mcp-searxng/pull/179))

- **Logging now honors all eight MCP severity levels:** Filtering recognizes `debug`, `info`, `notice`, `warning`, `error`, `critical`, `alert`, and `emergency`, so selecting a threshold such as `notice` or `emergency` no longer lets lower-severity messages through. ([#​178](https://redirect.github.com/ihor-sokoliuk/mcp-searxng/pull/178))

- **TypeScript test launchers now work consistently on Windows, Linux, and WSL:** Integration and end-to-end tests use Node's portable `--import tsx` loader instead of trying to execute npm's platform-specific `.bin/tsx` shim directly. This changes development and CI launchers only; production runtime behavior is unchanged. ([#​176](https://redirect.github.com/ihor-sokoliuk/mcp-searxng/pull/176))

##### Security

- **Authentication data is now sanitized at every diagnostic boundary:** Process output, MCP logging notifications, JSON-RPC errors, and HTTP diagnostic errors pass through a centralized redaction layer that removes configured credentials, URL userinfo, authorization values, proxy secrets, and structured authentication fields. Malformed SearXNG entries are reported without echoing their raw values. MCP registry metadata now marks `SEARXNG_URL`, `AUTH_USERNAME`, and `AUTH_PASSWORD` as secrets so compatible clients can mask and protect their values. If an older release exposed credentials in logs or client-visible errors, upgrade, rotate the affected credentials, and remove or restrict access to captured logs and telemetry.

- **Hardened HTTP bearer authentication now uses constant-time comparison:** Authorization accepts only the documented exact, case-sensitive `Bearer <token>` form, fails closed when either value is absent, hashes the complete presented and expected strings with SHA-256, and compares the equal-length digests with timing-safe equality. Raw-token and malformed authorization headers are rejected. Before upgrading, clients that previously sent an undocumented bare token must change the header to `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. ([#​177](https://redirect.github.com/ihor-sokoliuk/mcp-searxng/pull/177))

- **Vulnerable transitive dependencies were patched:** `fast-uri` is updated to 3.1.4 for its host-confusion fixes, the root install overrides `@hono/node-server` to patched 2.0.11, and the development graph uses `brace-expansion` 5.0.8. Applications that install `mcp-searxng` as a dependency may need their own `@hono/node-server` 2.0.11 override until the MCP SDK admits the patched 2.x adapter, because npm does not apply dependency-owned overrides in a consuming application's root graph. ([#​189](https://redirect.github.com/ihor-sokoliuk/mcp-searxng/pull/189))

author: lbruton
body:
> **Draft — QA preview.** Merge to `dev` after review.

## Summary

Second child of the STRK-268 Metal Ratios epic: the shared Layout C ("Signal") panel component both hosts will render — the in-app modal (STRK-271) and the standalone `/ratios/` page (STRK-273). Lifted from the approved `playground/ratios-panel-playground.html` prototype, not redesigned. **No UI entry point yet** — the component is mounted only by tests until the hosts land; the app's visible behavior is unchanged.

## Changes

- **`js/ratios-panel.js`** (new) — script-tag-global component:
  - Pure string builders (unit-testable): header with `{Num} ÷ {Den}` eyebrow + live/last-close badge, in-panel pair selector (4 real `<button>`s with `aria-pressed`), hero readout + delta vs prior close (one extra decimal; omitted honestly when no prior close exists), explicitly-labeled 52-week position bar ("52-week range" vs "Nth percentile all-time") with long-run-mean marker, 4 signed-magnitude trend tiles ("9.4% above trend"), chart block with 30D/90D/1Y/5Y/MAX control, provenance footer.
  - `renderRatiosPanel(mountEl, opts)` — mounts, wires pair/range controls, draws the Chart.js chart from **computed tokens at draw time**, repaints on `data-theme` mutation (STAK-504 precedent), returns a `{destroy, selectPair}` handle. Canvas is class-scoped within the mount so multiple mounts can't collide.
  - **Both prototype-caught defects are locked**: the long-run-mean dataset draws only within ~35% of the visible window (`ratioMeanLineVisible` — the Au:Pt y-axis hijack), and both bar scales are labeled.
  - **Copy rules**: interpretive mean-reversion line is Au:Ag only; Au:Pt/Au:Pd get position-without-verdict; Pt:Pd says "Both metals are"; precision 1dp Au:Ag / 2dp rest, deltas +1.
  - **Data sourcing honors the STRK-269 host contract**: series build from `[...historicalDataCache, ...spotHistory]` so live rows overlay the seed bundle; live ratio from `spotPrices` via `computeRatio`.
  - Deliberate port fix: the 5Y range slices **1,305 sessions** (5 × 261), not the playground's 1,825 calendar days — the series contains only trading sessions.
- **`css/styles.css`** — `.gsr-*` Layout C styles appended, tokens-only (D-7), accent via `data-accent` → `--silver`/`--platinum`/`--palladium`, legible in all four themes; mobile canvas height via media query.
- **`index.html`** — `ratios-panel.js` registered after the ratio math/chips scripts, before `init.js`.
- **`sw.js`** — `CORE_ASSETS` entry for the new script (cache name auto-stamped by hook).
- **Version bump 3.35.67** — 6 release files; spot bundle re-run (0 new rows — merged an hour ago in #1374).

## Tests

Inventory delta: **+30 tests, +2 files** (+25 unit in `tests/unit/ratios-panel.test.js`, +5 Playwright in `tests/playwright/core/ratios-panel.spec.js`; coverage-map row added).

- Unit (530/530 pass): formatting guards, ordinals incl. teens, trend-label signed magnitude + at-trend + unusable-average dash, mean-line visibility matrix (incl. the Au:Pt case and flat-window fallback), full Layout C markup contract, per-pair copy rules, degraded stats (null prevClose, null stats → empty state).
- Playwright (413/413 core pass): mounts against the **real seed bundle**, pair switch re-renders accent/aria/header and drops the interpretive verdict on Pt pairs, range control moves `aria-pressed`, `data-theme` flip survives the observer repaint with zero `pageerror`s, `destroy()` empties the mount.

## Issues

- STRK-270: Shared ratios panel component (Layout C) — In Progress (child of STRK-268 epic; unblocks STRK-271 and STRK-273)

author: nguyenhaihung0510
body:
fix(008k): ba mục đỏ của QA 25/07 — và mục nặng nhất suýt được "vá" bằng một dòng không chữa gì

## 1. 🔴 Tiêu đề dài tràn ra ngoài thẻ và đè lên ba nút hành động

Cần đủ BA lớp, thiếu một là không chữa được:

- `shrink` — lớp gốc của `Button` (shadcn) có sẵn `shrink-0`. Flex item từ chối
  co thì hộp luôn rộng bằng max-content, và khi hộp đã rộng bằng chữ thì KHÔNG
  có gì ép chữ phải xuống dòng cả. Đây mới là nguyên nhân gốc.
- `min-w-0` — gỡ `min-width:auto` mặc định của flex item.
- `break-words` — `whitespace-normal` chỉ cho xuống dòng ở khoảng trắng; một cụm
  70 ký tự liền thì không có chỗ nào để xuống.

Bản vá đầu của tôi chỉ có `break-words`. Nó qua sạch eslint, 13 test và build —
và **không sửa được gì**, vì `shrink-0` vẫn giữ hộp ở max-content. Chỉ lộ ra khi
đo trong trình duyệt thật trên CSS đã build.

Đo tại 390px (đúng bề ngang iPhone của chủ), chuỗi lớp lấy từ `cn()`/tailwind-merge
chứ không phải chuỗi tự nối tay:

| Tiêu đề | Trước | Sau |
|---|---|---|
| 70 ký tự liền không dấu cách | rộng 598px · tràn 224px · đè nút | rộng 297px · tràn 0 · không đè |
| Tiếng Việt 150 ký tự dấu dày | rộng 1071px · tràn 697px · đè nút | rộng 297px · tràn 0 · không đè |

Cùng bệnh ở mục checklist (`min-w-0 break-words`) — nội dung 200 ký tự đẩy rộng
cả thẻ y hệt.

## 2. 🟠 Đóng Dialog không trả focus về nút đã mở nó

Dialog chi tiết mở bằng state, không bọc `DialogTrigger`, nên Radix không có
`triggerRef` để trả focus về — focus rơi xuống `body` và người dùng bàn phím phải
Tab lại từ đầu trang. Tự nhớ nút đã mở, trả về trong `onCloseAutoFocus`. Kiểm
`isConnected` chứ không chỉ kiểm null: thẻ có thể đã bị xoá khỏi cây trong lúc
dialog mở, focus vào một node đã tháo là không làm gì cả.

## 3. 🟠 Viền checkbox 1,24:1 — sửa ở token, không vá tại chỗ

`--input` (viền của MỌI control: checkbox, input, select, textarea, nút outline)
đang là `--n-200`. Với checkbox chưa tick thì cái viền LÀ toàn bộ hình hài của
control, nên nó rơi đúng vào non-text contrast 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11).

| nền | n-200 (cũ) | n-500 (mới) |
|---|---|---|
| thẻ `--card` #ffffff | 1,32:1 | 4,99:1 |
| nền `--background` #faf7f7 | **1,24:1** | 4,69:1 |
| thẻ ghim `--brand-50` #fef2f5 | 1,21:1 | 4,57:1 |

1,24:1 khớp đúng số T3 đo được. `--border` (viền thẻ, đường phân cách) ở lại
n-200 — đó là ranh giới trang trí, WCAG không đòi 3:1 cho thứ không mang nghĩa.

Kèm theo: sửa chú thích của `--n-400`. Nó đang ghi "chỉ viền, icon trang trí" —
tức là CHO PHÉP dùng cho viền, trong khi n-400 chỉ đạt 2,70:1 trên nền trắng,
vẫn dưới ngưỡng. Chính câu chú thích đó là cái cửa để lỗi này đi vào.

Đây là lần THỨ BA cùng một luật phát biểu một chiều làm lọt: lần 1 chữ trên nền,
lần 2 viền focus, lần 3 viền control. Cấm một chiều = cho phép chiều còn lại.

## Phụ

`.claude/launch.json` — cấu hình chạy `vite preview` để lần sau dựng bản build
lên trình duyệt mà đo, không phải tự chế lại server. Không chứa secret.

Kiểm tay: eslint sạch · 13 test xanh · build PWA xanh, precache 12 mục · đo
tương phản bằng script tính WCAG · đo tràn bằng trình duyệt thật trên CSS đã build.

## Summary

- restore the unreleased v4.5.0 source line to the canonical policy-only package shape
- remove only the retained v4.4.2 production runtime bundle and replace its manifest with the exact empty schema-v3 policy manifest
- preserve the merged OpenCode Go policy while making v4.5.0 eligible for the governed private build/sign/notarize pipeline
- make the Codex-governance contract test valid for both policy-only source and activation-release trees

## Root cause

Plugin main declared v4.5.0 after PR #62 but still carried the v4.4.2 production bundle. The private builder correctly accepts a populated public runtime only from a trusted signed release tag that peels to the requested source commit. The untagged v4.5.0 tree was therefore neither a valid policy-only source nor a valid signed activation source.

## Boundary declaration

- [x] No provider executor source, raw provider command, credential, private absolute path, retired package tree, downloader, or post-install hook is included.
- [x] The only native-runtime change removes the older final signed artifact; no implementation, credential, unsigned replacement, or mock runtime is introduced.
- [x] The change does not create a host-specific preset or provider-specific plugin.

## Generated and release surfaces

- [x] Skill specs and generated `SKILL.md` files are in parity.
- [x] Claude and Codex marketplaces/manifests are in parity.
- [x] Unique fragment `changelog.d/2026-07-26-002-v450-policy-only-source.md` is present; generated `CHANGELOG.md` is intentionally untouched under the fragment-only convention.
- [x] Version metadata remains v4.5.0 because this repairs the already-bumped unreleased source line rather than introducing another public version.

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` — 576 passed
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` — 254 passed
- focused runtime/archive/release matrix — 289 passed

- `cut_release.py --dry-run` is intentionally deferred to the release PR because the fragment-only source PR does not commit the compiled `CHANGELOG.md`

## Review and post-condition

Tier 3 because this changes release-supply-chain and runtime-verification state. Gemini/Google governance reviewed the pre-edit plan and returned `RECONSIDER`; its required stale-attestation scan, policy-only local-development validation, and canonical manifest/schema validation were integrated. The mandatory revised-plan re-consultation was attempted and returned the serving broker's typed `gemini_containment_error`; it is not counted as convergence. author: abeken1026395
body:
## 問題（実測）
構文（先頭N字でなく主語・語順）で見ると M14「①{名}自体に崩れる材料は薄いが、{相手}{述語}」が **47.4%**、場内で最大 **7連続**（戸田10/12R）。先頭12字の分散は選手名によるもので、読者が読む構文は改善していなかった。

## 修正1：M14に構造の異なる型（言い換えでなく主語・語順を変える）
downFactors=0 かつ外に脅威、の同一条件に対し：
- **型A（①主語）**：「①{名}自体に崩れる材料は薄いが、{相手}{述語}」
- **型B（相手主語）**：「{相手}{述語}。①{名}に目立つ穴はない」
- **型C（①の実数）**：「①{名}は1着率{X}%。ただ{相手}{述語}」（inWinRate非null時のみ）
- **型D（機力上位）**：「①{名}は機力上位（{X}%）。{相手}{述語}」（①の機力が上位帯のときのみ）
- 型C/Dは「材料が薄い」の曖昧語を実数に置換＝情報量も増える。
- 併せて「①の出方ひとつ」(M6/M13)も連続しやすいため型A/B（相手主語版）を用意。

## 修正2：場内で直前2レースと同じ型を使わない（機械的担保）
観戦記の styleHistory（直近3回避）と同思想。場ごとに直近使用した型を保持し、直前2つと異なる型を決定的に選ぶ（無ければ交互）。**ランダムではなく決定的**＝同じ入力なら同じ出力（再現性を確認済み）。

## 検証（構文で測定）
1. **構文別占有**：M14系合計47.4%を型A/B/C/Dに分散。**最大構文 = M14-A 20.5%**（要件≤25%）。
2. **場内 同一構文 最大連続 = 2**（要件≤3。現状 戸田7・芦屋5→解消）。
3. **型別発火**：A=32 / B=25 / C=16 / D=1。
4. **差分ゼロ**：公開（見立て以外の全キー）=0、downFactors=0、collapse=0、波及=0、predictions コア（判定/主役艇/スコア/対抗艇/死角艇/死角ID/締めID/波及ID）=0。閾値・HARANTH無改変。
5. **矛盾ゼロ**：df=0 で「不安」= 0 維持。
6. **再現性**：2回生成で見立て差分 0（決定的）。

### 文面サンプル
- A「①吉武真也自体に崩れる材料は薄いが、⑤小倉康典は機力上位で連軸を脅かす」
- B「⑤山下大輝はダッシュから連絡み、連軸を脅かす。①吉田祐貴に目立つ穴はない」
- C「①本村大は1着率56.5%。ただ⑥上平真二はダッシュから連絡み、連軸を脅かす」
- D「①山道諄也は機力上位（37%）。⑤高石梨菜は機力上位で連軸を脅かす」
- 出方B「④村松遥輝の機力上位が連に絡む余地。①がどこまで残すか」

## 原則（記録）
文型の重複は「先頭N字の一致」でなく「構文の一致」で測る。先頭が選手名だと同じ構文でも別物としてカウントされ、改善したように見える。

## 不変条件
- 判定ロジック・predictions/・公開articles/・HARANTH・閾値は不変。波及ID(S系)無改変。index.html 無変更。
- マージは裁定後。

author: imthekeymaster
body:
### Motivation

- Add Tempestus Aquilons as a first-class, selectable Player Kill Team using the repository's official Tempestus PDFs and preserve the existing Deathwatch behavior. 
- Make small, data-driven generalizations to the Player Kill Team architecture so additional teams can be added with minimal code changes. 
- Present faction rules and strategic gambits as tabletop guidance rather than attempting to simulate complex positional rules. 

### Description

- Added a new data-driven team file `Player_Operatives/TempestusAquilons.json` containing an 11-operative roster with official names, roles, APL, Move, Save, Wounds, full weapon profiles (including multiple-profile weapons like plasma standard/supercharge, focused/salvo/point-blank, mobile/stationary/concealed, sweeping), melee/ranged stats, and operative abilities and guidance. 
- Generalized roster validation and UI logic in `app.js` by adding `playerRosterValidation` and `factionGuidanceHtml`, enforcing data-defined category minimums/maximums, `maxGunners`/`mandatoryTroopers`, category maxima, and making `randomPlayerRoster` and interactive selection respect these rules.

author: florianpfaff
body:
## What changed

- correct source-only kNN distance weighting so rows with one or more exact feature matches use only those zero-distance neighbors
- preserve the existing probability behavior for uniform weighting and for rows without exact matches
- add a regression where a deliberately large `epsilon` previously allowed farther neighbors to overturn an exact match

## Root cause

Distance weights were computed as `1 / max(distance, epsilon)` for every neighbor. This avoids division by zero, but it also leaves nonzero-distance neighbors with positive weight when an exact match exists. With sufficiently large `epsilon`, farther neighbors can even dominate the predicted class.

## Impact

Exact source feature matches now receive the expected kNN semantics: nonzero-distance neighbors are ignored, while multiple exact matches share probability according to their class counts.

## Validation

- reviewed branch diff against current `main`
- added `tests/test_source_knn_zero_distance.py`
- GitHub Actions will run the repository test suite on this draft PR

author: stevegjones
body:
## sdlc-model-council v1 — cross-model assessment, roster & Diff+Synthesis (#232)

Pivots `sdlc-simple-orchestration` (a "delegate one task to one CLI" wrapper that
the official codex/antigravity plugins already do better) into a **cross-model
council**: onboard the models reachable via locally-installed peer agentic CLIs
(codex, agy, opencode — gateways to 19+ models) by **assessing them against a
standardized problem stack**, cast them into a **roster**, and run **cross-model
fan-out plays** — the one thing no per-vendor plugin does. Built entirely as
choreography + arithmetic ABOVE the unchanged adapter engine (313 substrate tests
untouched throughout).

Built in 7 gated stages, each with the 313-test substrate gate green:

1. **Rename** simple-orchestration → model-council.
2. **Council scripts + v1 problem stack + golden tests** — priors/roster/diversity/
   cast arithmetic (small-sample-honest shrinkage, per-defect `both_wrong_rate`,
   greedy decorrelated casting), 4 objective scorers, 9 original judge-free items.
3. **`assess.sh`** — end-to-end assessment: estimate gate, free wave-0 calibration,
   paid waves at a concurrency cap with a budget hard-stop + resume + timeout rows.
4. **Commands + `council-policy` skill + `council-judge` agent + the Diff+Synthesis
   play** (`play.sh`: blind-labelled panel → quorum → blind judge → unblind, with a
   `baseline_member` for the measurability spine).
5. **Registration** (marketplace / CLAUDE.md / AGENT-INDEX).
6. **One gated live run** (see below).
7. **Validation + this PR.**

### The live slice earned its keep
On the real authenticated fleet: a 5-model assessment produced a genuinely
differentiated roster (codex A on bug-fix/instruction-format; agy-pro best
long-context; free opencode solid-B calibration), then a live **Diff+Synthesis
reviewing our own `assess.sh`** returned **Baseline-delta = "panel added material
value"** — the panel corroborated the baseline's top finding, surfaced 5 real bugs
it missed, and the **adjudication step caught the baseline's own hallucination**.
codex timed out mid-review and the play degraded gracefully (quorum held). The run
surfaced 3 real budget/safety bugs in our orchestrator, **all fixed** (usage.py
metered live cost at $0 → budget stop was ineffective; empty-status poll guard;
resume budget back-fill).

### Measurability & honesty (built in by design)
Every play keeps the roster's best single model as `baseline_member`; the synthesis
must state whether the panel beat it; `outcomes.jsonl` accumulates. **Pre-committed
rule:** if over ~20 real runs the panel helps <20% of the time, the honest product
is roster-driven single-model routing (already a shipped path), not fan-out.

### Tests & CI
**681 tests green** (368 council + 313 substrate, mock-only/no-token). flake8-clean
(repo config); technical-debt gate within framework limits.

### Honest caveats / follow-ups
- The pre-flight **estimate under-predicts codex ~5×** (reasoning + long-context
  inputs); the live budget hard-stop (now working) is the real guard. Wiring
  measured re-estimation from wave-0 is a follow-up.
- The **cost model is metered-API-equivalent** — on pro subscriptions marginal cost
  is ~$0; read $/item as a token-usage proxy.
- **Local MLX backend** (compare local models against the hosted fleet) is the next
  objective — a one-directory adapter, no engine change.
- Lower-severity `assess.sh` findings the panel raised are recorded in the
  retrospective, not yet fixed.
- Council Python follows the existing-plugin convention (flake8-clean, not
  black-formatted; black is a non-blocking CI warning that all plugins trip).

author: dsquaregee
body:
## Summary

A production optimization + quality pass after the 101-temple catalog went live.

**The fix — HTML pages weren't getting the CDN cache policy.** `firebase.json`
defined the intended HTML policy (`max-age=0, s-maxage=86400,
stale-while-revalidate=7d`) on `source: "**/*.html"`, but Firebase Hosting
matches header globs against the **request path** — and every page is a
trailing-slash directory URL (`/en/temples/x/`) with no `.html` in the path. So
the rule never matched real page requests, which silently fell back to
Firebase's `max-age=3600` default: **no CDN `s-maxage`, no
`stale-while-revalidate`.** (Confirmed on production: `/en/temples/brihadeeswarar/`
returned `cache-control: max-age=3600`.) Only the extension-based asset globs
were working.

**Fix:** move the HTML/default policy onto the broad `**` rule. Firebase applies
the *last matching value* per header key — verified on production, where
`/sw.js` resolves to `no-store` despite also matching the immutable `.js` glob —
so the `_next/static` + media immutable rules and the `sw.js`/manifest rules
still override for their own paths, while page URLs now receive the intended CDN
caching. The now-dead `**/*.html` rule is removed.

Verified end-to-end against the real export via `apps/web/scripts/serve-out.mjs`:

| Path | Cache-Control |
|---|---|
| `/en/temples/brihadeeswarar/`, `/en/`, `/` | `max-age=0, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800` ✅ |
| `/_next/static/….js` (hashed) | `max-age=31536000, immutable` ✅ (unchanged) |
| `/sw.js` | `no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` ✅ (unchanged) |
| `/manifest.webmanifest` | `max-age=3600` ✅ (unchanged) |

## Quality baseline re-verified at 101 temples (all green)
- ✅ Unit tests — 59/59
- ✅ Content validate — 101 temples × 6 locales, 17 circuits; cross-locale parity
- ✅ Translation QA — 0 errors, 100% target-script (ta/te/kn/ml/hi)
- ✅ Web build — 736 HTML pages, CSP hashes injected (736/736)
- ✅ Byte budget — largest JS 53.7 KB/90, total JS 218.8 KB/320 (68%), largest HTML 254 KB/320 (79%)
- ✅ Lighthouse — a11y 96–100, best-practices 96–100, SEO 100, CLS 0.004 (all hard gates pass); performance 82–95 is the standing non-blocking warn (headless LCP variance — hero is already preloaded `fetchPriority=high`, 0 render-blocking)
- ✅ Live security headers — HSTS+preload, nosniff, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, COOP, Permissions-Policy; strict per-page **meta CSP with script hashes** enforced; Brotli on the wire
- ✅ SEO — sitemap has all 606 temple + 102 circuit URLs; robots.txt correct

## Recorded, deferred as its own PR
The **Discover payload** optimization (roadmap's durable lever). The largest page
is 254 KB/320 (79%) at 101 temples, ~2.5 KB/temple (~26 temples runway; ~20 KB
Brotli on the wire). The five **search-only** fields (`deity`, `tradition`,
`style`, `period`, `dynasty`) are ~22% of that page and never displayed/faceted —
moving them to a lazily-fetched per-locale search index cuts the page ~22%. It
changes a live core feature's search behavior, so it's specced (with the measured
numbers and a step-by-step plan) in `docs/roadmap-next.md` for a focused, tested
follow-up rather than bundled here.

## Notes
- Headers-only + docs change; no content or app-code change, so the deployed
  catalog is untouched. On merge, `deploy.yml` republishes with the corrected
  cache headers.

body:
## What changed

- validate numeric table cells without concatenating comma- or space-delimited value lists
- preserve ambiguous source values as exact text and only tolerate explicit missing-value markers in numeric columns
- exclude temporal metadata such as completion years from categorical chart measures
- bump the extractor version so cached manifests refresh after deployment
- add regression coverage based on the Nile hydropower table

## Why

Wikipedia lists several construction and upgrade years for the Aswan Low Dam and Roseires Dam. The extractor removed separators and treated each list as one enormous integer, then selected `Year completed` as the default bar series. This produced a misleading chart and corrupted the exact-data view.

After this change, the chart displays hydropower capacity in MW while the complete year lists remain intact in Exact chart data.

## Validation

body:
fix(wasm): gate dispatch_pep crate::service off wasm32 — unblock PR queue (same as #1307)

## The break
`crates/hyprstream-rpc/src/auth/mac/dispatch_pep.rs:51` imports `crate::service::EnvelopeContext`, which does not resolve on wasm32 — the `service` module is compiled out on the wasm target (`lib.rs:166`). This reds the **WASM (browser client)** CI job on main and on every PR.

## The fix
The MAC dispatch PEP is server-side dispatch enforcement; the wasm browser client does no dispatch PEP. Gate the module inclusion and its re-exports in `auth/mac/mod.rs` behind `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` — same gate pattern as #1307.

author: vammad21
body:
## Summary

Adds `examples/crewai_governance_benchmark/` — a reproducible, offline A/B benchmark that measures what Nornyx governance concretely adds to an ordinary CrewAI application, and lets an external developer verify the difference rather than take it on faith.

**Audited starting commit:** `d4026a1a06789453de86ea60cd4a78c31da87da2` (`main`) — *"Merge pull request #50 … feature/agentic-adapter-crewai"*.

This is a **governance-effectiveness** benchmark. It is not an LLM-quality benchmark and not a production-performance benchmark.

> **Read the result without running anything:** [`examples/crewai_governance_benchmark/results/`](../examples/crewai_governance_benchmark/results/) contains a recorded run, including a fully self-contained `dashboard.html` (no CDN, no script, no network reference). Download and open it in a browser — GitHub does not render committed HTML inline.

## Purpose

Answer one question with evidence: *what governance capability does Nornyx add to an ordinary agentic application, and can an external developer verify the difference themselves?*

## Methodology — with vs. without Nornyx

One customer-support and financial-remediation workflow runs twice.

* **Variant A — plain CrewAI.** Real `Agent` / `Task` / `Crew` / `BaseTool` and a real `Crew.kickoff()`. Every ordinary application control is kept, including a genuine refund auto-approval limit. The baseline is **not** weakened; where it performs a prohibited action it does so for the ordinary reason — the tool was attached to the agent and nothing else was asked.
* **Variant B — the same application governed.** Same agents, tasks, scripted offline model, inputs, business rules, and **the same business callables** (one shared `business.py`, not a second copy). The only difference is that each tool is built by the supported adapter.

Supported path only, as of the audited revision:

| Layer | Used |
|---|---|
| Core SPI | `nornyx.agentic` (ADR-0039, `SPI_VERSION == "1.0"`) — `load_authorizer`, `Authorizer.evaluate`, `EvidenceRecorder` |
| Adapter | `nornyx-agentic-adapters` 0.1.0 — `SurfaceBinding`, `enforce`, `crewai_adapter.make_governed_tool`, `resolve_identity` |
| Framework | `crewai==1.15.4` (the single supported version, enforced at import) |

No private kernel API and no CrewAI internal is touched. The legacy unpackaged kernel under `integrations/` is **not** used.

Two integration choices are disclosed in-code and in the report: a thin CrewAI tool delegates into the adapter's own governed `_run` to (1) mint one mission id per invocation and (2) convert `AdapterDenied` into a tool observation. `enforce` still raises before the wrapped action — the fail-closed guarantee is untouched.

## Scenario summary — 19 scenarios, 5 stages

Stages are reported separately and **never summed**: `runtime`, `binding`, `load`, `bypass`, `application`.

| # | Scenario | Stage | Baseline → Governed | Diagnostic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | Valid low-risk action | runtime | 1 → 1 allowed | `ALLOWED` |
| S02 | High-risk external action, valid human approval | runtime | 1 → 1 allowed | `ALLOWED` |
| S03 | Undeclared capability (delete customer records) | runtime | 1 → **0** | `CAPABILITY_UNKNOWN` |
| S04 | Known capability, wrong identity | runtime | 1 → **0** | `CAPABILITY_DENIED` |
| S05 | Unknown / unmapped runtime identity | binding | 1 → **0** | `IDENTITY_UNKNOWN` |
| S06 | High-risk action without approval | runtime | 1 → **0** | `CROSSING_APPROVAL_REQUIRED` |
| S07 | AI-generated (non-human) approval | runtime | 1 → **0** | `APPROVAL_NON_HUMAN` |
| S08 | Approval bound to the wrong action | runtime | 1 → **0** | `APPROVAL_ACTION_MISMATCH` |
| S09 | Expired approval | runtime | 1 → **0** | `APPROVAL_STALE` |
| S10 | Restricted-data sharing | runtime | 1 → **0** | `SENSITIVE_SHARING` |
| S11 | Undeclared trust-zone crossing | runtime | 1 → **0** | `ZONE_CROSSING_DENIED` |
| S12 | Contract / lock drift | load | n/a → 0 | `LOCK_STALE` |
| S13 | Malformed governance metadata | runtime | 1 → **0** | `REQUEST_MALFORMED` |
| S14 | Governed action that fails after authorization | runtime | 0 → 0 | `ALLOWED`; 3 entries, 0 completions |
| S15 | **Deliberate unwrapped-tool bypass** | bypass | 1 → **1** | `NOT_GOVERNED` |
| S16 | Valid bounded delegation | runtime | 1 → 1 allowed | `ALLOWED` |
| S17 | Runtime revision mismatch | runtime | 1 → **0** | `REVISION_MISMATCH` |
| S18 | **Application business rule (fairness control)** | application | 0 → 0 | refused by the app in both arms |
| S19 | Compliance role closes the case | runtime | 1 → 1 allowed | `ALLOWED` |

## Side-effect ledger results

Prevention is proved mechanically, not inferred from an exception. Every business tool writes to a ledger, and every governance decision is stamped on the *same* monotonic clock.

| | Plain CrewAI | Governed by Nornyx |
|---|---|---|
| Business side effects executed | **16** | **5** |
| Prohibited actions executed | **11** | **0** |
| Governance decisions recorded | 0 | 27 |
| Evidence events emitted | 0 | 51 |

* **11 / 11** prohibited callables the baseline executed were prevented with **exactly zero** attempts and zero completions (10 runtime-stage, 1 binding-stage, reported separately).
* **4 / 4** valid actions allowed, with **byte-identical** business output in both arms.
* **0** false denials, **0** false allows.
* Ordering is checked **pairwise**: the k-th entry into a business callable must be preceded by a k-th recorded decision, so a silently reused authorization fails the check.
* S14 shows CrewAI's internal 3× tool retry produces **3 independent authorization decisions** — retries re-enter governance rather than reusing the first.
* Post-success observations (4) exactly match governed-surface completions (4); an authorized action that then fails records no `tool_invoked`.

## Evidence-validation results

* 51 events emitted; **51 / 51** bind the exact contract digest `sha256:79b44dfd…585278` and lock digest `sha256:e43e1fbf…37537b8`.
* Full-stream validation: **`fail`** — reported, not hidden.
* Excluding only the events affected by the two disclosed upstream defects: `pass` (a diagnostic aid, never presented as the headline).

Both remaining diagnostics are defects **in the audited packages, not in the benchmark**, each reproduced by a *mandatory* scenario, each with a minimal reproduction that uses no benchmark code (see `FINDINGS.md`):

1. **`AN_EVT_APPROVAL_NON_HUMAN`** — `authz.py:616` emits `approval_rejected` carrying the *claimed* non-human `actor_type`; `agentic_evidence.py:660` rejects any approval-outcome event whose approver is not human. A **correctly refused AI approval therefore cannot appear in a valid stream** — the strongest governance outcome is the one that cannot be evidenced.
2. **`AN_EVT_CAPABILITY_NOT_HELD`** — `crewai_adapter.py:239` records `tool_invoked` without `delegation_ref`; `agentic_evidence.py:279` fails closed without it. **Delegation and validatable evidence are currently mutually exclusive** on the supported CrewAI path.

Neither affects any enforcement result. I did not patch either — fixing the product to make my own benchmark pass would have destroyed the finding.

Also recorded as non-defect observations: CrewAI's `ToolUsage._max_parsing_attempts = 3` retry has no public knob; `EvidenceRecorder` timestamps from the bound `decision_at` with no monotonic component, so repeated decisions in one mission look like replays (the benchmark mints one mission per invocation to avoid this, and integrators should too); and the adapter README's `pip install nornyx-agentic-adapters` does not resolve.

author: shubhamtaywade82
body:
## Summary

Three items from the Clean Ruby guide review. None changes behaviour; 1,062 examples pass, RuboCop clean.

## 1. `with_transient_retry` no longer duplicates its retry branch

Two rescue clauses ran near-identical backoff → log → sleep → retry logic, differing only in what they raised once retries were spent. Even the log wording differed for no reason (`"Transient error"` vs `"Network error"`), and no spec asserted either.

Collapsed into one clause, with an `exhausted_error` helper naming the actual difference:

```ruby
# Faraday's transport errors are translated to DhanHQ::NetworkError, so a caller
# rescuing DhanHQ::Error sees every failure this client can produce. This gem's own
# errors already belong to that hierarchy and are re-raised unchanged.
def exhausted_error(error, retries)
  return error unless RETRYABLE_TRANSPORT_ERRORS.any? { |klass| error.is_a?(klass) }

  attempts = retries.zero? ? "" : " after #{retries} retries"
  DhanHQ::NetworkError.new("Request failed#{attempts}: #{error.message}")
end
```

Guide §3.6, and clears the `Lint/DuplicateBranch` pressure on this method.

## 2. `Client#initialize` no longer opens a connection

It built a Faraday connection, so constructing a client did network setup — guide §5.1, "keep `initialize` boring". It now establishes state and checks its one invariant (§5.2); `#connection` builds on first use.

The rebuild-on-base-URL-change logic that `refresh_connection!` provided moves into `#connection` itself, so `request` no longer has to remember to call it first. `#connection` stays public, and a sandbox toggle still takes effect mid-process.

## 3. `Naming/PredicateMethod` scoped by method name, not by file

This was suppressed across **seven whole files**. My first pass at this item was going to add `?` aliases — that would have been wrong. Every flagged method is a *command* that reports success, not a query:

```ruby
def cancel   # performs cancellation, returns whether it worked
def modify
def destroy
def acquire!
```

`cancel?` reads as *"should I cancel?"*, which is worse than the name it replaces. The real answer for an ambiguous boolean return is the bang variant — `cancel!`, `modify!` — which is #47's job, not a naming change.

So the fix is to make the suppression state the actual reason:

```yaml
Naming/PredicateMethod:
  AllowBangMethods: true
  AllowedMethods: [cancel, modify, destroy]
```

Strictly better debt than seven file exclusions: it says *why*, and a genuinely mis-named predicate elsewhere in those same files is still caught. It also surfaced a now-redundant inline `rubocop:disable` in `risk/pipeline.rb`.

## Tests

New specs for the lazily-built connection (not opened on construction, memoised, rebuilt on a base-URL change) and for retry exhaustion (transport errors translated, SDK errors re-raised unchanged, reads still retried).

author: franckolv-dev
body:
Suite de l'incident du 26/07 : le compte Serper est tombé à court de crédits, consommé par une tâche de prospection quotidienne qui bouclait sur `web_search` sans jamais aboutir.

## 1. SearchCans rejoint la chaîne

Contrat **lu sur leur documentation**, pas deviné :

```
POST https://www.searchcans.com/api/v1/search
Authorization: Bearer <clé>
corps    {"t":"google", "s":<requête>, "country", "language", "p"}
réponse  {"code":0, "data":{"organic":[{title, link, snippet, …}],
                              "knowledgeGraph":{…}}}
```

La forme est proche de Serper — le mapping en est le miroir. Réglage : `searchcans_api_key`.

**Constat au passage** : **Tavily était déjà implémenté et déjà dans la chaîne**, mais aucune clé n'est configurée dans le conteneur — il n'a donc **jamais été atteint**. Implémenter un fournisseur sans le brancher ni le vérifier ne sert à rien ; un test verrouille désormais leur présence dans la chaîne.

## 2. Disjoncteur de quota

Un fournisseur qui répond « plus de crédits » est **écarté 30 minutes**. Sans ça, **chaque** recherche repayait un aller-retour vers un service dont on savait qu'il refuserait — de la latence pure, sur toutes les requêtes.

L'oubli est court volontairement : recharger suffit, sans redémarrer le backend.

## Correction d'un test de #257 qui passait pour la mauvaise raison

`_dispatch_search` importe `get_settings` **localement** : patcher l'attribut du module  n'a aucun effet. Le test « un fournisseur à court de crédits est signalé » ne prenait donc **même pas la branche** qu'il prétendait vérifier — la clé Serper étant absente en environnement de test. Il patche maintenant la source.

## Tests

9 tests écrits avant le code : mapping de la réponse documentée · une panne rend `None` et laisse la chaîne continuer · **les fournisseurs sont bien branchés dans le dispatcher** · le réglage existe · les messages de quota sont reconnus · **un fournisseur à sec n'est appelé qu'une fois** · l'oubli expire.

**Suite complète en configuration CI (`:memory:`) : 3111 passed, 5 skipped.** Ruff : clean sur le périmètre.

## À faire côté Franck

Ajouter `SEARCHCANS_API_KEY` et `TAVILY_API_KEY` dans le **`.env` RACINE** (le conteneur lit celui-là, pas `backend/.env`), puis `make restart s=backend`.

author: talchain
body:
## ⚠️ Two things a reviewer should read first

### 1. A divergence nobody knew existed, surfaced *because* the reader was unified
Unifying the reader exposed that the two surfaces formatted the **same value** differently:

| surface | rendered |
|---|---|
| Decision Overview card (before) | `20%` |
| pre-analysis hero | `20 percent` |

**Cause:** the wire spells the unit as the **word** `'percent'` (CEE's `goal_threshold_unit`), but `classifyUnit` (`src/utils/unitClassifier.ts:80`) recognises only the **glyph** `'%'` — so `'percent'` fell through to `kind: 'other'` and rendered as a trailing suffix.

**The pre-analysis hero panel has therefore been rendering "20 percent" all along.** Nobody knew, because no single reader saw both.

Normalised inside `computeSuccessState` (`percent|percentage → '%'`) rather than widening `classifyUnit`, which is a shared primitive with many other consumers and its own tests. Both surfaces now agree, on the better of the two renderings.

**One narrowing is accepted and stated, not absorbed:** the retired `goalUnitRaw` selector also consulted `observedState.unit`, which `computeSuccessState` does not. That is a **third divergence**, on unit resolution. It is left for a follow-up rather than silently papered over in this PR.

### 2. Test re-pointing — the thing to check quickly
`DecisionOverviewCard.spec.tsx` expressed *"this decision HAS a success measure"* as `goalThreshold: 20` — the store field the card used to read. **19 tests depended on that harness assumption.**

- **Every one was re-pointed at source**, to `GOAL_NODE_WITH_MEASURE`, where the real reader now looks.
- **None deleted. None weakened. No baseline bumped. No test disabled or excluded.**
- The rationale is recorded **in the spec file itself**, next to the fixture, so the next reader does not have to find this PR.

Every test keeps its original intent and its original assertions.

---

## The defect

"Does this decision have a success measure?" was answered independently in two places, from two different sources, and they disagreed:

- **`computeSuccessState.ts`** reads the **wire**: `goalNode.data.goal_threshold_raw ?? analysisReady.goal_threshold_raw` → `isSet: true`, renders the value. **This one is honest.**
- **`DecisionOverviewCard`** read **`store.goalThreshold`**, which `deriveGoalThresholdFromNode` (`canvas/store.ts:1180-1196`) populates **only** when `data.threshold_source === 'user'`.

Verified at the bytes: `store.goalThreshold` is `null` for a goal node carrying `goal_threshold_raw`. So a **CEE-derived** threshold — the drafting path's normal output — was invisible to the card, which rendered **"Success measure missing"** *and* fell to the derived `thin` state (*"The goal has no success measure yet"*) for a decision that demonstrably had a measure on the wire.

That is a **false denial**: absence of a value in the wrong field rendered as positive evidence of absence.

## The fix is reuse, not addition

The card now routes through the **same two existing selectors** `usePreAnalysisModel` uses — `computeGraphFacts` for goal-node selection, `computeSuccessState` for the measure. No third derivation was introduced. Writing a local goal-node finder here would have minted exactly the mirror this lane exists to retire.

### Deletions this enabled
- the card's own **`goalUnitRaw`** selector — which carried a **fourth** independent goal-node finder (`nodes.find(n => n.type === 'goal')`, vs `graphFacts`' `kindOf()` **with an outcome fallback**, so the two could disagree)
- **`mapOutcomeUnit`** (a second unit vocabulary)
- the **`formatTargetValue`** import

## Evidence

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| **RED-first** (pristine `d7c55a18`) | **3 failed / 2 passed of 5.** The **PREMISE** test passed — proving the divergence is *real* (store `null`, selector `isSet: true`), not asserted. The **POSITIVE CONTROL** passed — proving the spec can see the "missing" copy, so the absence assertions are not vacuous. |
| **GREEN — targeted** | **28 files / 501 tests passed**, covering the decision-overview suite **and the whole pre-analysis-v3 suite** (the unit change's blast radius). |
| **GREEN — broad** | `src/components/results/` + `src/canvas/components/` + `src/canvas/nodes/` → **449 files, 7467 passed, 37 skipped, 0 failed, 0 collect errors**. |
| **MUTATION** | Throwaway worktree, production files reverted to HEAD, **anchor asserted** (0 remaining `successState.isSet` reads) → **3 failed / 2 passed**: exactly the three behavioural tests, with premise and positive control still green. |
| **Typecheck gate** | **PASSED** — 2661 vs baseline 2663, **identical to the pristine-`d7c55a18` control**, so this PR is exactly gate-neutral. Baseline deliberately **not** tightened. |
| **Lint** | clean |

## Scope
Files touched: `computeSuccessState.ts`, `DecisionOverviewCard.tsx`, its two specs. **No Lane R files touched** — `store.ts` was **read only**, to verify `deriveGoalThresholdFromNode`. Lane R is actively changing scenario persistence in that file.

## Measurement hygiene
`VITE_SUPABASE_URL` / `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` were set for every measurement (placeholder values, never printed). Every run reported **0 collect-time failures**, so no run silently measured a smaller suite.

author: axlguillen
body:
Answers the three questions a fleet monitor needs about this project: is data still being saved, is the MCP healthy, and does the page load.

- modules/health/status.ts holds the pure part (types + rollupStatus, unit tested); checks.ts holds the ones that touch DB/network. Split because server-only can't be imported from a test.
- Checks: database, page (self-fetch /login), mcp (self-fetch /api/mcp with no token, expecting 401 *with* WWW-Authenticate — the exact regression that bit us), ingestion.* (reuses getCaptureStatus), tokens.* and mcp.connectors. All run through allSettled with fetch timeouts so a hung check can't hang the endpoint, and one failing check doesn't hide the others.
- Without credentials it returns only {status, checkedAt}; the breakdown needs Authorization: Bearer $HEALTH_SECRET, so token expiry and cron state stay out of a public repo. A wrong secret answers like the public case rather than 401, so a bad header never looks like an outage.
- 503 only when something is actually broken; "ingestion late" or "token expiring" report degraded with 200 to keep the monitor quiet.
- HEALTH_SECRET is deliberately separate from CRON_SECRET: this URL is handed to a third-party monitor, and the cron secret would let it trigger ingestion.
- Platform tokens expose dates only, never the token itself.

Verified live: healthy run reports all 8 checks green with values matching reality (IG token 38 days out, captures 10.5h old); pointing the self-fetch at a dead host correctly produced down + 503 on both the public and detailed shapes.

* `completedRiemannZeta₀_conj : completedRiemannZeta₀ (conj s) = conj (completedRiemannZeta₀ s)`
* `completedRiemannZeta_conj : completedRiemannZeta (conj s) = conj (completedRiemannZeta s)`
  (both in `Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean`)

All three hold for **every** `s : ℂ`, with no points excluded — in particular no exclusion of the
poles `s = 0, 1` of `Λ`, since `Λ` is built from the entire function `Λ₀` by subtracting
`1 / s + 1 / (1 - s)` and Mathlib's `1 / 0 = 0` convention makes both sides agree there. They are
tagged `@[simp]`, matching the existing `riemannZeta_conj`.

### Why

Conjugation symmetry is a basic structural fact about `ζ` that Mathlib already has
(`riemannZeta_conj`, in `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Harmonic/ZetaAsymp.lean`), but the corresponding
statements for the completed functions `Λ`, `Λ₀` and for `Gammaℝ` were missing. The `Λ` version is
the one actually needed for work on the critical line: combined with the functional equation
`completedRiemannZeta_one_sub` it gives `conj (Λ ⟨1/2, t⟩) = Λ ⟨1/2, t⟩`, i.e. the Riemann
Ξ-function is real-valued on the critical line. It is also the natural form for completed
L-function arguments generally, where `Λ` rather than `ζ` is the object with the clean symmetry.

Note the `Λ` statements do **not** follow formally from `riemannZeta_conj`: the bridge
`riemannZeta_def_of_ne_zero` reads `ζ s = Λ s / Gammaℝ s`, and `Gammaℝ` vanishes at the trivial
zeros, so it cannot be inverted. The proof here instead runs the identity principle directly on the
entire function `Λ₀`.

### Proof

On the halfplane `1 < re s` the Dirichlet-series representation
`completedZeta_eq_tsum_of_one_lt_re` conjugates termwise (real coefficients), giving the result for
`Λ` and hence for `Λ₀` via `completedRiemannZeta_eq`. Since `Λ₀` is entire
(`differentiable_completedZeta₀`) and `conj ∘ Λ₀ ∘ conj` is entire by
`DifferentiableAt.conj_conj`, `AnalyticOnNhd.eq_of_eventuallyEq` propagates the identity from a
neighbourhood of `2` to all of `ℂ`. Transferring back through `completedRiemannZeta_eq` — which is
unconditional — yields `completedRiemannZeta_conj` with no side conditions.

### Drive-by

`riemannZeta_conj` in `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Harmonic/ZetaAsymp.lean` is golfed from ~25 lines to 4
by deriving it from `completedRiemannZeta_conj` and `Gammaℝ_conj` (statement, name and `@[simp]`
attribute unchanged); its two now-unused private imports are dropped. It no longer depends on
anything in `ZetaAsymp`, so it could reasonably be relocated to `RiemannZeta.lean` alongside the new
lemmas — happy to do that in this PR if reviewers prefer.

`Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean` gains one import,
`Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Star` (2 extra modules in the transitive closure).

### Checks

Built locally against master (`v4.33.0-rc1`): full `lake build Mathlib` completes with zero errors
and zero warnings; `lake exe lint-style` is clean on all three touched files. No `sorry`, no new
axioms.

Parts of this contribution were developed with AI assistance (Claude). All statements are machine-checked by the Lean kernel; `#print axioms` on the new declarations reports only `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

This PR is standalone and independent of my other open PRs (#42093, #42095, #42100).

author: tommy-xr
body:
## What

The `functor-lang` skill is the repo's stated **source of truth** for Functor Lang syntax and semantics — agents write game code from it, so a wrong claim propagates into broken games. A docs agent (#484) found the public manual had drifted *and* that some of the same errors lived in the skill. This PR audits the skill by **executing** its claims and fixes every one that disagreed with observed behavior.

## Verification method

No claim here was documented from reasoning — the pipe-direction and physics-timing semantics have burned agents doing exactly that.

- **Plain-language claims** — `cargo run --release -p functor-lang -- run|check|test` over scratch projects: one 56-assertion `expect` suite (builtins, stdlib, operators, precedence), 56 isolated single-claim programs for the error/negative cases, and 12 module/`.funi` cases.
- **Engine-prelude claims** — four scratch projects through the prebuilt release CLI (`build native` **plus** headless `run native`, since `check` alone does not validate that a member actually resolves in the host registry).
- **Remaining claims** — cross-checked against `functor-lang/src/`, `functor-prelude/prelude/*.funi`, and the runtime crates.

**~380 testable claims** inventoried; **9 errors found and fixed**, 6 omissions filled, 3 additions made. The large majority of the skill verified correct as written — including every one of ~180 prelude member names, arities, and argument orders across 25 namespaces.

## Errors corrected

| Claim | Reality |
|---|---|
| `f: ('a) => 'b` "does not parse" | Parses, checks, runs — and the file's own Syntax block already showed the feature, so it self-contradicted |
| Non-identifier file stem = load error | Warning + file skipped; the project loads fine (so the file contributes nothing) |
| Ctors: "the runtime checks ARITY only" | Ctors **curry** — `Rect(1.0)` is a partial that `Rect(1.0)(2.0)` completes; only over-application errors |
| Comparing functions = runtime error | Rejected at **check** time |
| "keep physics reads in `draw`" | Reads work in `tick`/`update`/`input` too — one step stale |
| *(implied)* physics hook can read bodies | **Deadlock** — see below |
| Commands apply "at the next stepped frame" | The next step *after queueing*; from `tick` that is this frame — except on zero-substep frames |
| `--fixed-time`: physics "never steps" | Exactly one bootstrap substep |
| Recursion trips "around n≈60" | Shape-dependent: bare tail call 62, operator-wrapped 42 |

The physics-hook item was caught by review, not by my first pass: reading `Physics.position` inside the `physics` hook is not a stale read but a **permanent deadlock** — the read raises before the hook returns its declaration, so the world is never declared, so the body never exists, so it raises again every frame (and takes `draw` down with it). My initial correction had over-generalized the benign tick-only case into "valid in ANY entry point". Reproduced across every frame of a live run.

## Additions

- ⚠️ **A miscased/misspelled type annotation silently disables checking.** `let f = (x: Float): Float => …` resolves to `Unknown`, and `f("a string")` then passes `check` with exit 0. This is the highest-value addition — it makes annotations look like they are working while they are not.
- The operator list is **exhaustive**: no `>=`, `<=`, `!=`, `<>`, `%`, `^`. (`x >= 0.0` is a parse error; this bit me during the audit itself.)
- Bare `Some`/`None`/`Ok`/`Error` do not resolve — qualify, or `open Option`.
- Omitted prelude members, each verified to resolve at runtime: `Scene.litTexture`/`emissiveTexture`, `Texture.file`, `Terrain.color`, `Effect.httpGet`/`httpPost`, `Net.HttpResponse`.

## Landing behavior (not documented as current)

Both are still open, and both are marked as landing rather than as today's behavior:

- **#485** — unknown builtin-module members become check-time errors. Today `List.thisDoesNotExist(…)` passes `check` (verified), so the skill documents the gap *and* the fix.
- **#488** — `functor test` runs expects under the engine prelude. The CLI has no `test` subcommand yet (verified against `--help`).

## Review

`/xreview` — both engines, Claude subagent + Codex CLI, run independently over the diff.

**Five findings [AGREED] by both engines**, all fixed: the physics-hook deadlock; the zero-substep exception to same-frame commands (the first pass contradicted the file's own raycast paragraph); "the checker is what catches" a dropped ctor argument being overstated; `Terrain.color` shown chained into `Terrain.layered` when `with_color` clears layers (`terrain.rs:191-195`), making the chained call dead; and "the two brands the signature accepts" versus an unconstrained `'texture` signature.

**Codex-only:** `update` is not uniformly pre-step — raycast and physics-event handlers run it POST-step against the current world; a "silently" that contradicted the warning it described; two quoted diagnostics missing their embedded token backticks.

**Rejected one finding with evidence:** the Claude reviewer's recursion figure (62/63) and my own (41/42) both reproduced — they are different recursion shapes. Bisected both and documented the range and the cause (an operator around the recursive call costs an extra eval level) rather than picking one misattributed number.

Re-validated after the fixes: 62 expects pass across the two scratch suites, the engine-prelude project still builds clean, prelude comment columns are unbroken, and every fenced and inline code span balances.

author: hmbown
body:
Finishes #4809. Part 1 (dropping the muted `Draft` title) landed in #4824; this is the height half.

## What was broken

`ComposerChrome::for_density` carried a `min_content_rows` floor (Compact 2 / Comfortable 3 / Spacious 4) and `desired_height` applied it whenever the terminal was tall enough. Consequences:

- an empty composer on a fresh session rendered 3 blank input rows plus chrome (Comfortable), spending vertical space on nothing;
- height was a function of the density setting, not of the draft, so it never came back down to one row after submit or clear — the floor was already the height.

## Why the fix is shaped this way

Density becomes a *cap*, not a floor. `min_content_rows` and `absolute_min_total` are deleted; `ComposerChrome` keeps `border_rows` and `max_total_rows`. `desired_height` is then just `content_lines (>=1) + menu rows + border`, clamped by `min(available_height, max_total_rows)`. That gives all three acceptance behaviors from one expression rather than special cases:

- empty / single-line -> `content_lines == 1` -> one input row;
- N typed lines -> N input rows until the density cap clamps -> `min(N, cap)`;
- submit or clear empties `app.input` -> back to `content_lines == 1` -> one row.

The compact-terminal rule is preserved: the border is shed before typed content. Menus, the panel-vs-quiet-rule shape decision, top-right chrome, and `top_padding` are untouched. No new per-frame work — the wrap/line count was already computed for `desired_height`.

## Tests

Rewrote the four `composer_chrome` unit tests around the new contract (exact equalities instead of `>=` floors) and updated the widget tests that asserted the old baseline heights. Added one end-to-end acceptance test that goes through the real widget and the real `App` mutators (`insert_str`, `submit_input`, `clear_input`) rather than the pure helper:

`tui::widgets::tests::composer_auto_fits_typed_lines_and_returns_to_one_row_on_submit_or_clear`

It asserts: empty -> (3 total, 1 inner); single line -> (3, 1); N=2..7 typed lines -> (N+2, N); 40 lines -> clamped to the Comfortable cap of 9; after `submit_input()` -> (3, 1); a fresh 4-line draft -> (6, 4); after `clear_input()` -> (3, 1).

## Gates actually run (macOS, local)

```
cargo fmt --all && cargo fmt --all -- --check   # clean
git diff --check                                # clean
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --bin codewhale-tui --locked composer
  -> test result: ok. 109 passed; 0 failed; 8063 filtered out
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --bin codewhale-tui --locked widgets::
  -> test result: ok. 268 passed; 0 failed; 7904 filtered out
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --bin codewhale-tui --locked height / layout / chrome
  -> ok. 15 passed / 7 passed / 16 passed; 0 failed
```

`cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` does **not** pass on this machine — but it does not pass on the base commit either. I measured both: 42 `^error` lines on `32e6dec` (stashed working tree) and 42 with this change, and none of them are in `composer_chrome.rs` or `widgets/mod.rs` (they are `settings.rs`, `ambient_life.rs`, `setup/tools_mcp.rs`, `commands/groups/**`, etc. — local clippy is newer than CI's). So this PR adds zero lint findings, but I cannot claim a green clippy run.

## Not verified

- No `cargo test --workspace` and no `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo test -p codewhale-tui --all-features` run (parallel agents are sharing the build slot); other crates' tests are unexercised, though nothing outside `crates/tui` is touched and `min_content_rows`/`absolute_min_total` had no other referents (`rg` across the repo).
- No visual dogfood pass in a real terminal — the evidence here is buffer-level assertions, not a screenshot.

author: luckythemonster
body:
Replaces the generic `monospace` / `"Courier New"` stack throughout.

- **Share Tech Mono** for everything.
- **Share Tech** — the proportional cut of the same family — for the three big scene titles (`ARTICLE ZERO`, `ALIGNED`, `INTO THE LATTICE`).

Both are self-hosted from `src/ui/fonts/` under the OFL rather than linked from a CDN: the game otherwise makes no third-party requests, and the typeface decides every Phaser `Text` object's metrics — not something to put behind a network the player may not have. They sit under `src/` rather than `public/` so Vite fingerprints them and rewrites the URL against `base: "./"`; a `public/` font would need a root-absolute `/fonts/...` that breaks off a domain root.

The two faces are named once, in `src/ui/fonts.ts`, rather than at each of the ~40 call sites that carried the literal. Share Tech Mono is a true monospace (every advance is 540/1000), which the HUD depends on — the SRP axes, the inventory's right-aligned counts and the pause menu's indented rows all line up by character cell. Share Tech is proportional, so it's confined to standalone centred titles.

## Three things this needed beyond a find-and-replace

**Boot now waits for the fonts** (`src/ui/fontsReady.ts`). Phaser rasterises a `Text` to a canvas texture at construction and never redraws it, so a label built while the font is still in flight keeps the fallback face for the entire session — silently, with no error and nothing to retry. `TitleScene.create()` runs almost immediately, so this race is lost on a cold cache without the wait. It's bounded by a timeout and fails open: a blocked font costs the typeface, never the game. The same reasoning drives `font-display: block` here — a face that swaps in late never reaches the canvas at all, so the usual swap advice is backwards for a canvas game.

**`Menu` draws its selection caret as its own object.** Neither cut carries `✓ ○ ▸ ◎ ← → ↑ ↓` — checked against the full upstream TTFs, not just Google's web subset — so those fall back per glyph. That's harmless for centred one-off lines, and harmless for the objective list where every line starts with a fallback glyph so they all shift together. But the menu prefixed `"▸ "` against two spaces, so the swap resized the string and slid the centred label sideways on every selection change. Now the caret is positioned separately at a fixed x; verified fixed by pixel-measuring both states, where the labels' ink extents come out identical.

**`@font-face` lives in its own `fonts.css`**, imported once per page entry. Declaring it in `theme.css` put five copies in the built CSS, since Vite inlines an `@import` into every chunk and four stylesheets pull that file.

## Verification

`npm run build` and `npm test` green (255 tests). Driven against the built bundle in a browser: both faces fetch 200 and report `loaded`, `document.fonts.check` passes for both families, all three pages (game + the two minigame harnesses) link the chunk carrying the declarations, and the title screen, HUD, codec and all nine pause tabs render in the new face with no console errors.

author: fiorelorenzo
body:
`SessionManager`'s class doc says "`.loombox/` is expected to be git-ignored by consuming projects", which quietly made every user responsible for cleaning up after us. The node writes worktrees into their repo, so the first isolated session leaves an untracked `.loombox/` in their `git status` forever unless they happened to read that comment and act on it.

loombox's own repo was no exception, which is how I noticed: creating one real session to verify #507's worktree wiring end to end left `.loombox/` sitting untracked here.

The node now writes the standard self-ignoring `.gitignore` (`*`) into the directory before the first worktree lands. It needs no cooperation from the project and cannot be forgotten. It never overwrites an existing file, so a project that deliberately committed something under `.loombox/` keeps its own rules, and a failure to write it only warns: a dirty `git status` is a much smaller problem than refusing to start the session the user actually asked for.

Two tests: a real session in a real temp repo leaves `git status --porcelain` empty, and an existing `.loombox/.gitignore` is left alone.

| `/backend/` directory | No such directory; the app lives at the repo root |
| `python -m venv` + `pip install -r requirements.txt` | `uv sync` (there is no `requirements.txt`) |
| `app/api/`, `app/models/`, `app/schemas/`, `app/core/`, `app/services/` packages | Flat modules: `api.py`, `models.py`, `auth.py`, `db.py`, `cli.py`, `feed.py`, `scheduler.py`, `storage.py`, `tag_suggester.py`, plus `digest/` and `images/` |
| `uvicorn app.main:app`, port 8000 | `app.api:app`, port 8100 |
| `npm install` | pnpm 10.33.0, pinned via `packageManager` |
| Python 3.11+, Node 18+ | 3.13 and 22, pinned in `mise.toml` |
| React 18+ | React 19 |
| Theme has `title` + optional `description` | Theme has `body_md`; a migration merged those fields |
| Work tracked in `.llm/active-plan.md` | That file does not exist; work is in GitHub Issues + `docs/roadmap.md` |
| Railway auto-deploy from main | Dockerfile build, deployed by GitHub Actions |

Rewritten from the code. Route list re-derived from the actual decorators, which surfaced the digest, subscriber, internal-cron and auth routers that were missing entirely. Added digests and cover images (both postdate the original). Added mise as the setup path. Verified all five `mise run` task names exist in `mise.toml`.

## `README.md`

Two claims that would actively mislead a newcomer:

1. **"auto-deploy from main"** — Railway's native git trigger is deliberately disconnected. Someone reading this would re-enable it, which `CLAUDE.md` explicitly forbids (it restores the silent-failure mode and causes double deploys).
2. **`npm install`** — the frontend is pnpm-pinned; npm would produce a stray `package-lock.json` and bypass the pinned version.

Also added the mise quickstart and corrected the stack line.

## `docs/roadmap.md`

The one-line Deploy entry predated all of this; it now records the 2026-07 hardening and points at the postmortem.

## Also checked, no change needed

- No dangling references anywhere in `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/`, `README.md`, or `llms.txt` (the #99 problem class is now clear).
- `docs/log/` index is consistent with its five entries.
- `.llm/` does not exist, so there are no raw learnings pending promotion.

## Noted, left alone

`docs/backfill.md` (199 lines, untouched since 2026-02-14) is orphaned: nothing references it, and it is a one-time working document for populating the production database, a task long since completed. By the `.llm/` vs `docs/` split it was ephemeral material filed in the durable home. Flagging rather than deleting, since that is the owner's call.

Docs only, no code changes.

author: seanfillmore
body:
## Why

Sean asked why he was doing the 10%→15% plan fix by hand when I have Recurpay credentials. Fair question — so I checked properly instead of repeating the handoff doc.

**The API genuinely cannot do it. But the handoff's stated reason was imprecise**, which is what made it worth re-testing.

## Root cause, verified live

```
POST/PUT reject any selling_plans array with more than one item
422 "The selling_plans must contain exactly one item."
```

So the single selling plan you send **always lands at position 1**, carrying your delivery and billing policy with it. That is precisely why a 12-week payload sent to plan `11150632` previously rewrote that plan's *4-week* position-1 plan to deliver every 12 weeks. It's an arity constraint, not a quirk of which id you pass.

**My first hypothesis was wrong** — I expected sending the *full* array would make positions 2+ addressable. The API refuses it outright. Tested by creating throwaway plan `11151694`, attempting a 2-item PUT, and deleting it. No production plan touched.

**Shopify isn't an alternative route either.** `sellingPlanGroupUpdate` on a Recurpay-owned group returns `"Selling plan group does not exist."` even though the group reads fine per-product. Tested; errors without mutating.

So positions 2+ really are UI-only, and the three plans at 10% really do need Sean — now proven rather than inherited.

## What's in the library

`lib/recurpay.js` carries the client and every constraint found, including the ones that cost time:

- Auth is `X-Recurpay-Access-Token`, **not** `Authorization: Bearer` — which 404s with an empty body and reads like a wrong path
- Subdomain is the Shopify store handle minus `.myshopify.com`
- The discount field is spelled **`pricing_polices`** — Recurpay's typo, in request and response both

**`updatePlan()` refuses a target holding more than one selling plan** unless forced, and prints the positions it would destroy. That guard is the real fix: the destructive incident is now unreachable by accident, rather than documented in a doc nobody reads at the right moment.

## Audit

`npm run recurpay-audit` prints every plan with cadence, discount, and writability; exits nonzero while any plan is off the flat-15% rule.

```
PLAN       POS  CADENCE      DISCOUNT  WRITABLE      NAME
11150631   2    8 week       10%       UI only       8 Week subscription   <<< not 15%
11150632   2    8 week       10%       UI only       8 Week subscription   <<< not 15%
11150632   3    12 week      10%       UI only       12 Week subscription  <<< not 15%
```

author: aias00
body:
## Related issue

Closes #2134

## Summary

`BaseImporter.getSQLDataValue` set `dataType.setScale(column.getColumnSize())` and `dataType.setPrecision(column.getDecimalDigits())` — inverted. Precision is the total digit count (column size) and scale is the digits after the decimal point (decimal digits). The sibling `BaseExcelImporter.getSQLDataValue` does it correctly: `setScale(column.getDecimalDigits()); setPrecision(column.getColumnSize());`. `BaseImporter` is live (`JSONImporter` extends it), so JSON imports fed value processors swapped precision/scale for `DECIMAL`/`NUMERIC` columns. Swapped the two lines to mirror `BaseExcelImporter`.

## Affected surfaces

- [ ] Frontend / Web
- [x] Backend / API / Storage
- [ ] Database plugin / Driver
- [ ] JCEF / Desktop packaging
- [ ] CI / Build / Release
- [ ] Documentation only

## Verification

- Commands and results: `mvn -B -q -f chat2db-community-server/pom.xml -pl chat2db-community-domain/chat2db-community-domain-core -am -Dmaven.test.skip=true compile` -> BUILD SUCCESS.
- Manual verification: `getSQLDataValue` now sets `scale=decimalDigits` and `precision=columnSize`, matching `BaseExcelImporter` (and `DefaultSqlBuilder`).
- UI evidence: N/A

## Risk and compatibility

- Public API or stored data: N/A — only changes the precision/scale assignment for the JSON import path.
- Database or driver compatibility: JSON imports into `DECIMAL`/`NUMERIC` now produce correct literals.
- Network, privacy, or security: N/A.
- Community / Local / Pro boundary: N/A.
- Backward compatibility: Fixes inverted precision/scale; no API change.

## Reviewer map

- Start here: `BaseImporter.java:39-40` — swapped `setScale`/`setPrecision` to `setScale(decimalDigits)` / `setPrecision(columnSize)`, mirroring `BaseExcelImporter`.
- Failure condition: JSON import of a `DECIMAL`/`NUMERIC` still produces swapped-precision literals.
- Rollback or disable path: Revert this single commit.

## Contributor declaration

- [x] I linked the Issue that defines this change.
- [x] I tested the affected behavior and reported the actual results above.
- [x] I did not include credentials, private data, or generated build output.
- [x] I disclosed substantial AI assistance below, or this PR contains no substantial AI-generated code.

author: kimdem
body:
## Why

QA Cycle(`qa_try`) 실행 중 Agent가 게임에서 발견한 이슈(버그)를 심각도와 함께
보고하지만, 이를 받아 저장하거나 조회할 곳이 없었다. Agent → Orchestration
인바운드 경로로 이슈를 받아 새 `issue` 도메인에 저장하고, FE/사용자가 조회하는
엔드포인트를 추가한다.

Agent 서버는 아직 이슈 메시지를 정의하지 않았으므로, **인바운드 계약을 먼저
정의**한다(아래 "제안 계약" 참고 — Agent 팀이 구현할 스펙).

## What Changed

- **심각도 사다리(ordered enum)** 신설
- **`issue` 테이블(Flyway V12)** + entity/repository/service/dto/controller (package-by-feature)
- 기존 QA WebSocket 인바운드 라우터에 **`ISSUE` 타입 라우팅** 추가 → 저장(멱등)
- **조회 엔드포인트** `GET /api/issues`(JWT + 프로젝트 멤버)

### 심각도 사다리 (높음 → 낮음)

`BLOCKER > CRITICAL > MAJOR > MINOR > TRIVIAL`

| 값 | 의미 |
|---|---|
| `BLOCKER` | 게임이 아예 진행 불가 — QA 자체를 더 못 이어감 |
| `CRITICAL` | 핵심 기능이 깨졌고 우회 수단 없음 |
| `MAJOR` | 중요한 기능이 깨졌으나 우회 수단은 있음 (사용자 언급) |
| `MINOR` | 영향이 작거나 국소적인 결함 |
| `TRIVIAL` | 외형/문구 등 사소한 결함 |

저장은 이름 그대로 VARCHAR + CHECK(`qa_try.status`와 동일 방식).

### 제안 인바운드 계약 (Agent → Orchestration, PROPOSED)

기존 `QaAgentEnvelope` 프레임을 그대로 재사용하고 `type = "ISSUE"`만 신설한다:

```jsonc
{
  "messageId": "<uuid>",            // 필수, UUID (기존 라우터 가드)
  "type": "ISSUE",
  "qaTryId": "<qa_try id>",
  "correlationId": "<uuid|null>",   // 선택: 이슈를 유발한 ACTION/스텝
  "timestamp": "<ISO-8601>",
  "payload": {
    "severity": "BLOCKER|CRITICAL|MAJOR|MINOR|TRIVIAL",  // 필수
    "title": "<한 줄 요약>",                               // 필수 (타임라인 표시 문구)
    "detail": "<상세 설명>",                               // 선택
    // ...expected/actual, 재현 스텝, 스크린샷 참조 등 구조화된 근거...
  }
}
```

- `payload` 전체가 `issue.detail`(JSONB)로 저장되고, `severity`/`title`은 조회·정렬을 위해 컬럼으로 승격된다.
- `severity`가 없거나 사다리에 없는 값이거나 `title`이 비면 → `ORCHE_INTERNAL` ERROR 로그를 남기고 이슈는 저장하지 않는다(프레임 드롭, 실행은 실패시키지 않음 — 라우터의 기존 "throw 대신 값 검증" 정책과 동일).
- `messageId`로 멱등하다. 재전송된 프레임은 중복 행을 만들지 않는다.

### 마이그레이션 버전 주의 (V12, V11 아님)

이 브랜치에는 이미 `V10__create_reference_context.sql`, `V11__add_qa_chat_direction_and_type.sql`가 커밋되어 있다. 원래 계획은 V11이었으나 충돌하므로 **V12**를 사용한다. (Flyway 버전 충돌이 과거 develop을 조용히 깨뜨린 이력이 있어 주의.)

## Code Walkthrough

- `src/main/resources/db/migration/V12__create_issue.sql` — `issue` 테이블. `qa_try`에 하드 FK `ON DELETE CASCADE`(qa_log와 동일: 이슈는 실행에 종속된 증거), `severity` CHECK, `detail` JSONB, `uk_issue_message (qa_try_id, message_id)` 부분 유니크로 재전송 멱등, `idx_issue_qa_try_id_desc (qa_try_id, id DESC)`로 최신순 조회.
- `issue/entity/IssueSeverity.kt:20` — 심각도 enum + `NAMES`(라우터 검증용).
- `issue/entity/IssueEntity.kt` — R2DBC 엔티티. created/updated는 서비스에서 stamp(R2DBC가 기본값 컬럼을 다시 읽지 않음 — QaLogEntity와 동일).
- `issue/service/IssueService.kt:41` — `recordAgentIssue`(payload를 detail로 저장, 1 MiB 상한, `DataIntegrityViolationException` 캐치→조회로 멱등)와 `listByQaTry`(qa_try 접근권한 가드, `Mono<List>`로 접근불가 404 vs 접근가능 빈목록 200 [] 구분).
- `issue/controller/IssueController.kt:31` — `listIssuesForQaTry`, thin, size 1..200 바운드.
- `qa/service/QaAgentInboundRouter.kt:77` — `ISSUE` 타입을 `SUPPORTED_TYPES`에 추가, 표시 필드는 `payload.title`, `routeIssue`가 severity 검증 후 `IssueService`로 위임.
- `auth/config/SecurityConfig.kt:85` — `/api/issues/**` 인증 필요(조회는 엔드유저 경로).

## Validation

- [x] `./mvnw test-compile`
- [x] `./mvnw -Dtest=IssueIntegrationTest test` (실 PostgreSQL) — 5/5 통과: 저장(severity/title/detail), messageId 멱등, 잘못된 severity 드롭, 멤버 조회 200 / 비멤버 404 / 접근가능·이슈없음 200 []
- [x] IssueIntegrationTest + 기존 game/qa 통합 테스트 동시 실행 20/20 통과(FK 격리 확인)

전체 스위트를 한 번에 돌리면 실패가 나오지만, 이는 이 변경 이전 clean 체크아웃에서도 재현되는 **기존 공유 DB 테스트 격리 문제**(app_user/project_document FK)로 본 변경과 무관하다.

## Risks

- QA 인바운드 수신 루프(`QaAgentInboundRouter`)를 건드리지만 `ISSUE` 분기는 독립적이며 severity/title 검증 실패 시 실행을 죽이지 않는다.
- `qa.service` → `issue.service` 패키지 의존(요구된 통합 지점).

## Rollback

`issue` 도메인 파일 삭제 + 라우터/SecurityConfig 되돌림 + V12 롤백. `issue` 테이블은 다른 테이블이 참조하지 않아 drop 안전.

## Agent 팀에 남은 작업 / Open questions

- Agent 서버가 위 **제안 계약**대로 `type=ISSUE` 프레임을 QA 세션 소켓으로 전송하도록 구현.
- `detail`의 구조화 필드(expected/actual, 재현 스텝, 스크린샷 참조 포맷) 세부는 Agent 팀과 합의 필요 — 현재는 자유형 JSON을 그대로 저장.
- (범위 밖) 이슈 상태 워크플로우/담당자/알림, ISSUE의 qa_log 타임라인 동시 기록은 의도적으로 제외.
