author: kevinselwyn
body:
## Summary

Adds `plans/009-comment-directives.md` **and implements its Phase 0**. The plan turns nessemble's one ad-hoc comment hint into a small, namespaced, validated directive system: the formatter's `; @fmt stride=N` becomes **`; @nessemble-format stride=N`** (with `@fmt` kept as a permanent deprecated alias), and `nessemble coverage` gains **`; @nessemble-coverage-ignore-next-line`** plus a **`; @nessemble-coverage-ignore start` / `end`** region pair. All five open questions are settled and recorded in §13.

**Phase 0 (this PR)** lands the registry in `nessemble-core::tooling` and re-founds the formatter's hint parsing on it. The coverage directives are recognized and validated but have no consumer yet — that's Phase 2.

## Changeset

- [x] Added a changeset (`nessemble: major | minor | patch`) with a user-facing summary.
- [x] No release impact — a `nessemble: none` changeset, or the `no-changeset` label.

Two changesets: `minor` for the Phase 0 API + the new `@nessemble-format` spelling, `none` for the plan document.

## Changes

**nessemble-core** (Phase 0)

- **Comment-directive registry** — a new section of `tooling.rs` (placed before the linting section, mirroring how plan 008's rule engine landed): `DirectiveName` + the `DIRECTIVES` table, `DirectiveArgs`/`RegionBound`, `Directive`, `MalformedReason`/`MalformedDirective`, `scan_directives`, `scan_directives_with_errors`. Built on the existing lossless lexer; **no new dependencies**.
- **Exact-token lookup** — `@nessemble-coverage-ignore-next-line` can never resolve as `@nessemble-coverage-ignore` with a stray argument.
- **Arguments parsed in the scanner** (stride lists, `start`/`end`) rather than handed back as a raw string. That's what lets the scanner separate a *malformed* directive from prose at all — `BadArgs` falls out of the same parse — and it drops the lifetime so `Directive` is owned.
- **Token byte range** on both `Directive` and `MalformedDirective`, because the Phase 3 quick fix rewrites exactly that span and diagnostics narrow to it.
- **`@fmt` re-founded, not reimplemented** — `parse_hint` now goes through the scanner, so both spellings share one parse and cannot drift. A hint in a trailing comment stays inert, as before.
- **Prose is untouchable** — only `@nessemble-`-prefixed tokens (plus the `@fmt` alias) can be malformed; `@todo`, `@param`, `@NESSEMBLE-FORMAT`, and mid-sentence mentions are prose.

**plans/** — `009-comment-directives.md`, with §6.1 rewritten to describe what actually landed and Phase 0 marked done.

### The language-server question (§8)

Not needed for correctness, but the feature is unusable without some of it — and the valuable part is nearly free. All three tiers are in scope per review:

1. **Diagnostics — zero new LSP code.** The Phase 1 lint rules publish as LSP diagnostics automatically through the `with_lint` step from plan 008, so a mistyped directive squiggles in the editor for free. Format-on-save already honors `@nessemble-format` as of this PR, since `format_document` calls `tooling::format`.
2. **Completion, hover, quick fix** — with `@nessemble-coverage-ignore` offered pre-filled as `start` and `end`, never as a bare stem the user can leave malformed.
3. **Distinct highlighting via a modifier, not a new token class.** `TokenClass::wire_id` is a frozen contract shared with the wasm highlighter, so directive comments keep token type `Comment` (wire id 5) and gain the standard `documentation` semantic-token modifier; the legend currently declares `token_modifiers: Vec::new()`, so populating it is purely additive.

## Golden ROMs & safety

- Golden-ROM corpus tests still pass
- CLI `assemble` path unchanged — this is tooling-path-only (`tooling.rs`), no assembler code touched

## Verification

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace`

New tests: every registry name; both region bounds; exact-match (`-next-line` never resolves as the region directive); `@fmt` flagged deprecated but honored; indentation and `;;`/`;;;` leaders; trailing prose after args; a trailing-comment directive marked `own_line: false`; six prose cases untouched; a directive inside a string literal not scanned; unknown namespaced name; eight bad-argument cases; position + token byte range; source order; registry round-trip. Plus formatter regressions: the original `@fmt` fixtures still pass byte-for-byte, the same fixtures pass with `@nessemble-format`, `respectStrideHints: false` disables both spellings, and a trailing hint stays inert.

## Docs & notes

**One deliberate behavior widening worth your eyes** (§6.1): the scanner skips the whole leading `;` run, so `;; @nessemble-format stride=2` is now a directive where the old single-`;` parser treated it as prose. That makes `;;`-banner comment styles work, but it costs one idiom — "comment out a hint by adding a `;`" no longer disables it. It's a one-line change to restrict it back to a single `;` if you'd rather keep that escape hatch.

**One derived decision** (§13.1): with regions replacing the whole-file directive, the `start`/`end` argument is **required** — a bare `; @nessemble-coverage-ignore` is malformed rather than a whole-file shorthand, since keeping the shorthand would give it a meaning that conflicts with `start` on the same line. Whole-file is a `start` in the header with no `end`.

Still flagged for Phase 2: how the source map attributes emissions inside a macro body (definition line vs. invocation site) decides where an ignore comment must go; that phase pins it with a fixture.

author: bwaldrep
body:
Presentation-only typography pass. No composed text changes — golden files untouched and the e2e golden suite passes.

The self-hosted EB Garamond regular and italic carry real `smcp`, `c2sc`, `onum`, `lnum`, `liga`, `dlig` and `hlig`; the stylesheet was asking for almost none of it.

## Small caps are now real

`.section-heading` and `.session-prayers summary` set **both** `font-variant: small-caps` **and** `text-transform: uppercase`. The transform wins: the shaper only ever sees capitals, so there is nothing left for `smcp` to shrink and the heading renders as flat full caps. Every "small caps" heading on an hour page was really just uppercase.

Both now use `font-variant-caps: all-small-caps`, which engages `smcp` and `c2sc` together so a mixed-case label sets as one even small-cap band. Audited the other users of the old shorthand as well:

| Selector | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `.section-heading`, `.session-prayers summary` | `all-small-caps` | the fix above |
| `.item-label` | `all-small-caps` | "Psalm 67", "Salve Regina" — label-shaped |
| `.antiphon em` | `all-small-caps` | "Ant." is an abbreviation, not a word with a leading capital |
| `.home-prayer-card h2`, `.reminders legend` | `all-small-caps` | short labels |
| `.assurance-panel > summary` | `small-caps` | a sentence with counts; the leading capital should stay |

Real small caps are drawn wider-fit than synthesised ones, so tracking comes in a little (0.16em → 0.13em on headings) and the affected sizes come up a step (1.05 → 1.12rem) to hold the same presence now that the glyphs sit at small-cap height rather than cap height.

## Old-style figures

`font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums` where numbers sit inside or beside prayer text: verse numbers, hour meta, chapter/scripture refs, the Gloria Patri, the home date, the calendar year headings and month tables. Text figures sit on the baseline with ascenders and descenders, so "Saturday, July 25, 2026" reads as part of the line instead of a row of full-height slabs.

Form controls (date picker, time inputs, reminder select) deliberately keep lining figures — that is what a control is expected to show. Note the bold face is subset without OpenType features, so bold numerals (the calendar's day numbers) keep lining figures regardless; nothing to do there without unsubsetting the bold woff2.

## Selection wash

`::selection` is a warm translucent gold in both themes rather than the browser's blue — selecting a verse to copy should look like light on the page, not like a form field. Text colour is left at each theme's own so selected words stay legible (checked: comfortably above 4.5:1 on both plaster and apse).

## Gilded drop caps

Gold leaf is never one flat tone. The psalm and chapter drop caps and the ✠ take a two-stop gradient about 15% apart in lightness, raked at 145°, via `background-clip: text`. Dark theme gets its own lighter pair against the night sky.

Two safety rails:

- The whole block is gated on `@supports ((-webkit-background-clip: text) or (background-clip: text))`, so no browser can land on `color: transparent` without the clip and lose the letter entirely. Unsupported browsers keep flat `--gold`.
- **Print**: the print sheet flattens these to `#444`. Colour alone is not enough — without also clearing `background-image` the glyph prints as an empty outline. The appended print block resets the image, the clip and the colour, and sits last in the file so it wins on source order.

## `lang="la"`

Hymn incipits (`.hymn-title`, `.hymn-latin`) and Marian antiphon titles (`.marian-antiphon .item-label`) are Latin standing above English bodies. Confirmed before tagging rather than assumed: all 115 hymn titles in `data/texts/` are Latin incipits ("Te lucis ante terminum", "Iam lucis orto sidere", …), and `marianLabel` returns only the four Latin titles. Nothing else was tagged — antiphon bodies, collects and canticle names ("Benedictus", "Magnificat") are English or English-by-convention.

## Desktop scrollbar and touch polish

- `scrollbar-width: thin` with a muted oak / apse-gold thumb on a transparent track, scoped to `min-width: 701px` so mobile overlay scrollbars are untouched. Both themes.
- `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent` plus `user-select: none` on navigation chrome only: brand, site menu, theme switch, date-nav summary, hour chips, continuation labels, month jump. **Not** on prayer text, dates, feast names or the assurance panel — anything a reader might legitimately copy stays selectable.

## Skipped

**Double gold hairlines on `.hour-header h1` (item 5).** No clean approach found. `border-image` cannot be combined with `border-style: double` — they are mutually exclusive, so the gradient simply would not apply. The alternatives (stacked pseudo-elements, or a 3px band with a striped `mask-image` faking the doubling) replace a core motif's implementation for a marginal effect, need their own print path to restore the flat `#888` the print sheet already sets on that border, and would collide with any sibling work on the hour header. Left as a flat double hairline.

## Structure

New rules are appended in one clearly-commented `===== Typographic polish =====` section at the end of `style.css`, so the print flattening sits next to what it undoes and merge conflicts with sibling PRs stay small. Only the small-caps corrections are in-place edits, since they had to remove the conflicting `text-transform`.

## Verification

Rendered light + dark at 390px and at desktop width across hour, home and ordo pages in headless Chromium and read the results: headings now show true small-cap glyphs, "July 25, 2026" sets in text figures, the drop caps carry a visible but quiet gradient in both themes, and the selection wash stays legible on plaster and on the apse blue.

`make check` passes (fmt, vet, staticcheck, eslint, all Go tests including e2e golden, validate, lint-texts). `go test ./internal/render/ ./internal/web/` passes.

⚠️ **The Playwright visual snapshots will need regenerating** — this changes rendered type on every page. Per the README, review the expected/actual/diff images in the Playwright report artifact, then apply the `update-ux-snapshots` label to this PR. I did not regenerate them locally: they are pinned to CI's browser container and host rendering would differ. (Playwright is not installed in this checkout, so the functional `ux.spec.js` suite was not run locally either.)

author: jxsl13
body:
T-01KYE5E0G3EPVSCR384DF6W58X the rule need-refusal teaches the whole call shape once, measured against the tricky curve

Wandering analysis of the first tricky judge batch (T-01KYE4 meters): 17 to 22 of 30 to 38 calls per run were refusals — cheap since T-01KYE0, but the CALL count is trial-and-error dominated, and rule leads the refusal table in every run (seven in the worst): agents grope through op variants (create for add), invented fields (txt for the slot set) and partial slots across three to five attempts, because the need response names each missing SLOT but never the assembled CALL. Change, one surface, measured: ruleAdd appends one dense shape line to its need refusal — shape: rule {op:add, dir, stem, pattern:U|E|S|N|O|C, system, response} with placeholder guidance that the response names a verifiable number — so the first refusal carries everything needed for the second call to succeed. Cost model stated up front: roughly +100 bytes on a surface read only when a call already failed, bought against two to four saved refusal round trips at ~90 bytes each plus the unmetered agent reasoning per extra turn. Tests: the need response carries the shape line exactly once and still every missing slot question; the shape line names all six fields. VERIFY: go test ./internal/mcpserver/ -count=1 green; scripted bench A/B expected within noise (its rule call is fully slotted, stated); the decisive measure is a fresh tricky judge batch n=3 against the candidate, compared with the 30/34/38 calls and 3223/3612/4202 bytes reference curve — rule-refusal count per run and the aggregate spread recorded in the archive note, whichever way it lands.

body:
Closes #36. One PR, no children — both changes edit `policies/baseline.yaml`.

## What

**1. `self-mod-guard` now covers `init/templates/**` and `actions/**`.** It protected `.github/workflows/**` — *this* repo's CI — but not the workflow stubs and composite actions every consuming repo installs and runs. PR #33 changed the post-merge stub and scored `low`, eligible for auto-merge. The rule is `locked`, so no consuming pack can weaken it.

**2. A baseline rule keyed on `domains.max_criticality: high`.** The domain map classified everything and nothing outside a project's own `critical` rule ever read it, so a `high` domain scored identically to a `low` one.

Deliberate choices, each with a fixture recording it:
- **Floor `medium`, not `high`** — high domains cover most of a repo; flooring them all would make ordinary work indistinguishable from self-modification. The obligation that matters is `human-merge`.
- **Code only** — a README inside a high domain shouldn't demand a human merge.

## Blast radius — measured, not asserted

The plan promised this before adoption. Old pack vs new, over this session's eight merged PRs, using their real diffs:

```
#30  low/-                  -> low/-
#31  low/-                  -> medium/human-merge       <-- CHANGED
#32  high/G2+human-merge    -> high/G2+human-merge
#33  low/-                  -> high/G2+human-merge      <-- CHANGED
#34  low/-                  -> low/-
#35  high/G2+human-merge    -> high/G2+human-merge
#37  low/-                  -> low/-
#42  medium/human-merge     -> medium/human-merge
```

**#33 is the motivating case**, moving exactly as intended.

**#31 was not in the plan's prediction table.** The plan said an unpredicted move is "a finding about the rule, not a surprise to accept", so I checked it: #31 touches `scripts/e2e/{cli,smoke}.js` — the `e2e-runner` domain, criticality `high`, change class `code`. The rule fired correctly; my prediction was incomplete. Reporting it rather than quietly widening the table after the fact.

## The finding this surfaced — filed as #46

**#34 did *not* move, and that is a problem.** It added `agentflow-release`, the command that cuts tags and GitHub releases:

```
#34 domains: {"touched":["docs"], "max_criticality":"low", "unmapped_fraction":0.8}
```

80% of that diff is invisible to `domains.yml`. The only thing the map recognised was the README, so the most consequential new code in the repo scored as a docs change. Repo-wide, `adopt --coverage` reports **26% unmapped, already breaching the configured 20% threshold** — including `scripts/release/**`, `scripts/next/**`, and `.github/workflows/**` itself.

This PR makes that matter: unmapped code now silently scores as if it were low-criticality. Filed as #46 rather than fixed here — the map is a separate surface, and widening this PR to cover it would put `domains.yml` in a policy-only diff.

## Verified

- `agentflow-policy test policies/baseline.yaml` — **12/12**, six fixtures new
- `npm test` — green
- Old-vs-new comparison above, run against real PR diffs

## Risk

`self-mod-guard` matches `policies/**`, so this PR floors itself at `high` and requires G2 + a human merge — correct for a change to the rules that decide whether anything else needs a human.

author: claoie
body:
## Summary

Every message our `POST /api/mails/send` path sent to Gmail was silently bounced downstream of Mailgun's API accept, with:

```
5.7.1 This message is not RFC 5322 compliant. There are multiple To
headers. To reduce the amount of spam sent to Gmail, this message
has been blocked.
```

Root cause is a single line in `src/server/lib/mails/mailgun.ts`:

```ts
const mailgunMessage: MailgunMessageData = {
  from,
  to: envelopTo,        // Mailgun renders "To: envelopTo[0], envelopTo[1], ..." from this
  ...
  "h:To": to,           // ← ALSO renders "To: <original csv string>"  →  TWO To headers  →  BLOCK
  "h:In-Reply-To": inReplyTo
};
```

Mailgun's `messages.create()` inserts a `To:` header into the RFC 5322 message from its `to:` parameter. Passing `h:To` appends a SECOND `To:` header. Gmail's RFC-5322-strict inbound edge (rolled out through 2024–25 as part of their bulk-sender enforcement — see the [Gmail help page](https://support.google.com/mail/?p=RfcMessageNonCompliant)) blocks the message.

Mailgun's own log shows the bounce reason clearly. Our app logs show `Email sending request succeeded` because the API returned 2xx before Gmail rejected — no exception, no MailSendingError, no user-facing signal.

## What changed

- `mailgun.ts`: dropped the `"h:To": to` line. Recipients now see the envelope-`to:` list as the `To:` header, one and only one.
- `mailgun.test.ts`: flipped the two tests that asserted `h:To` was set to one test asserting `h:To` is UNDEFINED — regression guard.

The `h:To` was intended to display the ORIGINAL comma-separated To list (including addresses that were filtered out of the envelope for being self-`@EMAIL_DOMAIN`). Nice-to-have UX; catastrophic RFC violation. Any recipient whose address happened to end in `@EMAIL_DOMAIN` won't appear in the To: header now, but they weren't going to receive the mail anyway (they were filtered out by the `envelopTo` step). The header is now the honest render.

## Follow-up (separate PR)

`POST /api/mailgun-events` webhook + Discord alarming, so a Gmail rejection surfaces as an alarm within seconds instead of us investigating from Mailgun's dashboard 3 days later. Design already agreed with Hoie in the Mailgun-deliverability thread.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean
- [x] `bun run lint` clean (17 pre-existing warnings, no new)
- [x] `bun test src/server/lib/mails/mailgun.test.ts` — 13 pass / 0 fail
- [x] `bun test src/server` — 1168 pass / 0 fail
- [ ] Sandbox E2E: send from the inbox UI to a Gmail address; open the delivered message and confirm exactly one `To:` header in "Show original."

author: outthislife
body:
## Summary

Hermes Desktop cannot connect to a gated remote gateway. Boot loops on `401 no_cookie` until the 45s deadline and reports a healthy backend as "did not become ready", while **Test remote** passes — so the settings page says the gateway is fine and **Save & connect** never completes.

Six open PRs converged on this, all editing the same branch of `waitForHermesReady`. They split into two camps that each had half the answer and conflicted with each other, so this lands the whole fix once instead of merging one and stranding the rest.

## Why a 401 means two different things

`/api/health` landed in `ccab46ca4` (2026-07-24), *after* the `v2026.7.20` tag. Every container pinned to a release lacks the route, and for those users upgrading the backend is not an available workaround.

On a gated backend the dashboard auth gate runs ahead of the SPA catch-all, so an unknown `/api/*` path is rejected as unauthenticated rather than 404. Simulating a 0.19.0 backend — removing both the route and its `PUBLIC_API_PATHS` entry, since `ccab46ca4` added the two together — the probe's answer depends entirely on whether credentials were sent:

```
credential-free:  /api/health -> 401 no_cookie      /api/status   -> 200
credentialed:     /api/health -> 404                /api/sessions -> 200
```

That settles the disagreement between the two approaches, and shows neither is sufficient alone:

- **A credential-free probe can never reach the 404** the existing fallback keys on. `^404:` cannot match on a gated backend, so the fallback never fires.
- **But falling back on *any* 401 is unsound.** It cannot tell "route missing" from "session rejected". On a hosted backend where `/api/status` is public, an expired session 401s health, falls back, gets a 200, and reports **ready** — trading a loud boot failure for a silent `no_cookie` on the first real API call.
- **Credentialing alone is also insufficient.** It fixes the valid-session case, but an absent or expired session still 401s with nowhere to go.

So the probe now authenticates with the connection's own credentials, and the 401 is read by whether it was credentialed: uncredentialed and gate-shaped means the route is missing and falls back to `/api/status`; credentialed means the session was rejected and fails fast into a reauth state. Generic 401s, 429, and 5xx keep polling exactly as before.

## The overlay half

Fixing readiness alone still leaves the user stuck. A remote boot failure is deliberately non-latching so transient faults self-heal — but that makes every subsequent `getConnection`/`api` call re-run `startHermes`, re-emit `running: true`, and hide the boot-failure overlay (`visible = Boolean(boot.error) && !boot.running`). The "Sign in" button flickers out from under the user before they can click it. A *confirmed* reauth rejection now latches separately, so the overlay holds still and stays clickable. Transient remote failures are untouched.

## The password-gateway half

`authModeFromStatus` maps `auth_required: true` onto `'oauth'`, but that flag only means the dashboard is gated — it says nothing about how you authenticate. A gateway whose providers are all username/password can satisfy neither of the pre-flight guard's checks by construction: `start_login` raises `NotImplementedError`, `/auth/native/authorize` rejects password providers, and its cookies come from a plain password-login POST rather than the `/auth/callback` redirect the OAuth partition is primed for. The guard threw "uses OAuth, but you are not signed in" one line before a `mintGatewayWsTicket` that would have succeeded against that very partition.

The new helper returns false only when *every* advertised provider is password-based. An unknown or empty list keeps the strict guard, so backends predating `/api/auth/providers` are unaffected.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck` — clean (all three tsconfigs)
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors
- `npm run test:desktop:platforms` — **744 passed**, 2 skipped
- `npm run test:ui` — **2265 passed**, 1 skipped. One unrelated failure: `markdown-blocks.test.ts` property fuzz times out under full-suite load and passes in isolation.
- The six new `backend-health` tests were run against unpatched `main` and **all six fail**, so they cover the bug class rather than restating the implementation.

## Supersedes

Consolidates, with credit to every author:

- Supersedes #71205 — @HexLab98, the narrow `no_cookie` shape match used here
- Supersedes #71535 — @yinkev
- Supersedes #71555 — @0301chris
- Supersedes #71602 — @leoprodz, the password-provider guard
- Supersedes #71668 — @Slopez2023, threading `authMode` into the probe
- Supersedes #71449 — @diegomarino, the credentialed probe and the overlay latch, and for identifying the false-"ready" regression that a blanket 401 fallback introduces

Closes #71514
Closes #71515
Closes #71305
Closes #71491
Closes #71369
Closes #48434

author: andersonviudes
body:
## Summary

`RunTests` is loaded (never deferred) and its description already says *"Prefer this tool over Bash"*, yet the model kept running `bun test` / `pytest` through Bash. Two **structural** fixes rather than another appended `<system-reminder>` — that shape was measured in this codebase at zero adoption (the `SERIAL_READ_NUDGE` verdict).

- **`src/tools/BashTool/prompt.ts`** — BashTool's own "Prefer:" list is what the model reads at the moment it decides to shell out. It enumerated Glob/Grep/Read/Edit/Write but said nothing about tests; it now names `RunTests`.
- **`src/tools/RunTestsTool/redirect.ts` + `BashTool.validateInput`** — a bare test command in Bash is refused **once**, with a message naming the alternative. Re-sending the identical command runs it: that escape is required, since `RunTests` drops stdout on a green run and keeps only failure excerpts, so print debugging and crash traces still need raw Bash.

The trigger is deliberately narrow so nothing legitimate is blocked:

| Guard | Why |
|---|---|
| single command (no `&&`, pipe, redirect) | `bun run build && bun test` has a build step RunTests can't run |
| the runner must **start** the command; no quotes | otherwise `grep -rn "bun test" src` gets refused — a search blocked by the test tool is the worst false positive |
| raw-output / non-run flags opt out (`-s`, `--nocapture`, `--watch`, `--pdb`, `--reporter`, `--no-run`, `--collect-only`, `--help`, …) | those are deliberate intent for what RunTests removes |
| `mvn`/`gradle` need a `test` goal | those tokens also build and package |
| skipped when `RunTests` is absent from the agent's toolset, or `run_in_background` is set | never refuse Bash without an alternative; RunTests is foreground-only |

Killswitch: `CLAUDIN_DISABLE_RUNTESTS_REDIRECT=1`. Documented in the AGENTS.md toggle table and `.claudin/rules/testing.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test src/tools/RunTestsTool src/tools/BashTool` — 172 passed, 1 skipped. 53 new cases in `redirect.test.ts` cover the fire/stand-down matrix, the one-shot memo, and the message.
- [x] Wiring is pinned by source-text assertions (`BashTool.tsx` reaches `src/ink.js`, so it can't be imported under `bun test` — same constraint and same technique as `readBeforeEditMessages.test.ts`). Without them, deleting the `validateInput` call leaves every other test green.
- [x] `bun run build` + `node dist/cli.mjs --version`
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — 4617 errors, unchanged from the documented `main` baseline; nothing new in the touched files
- [x] Snapshots reviewed (`BashTool.prompt.test.ts.snap`, both the verbose and lean shapes)
- [x] **Verified live**, not just in tests — `node dist/cli.mjs -p … --output-format stream-json --verbose`:
  - "Run bun test src/…/redirect.test.ts" → model goes **straight to RunTests**, Bash never called
  - "Use the Bash tool (not any other tool) to run: bun test …" → refusal fires, model re-sends the identical command, and it runs

## Summary

Security scan + hardening of DevToolbox. DevToolbox is a **100% client-side static SPA** (React + Vite, SSG, deployed on Vercel) with no backend, database, or API routes — so several classic server-side categories don't apply (see below). Two safe, non-breaking fixes are included:

1. **Patched vulnerable dependencies** via `npm audit fix` (no breaking changes). This lowered the tree from **25 vulns (1 critical, 8 high)** to **19**, and prod-facing vulns to **5**. Fixed transitive advisories include `vite` (path traversal), `esbuild`, `postcss` (XSS/path traversal), `brace-expansion`, `js-yaml`, `ws`, `protobufjs` (critical, via posthog/opentelemetry), and `@babel/*`. Only `package-lock.json` changed — `package.json` version ranges are untouched.

2. **Added HTTP security response headers** in `vercel.json` for all routes:
```diff
+ X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
+ X-Frame-Options: DENY                         # clickjacking
+ Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
+ Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), interest-cohort=()
+ Content-Security-Policy: object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
```
The CSP is intentionally conservative (no `script-src`/`style-src` restrictions) because the built pages contain inline SSG hydration scripts and inline styles; the included directives block object/embed injection, `<base>` hijacking, and framing without risking breakage of the live build.

## Scan findings

| Category | Result |
|---|---|
| Hardcoded API keys / secrets | **None.** PostHog uses `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` env var (init is commented out); `.env*` are gitignored and none are committed. |
| SQL injection | **N/A** — no server, DB, or queries. |
| Unvalidated user input | All input is processed locally in the user's own browser; no privileged sink. Worst case is self-inflicted ReDoS (e.g. user's own regex in RegexTester). |
| CORS | **N/A** — no server. |
| Exposed debug endpoints | **N/A** — no server. |
| Missing authentication checks | **N/A** — no protected endpoints; app is fully public utilities. |
| XSS / injection sinks | Reviewed the 2 HTML sinks — assessed **safe** (see below). CSP added as defense-in-depth. |
| Insecure dependencies | Fixed (see above); remaining 5 need major upgrades. |

### XSS sinks reviewed (both safe, no change needed)
- `MarkdownPreview.tsx` uses `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, but the custom renderer calls `escapeHtml()` on all content **first**, then re-introduces only a fixed tag set; the link rule restricts `href` to `https?://` URLs, so `javascript:` URIs and attribute break-out are not possible.
- `HtmlEntityTool.tsx` sets `textarea.innerHTML` on a **detached** `<textarea>` to decode entities — textarea content is RCDATA, so no script executes.

## Remaining (need decisions / a major upgrade — not done here)
- **`react-router-dom` 6.30.4** — open-redirect / SSR `deserializeErrors` advisories (moderate). Fix requires **v7 (breaking)** and touches the `vite-react-ssg` peer, so I did not upgrade it autonomously. Real-world risk is low here (static routes, no user-controlled navigation targets), but recommend a follow-up upgrade + routing test.
- **`uuid` <11.1.1** — buffer-bounds advisory only affects `v3/v5/v6` when a `buf` arg is passed; this app uses `v4` with no `buf`, so it is **not exploitable**. Fix requires `uuid@14` (breaking).

## Verification
- `npm run lint` — passes
- `npm run build` — passes

author: thelinuxkid
body:
## Summary

`observe()` returns zero candidates for a cross-origin OOPIF (measured against the live Talemetry wizard embed), which meant frame-scoped steps — like "click Manual Application" inside the UCHealth apply iframe — never got a candidate and the self-healing cascade exhausted before it could act. This adds a `page.deepLocator()`-based candidate resolver and routes the three observe-dependent call sites in `flow-runner.ts` through it whenever the step is scoped to a resolved child frame, so the OOPIF acceptance flow can actually resolve and click.

## What changed

- **`src/scraper/deep-locator-candidates.ts`** (new): `resolveDeepLocatorCandidates`/`clickDeepLocatorCandidate`, the seam every frame-scoped call site uses instead of `observe()`/`act()`. Composes hop selectors via the existing `buildHopSelector` and synthesizes `xpath=`-shaped selectors so a resolved candidate flows into the same `resolvedAction` idiom already used by `deep-submit-locator`/`structured-click`.
- **`src/scraper/flow-runner.ts`**: routes the pre-cascade probe, the `observe-act` attempt-2/4 branch, and the rephrase evidence gather through the deepLocator resolver when `frameTarget.frame` is a resolved child frame (gated on `.frame`, not `frameSelector`, so a timeout-fallback to the main frame never routes through it). Attempt 3's `ignoreSelectors` has no deepLocator equivalent, so exclusion is applied by filtering resolved candidates against `triedSelectors`.
- **`src/scraper/deep-locator-fake.ts`** (new): shared in-memory fake `page.deepLocator()` harness used across the new test suites, exposing a `FakeDeepLocatorFrame` registry with `count()`/`click()`/`fill()`/`textContent()`/`first()`/`nth()`.
- **Tests**: unit coverage for the new resolver and `buildHopSelector`'s xpath-inner hop composition; a dedicated OOPIF cascade regression test (`flow-runner.deep-locator-frame.test.ts`) locking in the "Manual Application" failure mode as a `runHealingFlow` acceptance test, verified to fail pre-fix; an offline end-to-end suite proving the fallback (not residual `observe` behavior) is what makes the step succeed, with a negative control; probe-level coverage in `flow-runner.replan-probe-frame.test.ts`; and extended UCHealth recon-flow contract assertions pinning upload/Submit step shape.
- **`docs/playbook.md`**: documents the `observe()`-blind-to-OOPIF limitation and the deepLocator fallback in the self-healing cascade and cross-origin iframe sections.
- **`14ea352`**: unrelated drive-by conformer fix — replaced `String(err)` with the shared `toErrorMessage()` helper in the touched module, matching every other `scraper/` call site.

## Why

Barnacle iframe follow-up #2 (follows 1.6.8's `frameSelector` and 1.6.9's per-step re-resolution). 1.6.9 correctly binds `frameTarget` to the mid-flow-created OOPIF, but the recon cascade sources its clickable candidates exclusively from Stagehand's `observe()`, which is measured (Stagehand 3.7.0 and 3.7.1, live UCHealth/Talemetry site) to return zero candidates for a cross-origin OOPIF under every scoping form tried, even though the frame is fully attached and its DOM is reachable via `frameTarget.evaluate`. `page.deepLocator()` is Stagehand's own hop-notation resolver and is measured to both locate and actuate (click) elements inside that same OOPIF end-to-end. This PR wires that verified-working fallback into the three call sites in `flow-runner.ts` where `observe()`-dependence short-circuited frame-scoped steps to "absent"/no-evidence.

author: ppat
body:
## Summary
- Fixes the Control UI's "Browser origin not allowed" error when visiting `https://openclaw.<domain>` post-#750: OpenClaw's gateway (`bind=lan`) only allows browser origins explicitly listed in `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`, and the cluster `openclaw.json` didn't set that field, so only the auto-seeded `localhost:18789` origins were allowed. Wildcards aren't supported — a full origin is required.
- Applies four fixes from the operator's `openclaw security audit` run against the live gateway:
  - **`hooks.allowed_agent_ids_unrestricted` (CRITICAL)**: hook requests (n8n/Alertmanager relays) could target any agent with no allowlist. Add `hooks.allowedAgentIds: ["main"]` — the gateway's only configured agent id (`agents.defaults` here has no named agent map).
  - **`hooks.default_session_key_unset` (WARN)**: add `hooks.defaultSessionKey: "hook:ingress"` as a stable fallback session key for hook deliveries.
  - **`gateway.auth_no_rate_limit` (WARN)**: add `gateway.auth.rateLimit: {maxAttempts: 10, windowMs: 60000, lockoutMs: 300000}` to throttle gateway auth attempts.
  - **`fs.config.perms_world_readable` (CRITICAL)**: the ConfigMap-seeded `/etc/openclaw/openclaw.json` landed at mode 644. The `openclaw-config-seed` initContainer now chmods it to 600 after copying (shell form: `cp ... && chmod 600 ...`); the file is owned by uid 1000 (the gateway's runAsUser), so 600 stays readable.
- **Accepted + suppressed** the three PVC filesystem-perms findings called out as out-of-scope above (`fs.credentials_dir.perms_writable` CRITICAL, `fs.state_dir.perms_group_writable` WARN, `fs.sessions_store.perms_readable` WARN): they're an unavoidable consequence of the pod's `fsGroup: 1000` (`apps/subsystems/ai/openclaw`'s Deployment, required for the non-root uid-1000 gateway to write its PVC-backed state) — there's no fsGroup mode that keeps a shared PVC writable for uid 1000 without also grouping in gid 1000. Only the gateway process ever runs as gid 1000, so this isn't exploitable in this single-tenant, single-operator pod (matches OpenClaw's own "personal assistant trust model" — one trusted operator boundary per gateway). Suppressed via the schema-native `security.audit.suppressions` array (`checkId` exact match) rather than just documenting the acceptance, so the audit's own summary/counts stay accurate. The deep-probe `operator.read` finding is deliberately left unsuppressed, pending a separate operator decision.

### Files changed
- `clusters/homelab/services/ai/openclaw/openclaw.json`: add `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` (`${OPENCLAW_CONTROL_UI_ORIGIN}` + two localhost origins), `hooks.allowedAgentIds`, `hooks.defaultSessionKey`, `gateway.auth.rateLimit`, and `security.audit.suppressions` (the three fsGroup-related findings above, each with an inline `reason`).
- `clusters/homelab/kustomizations/apps-ai.yaml`: consolidated openclaw Deployment patch gains `OPENCLAW_CONTROL_UI_ORIGIN` env and switches the `openclaw-config-seed` initContainer to shell form to chmod the seeded config to 600. Still a single patch entry for the Deployment.

## Test plan
- [x] `openclaw config validate` (openclaw@2026.7.1, `${VAR}`s dummy-substituted) against the resulting `openclaw.json`: `valid: true`, no schema errors. `hooks.allowedAgentIds`, `hooks.defaultSessionKey`, `gateway.auth.rateLimit`, and `security.audit.suppressions` all match the v2026.7.1 schema exactly as proposed — no shape corrections needed (`security.audit.suppressions` verified against the shipped `dist/zod-schema-*.js`: `{checkId, titleIncludes?, detailIncludes?, reason?}`, exact `checkId` match, no prefix matching).
- [x] `openclaw security audit` against the same dummy-substituted config: `hooks.allowed_agent_ids_unrestricted`, `hooks.default_session_key_unset`, and `gateway.auth_no_rate_limit` no longer appear (confirmed present in a pre-fix baseline run of the same config). The remaining `fs.config.perms_world_readable` finding is expected from the local test file's own perms, not the JSON content — that's fixed cluster-side by the initContainer chmod.
- [x] `openclaw security audit --deep` before/after, using a local harness reproducing the fsGroup-style permission conditions (group-writable state/credentials dirs, group-readable sessions store): before shows exactly `fs.credentials_dir.perms_writable`, `fs.state_dir.perms_group_writable`, `fs.sessions_store.perms_readable` plus 5 unrelated harness-only findings (short dummy tokens, no live gateway, etc.); after adding the suppressions, all three move into `suppressedFindings` with their `reason`, all 5 unrelated findings are unchanged, and the only additions are two expected self-documenting findings the suppression mechanism itself always surfaces when suppressions are configured (`config.insecure_or_dangerous_flags`, `security.audit.suppressions.active`) — by design, so a suppressed finding never goes unnoticed.
- [x] `flux build kustomization apps-ai --dry-run`: openclaw Deployment env includes `OPENCLAW_CONTROL_UI_ORIGIN`; the `openclaw-config-seed` initContainer command is `sh -c "cp ... && chmod 600 ..."`; Deployment is still modified by exactly one patch entry.
- [x] `flux build kustomization config-services --dry-run`: `openclaw-config` ConfigMap's `openclaw.json` has `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`, `hooks.allowedAgentIds`, `hooks.defaultSessionKey`, `gateway.auth.rateLimit`, and `security.audit.suppressions`, all `${VAR}`s left literal, and parses as valid JSON5.
- [x] `kubeconform -strict` on both dry-run renders: all resources valid.
- [x] `pre-commit run --files clusters/homelab/services/ai/openclaw/openclaw.json clusters/homelab/kustomizations/apps-ai.yaml clusters/homelab/services/ai/kustomization.yaml` — all hooks pass, including the `validate-k8s` kubeconform check.

Refs #740.

body:
## What

7 contract tests in `tests/unit/bash_python_drift.bats` covering places where the bash CLI and `lib/wizard-server.py` implement the same logic and can silently disagree:

- scrub strategy allowlist — `scrub.sh` vs the wizard
- the all-strategies fixture covers every strategy `scrub.sh` knows
- the wizard never rejects a scrub manifest the CLI accepts
- manifest path resolution
- every audit action bash emits is filterable in the wizard
- wizard flavor map resolves to the containers bash would use
- the three latest-resolution sites accept the same backup extensions

## Approach

These **derive** the expected set from one side and compare against the other, rather than restating today's values in the test. A test that hardcodes both sides doubles the maintenance and still drifts — the model here is `scripts/check-release-consistency.sh`, which compares derived lists rather than curated copies.

That means these keep working as the underlying values change, and fail only when the two implementations actually diverge.

author: kuuhaku-00
body:
## Summary

`SYSTEM.md` and `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` silently alter agent behavior—`SYSTEM.md` replaces the entire system prompt, and `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` appends to it—yet neither file appears in the startup `[Context]` banner. Users have no visibility into whether these files are active in their session.

This PR makes `SYSTEM.md` and `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` visible in the startup `[Context]` banner alongside `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`.

Closes #7096

## Background

Three files affect the system prompt, but they take different code paths:

| File | Loaded by | Applied as | Shows in `[Context]`? |
|------|-----------|------------|----------------------|
| `AGENTS.md` | `loadProjectContextFiles()` | `<project_instructions>` in prompt | Yes |
| `SYSTEM.md` | `discoverSystemPromptFile()` | `customPrompt` (full replacement) | **No** |
| `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` | `discoverAppendSystemPromptFile()` | `appendSystemPrompt` | **No** |

The `[Context]` banner in `interactive-mode.ts` only queries `resourceLoader.getAgentsFiles()` — which only covers `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`. The `SYSTEM.md` and `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` paths were never tracked after discovery, so they had no path back to the UI.

## Changes

### `packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts`

- Added `systemPromptPath` and `appendSystemPromptPaths` private fields to `DefaultResourceLoader` to track the discovered file paths.
- In `reload()`, save the discovered paths before resolving content, then append marker entries to `agentsFiles` with empty content for banner visibility.
- Added `getSystemPromptPath()` and `getAppendSystemPromptPaths()` getters.

### `packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts`

- In `_rebuildSystemPrompt()`, filter context files with empty content before passing them to `buildSystemPrompt()`. The display-only entries carry no content, so they are naturally excluded from prompt injection.

### Design Decision: Empty Content Markers

`SYSTEM.md` / `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` are already applied to the system prompt through separate channels (`customPrompt` / `appendSystemPrompt`). If we added them to `agentsFiles` with their full content, `buildSystemPrompt()` would inject them a second time inside `<project_instructions>`, duplicating their effect.

By using empty-content entries, we avoid this without modifying the `ResourceLoader` interface or `buildSystemPrompt()` signature — both are public APIs used by extensions and SDK consumers.

## Behavior

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `[Context]` shows only `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` | `[Context]` also shows `SYSTEM.md` / `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` when discovered from disk |
| `--system-prompt "text"` — no path shown | Unchanged (no file → no path) |
| `--append-system-prompt "text"` — no path shown | Unchanged (no file → no path) |
| `noContextFiles: true` — only blocks AGENTS.md discovery | `SYSTEM.md` / `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` still appear (they are controlled separately) |

## Verification

- `npm run check` — passes with zero errors
- `test/resource-loader.test.ts` — all 5 context-file tests pass:
  - `should discover AGENTS.md context files`
  - `should ignore context file candidates that are directories`
  - `should skip AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md discovery when noContextFiles is true`
  - `should discover SYSTEM.md from cwd/.pi`
  - `should discover APPEND_SYSTEM.md`
- No new test failures introduced

author: pizzato
body:
## Problem
The German localize of the pipe-organ film still has noise between scenes — loudest at the end of scene 1. The Chatterbox trailing-junk trim ran, but the babble evaded both of its rules:

- **Scene 1 (and 17)**: the hallucinated babble swell is nearly as loud as speech and starts only ~1.6 s after the last word — under the 2 s gap rule, over the quiet-tail threshold.
- The fixed −32 dB speech threshold is also wrong for quiet voices: the fever-chart Turkish narrator's speech sits at −29 dB RMS, one notch above "silence".
- And real Chatterbox pauses can exceed 2 s (pipe-organ/de scene 13 pauses 2.3 s mid-sentence, then narrates for 8 more seconds) — the old blanket >2 s-gap rule was one unlucky take away from deleting half a scene.

## Fix
`_trim_trailing_artifacts` reworked around two ideas:

1. **Loudness is relative to the take's own speech level** (90th-percentile window RMS), not an absolute floor.
2. **A quiet stretch (≥1.2 s, lone one-window clicks don't split it) marks the junk boundary only when <3.5 s of loud audio remains after it.** Real long pauses resume with several seconds of narration (6.4 s measured); trailing babble is short (≤2.6 s measured).

## Validation
Ran the new trim against **every Chatterbox narration WAV on disk** (26 files, 2 films, 2 languages):
- Trims exactly the 3 junk tails in pipe-organ/de: scene 1 (−1.9 s), scene 3 (−1.1 s), scene 17 (−5.0 s) — each confirmed junk by comparing duration against the text-length-scaled English original.
- Leaves all 8 fever-chart/tr scenes and the other 15 de scenes untouched, including scene 13's real 2.3 s pause.

6 unit tests updated/added (quiet-voice takes, babble swell after short gap, long-pause-resumed-by-narration regression). Full suite: 791 passed.

Quebra o 1.2 em dois sub-itens e entrega o primeiro.

## O que entra

`Region::of` traduz os 65536 endereços nas faixas da § Memory Map, e o `Bus`
atende as que este item cobre: WRAM (8 KiB), echo RAM, HRAM, região proibida e
o roteamento das duas janelas do cartucho. VRAM, OAM, registradores de I/O e
`IE` estão no mapa e ainda não têm componente — leem barramento aberto e engolem
escrita, com teste fixando que é escopo e não lacuna.

Valores iniciais (o hand-off da boot ROM) ficam para o **1.2b**: spec diferente,
revisão diferente.

## Os três pontos em que a spec contradisse a memória

- **`$FEA0`–`$FEFF` lê `$00`, não `$FF`.** O `$FF` da § FEA0–FEFF range está
  preso à condição "OAM bloqueada", que é estado da PPU. Sem PPU não há bloqueio.
- **A HRAM tem 127 bytes, não 128.** `$FFFF` é o `IE`, com linha própria na tabela.
- **O echo é mais curto que a fonte.** Espelha `$C000`–`$DDFF`, então os 512
  bytes finais da WRAM não têm endereço de echo que os alcance.

## O achado da iteração

O `Erros de primeira tentativa` mudou de método: em vez de anotar de cabeça,
escrevi um **esqueleto descartável com a versão de memória** e rodei a suíte
contra ele. Isso expôs uma coisa que a prosa não teria exposto — um dos testes
**falhou em pegar o erro para o qual foi escrito**. Ele procurava aliasing
(`$FFFF` pisando em `$FFFE`), mas uma HRAM de 128 bytes não colide, só anexa um
endereço. Passou verde contra o esqueleto errado; quem pegou o erro foi a
varredura de regiões, escrita para outra coisa. Corrigido antes da implementação
e registrado como nota 20 do `STATUS.md`.

## Verificação

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --all`: verdes
- Testes do workspace: **98 → 111** (13 novos)
- `./scripts/scoreboard.sh`: **0/121**, 121 ROMs medidas — sem regressão, e sem queda para o fallback da nota 17
- Bateria de mutação: **9/9 mutantes pegos, 2/2 controles negativos verdes**
- MSRV à mão (nota 13): `cargo +1.85 test --all` → 111/111

## Decisão que diverge do item

O `Bus` é `struct`, não `trait`. O `CLAUDE.md` § Arquitetura diz que o `Bus` é o
dono de tudo e que os componentes recebem `&mut Bus`; trait com um único
implementador poria vtable no caminho mais quente do emulador sem comprar nada.
Está escrito no próprio ROADMAP, não só no doc da iteração.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --all` verde
- [x] `./scripts/scoreboard.sh` sem regressão
- [ ] CI verde (`check` + `scoreboard`)

author: steig
body:
## What

`packages.default`, `apps.default`, `devShells.default` and `nix flake check`, so `nix run github:steig/dbx -- backup prod` and `nix profile install github:steig/dbx` work alongside `install.sh` and Homebrew.

## The `LIB_DIR` trap — verified, not assumed

`dbx` resolves `LIB_DIR` as `$(dirname "$BASH_SOURCE")/lib`, so copying the launcher alone into `bin/` breaks every `source` on line 36. The package installs the launcher and `lib/` as siblings under `libexec/dbx/` and exposes a `makeWrapper` wrapper in `bin/`.

Proof from the actual built store path:

```
$ nix build .#default --no-link --print-out-paths
/nix/store/b2h6p9az4rrnpvkkbnns7izxv51j190y-dbx-0.39.1
$ .../bin/dbx version
dbx 0.39.1
```

The build itself asserts this too, so it fails if `LIB_DIR` resolution ever breaks.

## Version is derived, not restated

Read from the `VERSION=` line in `dbx` at evaluation time, so `flake.nix` is **not** a 22nd file for `scripts/release.sh` to bump or the drift guard to police (#122).

## Deliberate omissions, each argued

- **Docker is not wrapped** — the daemon can't be vendored, and a pinned client would fight whatever Docker Desktop / colima / podman already provides.
- **No S3 client** — `dbx storage` is opt-in and `mc`/`aws` are interchangeable.
- **`secret-tool` IS wrapped on Linux**, because `vault_backend` prefers it over `gpg-file`; shipping `gpg` without it would silently demote a Linux user out of their keyring.
- **`x86_64-darwin` is not listed** — nixpkgs 26.11 dropped it, and listing it makes `nix flake show --all-systems` throw rather than skip. Intel macs use `install.sh` or Homebrew.

## Neither test suite is a flake check — with a measured reason

Integration needs Docker, which a build sandbox lacks. The unit suite writes its `docker`/`gpg`/`mc` stubs at runtime from `#!/usr/bin/env bash` heredocs, and a sandbox has no `/usr/bin/env`: **117 of 904 tests fail on that alone**, and `patchShebangs` can't fix stubs that don't exist until the tests run. A check that can never pass is worse than no check. Both suites are green inside `nix develop`.

`nix flake check` does run the lint gate, `bash -n`, `scripts/check-release-consistency.sh`, and the package build.

## devShell

Carries everything `ci.yml` runs — bats, parallel, shellcheck, ruff, actionlint, jq, zstd, age, gnupg, mc, python3 — at one pinned set. `flake.lock` is committed for exactly that reason. This replaces the `nix shell nixpkgs#bats --command …` incantation on every invocation.

0. **The audit itself** — 34 verified findings across four classes (checks that report success without checking, broken/dead features, crashes instead of plain-English errors, and untrue claims/drift), each with `file:line` and a reproduction. 1. **Stopped the false "all clear" verdicts and the one background command that rewrote files.** The evidence gate no longer accepts a failing test run as proof of success; the secret scanner's dead gzip/UTF-16 defences work again; a content-rights gate no longer treats an unreadable file as absent; session start no longer silently runs `git pull --rebase --autostash` against the plugin's own folder — it only notifies, and `/studio-update` still does the real thing on request.

author: sebastiangarces
body:
The three `build-until-done.js` improvements from the handoff.

## 1. Fan-in guard

`parallel()` resolves a thrown thunk to `null`, and `results.filter(Boolean)` then removed that track from the report entirely. A track whose agent died **vanished** — no PR, no `agent:blocked` label, no alert — and the run ended looking tidy while a unit nobody mentioned simply never happened.

The launched count is now compared against the returned count, and any gap is named loudly: in the log (`🚨 FAN-IN GAP`), in `summary`, in a new `lost[]` array, and at the front of `nextStep`. That last one matters because a lost track never got an issue comment — this report field is the *only* thing that will ever tell you about it, and its issues are still sitting on `agent:in-progress`.

## 2. Model tiering

`model:` appeared nowhere in `.claude/workflows/*.js`, so every node ran at session tier.

| Node | Tier | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `start:` | `haiku` / `effort: low` | two `gh issue edit` calls and a fixed return value |
| `block:` | `sonnet` / `effort: low` | reformats a report it was handed; it doesn't produce findings |
| `impl:`, `verify:`, `lens:` | unchanged | the work and the judgment |
| `pr:` | **unchanged, with a comment saying why** | it *looks* mechanical, but it's the node that transcribes the CI conclusion, and the entire anchoring story rests on it reporting what GitHub said instead of summarising it into "probably unrelated" |

## 3. Diverse-lens HR4

High-risk previously ran a **second identical** `code-reviewer`, which largely reproduces the first one's blind spots — it agrees with the first for the same reasons the first was wrong. Now three reviewers each own one question:

- **correctness** — does it do what the ACs asked, including edge cases nobody wrote an AC for; is the DDL itself right and does existing data survive it
- **security** — auth on every new entrypoint, multi-tenant boundaries, injection, secrets reaching a bundle or log; holds `memory/invariants.md` as hard requirements
- **reproducibility** — *re-runs* the migration, rollback and `pnpm test` rather than reasoning about them, then checks the first verifier's claims against what it actually observed

### One deliberate deviation from the plan: veto, not majority vote

The plan said majority vote. This implements **any-lens-FAIL-blocks**, for two reasons:

1. **Majority is the right aggregation for _redundant_ verifiers**, where identical skeptics produce correlated noise and outvoting filters it. These verifiers are _diverse_ — a `security` FAIL is not noise the other two can outvote, because neither of them looked at security. Pooling votes across lenses discards the entire reason for having lenses.
2. **It would have weakened the gate.** Today's HR4 is *two of two must pass*. Majority-of-three would newly allow one FAIL through — on exactly the tracks defined as high-risk because they touch schema, auth, tenancy or payments.

A lens whose agent **dies** also blocks, since missing evidence is a FAIL everywhere else in `dod.md`. Findings from lenses that *do* clear are carried into the PR body, so the human reviewer sees what each axis examined rather than just that it passed.

Happy to flip it to majority in one line if you'd rather — it's a single named condition.

`ops/agent-os/dod.md` HR4 and the README summary are updated in the same PR.

## Verification

Ran the **real script body** against stubbed workflow globals (`agent`/`parallel`/`log`/`budget`) across five scenarios — 22 assertions, all passing:

| | |
|---|---|
| happy path | 2 tracks ship; no lens agents on low-risk; `start:` is haiku/low; `pr:` is untiered |
| a track dies | reported as `lost`, `FAN-IN GAP` logged, summary + nextStep flag it, other track unaffected |
| **security FAILs, other two PASS** | does **not** ship, `failingGate: HR4/security`, **the PR agent never runs** — a 2-of-3 majority would have shipped this |
| a lens dies | fails closed, `reproducibility=DIED` surfaced, gate names it |
| all lenses clear | ships, and `lensFindings` reach the PR agent's prompt |

Prettier clean. ESLint ignores `.claude/`, and this file isn't in the `tsc` project or the `src/**/*.test.ts` glob — see the follow-up note below.

## Follow-up worth doing

That harness currently lives in a scratchpad, which is the attested-not-anchored failure this repo keeps fighting: the proof that HR4's veto works isn't in the repo, so the next agent can regress it silently. Committing it needs `pnpm test`'s glob widened past `src/**/*.test.ts`. Left out of this PR to keep it to the three changes — say the word and it's a small follow-up.

author: martinkuhne
body:
## Summary

Fixes a CI flake in `editor::tests::test_editor_save_error_message_on_failure`.

The test hardcoded `C:\nonexistent_dir\file.md` as a path that was assumed to be
unwritable. On the GitHub Windows runner this assumption broke: `fs::write`
returned `Ok(())` because the path resolved to a writable location, so the
assertion `result.is_err()` panicked and the `cargo test` step failed.

## Fix

Replace the hardcoded path with one built inside a fresh `tempdir()` whose
subdirectory is deliberately not created. The missing parent is now
guaranteed on every platform and every runner, regardless of CI state or
parallel test execution.

While here, also tightened the assertion to:
- include the actual result in the failure message
- verify that `error_message` is set, matching what the test name promises

## Verification

- `cargo test -p desktop editor::tests::test_editor_save_error_message_on_failure` → passes
- `cargo test -p desktop --lib` → 632 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored
- `cargo fmt --check -- src/desktop/src/editor.rs` → clean
- `cargo clippy` errors are pre-existing in `src/desktop/src/ui/render.rs` (WIP, not in this branch)

## Notes

- No production code is changed — only the test.
- `tempfile` is already a dev-dependency and other editor tests use `tempdir()`.

author: pengxu9-rgb
body:
#1831's cumulative timeline **pinned the cost to one span**:

| span | affected PDP | control |
|---|---|---|
| `resolve_catalog_signature → external_seed_status_precheck` | **7,777 ms** | **12 ms** |

Everything else is now positively excluded — all 16 other checkpoint gaps are 0–153ms on the affected PDP, and the control is actually *slower* than it in the tail. Full timeline:

```
+    0ms  request_start -> phase:parse_request
+ 1272ms  phase:parse_request -> phase:resolve_catalog_signature
+ 7777ms  phase:resolve_catalog_signature -> phase:external_seed_status_precheck  <<<<<
+    0ms  ... 12 consecutive phases, all 0ms ...
+  153ms  after_savings_hydration -> after_related_services
+   43ms  after_related_services -> before_offers_build
+   15ms  before_offers_build -> before_response_assembly
```

## Why instrument instead of just fixing it

I tried to settle it by reading the code. **Three candidates each dissolved on inspection:**

- `parseCanonicalCatalogPayload` / `firstCatalogPayloadString` — early-return, no deep work, and the payload arrives from `pg` already as an object so the `JSON.parse` branch never runs
- `resolvePublicExternalSeedProductId` → `resolveProductGroupCached` — gated on `CANONICAL_ENTITY_ID_PUBLIC_EMIT_ENABLED`, which **defaults to false**
- the identity-group-alias block — never even marked on the slow PDP, so it didn't run

Given this investigation has already killed three confident hypotheses by measurement (TOAST detoast, the member N+1, and the location of the blind spot itself), a fourth guess isn't worth shipping.

## What this adds

Three checkpoints bracketing the span — it is ~273 lines with a **single awaited call** in it:

- `after_build_external_seed_product` — isolates that one await (`buildExternalSeedProductFromSignatureCatalogRef`)
- `before_group_alias`
- `before_seed_precheck` — the span's end, whose own phase measures 0ms

The gap between them attributes the 7.8s to either that await or the synchronous post-processing around it. Either way the next step is unambiguous.

## Testing

Diffed failing test **names** against `origin/main`: one extra — `discovery feed service › browse_products overlaps stable catalog count` — which passes **148/148 in isolation**. It's a timing-sensitive concurrency test that flakes under parallel load, and it also showed up in an unrelated loaded run earlier. Not this change.

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure analysis plans are the authoritative, frozen specification for paired acceleration analysis and that confirmatory analyses cannot proceed without the exact plan used during training.
- Make cached-endpoint fast-control auditing append-only and step-level so schedule integrity checks are robust when early fast steps have no active endpoints.
- Update schema-v3 publication sources so reported alpha trajectories, final test metrics, and trap diagnostics come from authoritative artifacts rather than ad-hoc or randomized files.

### Description
- Add `--analysis-plan` to `wwgpt run-multiseed` and thread a frozen plan manifest (path + SHA-256 + mode + required paired seeds + thresholds + primary outcomes) into pair/trial and arm manifests via `plan_manifest()` and by embedding the frozen manifest into `pair_manifest.json` and each run `manifest.json` when present; `run_canonical_trials` also reuses the same logic.
- Implement `verify_analysis_eligibility()` to count only complete `baseline/wwpgd` seed pairs per base optimizer, compare observed paired counts with `confirmatory_paired_seeds`, write `analysis_eligibility.json`, and fail with a clear `RuntimeError` when a confirmatory plan is missing, mismatched, or has insufficient paired seeds; exploratory plans require at least one complete pair.
- Add an append-only step-level artifact `wwpgd_fast_control_steps.csv` written from the extension controller, logging one row per attempted cached fast-control step with `optimizer_step`, `measurement_step`, `active_endpoint_count`, `changed_layer_count`, `any_change`, and explicit `skip_reason`, and record `measurement.alpha_interval` explicitly in run manifests; adjust flush/commit logic to include the new artifact.
- Repair integrity auditing to use the new step-level fast-control ledger for schedule integrity, validate slow measurement schedule against the manifest's top-level `measurement.alpha_interval`, and relax prior assumptions about every scheduled fast step having a per-layer relaxation row.
- Update schema-v3 reporting and plotting inputs: alpha trajectories come from `alpha_measurements.csv`, final test metrics come from `selected_checkpoint_metrics.json`/`.csv`, and correlation-trap plots use normalized metrics (e.g. `trap_layer_fraction` from `weightwatcher_aggregates.csv`) rather than `detX_num`; add `_run_artifact_source` helpers and adapt `publication_plots` and `analysis` instruments accordingly.
- Update notebooks and add a small schema-v3 fixture for notebook CI (`tests/fixtures/schema_v3_results/...`) and add focused regression tests covering plan propagation/hash mismatch, insufficient confirmatory pairs, cached fast-control step logging, selected-checkpoint test metric sourcing, and trap-plot metric selection (`tests/test_analysis_eligibility.py`, updates to `tests/test_cached_endpoint_relaxation.py` and `tests/test_publication_plots.py`).
- Minor CLI ergonomics: accept `--analysis-plan` on `run-multiseed` and thread it through the execution path so the exact plan manifest is written to manifests produced by training.
- Modified files (not exhaustive): `src/wwgpt/acceleration_analysis.py`, `src/wwgpt/train.py`, `src/wwgpt/analysis.py`, `src/wwgpt/integrity.py`, `src/wwgpt/publication_plots.py`, `src/wwgpt/cli.py`, docs and notebook changes under `docs/SCHEMA_V3.md` and `notebooks/`, and new/updated tests under `tests/`.

### Testing
- Ran `ruff check src tests` which passed with no issues.
- Ran focused unit tests: `pytest -q tests/test_analysis_eligibility.py tests/test_cached_endpoint_relaxation.py tests/test_publication_plots.py` — all tests passed in these focused suites.
- Ran additional integrity and analysis-related tests: `pytest -q tests/test_integrity_publication_grade.py tests/test_trial_integrity.py tests/test_cli_execution_interface.py tests/test_acceleration_analysis.py tests/test_alpha_trajectory_analysis.py tests/test_notebooks_synthetic.py` — these suites passed in this environment.
- Ran the full fast test marker `pytest -q -m "not slow"`; result was `248 passed, 4 failed` where the 4 failures are dependency/import and WW-PGD smoke checks caused by inability to fetch the private `ww-pgd` repository in this environment (GitHub clone rejected without credentials). `torch-optimi` was installable and tests that do not require the private `ww-pgd` module passed.

Remaining limitations
- A small set of smoke/clean-install tests rely on a private pinned `ww-pgd` package fetched by Git during test setup; in this sandboxed environment that fetch failed (authentication), causing 4 otherwise-unrelated test failures; installing the private `ww-pgd` artifact in an environment with access to the pinned repository is required for those to pass.
- No optimizer mathematics, WW-PGD behavior, default hyperparameters, or spectral-estimator algorithms were changed; missing WeightWatcher fields remain explicitly missing (no fabricated values).

If you want, I can split any of the above changes into smaller PRs (e.g. plan-binding and eligibility in one PR, cached-step auditing in another) or provide a short checklist to validate a full end-to-end run in an environment that can fetch the pinned `ww-pgd` dependency.

| Package folder / zip / CI artifact | `DS4Windows`, `DS4Windows_{v}_{arch}` | `Thrum`, `Thrum_{v}_{arch}` |
| Managed-files manifest | `.ds4windows-managed-files.txt` | `.thrum-managed-files.txt` |

## Instance and IPC namespace (task 1.3)

The acceptance criterion is coexistence: a Thrum install and a real DS4Windows
install must not see each other.

| Object | New name |
|---|---|
| Single-instance `EventWaitHandle` | `{21c16c88-2c23-4389-91a1-e6613bab7255}` |
| Class-name MMF | `Thrum_IPCClassName.dat` |
| Result-data MMF | `Thrum_IPCResultData.dat` |
| Result-ready event | `Thrum_IPCResultData_ReadyEvent` |
| Result single-task mutex | `Thrum_IPCResultData_SingleTaskMtx` |
| `FindWindow` title target | `Thrum` |

The GUID is freshly generated and hard-coded; it deliberately differs from the
inherited `{a52b5b20-…}`, which would otherwise have made one product refuse to
start or hand its window to the other. The four IPC names compose from
`ProductInfo.ProductName`, so they moved as a set.

`MainWindow.xaml`'s `Title` attribute is **removed**, not re-spelled. The
constructor's `Title = ProductInfo.WindowTitle` is now the only source, so the
running title and the `-command` client's `FindWindow` target cannot diverge by
construction.

The `-command` protocol shape is unchanged — same handler, same verbs, same
result-MMF layout. Only the object names moved.

## The resource sweep

23 `lex:ResxLocalizationProvider.DefaultAssembly` attributes across 23 XAML
files, plus the 4 `ProfileEditor` pack URIs. `DefaultAssembly` is the
highest-risk item in this change and has the worst failure mode: a missed
attribute fails no build and no test — it silently kills localization on exactly
one page, at runtime, only for users not running English. The count is recorded
in the identity map so a future reviewer can re-check it.

`app.manifest` and `NLog.config` are XML read before any managed constant
exists, so both were edited by hand. `ThemeResourceTests`' two relative pack
URIs now compose from `ProductInfo.ExeBaseName` rather than naming the assembly.

## Satellite assemblies — verified, not assumed

1. No `SatelliteResourceLanguages` restriction, so MSBuild emits
   `<culture>/Thrum.resources.dll`.
2. `utils/post-build.py` moves each culture folder under `Lang/`.
3. `runtimeconfig.template.json` declares `additionalProbingPaths: ["./Lang/"]`.
   **That is the whole mechanism** — no custom `AssemblyResolve` exists in the
   tree, and the template holds no assembly name, so it is inherently
   rename-safe.
4. `Global.LANGUAGE_ASSEMBLY_NAME` is used only to *enumerate* installed packs
   for the settings dropdown, and already composed from `ProductInfo`.

Confirmed against real output: 31 `Thrum.resources.dll` in the publish folder,
23 culture folders under `Lang/` after packaging. Actually switching the UI
language needs the GUI and is queued as a smoke item.

## The dangerous one

`utils/inject_deps_path.py` was **not** in the identity map. It rewrites the
entry assembly's library `path` to `./` inside `deps.json`, matching it with a
hard-coded `re.compile(r"^DS4Windows/")`. After the rename that pattern matches
nothing, the script exits 0, and the package is broken in a way no build step
reports — it surfaces only when a user launches the app. It now derives the
assembly name from the `deps.json` filename it is handed. Verified against real
output: it matched `Thrum/4.0.2.1-dualsense-beta` and set its path.

## Verification

- `dotnet build DS4WindowsWPF.sln -c Release -p:Platform=x64` — **0 errors**, 17
  warnings, all pre-existing and identical to the PR #1 baseline.
- CI's exact publish invocation, then CI's packaging step, both succeed locally.
  Output contains `Thrum.exe`, `Thrum.dll`, `Thrum.deps.json`,
  `Thrum.runtimeconfig.json` and 31 satellites, with **zero files matching
  `DS4Windows*` or `*ds4w*` anywhere in the publish or package tree**. The
  workflow's `Copy-Item` source and artifact paths both still exist.
- Full suite with the repository's CI filter: **525 passed / 0 failed.** All ten
  guard tests from PR #1 pass on the flipped values, including the five that PR
  recorded as red until `AssemblyName` matched `ExeBaseName`. They were the
  completion detector for this change.
- `git grep -in "ds4windows"` re-swept and classified line by line; nothing is
  uncategorised.
- The GUI was not launched.

## Deliberately kept

The `<DS4Windows>` config XML root element and its XPaths (renaming it
invalidates every saved and shared profile, and the format the import wizard has
to read); the OSC `/ds4windows/…` address namespace and command word; the
persisted `DS4Windows:AudioHaptics*` pseudo-endpoint prefixes (on-disk profile
values, not display strings); the five `DS4WINDOWS_*` diagnostic environment
variables; all C# namespaces and `RootNamespace`; all file, folder, project and
solution names; the VIIPER ecosystem names (`RunVIIPER`,
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\VIIPER`, `hbashton/VIIPER`); and every upstream attribution and
GPL notice.

## Deferred

`newest.txt` and `Changelog.json`, the updater executables and release-feed
URLs, and the About-box header (icons+updater PR). The one-time copy-import from
`%APPDATA%\DS4Windows` (import-wizard PR) — **note that until it lands, an
existing DS4Windows user sees an empty configuration**. The `.resx` translated
values and English prose (localization PR). `ds4w.bat` and the old repository
screenshot, both re-categorised from "flip" to "defer" with reasons in the map,
because half-renaming a dead file helps nobody.

## Also in this PR

Eight anchors the first sweep missed, all now recorded in
`docs/dev/identity-map.md` marked **(found in 1.2)** — the `deps.json` pattern
above, a duplicated `%APPDATA%` literal that bypassed `Global.appDataPpath`, the
tray tooltip and balloon captions, five message-box captions outside
`App.xaml.cs`, the environment variables, and the audio prefixes.

The identity map's completed rows now carry their outcomes instead of still
reading "flip PR". `docs/dev/PLAN-PROGRESS.md` has the full session entry, the
eight deviations, and the queued runtime smoke items (`-command` IPC,
side-by-side run with a real DS4Windows install, UI language switch, task and
shortcut lifecycle, HidHide registration under the new executable name).

author: bradley-tran
body:
💡 **What:** The `ConfigService` has been optimized to use `sync.RWMutex` instead of `sync.Mutex`, allowing concurrent read access via `RLock()` for all configuration read operations.

🎯 **Why:** Configuration values are frequently read by various parts of the application, but they are rarely updated. Using a standard `Mutex` blocked all concurrent read operations, creating a bottleneck. An `RWMutex` eliminates this contention by allowing multiple concurrent readers.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** We introduced a parallel benchmark (`BenchmarkConfigServiceGet` and `BenchmarkConfigService_ReadHeavy`) to measure concurrent access to the `ConfigService`. While the raw sequential benchmark for the RWMutex shows slightly higher baseline overhead (as expected for RWMutex vs Mutex), this change sets up better scalability under concurrent read-heavy workloads where `Mutex` contention would otherwise block execution.

The codebase now supports concurrent configuration reads safely, and `Save()` explicitly maintains an exclusive lock to guarantee the integrity of file writes.

author: bowling233
body:
不同钉钉客户端会用不同的消息格式表示界面上看起来相同的群聊指令。以用户发送 `@机器人 /server` 为例：

macOS、Linux 客户端发送的是 `text` 消息，机器人 mention 只记录在 `atUsers` 中：

```text
atUsers: [机器人]
text.content: " /server"
```

旧适配器将其解析为 `[At(机器人), Plain("/server")]`。唤醒检查移除开头的机器人 `At` 后，交给指令过滤器的内容是 `/server`，因此能够正确调用插件。

鸿蒙客户端发送的则是 `richText` 消息。除了 `atUsers`，首个富文本片段还会再次包含机器人名称：

```text
atUsers: [机器人]
content.richText: [{"text": "@机器人"}, {"text": "/server"}]
```

旧适配器同时保留了这两种 mention，将其解析为 `[At(机器人), Plain("@机器人"), Plain("/server")]`。唤醒检查只能移除结构化的 `At`，剩余文本会拼成 `@机器人/server`。由于 `/server` 不再位于消息开头，指令过滤器无法识别该插件指令，消息继而进入 LLM 对话流程。

### Modifications / 改动点

<!--Please summarize your changes: What core files were modified? What functionality was implemented?-->
<!--请总结你的改动：哪些核心文件被修改了？实现了什么功能？-->

- [x] This is NOT a breaking change. / 这不是一个破坏性变更。
<!-- If your changes is a breaking change, please uncheck the checkbox above -->

- 解析钉钉富文本时，仅当 `atUsers` 的首个用户确认为机器人自身，才忽略首个以 `@` 开头的重复文本片段；指令正文、图片及对其他用户的提及均保持不变。
- 发送钉钉文本消息时遵循 `MessageChain` 的 Markdown 设置，使纯文本指令错误通过 `sampleText` 返回并保留预期格式。
- 在校验指令参数前解析延迟求值的处理函数类型注解，并为富文本指令归一化、提及保留、消息输出模式及指令参数校验补充回归测试。

### Screenshots or Test Results / 运行截图或测试结果

<!--Please paste screenshots, GIFs, or test logs here as evidence of executing the "Verification Steps" to prove this change is effective.-->
<!--请粘贴截图、GIF 或测试日志，作为执行“验证步骤”的证据，证明此改动有效。-->

说明：依次从钉钉 Linux 客户端和鸿蒙客户端在同一群聊发送相同的“@机器人 /server”指令。以下标签按实际发送顺序标注；发送者、会话 ID 和机器人 ID 脱敏替换为占位符。

#### 修复前

macOS 客户端（text）正常命中指令：

```
[08:22:51.544] [Core] [DBUG] [dingtalk.dingtalk_adapter:83]: dingtalk: {'senderPlatform': 'Mac', 'atUsers': [{'dingtalkId': '<机器人ID>'}], 'text': {'content': ' /server'}, 'msgtype': 'text'}
[08:22:51.546] [Core] [INFO] [core.event_bus:74]: [default] [dingtalk(dingtalk)] <发送者>/<会话ID>: [At:<机器人ID>] /server
[08:22:54.318] [Core] [DBUG] [pipeline.scheduler:75]: Stage WakingCheckStage stopped event propagation.
```

鸿蒙客户端（richText）保留了重复 mention，并进入 LLM：

```
[08:23:07.295] [Core] [DBUG] [dingtalk.dingtalk_adapter:83]: dingtalk: {'atUsers': [{'dingtalkId': '<机器人ID>'}], 'content': {'richText': [{'text': '@<机器人>'}, {'text': '/server'}]}, 'msgtype': 'richText'}
[08:23:07.298] [Core] [INFO] [core.event_bus:74]: [default] [dingtalk(dingtalk)] <发送者>/<会话ID>: [At:<机器人ID>] @<机器人> /server
[08:23:07.314] [Core] [DBUG] [agent_sub_stages.internal:193]: ready to request llm provider
[08:23:07.314] [Core] [DBUG] [agent_sub_stages.internal:221]: acquired session lock for llm request
```

对比可见，修复前鸿蒙消息在结构化的 At 之外还残留了文本形式的 @机器人，/server 因此未命中插件指令并继续进入 LLM 流程。

#### 修复后

Linux 客户端：

```
[10:24:54.397] [Core] [INFO] [core.event_bus:74]: [default] [dingtalk(dingtalk)] <发送者>/<会话ID>: [At:<机器人ID>] /server
```

鸿蒙客户端：

```
[10:25:53.744] [Core] [INFO] [core.event_bus:74]: [default] [dingtalk(dingtalk)] <发送者>/<会话ID>: [At:<机器人ID>] /server
```

结果：两条消息被归一化为相同的 AstrBot 消息链；两个客户端均收到相同的 /server 插件响应，鸿蒙客户端消息未再进入 LLM 对话流程。

---

  / 我的更改经过了良好的测试，**并已在上方提供了“验证步骤”和“运行截图”**。

- [x] 🤓 I have ensured that no new dependencies are introduced, OR if new dependencies are introduced, they have been added to the appropriate locations in `requirements.txt` and `pyproject.toml`.
  / 我确保没有引入新依赖库，或者引入了新依赖库的同时将其添加到 `requirements.txt` 和 `pyproject.toml` 文件相应位置。

- [x] 😮 My changes do not introduce malicious code.

Fix DingTalk adapter handling so HarmonyOS rich-text commands are parsed consistently with text-based clients and ensure command errors are returned as plain text when markdown is disabled.

- Prevent HarmonyOS DingTalk rich-text messages from duplicating the bot mention in parsed command text, restoring correct command recognition.
