author: jonhill90
body:
## The problem

The local Docker provider constraint lists the two infra compose projects explicitly:

```
constraints: "Label(`com.docker.compose.project`,`hill90-local-edge`) || Label(`com.docker.compose.project`,`hill90-local-observability`)"
```

The app stack ([hill90-app](https://github.com/jonhill90/hill90-app)) runs as project `hill90-local`. Its `compose/local.infra.yml` overlay attaches it to `hill90local_edge` with its own Traefik labels, but every one of those routers is dropped by the constraint — so all five app hostnames 404 while the infra surfaces work fine.

The existing comment says the constraint was added after observing "an older Hill90 app stack still running". That was this stack, before it had routable labels; it is now a deliberate tenant of these networks.

## The change

One additional clause for `hill90-local`. Nothing else.

**Why literals and not `${VAR:-default}`:** Traefik 2.11 does no environment interpolation in the static config file. I verified rather than assumed — with `constraints: "Label(...,\`${TEST_PROJECT}\`)"` and `TEST_PROJECT=substituted` in the environment, Traefik loaded the file without error and discovered **zero** routers from a container labelled `com.docker.compose.project=substituted`. The placeholder is matched as a literal string. The `${VAR:-prod_default}` pattern from #500 applies to the compose files, which Compose does interpolate; this file is not one of them.

`LabelRegexp` would collapse all three clauses into one pattern, but it is Traefik v3 only — the existing comment already records that it breaks on 2.11.

## Expected effect on the live VPS: none

- **No workflow triggers on this path.** The only two push-triggered workflows are `deploy.yml` (paths: `platform/observability/**`, `docker-compose.vault.yml`, `docker-compose.observability.yml`) and `tailscale.yml` (`policy.hujson`). `platform/edge/traefik.local.yml` matches neither, so merging deploys nothing.
- **The file is never mounted in production.** `docker-compose.infra.yml:60` mounts `platform/edge/${TRAEFIK_STATIC_CONFIG:-traefik.yml}`; only `.env.local` sets it to `traefik.local.yml`. Production keeps using `traefik.yml`, which this PR does not touch.
- Nothing under `deploy/`, no vault paths, and no `platform/observability/**` are touched. The uninitialized `openbao` container is untouched.

If a redeploy were somehow triggered manually, it would restart Traefik with an unchanged production config.

## Verification

Ran the real stacks together on this branch — `scripts/local.sh up`, then the app with `--infra`:

```
SERVICE          URL                                            CODE
UI               http://app.localtest.me:8080/                  200
API health       http://api.localtest.me:8080/health            200
Keycloak realm   http://auth.localtest.me:8080/realms/hill90    200
MCP gateway      http://ai.localtest.me:8080/mcp/health         200
MinIO console    http://storage.localtest.me:8080/              200

infra own surfaces (must be unaffected):
  traefik      302
  grafana      302
  portainer    200

internal-only app services (must stay unrouted):
  ai.localtest.me/health         404
  knowledge.localtest.me/health  404
```

Plus a full browser login through Traefik ending on an authenticated dashboard. Before this change all five app rows were 404; the infra rows are unchanged either way, and `ai`/`knowledge` stay correctly unrouted because the app sets `traefik.enable=false` on them, matching production.

Local run of the checks CI runs — `check_md_links`, `check_volume_names`, `check_env_surface`, `check_secrets_schema`, `check_destructive_commands`, `shellcheck` — all pass, and `docker compose config` on the production infra file is still valid.

## Unrelated observation, not fixed here

The comment above `providers.docker` cites `scripts/checks/check_local_parity.py`, which does not exist in the tree. Left alone to keep this diff to one line of behaviour.

author: gauravsaini
body:
## Summary

This PR adds **Parallel Mode** chunked decoding for Whisper models in Hex, alongside a user-facing toggle setting and local `~/Documents` model discovery.

### Key Changes
1. **Parallel Mode Core Engine (`TranscriptionClient.swift`)**:
   - Implements multi-chunk concurrent transcription using WhisperKit's batch decoding engine across Apple Silicon CPU/GPU/ANE cores.
   - Fixes `concurrentWorkerCount` logic so passing `0` when Parallel Mode is OFF ensures standard single-pass sequential transcription is executed without WhisperKit overriding `nil` to `16`.

2. **Settings UI Integration (`GeneralSectionView.swift` & `SettingsFeature.swift`)**:
   - Adds a **"Parallel Mode"** toggle setting in the **General** section under *Super Fast Mode*.
   - Wires `toggleParallelMode` action in `SettingsFeature` reducer to persist user preference in `hex_settings.json`.

3. **`~/Documents` Local Model Discovery (`TranscriptionClient.swift`)**:
   - Adds candidate path resolution for custom/offline models located in `~/Documents`, `~/Documents/models`, or `~/Documents/huggingface/models`.

4. **Public Log Privacy Annotations (`HexLog.transcription`)**:
   - Adds `privacy: .public` annotations to duration, realtime speed, and chunk count log interpolations for clean diagnostic streams in Console.

5. **Release Changeset**:
   - Includes `.changeset/9b51fe61.md` patch fragment following repository guidelines.

### Benchmarks (Whisper Large v3 Turbo, 10-core Apple Silicon)
- **Short Audio (4.1s)**: 0.448s (Parallel Mode ON) vs 1.052s (Sequential Mode OFF) — **2.35x speedup**
- **Long Audio (292.2s / ~5 mins)**: 39.144s (Parallel Mode ON across 10 chunks) vs ~391.4s (Sequential Mode OFF) — **~10x speedup**

author: steeldevandroid
body:
## Description

Two related pieces of work, four commits.

1. **`2ffa92a` + `ac0670c` — audit of the Cluster Audit feature itself** (`AuditService`, `AuditController`, `NamingConventionService`, `MessageFieldExtractorService`, `Audit.tsx`): bugs, optimisations, ergonomics. `AUDIT-FEATURE-REVIEW.md` documents the pre-fix state and the decision taken for each finding (B1–B9, O1–O3, E1–E8, S1–S3), plus a "constaté, non traité" section listing what was deliberately left open.
2. **`2700880` + `66c9096` — data entry across every form in the app.** The design system already shipped a `Field` wrapper doing label/error/aria plumbing, and exactly two files used it; Config (17 controls), Metrics (15) and StreamFlow (5) hand-rolled their own inputs with `<label>` elements bound to nothing.

---

## Part 1 — Cluster Audit

### Bugs

- **`GET /audit` shadowed the SPA route and returned a 500.** `AuditController` was an MVC `@Controller` mapping `/audit` and returning the view name `"audit"`, but the project has no template engine and `/audit` is a client-side route. A refresh or a bookmark resolved to a circular view path → HTTP 500; the page was only reachable via in-app navigation. The handler also kicked off a **full cluster scan as a side effect of a GET**. Removed — the controller is now a `@RestController` under `/api/audit` only.
- **Flow health score rendered as "10000%".** `overallHealthScore` stored a 0..100 percentage that the UI multiplied by 100 again, so every colour threshold was always met — a flow losing 99% of its volume showed green. Normalized to a 0..1 ratio (clamped for fan-out).
- **A failed run looked like a perfect cluster.** The KPI grid rendered for `FAILED` too: 0 topics, 0 unhealthy, **100% health score**, with `globalStats.error` shown nowhere. `Map.of("error", e.getMessage())` also threw an NPE on a null message (NPE, TimeoutException…), leaving the run stuck in `RUNNING` forever.
- **`GET /api/audit/status/{id}` answered 200 with an empty body** for an unknown id; the client read that as "finished", stopped polling and left a blank screen. Now 404, handled distinctly client-side.
- **Checks degraded to a silent zero.** With schema inference off, poison detection could never match (format stayed `AUTO`) and duplicate detection gave up for lack of a key field — both reported a clean 0. Poison detection now derives the sample's dominant format, duplicate detection falls back to the Kafka record key (previously ignored entirely), and an exact count that errors reports the reason as a topic issue.
- **Poison detection only checked the first character**, so a truncated `{"id":` passed as valid JSON — exactly the payload the check exists to catch. It parses now.
- **Bounded scans never stated their bounds.** `globalStats.scopeNotes` reports what the run did not cover (10 000 messages for duplicates, 10 for poison, 1 000 for latency), and duplicate issues name the key grouped on and the window scanned.
- **The retained-runs map grew without limit.** Bounded to the last 20.
- Unhealthy topics wore a **grey** badge: `HEALTH_TONE` had no entry for the one failure state the backend could emit.

### Graded severity

`HealthStatus` was binary, so a topic with one duplicate key out of ten thousand messages and a topic whose audit could not run at all both came back `UNHEALTHY` — the count and the health score were noise on a real cluster. It becomes `HEALTHY < WARNING < CRITICAL`, and each finding carries its own severity through a new `TopicIssue(message, severity)` record (issues were bare strings, so the UI painted every one of them error-red). A topic takes the worst severity among its issues.

| Finding | Severity | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The topic failed to audit | `CRITICAL` | No verdict at all — the worst outcome |
| Unparseable payloads in the sample | `CRITICAL` | Malformed data; consumers will break on it |
| `COUNT(*)` returns 0 on a non-empty topic | `CRITICAL` | A real inconsistency |
| Duplicate keys | `WARNING` | Frequently legitimate (updates keyed by entity id) |
| Exact count unavailable | `WARNING` | The measurement is degraded, not the data |

`AuditReport` replaces `unhealthyTopicsCount` with `criticalTopicsCount` + `warningTopicsCount`, and `globalStats.healthScore` (0..1, critical −1, warning −½) is computed server-side so it is frozen into the persisted report.

### One run at a time, consistent totals

`startAudit` queued runs behind a single-threaded executor: clicking "Run new audit" five times lined up five full cluster scans with no way to cancel them. It now returns `AuditStart(auditId, started)`; `POST /api/audit/start` answers **409 with the id of the run already in flight** and the UI attaches to it. The slot is released in a `finally` — otherwise one failed run would block every later start.

`totalMessages` summed `topicSizes` (the offset estimate) while the per-topic column showed the exact Flink counts; it now sums the counts actually reported.

### Optimisations

- Format detection, schema inference and the poison check each opened their **own KafkaConsumer to read the same ten messages** — 3 round trips per topic, on every topic. One sample now feeds all three via new `detectFormat(topic, samples)` / `inferSchema(topic, format, samples)` overloads.
- Flow latency refetched every middle topic twice (target of one pair, source of the next). Memoized per run; both sides are also reduced to one delta per id.
- `MessageFieldExtractorService` rebuilt a `DocumentBuilderFactory` per XML message, up to 10 000 times per topic during duplicate detection — the pattern `CLAUDE.md` already forbids for `FlinkSqlService`. Now a `ThreadLocal<DocumentBuilder>`.

### Audit UI

Real progress bar fed by `phase` / `topicsCompleted` / `topicsTotal` (was a decorative bar frozen at 60% for a multi-minute scan). The last report is restored from the new `GET /api/audit/last` on mount instead of being lost on refresh — reports were already persisted to `internal.audit.history`, a topic nothing ever read back. Plus: "Needs Attention" tile splitting critical/warning, issue chips coloured by severity, run recap (timestamp, duration, prefix, checks), scope notes, the full lagging-features list, filter + sort on the topics table, links to the Topic Explorer, exact values in `title` on compacted numbers, JSON export, and proper `tablist`/`tab`/`tabpanel`/`progressbar` ARIA roles.

---

## Part 2 — Form data entry

### New primitives (`components/ui/`)

- **`Combobox` / `TopicInput`** — filtered suggestions with full keyboard support (ARIA combobox pattern: `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant`, `role="listbox"`), fed by a new `catalogStore`. `Layout` already polls `/api/dashboard` every 30s for the command palette; it now shares that list instead of keeping it, so autocomplete costs **no extra request**. Free text stays valid — a topic can exist before the 30s cache shows it.
- **`NumberInput`** — keeps the raw string while typing, coerces and clamps on blur. The previous `parseInt(e.target.value, 10) || 4096` on every keystroke made the field unusable: clearing it to retype snapped it back to the default mid-typing, and since `0` is falsy, a leading zero did too. The same pattern was in Config (×4) and `TopicSelectorPanel`.
- **`PasswordInput`** — reveal toggle and `autoComplete="new-password"`. Keystore passwords and API secrets were typed blind; a typo only showed up as a connection failure with nothing to diagnose.
- `Field` accepts an explicit `id`, so a form can focus the first invalid control.
- **`Button` defaults to `type="button"`** — inside a `<form>` an untyped `<button>` submits, which would turn every secondary action into an accidental submission.

### Per-field validation

`Config.validateConfig()` returned the **first** error as a string, rendered in a banner at the bottom of a scrolling page. Ten possible errors meant fixing one, saving, and getting the next, with no indication of which field was at fault. It now retur

## 왜

부록 A 를 실제로 따라가다 **두 군데서 막혔습니다.** 둘 다 문서 결함입니다.

## 1. `ts` 는 macOS 기본에 없습니다

```
zsh: command not found: ts
```

`ts` 는 moreutils 패키지라 별도 설치가 필요합니다. 같이 언급했던 `date +%3N` 도 BSD `date` 는 `%N` 을 모릅니다.

→ **`/usr/bin/perl`** 로 교체했습니다. macOS 기본 탑재라 설치가 필요 없고, 실제로 0.4초 간격을 정확히 잡는 것을 확인했습니다:

```
  + 0.04s  {"i":0}
  + 0.45s  {"i":1}
  + 0.85s  {"i":2}
  + 1.25s  {"i":3}
```

`$|=1` 을 빼면 안 된다는 점도 강조해 적었습니다 — **perl 이 출력을 버퍼링하면 우리가 재려던 바로 그 현상을 우리가 만들어내는** 꼴이 됩니다.

PR #11 을 머지하고 바로 측정하려다 **백엔드·Vercel 양쪽에서 404** 를 봤습니다.

함께 적은 유용한 사실: `gcloud run deploy` 에 `--image` 와 `--region` 만 주면
나머지 설정(동시성·타임아웃·시크릿·환경변수·서비스 계정)은 **이전 리비전에서 그대로 승계**됩니다.

## What does this PR do?

Adds the missing `reactions:write` bot scope to Slack manifests generated by both `hermes slack manifest` and the interactive setup flow. Without that scope, the processing reaction lifecycle is enabled by default but every `reactions.add` and `reactions.remove` request fails with `missing_scope`.

The adapter now logs one actionable warning per affected workspace for `missing_scope`, while keeping routine reaction failures such as `already_reacted` at DEBUG level.

Existing Slack apps must apply the updated manifest and be reinstalled to the workspace before the new OAuth scope takes effect.

## Related Issue

Fixes #71827

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] New skill (bundled or hub)

- Add `reactions:write` to the shared Slack manifest builder.
- Surface `missing_scope` as a once-per-workspace warning with remediation steps.
- Cover default and non-Assistant manifests, the real setup-generated manifest, and warning deduplication.

## How to Test

1. Generate a manifest with `hermes slack manifest --write` and verify `oauth_config.scopes.bot` contains both `reactions:read` and `reactions:write`.
2. Install or reinstall the Slack app using that manifest.
3. Send the bot a DM or mention and verify the processing and completion reactions appear.

```text
passed
```

author: bashfulrobot
body:
## What broke

`just qu` failed building the qbert system closure. Root cause: nixpkgs `python3.14-poetry-2.4.1` fails its own test suite during the build:

```
FAILED tests/installation/test_executor.py::test_execute_prints_warning_for_yanked_package[operations1-False] - AssertionError
FAILED tests/installation/test_executor.py::test_execute_prints_warning_for_yanked_package[operations2-True] - AssertionError
```

The yanked-package warning tests assert against installer output that no longer matches verbatim under python3.14. Poetry is pulled into `system-path`, so its failed check cascades up through `man-paths` and `system-path` to the whole `nixos-system-qbert` derivation.

This is an upstream nixpkgs breakage, not a config error.

## Fix

Wrap `poetry` in `overridePythonAttrs (_: { doCheck = false; })` in `modules/dev/python/default.nix`, mirroring the existing `pipx` workaround a few lines above (same class of upstream test drift). Revert once nixpkgs ships a fixed poetry.

## Verification

`just build-host qbert` completes clean:

```
Done. The new configuration is /nix/store/...-nixos-system-qbert-26.11.20260723.e2587ca
```

body:
**Claude** (on behalf of Xerial):

`ops/hub_publish.py` pinned `LAN_IP` to `192.168.86.20` — one specific machine's address.

Every hub card published from any other host therefore advertised that host's servers at pinnacle's address. The card looks correct in the hub; spectators connecting from it reach the wrong machine, or nothing at all.

This surfaced moving the rtx bench rigs to `lanister` (`192.168.86.34`): the registrations went up looking healthy and pointed at a machine that had just been shut down.

## Change

```python
LAN_IP = os.environ.get("HUB_LAN_IP", "192.168.86.20")
```

The default is unchanged, so nothing moves for anyone already publishing from pinnacle. Hosts that are not pinnacle set `HUB_LAN_IP` in their unit file.

## Evidence

With `HUB_LAN_IP=192.168.86.34` set in lanister's `rtx-main2on2-hub` and `rtx-jumpcost-hub` units, the live registrations on `servexeri` now read:

```
rtx-main2on2.json    RTX-main-bench               192.168.86.34:27560
rtx-jumpcost.json    RTX-jumpcost (margin tax)    192.168.86.34:27640
```

and the QTV relay answers end to end through both reverse tunnels:

```
servexeri:31560 -> QTVSV 1
servexeri:31640 -> QTVSV 1
```

Before the change the same run wrote `192.168.86.20` into both cards while the servers were on `.34`.

author: nvsinha
body:
Release prep for the Claude Agent SDK migration (#14).

## Version bump

`backend/package.json` 0.1.56 → **0.2.0**. Minor rather than patch because the SDK migration changes runtime behaviour (system prompt handling, abort reporting, system-message filtering) — matching `.tagpr`'s mapping of the `enhancement` label to a minor bump. `generate-version.js` reads this file, so the built binary reports the right version (`cli/version.ts` is gitignored and regenerated at build time).

## npm publish is now opt-in

`release.yml` fires on **every** tag (`tags: "*"`) and ran `npm publish` unconditionally. That is effectively irreversible: npm unpublish is limited to a 72-hour window and a version number can never be reused. `pdlc-studio` has never been published, so the next tag would also have claimed the name on the public registry as a side effect of cutting a release.

The job is now gated behind the `ENABLE_NPM_PUBLISH` repository variable. Nothing depends on it — only `release` and `npm-publish` declare `needs: build` — so a tag still builds all four binaries and publishes the GitHub Release.

To publish to npm later, set `ENABLE_NPM_PUBLISH=true`. Note the first publish will likely also need a `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`: OIDC trusted publishing has to be configured against an npm package that already exists.

## Also worth knowing

`tagpr` is **failing on every push to main** because the `GH_PAT` secret is not configured (repo has 0 secrets). That is why this version bump and the tag are being done by hand instead of through the documented release-PR flow. Adding `GH_PAT` would restore automatic version bumps, changelog generation, and tagging.

Separately, `CLAUDE.md` documents a label set (`feature`, `backend`, `frontend`, `breaking`, …) that does not exist in this repo — only GitHub's defaults are present, so `.tagpr`'s `minorLabels`/`majorLabels` can only ever match `enhancement`.

This repository is public and published to npm, but it grew out of a working notebook. Two categories of content had never been cleaned up.

## 1. Chinese-language documentation (~12,000 CJK characters)

Nine ADRs were written entirely in Chinese (ADR-001/002/003/004/027/028/029/030/033) and are translated here. The CHANGELOG's v1.0.0 section — 224 lines of Chinese work log — is rewritten as English release notes. Thirteen further documents had Chinese fragments, mostly internal task titles.

Cleaned up alongside it, because it was the same content:

- A real name appeared in five places across four ADRs.
- `docs/releases/README.md` and ADR-035 referenced the maintainer's **private global config**, by path and by rule name.
- Two references to a sibling repository's absolute local path.
- Dead links to internal planning documents that were never public.

**Non-English text that is the *product* is deliberately kept**: the translation tables (ADR-023), the WCAG section headings (ADR-024), the Chinese and Japanese personas, and the tests asserting those translations are correct. Removing them would delete a shipped feature and make the README's localisation claims false.

## 2. `projects/` — 20 tracked files that were never meant to be public

`.gitignore` has said `projects/` is *"Operator-private, never committed"* since 2026-05-03. But `projects/talkbuddy/` was committed **2026-04-24, nine days earlier**, and gitignore does not apply to already-tracked files. The repository has therefore been publishing audit scenarios for two unrelated private projects, including their domains, a Google OAuth signup flow, an admin panel audit, a paywall enforcement flow, a crypto-tracing purchase flow, and a Chrome extension install.

Removed from the index. Local working copies are untouched, and gitignore keeps them out from here on.

> Note: this removes them going forward. Purging them from history is a separate, follow-up operation.

## The gate

Neither problem stays fixed by remembering the rule — that is exactly what failed the first time. `scripts/check-english-only.ts` fails the build on CJK outside the localisation surface and runs as part of `npm test`. It skips binaries via NUL-byte detection, or every screenshot fixture would trip it.

**Verified failing, not just passing:**

| Chinese comment added to `README.md` | exit 1, names file and line |
| Chinese entry added to `CHANGELOG.md` | exit 1, names file and line |
| New ADR written in Chinese | exit 1, names file and line |
| Existing i18n tables, personas, translation tests | exit 0 — not caught |

## Local gate

build, lint, `lint:no-console`, `lint:english-only`, vitest **2350 passed / 1 skipped**, schemas idempotent, `npm audit --production --audit-level=moderate` exit 0, `license:check`, vendor integrity, coverage 82.36/70.73/84.34/84.01, Playwright 22 passed, forks-pool integration 27 passed, SBOM, bench 0 regressions.

author: vikashloomba
body:
## Why

`fc50fae` (#297) landed agent attribution on `main` while the `commit-msg` hook was already in place — and **none of the three branch commit messages contained any**. Two gaps had to be open at once:

1. The hook inspected only the message file. Branch commit `ad2a30ac` was **authored** under the agent identity (committer was the owner), which the hook never looked at.
2. With `squash_merge_commit_message=COMMIT_MESSAGES`, GitHub composes the squash message from the branch commit messages **and synthesizes a co-author trailer for every distinct author identity among them**. That text is generated server-side, after the last local hook can run.

So the identity alone was sufficient, and no local gate could have caught it.

## What

`scripts/check-attribution.mjs` owns both axes and the pattern list, and runs in three places:

| Where | Scope | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| `.githooks/commit-msg` | pending message + the identity git is about to stamp (`git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT`, so amend/rebase replays are caught) | the commit |
| `.githooks/pre-push` | the commits actually being pushed — exact range from git's stdin; a new branch falls back to "not already on origin" after a refresh | the push |
| **Build & test** CI job | the PR's `base..head` | the **merge** |

Only the CI leg runs before the squash button, so it is the one that closes the hole. It is a **step of the existing required job**, not a new job, so the ruleset context is unchanged and it blocks merges immediately. Zero-dep script, so it runs before the install.

Also fixes a real hole in the old pattern list: `Co-Authored-By:` was matched case-sensitively and never matched the lower-case form GitHub actually emits.

## Verification

Run over PR #297's real `base..head`, the gate flags the commit that caused this:

```
attribution: 1 commit carries agent attribution — BLOCKED:

  ad2a30ac  feat(mcp-server): stop agent-driven panel re-renders...
    ✗ author identity is an Anthropic e-mail address / an agent identity: Claude <...>
```

10 hermetic tests in `packages/acp-agents/test/attribution-gate.test.ts`, following the `fork-sync-gitdir.test.ts` convention. Includes a false-positive guard: dependency-bump subjects naming the Claude/Anthropic SDK packages must still pass, or ACP maintenance becomes unmergeable. Both local hooks were exercised end-to-end (correct rev-list args for existing-branch, new-branch, deletion, empty-stdin and multi-ref pushes), and the CI step's bash was simulated for `pull_request`, `push` (including a zeroed `before`) and `workflow_dispatch`.

## Notes

- `fc50fae` itself stays on `main` — removing it means rewriting published history. This stops the next one. The pre-push hook uses git's reported remote tip as the range boundary, so already-pushed history never re-triggers it.
- The root cause is upstream of all three gates: the commit was authored under an agent identity because that is what the cloud session commits as. These gates catch it; configuring those sessions to commit under your identity prevents it.

author: hirosassa
body:
## Summary

Refactors the rule layer to remove tight coupling and redundant AST traversals.

- Rules were hard-wired into `main.rs`. Introduces a `Rule` trait and
  an `all_rules()` registry so adding a rule means one entry, not editing the
  analysis loop.
- Removes the duplicated `for node in traverse(...) { if node.kind() == ... }`
  boilerplate from the node-driven rules.
- The five rules each walked the whole tree independently. `run_rules()`
  now shares a single pre-order traversal across all node-driven rules.

## Changes

- Add `src/rules/rule.rs`:
  - `trait Rule { id(); check_node(); check_tree(); check() }`
  - `all_rules() -> Vec<Box<dyn Rule>>` — the single rule registry
  - `run_rules(tree, sql)` — one shared traversal fanning each node out to every rule
- Convert the four node-driven rules to structs implementing `check_node`
  (`UseCurrentDate`, `CompareTableSuffixWithSubquery`, `UnnecessaryOrderBy`,
  `InvalidGroupBy`).
- `UnusedColumnInCte` keeps its cross-node analysis via `check_tree`
  (its internal multi-pass work is tracked separately as P4/P5).
- Simplify `main.rs::analyse_sql` to a single `run_rules(&tree, sql)` call.

## Behavior

No change in what is detected. `run_rules` produces exactly the union of each
rule's own output (covered by a new test). Diagnostic **ordering** changes from
"grouped by rule" to source-position order for node-driven rules, followed by
the tree-driven rule.

author: colbyjack1134
body:
Walkers stopped piling onto a single point. Three causes:

- `separation_radius` defaulted to 60 while walker.tscn's body is 72 wide, so the push only started once two walkers already overlapped.
- `separation_strength` 140 against `chase_speed` 220 meant a converging pair still closed at 80 px/s at maximum repulsion. A gap needs strength * (1 - gap/radius) to equal chase_speed, which 140 over 60 cannot reach at any distance.
- `attack_slot_spread` 40 draws offsets averaging 27 px apart against 72 px bodies, so everyone steered at the same x.

walker.tres now carries radius 160, strength 540 and slot spread 160, settling pairs about 95 px apart. Since strength above chase_speed makes the summed push able to fling whoever is in the middle of a pack, `_separation_push` clamps its total to chase_speed * 1.5; that only bites below 62 px or with several neighbours.

Also de-stacks two things. Every enemy rolls a per instance speed scale of +-12 percent so a pack strings into a line instead of arriving as a wall. And budget cycling reuses spawn markers, which put every extra arrival on the identical point, so `_arrival` stamps an alternating +-90 offset per pass. The plan is built at generation time with no physics world, so `_telegraph` validates the offset against real geometry and falls back to the mirrored side then the marker itself, then passes the resolved spot to `_arrive` so the telegraph always marks where the enemy lands.

Tested in game. `attack_slot_spread` is the number most likely to want tuning: a large roll now holds off and dashes rather than pressing in for contact damage. 160 is half of `dash_range` 320 so every slot stays inside dash range.

Shooters, orbs and the late game wave budgets are deliberately out of scope, noted in project-state.

## Summary

Closes #690

GrantFox FWC26 (Stellar Wave) — Audit the Dashboard skeleton for height/spacing/shape parity with the final component so first-paint does not jump (CLS = 0).

## Root cause

The Dashboard skeleton placeholders used hardcoded `borderRadius` values (`4px`, `2px`) that did not match the design-token radii of the final rendered elements. Heights were approximate rather than measured from actual component CSS. The `Skeleton` component had a bug where the `variant` prop was referenced but never destructured, so `variant="subtle"` never applied the `skeleton--subtle` class.

## Changes

### `src/components/Skeleton.tsx`
- **Bug fix**: destructure `variant` prop (was referenced but undefined — `skeleton--subtle` never applied)
- **New `shape="pill"`** for full-pill badge/chip placeholders (StatusBadge, network-badge, wallet chip)

### `src/components/Skeleton.css`
- `--skeleton-radius` now resolves via `var(--radius-md, 0.5rem)` — matches card/button radius exactly
- New `--skeleton-radius-sm: var(--radius-sm, 0.375rem)` for text-line placeholders
- New `--skeleton-radius-pill: var(--radius-full, 9999px)` for badge placeholders
- New `.skeleton--pill` rule

### `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx`
- Remove all inline `borderRadius` hardcodes; replaced with semantic `shape` prop
- Skeleton heights matched to measured final element heights:
  - Summary cards: label=14px, value=32px, sub=12px
  - Activity: icon=28x28px, title=14px, sub=10px
  - Gauge meta: label=10px, value=14px
  - Credit line: name=14px, badge=18px, utilisation bar=3px
- Risk gauge placeholder replaced: 80px circle → 160:100 aspect-ratio rectangle matching SVG viewBox
- `aria-hidden="true"` on all skeleton wrapper divs

### `src/pages/Dashboard.css`
- `min-height` floors documented with precise measurements and derivation comments

## Tests

### `src/components/Skeleton.test.tsx`
- `shape="pill"` class application and CSS token assertions
- `--skeleton-radius` token resolves via `var(--radius-md)` (alignment check)
- New `--skeleton-radius-sm` and `--skeleton-radius-pill` token declarations
- `aria-hidden` default and override coverage

### `src/pages/Dashboard.test.tsx`
- **30 new focused parity tests** in `Dashboard skeleton — height/spacing/shape parity (FWC26 #690)` suite
- Covers: summary-card label/value/sub heights and shapes, skeleton-card min-height, risk-gauge arc width + meta heights, credit-line name/badge/bar dimensions, activity icon 28x28 + shape, CSS source assertions for `min-height` values

## Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)
- Skeleton containers carry `aria-hidden="true"` — AT skips decorative placeholders
- `aria-busy="true"` on loading regions (pre-existing, preserved)
- Reduced-motion: shimmer suppressed via `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` and `[data-motion="reduced"]`

author: 0xmhha
body:
## Summary

Moves the two post-launch steps a consensus-family handoff needs — full peer
mesh and producer bootstrap — out of the reproduction script and into the
handoff framework, so the launch sequence itself can drive them. Follows up on
the handoff framework merged in #27.

Previously the framework init'd and launched the mixed binaries but left peering
and bootstrap to the bash reproduction. Without a full mesh the go-wbft
validators seed the validator set at the fork block but never reach a quorum with
each other and stall; that fix now lives in the framework as a reusable, tested
primitive.

## Changes

- `WireMesh` calls `admin_addPeer` on every node for all the other nodes' enodes
  so the successor validators form a full mesh. The peer caller is injected; the
  default issues JSON-RPC.
- The plan carries each node's public key (optional `NodePubkeys` input) and
  `Plan.Enodes` derives the enodes the mesh wires.
- `LaunchHandoff` composes the full post-plan sequence: launch, wire the mesh,
  then bootstrap each producer. The peer caller and bootstrap are injected, so
  the orchestration is unit-tested without binaries.
- `Launch` gained an optional `ProvisionKeys` hook that runs after a node's
  datadir is initialized and before it launches — where external key material
  (the node key in the binary-specific instance dir, the producer keystore,
  static-nodes) is placed, without the framework hardcoding any key layout.

## Verification

- 29 Go packages pass (`go test ./...`); `gofmt` clean.
- New unit tests cover the full-mesh call pattern (self-skip, empty-skip, failure
  reporting), and that `LaunchHandoff` launches all nodes, issues the expected
  mesh calls, and bootstraps only the producer.

## Follow-up

A `chainbench upgrade run` command (and a gated live E2E) can now compose these
primitives with preset key material to reproduce the handoff end to end from Go;
`tests/repro/wemix-wbft-handoff.sh` remains the executable reference.

body:
The post-login **foundation** for the new views (Iteration 12) — server-rendered pages with real, shareable URLs and native back/forward — plus the individual view and a `/add` form that finally uses the design system.

### Route architecture
Each view is a real server-rendered URL (shareable, back/forward for free), slotting into the existing route dispatch. This PR adds `/u/:id`; `/leaderboard`, `/bots-vs-humans`, and `/compare` follow as their own PRs on this foundation. SSE board refresh is preserved.

### Shared nav + "your desk"
- A shared top nav (**Board · You · Add · Sign out**) on every authed page. Leaderboard / Bots-vs-Humans links are **flag-gated** so no merged state has a dead link.
- The board now marks the signed-in viewer's card **YOU** and pulls it to the front (the missing "your desk" distinction), and every card links to its `/u/:id` profile.

### Individual view (`/u/:id`)
Your own or anyone's (open to the league, per the board's existing model): hero equity with unrealized %, a stat row (cash / invested / unrealized / buying power), full positions + activity timeline, persona read for bots, and an **honest reserved "performance history" seam** — no fabricated history. body:
Auditoría de iPhone (390×844, dsf 3) sobre los módulos de **Operación**, **Marketing**, **Multifashion** y el **login**. Todo medido en browser real con emulación por CDP y `getBoundingClientRect()` — antes y después. Regla de la casa: **44×44 px mínimo al tacto**.

## Lo más importante: la única página de 23 que se iba de lado

`/productos/cargar` (Depurador). La barra de 6 pestañas era `inline-flex` sin wrap ni scroll, así que sus 543 px empujaban la **página entera**: `scrollWidth 547` vs `clientWidth 390` = **157 px de scroll horizontal**. "Reglas" e "Historial" quedaban fuera de pantalla y solo se llegaba arrastrando todo el layout de costado.

Ahora la barra scrollea sola (`flex-nowrap overflow-x-auto`):

| | Antes | Después |
|---|---|---|
| Página | 547 / 390 ❌ | **390 / 390** ✓ |
| Barra de pestañas | no scrolleaba | 651 px dentro de 356 ✓ |
| `window.scrollX` con la barra al tope | — | **0** (la página no se mueve) |
| Alto de cada pestaña | 41 px | **44 px** |

Verificado con click real: "Historial" abre y la página sigue en 390/390.

## Targets que pasan a 44×44

| Módulo | Qué | Antes | Después |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marketing | × de "Nuevo proyecto" — el target más chico de la app | 13.2×20 | **44×44** |
| Préstamos | modal "Seleccionar Empleado" **no tenía** botón de cerrar | — | **✕ 44×44** |
| Reclamos | ↓PDF / ↓Excel (×10 empresas) | 36 px, separados 6 px | **44 px, separados 8 px** |
| Reclamos | toggles "▶ Historial (n)" | 16.5 px | **44 px** |
| Cheques | 6 de 7 campos de "Nuevo Cheque" | 38-40 px | **≥44 px** |
| Gastos de Empresa | 8 botones "Guardar" | 41 px | **44 px** |
| Multifashion | toggle Mes/Año | 26 px | **45 px** |
| Multifashion | flechas de mes | 36×36 a 4 px del selector | **44×44 a 8 px** |
| Login | toggle "ver contraseña" | 19×18 | **44×44** |
| Login | "¿Olvidaste tu contraseña?" | 18 px de alto | **44 px** |

Los dos modales se verificaron **abriéndolos** en el iPhone emulado, y la ✕ de Préstamos con click real (el modal cierra).

## Texto por debajo del mínimo

`text-xs` en este repo son **13 px** (escala custom en `tailwind.config.ts`), no 12. Todas las clases arbitrarias sub-12px de estos módulos suben a `text-xs`:

- Reclamos: `text-[11px]` ×8 y badge "Alerta" 10 px ×3
- Gastos de Empresa: badge "Pendiente" 10 px ×9
- Marketing: `text-[11px]` ×7
- Multifashion: iniciales de día a **8.5 px** ×7 (el texto más chico de toda la app) y ejes de los gráficos a 10 px ×21

Las etiquetas de los ejes de "Ventas día por día" suben de 10 a 12 px; recharts adelgaza sola la grilla de 15 a 13 marcas de día y no queda ni un solape.

**Cuánto crece Multifashion:** la tarjeta "Mejor día de la semana" pasa de 174.8 a **178.3 px** (+3.5 px — el gráfico tiene alto fijo) y la página entera de 2201 a **2231 px** (+30 px, casi todo el toggle Mes/Año). Sin scroll horizontal.

## Barrido final

Las 9 vistas tocadas, en iPhone emulado, sobre esta rama ya rebasada encima de #297:

```
/                              hscroll 390/390 ✓   texto<12px: 0
/productos/cargar              hscroll 390/390 ✓   texto<12px: 0
/prestamos                     hscroll 390/390 ✓   texto<12px: 0
/marketing                     hscroll 390/390 ✓   texto<12px: 0
/cheques                       hscroll 390/390 ✓   texto<12px: 0
/reclamos                      hscroll 390/390 ✓   texto<12px: 0
/gastos-empresa                hscroll 390/390 ✓   texto<12px: 0
/multifashion                  hscroll 390/390 ✓   texto<12px: 0
/multifashion?subtab=clientes  hscroll 390/390 ✓   texto<12px: 0
```

## Queda pendiente (decisión de Daniel)

**Préstamos — los nombres cortados NO se arreglan bajando la letra.** Medido: "MARIA BETHANCOURTH" ocupa 191 px reales y la columna le da **90.3 px**. Para que entre completo haría falta bajar a **~7.6 px**, muy por debajo del piso del repo. Cuántos de los 12 nombres se ven enteros según el tamaño:

| Tamaño | Nombres completos |
|---|---|
| 16 px (actual) | **0 / 12** |
| 14 px (`text-sm`, piso del repo) | 1 / 12 |
| 13 px | 2 / 12 |
| 12 px (piso del encargo) | **3 / 12** |

Por eso **no se tocó la letra**: achicarla degrada la legibilidad y sigue sin resolver el problema. La fila mide 358 px y se reparte así: nombre 90.3 · chip "⚠ Pendiente" 89.7 · saldo 72 · chevron 44 · gaps 36. El chip de quincena se come tanto ancho como el nombre — ahí está el espacio, pero recuperarlo es un cambio de layout que no estaba autorizado.

## Tests

17 assertions nuevas en `src/__tests__/iphone-targets-operacion.test.ts` que congelan la **causa** de cada medición (jsdom no calcula layout, así que medir el rect no es opción): que ninguna barra de pestañas vuelva a ser `inline-flex`, que los modales conserven su ✕, que los targets sigan en 44 y que ningún módulo del lote reintroduzca clases de texto sub-12px.

author: xuepoo
body:
## Summary

Starts a `comparisons/` directory for **runnable, real-browser** head-to-head benchmarks against other libraries — and the first one already paid for itself with a real optimization.

## The finding

`@chenglou/pretext` (Cheng Lou, March 2026, 49k stars) independently arrived at the **same architecture** as `@vectojs/layout`: one-time `prepare()` measures via canvas and caches segment widths, then `layout()` is pure arithmetic so resize never touches DOM layout. That makes it the most directly comparable library available.

Measured Chrome 150 / Firefox 153, median of 7, 500 prose blocks relaid out at 4 widths:

| relayout hot path | Chrome | Firefox |
|---|---|---|
| `layoutPrepared()` (positions every glyph) | 30.71 ms | 25.38 ms |
| **`measurePrepared()` (new)** | **0.92 ms** | **4.02 ms** |
| `pretext.layout()` | 0.77 ms | 1.32 ms |

**pretext's hot path was ~39× faster than ours.** Reading their `line-break.ts` showed why: `layout()` walks **segment-level** width arrays and only counts lines (O(segments), zero allocation), while `layoutPrepared()` positions **every glyph** and allocates a `LayoutNode` each, on every relayout (O(glyphs), ~5–10× more items).

That's a scope difference, not a defect — we need glyph positions for selection geometry and the a11y projection. But we were paying glyph cost even for callers that only want *"how tall is this at this width"*: a virtualized list measuring rows, a resize pass, an autosizing container.

## The fix

`LayoutEngine.measurePrepared(prepared)` — same greedy wrap decisions walked over prepared **word** widths, no glyph positioning, no allocation. **15–33× faster than the full path in Chrome, 6–7× in Firefox**, closing the gap to pretext to **1.19×** at 500 blocks (Chrome).

It falls back to per-glyph stepping only for a word wider than the measure, which must break mid-word — **the first prototype got this wrong and the tests caught it** (it reported 1 line where the full path wrapped to 12).

## Tests (+15)

`measurePrepared.test.ts` asserts agreement with `layoutPrepared()` on line count and height across 8 text shapes × 3 widths, plus reflow-on-width-change and empty text. One subtlety documented in the test: an empty paragraph advances `y` without emitting a glyph, so a distinct-Y count can't see it — the reference adds the blank-paragraph count back rather than the fast path being "wrong".

`@vectojs/layout` 142 pass (was 127). core 448, ui 410, markdown 74 unchanged.

## Ground rules for `comparisons/`

Documented in `comparisons/README.md` so these stay engineering rather than marketing: same workload both ways in the same run; real browsers, both engines; **state the scope difference**; compare like-for-like work; and **report losses**.

Applying rule 4 to this PR: `prepare()` looks ~60× faster in VectoJS here, but only because the engine caches prepared paragraphs internally and the corpus repeats. That is **not** a like-for-like win and is excluded from any published table.

## Notes

- Libraries under comparison are cloned shallow into `tmp/references/` for source review (11 of them), and added as root `devDependencies` — dev-only, unreachable from any published `@vectojs/*` package.
- LightningChart JS is commercial/closed-source; any comparison must be doc-based and labelled as such.
- For the **rendering** libraries (Pixi/Konva/Fabric/Paper/Two/ZIM) a throughput number alone would be misleading — the meaningful differences are text crispness at DPR > 1, whether text is selectable, and whether an a11y tree exists. Those need real-browser screenshots + DOM probes, which is the next comparison.
- Baselines: `vectojs-docs/forge/baselines/cmp-text-layout-pretext-{chrome150,firefox153}-2026-07-26.json`.

## Summary

Two unrelated fixes bundled: the SEO metadata overhaul you asked for, plus a CSS precedence bug that was hiding the desktop navbar.

**The nav bug (root cause).** `app/layout.tsx` inlines "critical CSS" in a plain `<style>` tag. That sheet is *unlayered*, and unlayered rules beat everything inside `@layer utilities` — where all Tailwind utilities live. It contained `.hidden { display: none }`, so every `hidden md:flex` / `hidden sm:inline` element was permanently hidden regardless of viewport: the desktop nav links, the "Get Started" CTA and the WhatsApp button's label. Verified with CDP `getMatchedStylesForNode`:

```
.hidden   display:none   media: []                 layers: ["utilities"]
.md\:flex display:flex   media: ["(min-width:48rem)"] layers: ["utilities"]
.hidden   display:none   media: []                 layers: []      <-- inline critical CSS, wins
```

Fix: drop the display utilities (`.hidden`, `.lg\:block`) from the inline block; everything else stays.

**WhatsApp FAB**: 16px glyph / 40px tall → 24px glyph, `min-h-14 min-w-14`, so it's a 56px circle on mobile and a full pill with the label on ≥sm.

**/resources search**: the input existed but sat ~1000px down the page. It's now `sticky` under the navbar (`#search-guides`) and the hero has a "Search all 30 guides" jump link.

author: nexvelon
body:
The Sprint 6 keystone: a shared **`ReportDataset`** abstraction with three renderers (CSV / xlsx / PDF) so every report defines its data **once** and exports in all three formats, plus a real `reports:view`-gated **Reports hub** replacing the "Coming Soon" page. Proven end-to-end with the WIP portfolio report. **No migration.**

## The foundation

`lib/reports/dataset.ts` — `ReportDataset { title, subtitle, meta[], columns[], rows[], totals?, filename }` + the **single `formatCell(value, kind)`** (text/number/currency/percent/date). All three renderers format through it, so a report reads **identically** in every format — no drift between the CSV and the PDF of the same report.

Three renderers:
- **`to-csv.ts`** — reuses the existing RFC-4180 quoter `csvField` + `\r\n` (matches the current financial CSVs).
- **`to-xlsx.ts`** — server-side exceljs (`await import("exceljs")` → title band + bold header + rows + bold totals → `writeBuffer()` → base64). **No new dependency** — exceljs `^4.4.0` was already installed (used for import templates); this is the first *report* use.
- **`to-pdf.tsx`** — `renderToBuffer` (the same pattern the PO/invoice PDFs use) over a **new generic tabular `ReportDocument`** (title band + meta + repeating column header via `fixed` + rows + totals + page numbers). The existing Documents are all single-record invoice/PO layouts; a generic N-column data grid was the one net-new piece.

`export.ts` — `exportDataset(ds, format)` → `{ data, filename (with ext), mime, encoding }` (CSV as text; xlsx/pdf as base64 in the action payload — same in-payload delivery as the existing CSVs, no signed URL for v1). `download.ts` — the **one** client `downloadReport` (Safari-safe synthetic anchor), replacing the ~8 duplicated blob-download blocks.

## Audit findings

**2a** — `csvField` (RFC-4180 quoter) + the `ActionResult<{…, filename}>` envelope are reused verbatim.
**2b — xlsx pattern.** exceljs is installed and used only for import templates (client-side); mirrored it **server-side** (`writeBuffer` → base64 in the payload). Reported: durable bucket storage is *not* used for v1 — the file travels in-payload like the CSVs; a bucket+signed-URL path (the `lib/storage/*-pdfs.ts` flow) is available later if scheduled email delivery needs durable copies.
**2c — tabular PDF.** The existing `render-*.ts`/Documents are single-record; the generic `ReportDocument` is net-new but small, reusing `renderToBuffer`. **Deviation:** it uses @react-pdf's built-in Helvetica rather than `quote-fonts` — `registerQuoteFonts` auto-registers **only in the browser** (`typeof window`), so relying on it server-side is fragile; Helvetica needs no registration and renders robustly. Brand colours (navy/gold) keep the house look.
**2d — the ~8 duplicated anchor-download sites.** Added the shared `downloadReport` and used it for WIP now; the 7 financial-tab sites are migrated in **REP-2** (reported, not churned here).

## Consistency guarantee

Because `formatCell` is the single formatter, the same dataset renders identical values everywhere. Tested directly: the currency / percent / date cell in the xlsx equals `formatCell(...)` equals the value in the CSV.

## Proven with WIP + the hub

- `exportWipReportAction({format})` builds the WIP `ReportDataset` from `getWipPortfolio` (reuses the existing data), gated **financials:edit** (WIP's tier), returns the export payload; `/reports/wip` renders the table + **CSV / Excel / PDF** buttons → `downloadReport`.
- `/reports` is now a real hub (category cards: Financial / Operational / Compliance + Utilities), gated **reports:view**; WIP + the duplicate-quote utility are live, the rest marked **"coming in REP-2/3"**. Honest empty: an empty portfolio renders an empty table and exports a valid **headers-only** file, not an error.

## Tests

- `dataset-renderers.test.ts` (5) — CSV header+rows+totals with RFC-4180 quoting; `formatCell` per kind; **xlsx round-trip** (parse back with exceljs, assert title + header + cell values); PDF smoke (`%PDF` base64); **consistency** (CSV & xlsx show identical formatted currency/percent/date).
- `wip-report-export.test.ts` (6) — dataset built from `getWipPortfolio`; gated financials:edit (Technician denied, Admin/Accountant ok); csv/xlsx/pdf payloads with correct extension + mime + encoding; **empty portfolio → headers-only, not an error**.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm run build` — success (`/reports` 2.99 kB, `/reports/wip` 3.75 kB)
- `npm test` — **136 files, 899 tests pass** (+11 new; was 134/888)

## No migration

Pure assembly + rendering over existing data; no schema, no bucket.

## Deviations

- `ReportDocument` uses built-in Helvetica (not `quote-fonts`) for robust server-side rendering — see 2c.
- xlsx cells carry the **same formatted strings** as CSV/PDF (consistency-first + precomputed totals) rather than raw numbers with numFmt; native-numeric "live Excel" typing is a later enhancement (the report already provides totals).
- Export payloads travel in-payload (base64), not via a signed URL/bucket — v1 keeps it simple, matching the CSV pattern.

**REP-2 (financial reports: P&L, margin, AR/AP, HST, T5018, profitability) and REP-3 (operational: pipeline, labour utilization, vendor spend, inventory) follow**, each defining a `ReportDataset` and getting all three formats for free. Plus the honest **business snapshot** (run-rate/margin/backlog — no fabricated valuation multiple).

- Move required `$filename_unlock` before optional `$remove` and `$r_type` in `pfb_unlock()`.
- Reorder every affected production and generated-smoke positional call without changing argument meaning.
- Extend the tracked-source `E_ALL` lint sweep from `src/*.php` to `src/*.php` plus `src/*.inc`, and refresh the intentional function-signature inventory.
- Retire the two fixed optional-before-required fingerprints from the PHP diagnostic baseline.

## Root cause

`pfb_unlock()` declared optional parameters before the required unlock-state parameter. PHP 8 therefore treated the optional parameters as required and emitted declaration-time deprecations. Giving the state parameter a default would hide caller errors, so the required parameter and each positional caller move together.

## Verification

- RED: `vendor/bin/phpunit tests/php/SrcPhpDeprecationLintTest.php` failed under PHP 8.5.8 and named only `src/usr/local/pkg/pfblockerng/pfblockerng.inc`, with both optional-before-required diagnostics.

author: earelin
body:
Records **ADR-0015** — how `ui/src` is modularized. Documentation only; no code, no dependency changes, no task file.

## Why now

[ADR-0004](docs/architecture/0004-ui-stack-vite-mantine.md) settled the UI's build tool, router and component library but said nothing about `ui/src`'s internal structure. What grew there is **type-based** — `api/` and `commons/` — and that has three costs that all get worse as the product grows:

- **Every new feature smears across two folders.** `api/users.ts` belongs to the admin screens specifically; `api/httpClient.ts` is genuinely cross-feature infrastructure. Nothing in the tree distinguishes them.
- **Nothing encodes a boundary.** TypeScript won't stop a future feature reaching into another's internals — only convention would, and convention isn't checked.
- **Deleting a feature is archaeology.** Its files are spread across the tree rather than sitting in one folder.

The project overview commits this app to extracting, storing, analysing and exporting contract data. Search, analysis and export screens are coming, each with their own API calls and state, so `routes/admin/` will not stay the only feature and the cost of having no rule only grows.

## The decision

Feature slices with a shared core, dependencies pointing one way only:

```
app → features → shared/entities → shared/ui + shared/lib
```

A feature **never imports sideways** from another feature — cross-feature code moves *down* into `shared/` or *up* into `app/`. Each slice exposes a single `index.ts` and keeps the rest private.

This is the layering the backend already runs under. [ADR-0002](docs/architecture/0002-hexagonal-architecture.md) groups by bounded module with an enforced one-directional rule, and [ADR-0013](docs/architecture/0013-shared-commons-module.md) named an explicit shared layer rather than letting cross-cutting helpers leak into a domain module. Mirroring it keeps the two halves of the codebase legible in the same way.

## Two calls worth reviewing

**`shared/` is split three ways, not left as one folder.** `entities` (cross-feature domain shapes), `ui` (business-agnostic presentational components), `lib` (framework-free utilities). `shared/entities/` also carries an explicit **second-consumer rule** — a type only moves there once a second feature needs it, until then it stays local. This is the junk-drawer failure mode ADR-0013 warns about for the backend's `commons`, and the split is what keeps the layer defensible. The honest cost is recorded in Cons: `shared/entities/` starts with one thin file (`currentUser.ts`), so until a second consumer appears its payoff is speculative.

**Enforcement is `eslint-plugin-boundaries`, not `dependency-cruiser`.** The rules go in the existing flat `eslint.config.js` and ride the `npm run lint` step already in `ui-ci.yml` — no new toolchain, no new CI job. `dependency-cruiser` is declined as duplicative of what ESLint already enforces here. The package/monorepo split (the closest frontend analogue to ADR-0002's real module boundaries) is deliberately deferred until multiple teams or build times justify it — the same threshold logic this codebase applies on the backend.

## Status

`accepted`. The layering and its enforcement mechanism are agreed, so the record governs new frontend work from now on. Note this is accepted *ahead of* implementation — unlike ADR-0012 and ADR-0014, which sit at `proposed` in the same state — so the tree on `trunk` does not yet match the decision.

The follow-up work is **not** in this PR: migrating the tree (28 of the 33 files under `ui/src` move; only `main.tsx`, `vite-env.d.ts`, `App.test.tsx` and `test/` stay put) and wiring the boundary rules. Both need a task traced to a feature per the repo's `SPEC → FEAT → TASK` flow.

## Verification

`scripts/docs-lint.sh` passes all three checks — markdownlint, lychee offline link resolution, and Mermaid validation of the layering diagram.

The illustrative target tree was checked against the actual source rather than assumed: `api/systemStatus.ts` is imported only by the admin `DashboardPage`, so it lands in the feature slice rather than `shared/`, and the slice is named `features/administration/` since it holds both the system dashboard and the user screens.

author: peterknego
body:
Scratch-only: **docs + `proofs-veil/` models, 6 files, +901/−10.** No shipped-crate
changes. **`proofs/` untouched** — the trusted base and every "proved" claim are
unaffected, per the spike's standing guardrail that *Veil is never the record*.

Follows PR #4 (all must-pass bars discharged). Gate doc §3d/§3e; ledger sessions 5/5b.

## What this adds

**V2 was the only part of the spike hunting an *unknown* bug.** Everything before it
was backward-looking calibration — revert a known fix, confirm the checker finds the
known bug, restore it, confirm the CE disappears. Here every shipped fix is ON, so a
counterexample would have been a bug nobody knows about.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| **V2 forward hunt, n=3 / Fin 3** | **exhaustive, no violation — 11,697,699 states, 93m10s** |
| n=4 / Fin 3, constrained, depth 10 | attempt 1 **vacuous**; attempt 2 killed >60 min |

## The n=3 result (the substantive one)

`V2Hunt.lean` = `Finding9.lean` + `crashRestart` restored (the brief wants concurrent
`startElection`/`crashRestart`/gate-reopen/commit interleavings). 17 actions, 7
**proxy invariants** — aimed per the depth-probe calibration, since proxies sat at
depth 5–7 while end-to-end losses were beyond reach.

**No fifth coherence-window bug at this scale.** Per the brief's exit criteria this is
the acceptable non-discovery outcome, and it is stronger than the "credible bounded
coverage" it asks for: the search was **exhaustive**, not depth-limited.

Verified before being believed — **zero `error: Examples/...` lines** (an elaboration
error silently *voids* a `#model_check` into a vacuous pass; that bit twice in session 4)
and **no `maxDepth` anywhere**, so `✅ No violation` here is `exploredAllReachableStates`
rather than `reachedDepthBound`. The two render identically.

**Scope, stated plainly:** exhaustive *for this model*, not for UC. It inherits every
abstraction obligation recorded for `BootGate`/`Finding9` — nondeterministic grant guard,
collapsed tally, one tracked entry at one tracked position, concrete excluded-node
quorums, the narrowed `staleStreamAppend` guard — and says nothing about n≥4 or a fourth
term value. **Not a proof.**

`state_constraint` was deliberately **not** used here: constraints *prune* states, and
narrowing a hunt for the unknown is self-defeating. The unconstrained run completed, so
the lever was never needed at n=3.

## The n=4 result (a boundary, not a gap in diligence)

Asks what n=3 structurally cannot: does a **fourth node** enable a bug three cannot? At
n=4 the majority is 3-of-4, so two successive quorums can overlap in exactly **two**
nodes — no n=3 analogue — and #6b's full loss needed n=5 in Lean.

**Attempt 1 completed but was VACUOUS**, and the tell was the state count: 143,901 at
n=4 against 11.7M at n=3. *A larger configuration yielding 80× fewer states is a symptom,
not a result.* A vacuity canary confirmed no commit was reachable at all, so most of the
battery was trivially true.

The culprit was my own constraint. **C1 "at most one node awaiting reconciliation"**
sounded like an anomaly bound, but `deliverRequestVoteGrant` sets `awaitingReconcile` on
*every* node adopting a new term, and at n=4 a candidate needs three granters — so ≥2
awaiting is the **mainline election path**. C1 pruned normal elections. It is kept in the
file as a **retired** constraint with the explanation, which is a better warning than its
absence. Reported as "n=4 clean, 143,901 states", it would have read as coverage while
being the exact opposite.

**Why no cheaper retry exists.** A commit at n=4 needs ~10 steps minimum (two grants for
a 3-of-4 majority, two replicates, two reports) versus ~7 at n=3. So `maxDepth < 10` is
**vacuous by construction** and `maxDepth ≥ 10` is **intractable on this box**. The window
between them does not exist — sharper than "we ran out of time", because lowering the
bound cannot help when the bound is what makes the run mean anything.

## Capacity envelope, now closed in both directions

| Configuration | Outcome |
|---|---|
| n=3 / Fin 3, exhaustive, unconstrained | affordable — 11.7M states, ~93 min, ~7 GB |
| n=3 / Fin 4 | not viable — 12.1 GB RSS, killed (PR #4 §3c) |
| n=4 / Fin 3, constrained, maxDepth <10 | vacuous by construction |
| n=4 / Fin 3, constrained, maxDepth ≥10 | not viable — killed at >60 min |

**n=3 / Fin 3 is the frontier for this model class on a 15 GB box.** A larger box is
**not** required for V2 as scoped, but it is now the only way *past* the frontier —
relevant to the two still-blocked measurements: #6b's full-loss depth, and ReconfigLC's
`leader_completeness` counterexample hunt.

## Rule adopted

**Every constrained run must be paired with a vacuity canary, run first.** Constraints
can silently destroy the behaviour they were meant to make searchable, and a clean
verdict looks identical either way — the same class of trap as an elaboration error
voiding a `#model_check`. Both are greens that mean nothing.

## Three corrections to this PR's original description

**The `next` bump is gone from this diff, because main got it independently.** When PRs #473/#472 landed on the default branch they triggered a Dependabot rescan, which opened #477 (`next` 16.2.10 → 16.2.12) and the armed auto-merge landed it at 09:47:27Z. The four Next.js advisories this PR originally claimed are therefore already fixed on main, by a PR with a real `package.json` change. Nothing here duplicates that work.

**`brace-expansion` 1.1.16 does not fully fix the root instance.** The original description implied both brace-expansion advisories are cleared by both bumps. That is too generous. GitHub's advisory DB scopes GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg to `<= 5.0.7`, so it is the 5.0.7 → 5.0.8 bump that clears it; the 1.x line is cleared only of GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp. Worse, the advisory file shipped inside the 1.1.16 tarball itself states the unbounded-expansion logic is shared by the 1.x–4.x lines, and a diff of `index.js` between 1.1.14 and 1.1.16 shows the accumulation loop unchanged. **There is no fixed 1.x release**, so this is the best available position rather than a complete fix. Scope is dev tooling only (eslint/typescript-eslint), not shipped code.

**The original description miscounted the diff.** It said nine `@next/swc-*` platform binaries; `next` 16.2.12 ships eight. Moot now that the `next` bump is not in this diff, but recorded for accuracy.

npm also drops a stray duplicate `"lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu": "1.33.0"` key from the lockfile's root `packages[""].dependencies`, and prunes a redundant nested `vitest/node_modules/es-module-lexer`. Both are pre-existing lockfile inconsistencies that npm's own regeneration corrects — the package is declared only under `optionalDependencies` in `package.json`, where a correctly-ranged `^1.33.0` entry remains untouched. Left as npm generated them rather than hand-reverted.

body:
The `wrap` class (`[.columns.wrap]`) was usable but never documented on the Layout page — discoverable only by finding it in an unrelated example. Explains what it actually changes (every column in the row sizes itself to its own content and can wrap onto a new row, instead of the default equal-width/shrink-to-fit behavior) and why applying it to ordinary text columns usually produces the opposite of what someone reaching for it likely wants: equal-width columns already shrink their content to fit without wrapping, with no modifier needed. `wrap` is meant for content that shouldn't be shrunk, such as images.

Verified this is a pure documentation gap, not a code bug — rendered the reporter's exact repro and confirmed the default (no `wrap`) behavior already produces the equal-width, shrink-to-fit result they wanted.

Fixes #456

## Summary

Adds a production-ready Helm chart under `chart/` for deploying rootcoz on OpenShift and Kubernetes clusters, plus an interactive setup wizard (`scripts/setup.py`).

Closes #181

## Helm Chart Features

- **Routing**: OpenShift Routes, Kubernetes Ingress, or ClusterIP-only
- **AI Providers**: Gemini (API key), Claude (Anthropic API or Vertex AI), Cursor (API key + auth.json)
- **Security**: PodSecurity `restricted` compliant (seccomp, non-root, drop ALL caps)
- **Secrets**: Upgrade-safe via `lookup` fallback — existing secrets preserved when values omitted
- **PVC Snapshots**: Optional CronJob for automated VolumeSnapshot backup with retention
- **ImageStream**: OpenShift auto-deploy via scheduled import
- **Validation**: JSON Schema for values, mutual exclusion guards (Route vs Ingress)
- **Tests**: Helm lint + 8 template render scenarios via `tox -e chart`

## Setup Wizard (`scripts/setup.py`)

- Interactive prompts for all bootstrap settings
- Incremental value persistence — early values survive if later steps fail
- Split output: `values.generated.yaml` (non-secret) + `values.secrets.yaml` (mode 0600)
- `--dry-run` and `--skip-helm` modes
- Re-run friendly: loads prior values as defaults

## Code Quality Improvements (from review loop)

- **SSE log sanitization**: Added `\r` replacement alongside `\n` to prevent CR-based SSE framing attacks
- **Dead code removal**: Removed unused `_resolve_ai_config()` function
- **DRY extractions**:

author: alisonjenkins
body:
Follow-up to #104. Jellyfin has **no server-wide default** for track preferences — every account starts at the stock values and each person re-picks them by hand, so on a shared server everyone meets the same wrong-language playback before they find the settings page.

`[user_defaults]` supplies the four fields that matter, using Jellyfin's own names and values, so what's configured is exactly what jellyfin-web shows in Settings → Playback and any user can still change it afterwards.

Applied at **both** creation paths — the dashboard's `/Users/New` and `admin create-user` — because an account bootstrapped from the CLI starting on different preferences than one made in the UI is the sort of difference nobody notices until it confuses them.

## Deployed values

```toml
[user_defaults]
audio_language_preference = "OriginalLanguage"
subtitle_language_preference = "eng"
subtitle_mode = "Smart"
play_default_audio_track = false
```

`play_default_audio_track = false` is load-bearing: with it true (Jellyfin's default) a container's default-flagged track beats the language preference, which is precisely how Aliens kept playing its Ukrainian dub. `OriginalLanguage` + `Smart` gives Japanese-with-English-subs for anime and English for everything else from one setting — the only way to express that split, since Jellyfin has no per-library override.

Chart `0.1.11` → `0.1.12`: Flux reconciles on `ChartVersion`, so values/template edits without a bump don't deploy.

## Behaviour

- A **stock** section writes no configuration row at all — an operator who configured nothing leaves no trace on new accounts, which is what every account had before this existed.
- Seeding is best-effort: the account already exists by then, and failing user creation over a preferences row would be the wrong trade.
- **Existing users are untouched by design.** Changing an account someone already configured isn't a default, it's an override — the seven current accounts are being updated separately and deliberately.

## Testing

`just test` 1716 passed · clippy clean · `helm template` output verified to render the section, and a config test parses exactly what the chart emits.

author: jbergler
body:
## Summary
- `#827`: "Clock latched" read no forever on every WHOOP 5/MG strap — `GET_CLOCK`'s reply is sent on connect (#78) but was never decoded for that family, and the documented `GET_DATA_RANGE` fallback (#261) is also dead since `GET_DATA_RANGE` is never sent to a 5/MG strap.
- Adds a `GET_CLOCK` debug probe (mirrors #592/#690) to capture the raw reply from real hardware, then decodes it in `decodeWhoop5CommandResponse` using the same payload-relative offset as WHOOP4 (the "+4 rule"). Confirmed against two real WHOOP 5.0 captures 62s apart whose decoded clocks advanced by exactly that gap — locked in as a regression test.
- `FrameRouter` now publishes the decoded value on `LiveState.strapClockUnix`, which the Devices/Test Centre "Clock latched" readout falls back to when the WHOOP4-only log-scraped signal is absent.
- Cleanup: `configureCollectorFamily()` previously forced an **identity** clockRef (`device==wall`) for every 5/MG connection instead of ever using a real `GET_CLOCK` correlation — so a genuinely drifted 5/MG RTC was invisible, and the drift-triggered `SET_CLOCK` re-issue (`ClockPolicy.shouldSetClock`) only ever ran on the WHOOP4 branch. Both families now share one `applyClockCorrelation(from:)` path. Since both now write into the same `clockRef`, added a disconnect-time reset so a stale correlation from one family can't leak across a same-session strap-family switch.
- Ports the same `GET_CLOCK` decode fix + debug probe to Android (`Framing.kt`, `WhoopBleClient.kt`, `DevicesScreen.kt`), per the parity contract. **Not ported**: the `clockRef` correlation cleanup — Android has no `GET_CLOCK`-based `clockRef` for *either* family (it always derives a rough correlation from `GET_DATA_RANGE`'s newest banked record, see `beginBackfill`'s `#700` comment), so there's no WHOOP4 pattern for WHOOP5 to diverge from there; building that from scratch would be new work, not a port of this cleanup.

## Verification
- `swift build` / `swift test` pass (WhoopProtocol package).
- Full macOS `xcodebuild -scheme Strand build` succeeds; `SetClockPayloadTests`, `ConnectionTestModeEmissionTests`, `BackfillContinuationTests`, `AlarmReadbackDecodeTests` all pass.
- Android: `./gradlew compileFullDebugKotlin` succeeds. Could not run `./gradlew testFullDebugUnitTest` in the dev sandbox (missing macOS `aapt2` entry in `verification-metadata.xml`, pre-existing/environment-only, unrelated to this change) — please run on a machine where that works before merge.
- **Real hardware, confirmed on both a probe capture and a live connect:**
  - Two `#827` probe captures 62s apart: decoded clocks `1785050961` → `1785051023`, advancing by exactly 62s.
  - A live connect on 2026-07-26 (post-cleanup build) logged `Clock correlated: device=1785052722 wall=1785052723` — cross-checked against the raw captured frame by hand, exact match. The subsequent historical offload logged `rows landed on 2026-07-26 · clock ref in sync`, confirming the real correlation (not the old forced identity) drives correct date placement.
  - Confirmed the drift-triggered `SET_CLOCK` re-issue correctly did **not** fire at 1s of drift (under the 2s `ClockPolicy` threshold).
  - A strap restart mid-session triggered a clean reconnect + fresh re-correlation, with no stale leftover value — validating the new disconnect-time `clockRef` reset.

## Test plan
- [x] Swift package tests
- [x] macOS app build + targeted `StrandTests`
- [x] Android Kotlin compile
- [x] Real WHOOP 5.0 hardware: probe captures, live connect, strap restart
- [ ] Android unit tests (please run on a machine without the sandbox's aapt2 verification gap)

Fixes #827

author: emrahbaysal
body:
## Live evidence

hw289 (dep `44ac86240f0afab7`), a fresh 2-region Huawei prov, was stamped `status=partial-failure` with a self-contradicting error while **both regions were genuinely up and converging** (region-A 16/65 HRs, region-B 35/65 and climbing):

```
partial-region materialisation: declared 2 regions [me-east-215 me-east-215-b-1],
only 2 materialised [me-east me-east-215-b] (missing: [me-east-215 me-east-215-b-1])
```

"only **2** materialised" out of 2 — but both reported missing, because the codes were truncated.

## Root cause

`normalisePerRegionKeys` (provisioner.go) stripped a trailing `-<digits>` segment from every per-region key for every provider — a rule written for Hetzner's `<cloudRegion>-<index>` shape. Huawei region codes end in digits themselves, so `me-east-215`→`me-east` and `me-east-215-b-1`→`me-east-215-b`. `detectPartialRegionMaterialisation` found neither declared code → typed error → handler stamps `partial-failure` and **skips `commitPDMWithRetry` + `runPhase1Watch`**, so DNS never commits and the prov can never reach `ready`.

The function's own upstream comment already said Huawei is "keyed by cloudRegion **verbatim**" — the strip should never have applied to it.

## Fix

Declared-set-aware normalisation:
1. key exactly matches a declared `cloudRegion` → final, verbatim;
2. else `<declaredCode>-<digits>` → strip (Hetzner secondaries);
3. else raw.

Strict superset of prior Hetzner behaviour; provider-agnostic.

## Verification

- New `TestNormalisePerRegionKeys_HuaweiDigitTailedCodes_5381` reproduces the live failure **exactly** without the fix (`missing = [me-east-215 me-east-215-b-1]`) and passes with it.
- Companion `TestNormalisePerRegionKeys_HetznerIndexStripStillFires_5381` pins that the index-strip + literal `primary` remap still work.
- Full `internal/provisioner` suite green; `go build ./...` + `go vet` clean.

Existing Test 10 (Huawei pass-through) missed this because its codes end in **letters** (`me-east-215-a/-b`) — the digit tail was the untested edge.

Refs #5381 #2840

body:
##  📌 작업 내용 요약

- **PR 검증용 CI 워크플로 신설 (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)**
  - `pull_request` → `develop`, `main` 트리거로 `./gradlew test` 실행
  - JDK 25 / temurin / gradle 캐시 설정은 기존 `deploy.yml`과 동일하게 구성
- **Redis service 컨테이너 구성**
  - 토큰 블랙리스트 경로를 CI에서 실제로 태우기 위해 `redis:alpine` 기동
  - 이미지 태그는 `docker-compose.yml`과 동일하게 정렬
- **테스트 리포트 아티팩트 업로드 추가**
  - `if: always()`로 실패 시에도 `build/reports/tests/test/` 확보, 보관 7일
- **기존 `deploy.yml` 미변경**
  - 배포 경로에 영향을 주지 않도록 이번 PR에서는 손대지 않음
  - `src/` 코드 변경이 없어 런타임 동작 변화 없음

---

## 💬 참고 사항

- **도입 배경**
  - 기존 유일한 워크플로 `deploy.yml`은 `push: [main]`에서만 트리거되고 빌드 스텝이 `./gradlew build -x test`라 테스트를 전혀 실행하지 않음
  - 배포 job도 `needs: build-and-push-image`만 의존해 테스트 통과 여부와 무관하게 배포됨
  - 즉 회귀를 자동으로 잡아주는 장치가안전망 확보가 목적
- **회귀 기준선**                                                                           - 로컬 `./gradlew test` → `BUILD SUC개 테스트 / 실패 0 / 오류 0 / 스킵 0
  - 앞으로 진행할 리팩토링에서 이 수치가 줄어들면 회귀로 판단                             - **Redis 컨테이너를 넣은 이유**
  - Redis가 없어도 58개 테스트는 전부 통과함 (`JwtHandshakeInterceptor.isBlacklisted()`가 `RedisConnectionFailureException`을 ca
  - 다만 그 경우 토큰 블랙리스트 경로가 CI에서 한 번도 검증되지 않으므로 실제 경로를 태우기 위해 유지
- **이 PR에서 최초 검증되는 항목**
  - 워크플로 동작은 로컬에서 확인 불가하므로, Redis service 기동과 테스트 실행 여부를 이 PR의 Actions
탭에서 확인 필요
- **이번 범위에서 제외한 항목**

body:
Closes `overseer-bg2.6`.

The block justifying `source_trees = []` in `pyproject.toml` argued that *"livespec core itself currently has all four of these keys empty for the same reason"*, and that matching core kept the move behavior-preserving.

**That argument has expired.** Verified on livespec `origin/master`:

| Key | livespec core today |
|---|---|
| `source_trees` | `[".claude-plugin/scripts/livespec"]` |
| `io_trees` | `[".claude-plugin/scripts/livespec/io"]` |
| `commands_trees` | `[".claude-plugin/scripts/livespec/commands"]` |
| `covered_trees` | three entries |
| `supervisor_entry_files` | non-empty |
| `pure_trees` | `[]` — the only one still empty, gated on `livespec-mutreal.1` |

Three of the four keys the comment cited have flipped. Core is no longer where this repo is, so **"match core" now argues for arming rather than staying empty** — the comment had inverted into an argument against itself.

## What was kept

The still-true, still-load-bearing reason: declaring the tree activates the three Result-railway checks (`no-raise-outside-io`, `no-except-outside-io`, `public-api-result-typed`) over this package, and that blast radius must be **measured** before the keys flip. Gate E of `plan/overseer-productization` exists precisely because enforcement landing before adoption is the hazard.

Made concrete rather than left vague: arming is `overseer-bg2.4`, which depends on the LLOC split (`overseer-bg2.3`) **and** on the loop-iteration catch deletion (`overseer-bg2.2`), because arming before either reds master.

## Why the old reason is retained as labelled history

Deleted reasoning gets rediscovered and re-acted-upon. The expired parity argument stays in place under an explicit `HISTORY — do NOT reuse this reason` heading, so the next reader learns it was considered and why it no longer holds, instead of re-deriving it.

`just check`: **all 61 targets passed**. Comment-only change to a non-`.py` config file, so the Red-Green-Replay ritual does not apply and a `docs(...)` subject is used.

author: samcom593-creator
body:
Sam: *"the whole site should look better… this looks the same, moves the same,"* then *"I live in all the screens."*

## Why it read as unpolished
Not because any one page was ugly — because there was **no single system**. Counted across `src/pages` before this wave:

- **GlassCard 250** uses vs **shadcn Card 231** vs **~28 raw token divs** — three competing container conventions
- three different section-header structures
- competing type scales
- severity colours applied inconsistently (the same amber meaning "warning" on one page and "highlight" on another)

## What wave 1 does
Converges the six **primary-nav** pages onto one contract **derived from the app's own strongest pages, not invented**: one page wrapper, one section container, one header block (muted `h-4 w-4` icon + `text-sm font-semibold` title + `text-xs` muted description), one type scale, one spacing rhythm, one severity vocabulary (emerald good / amber watch / rose bad), `tabular-nums` + `toLocaleString` on every figure, truncation over overflow on mobile.

| page | why it's in wave 1 |
|---|---|
| `Dashboard.tsx` | Command Center — first screen opened |
| `DashboardApplicants.tsx` | Applications — *"should always be the highest"* |
| `CallCenter.tsx` | heavy mobile use |
| `DashboardCRM.tsx` | **/dashboard/crm binds this, not ClientPipeline** — I named the wrong file; the agent caught it from App.tsx and corrected |
| `CarrierContracts.tsx` | was a bare link grid |
| `Leaderboard.tsx` | the board shown to people |

## Presentation only
Verified across all six diffs: **no `.from()`, no `useQuery`, no `.rpc()`, no `.eq()/.select()`, no `isAdmin` gate, no rendered value changed.** The single hit in the logic grep is an indentation shift on an otherwise identical `isAdmin && managers.length > 0` line.

Also migrated **8 focus rings** the restyle introduced from the banned multi-utility halo (`focus-visible:ring-2` + `ring-ring` + `ring-offset-2`) to the canonical single token `focus-visible:shadow-[var(--apex-focus-ring)]`. `check:focus-ring-areas` caught them; `src/pages` is back to **0**.

Density over airiness, deliberately — this is an operations tool, so compact scannable rows beat decorative padding.

Verified: tsc **234/236** (improved by 2) · focus-ring 0/0 · hex-in-jsx 0 · stale-key 1/1 · relative-time 45/45 · empty-catch src@0 backend@56 · console-in-prod 0 · production build passes.
