## Objetivo

Aplicar hardening de segurança e pequenas otimizações sem alterar dados operacionais nem interromper os fluxos em uso.

## Alterações de código

- Corrige `/api/user/notification-preferences` para consultar apenas colunas existentes e combinar o schema legado com o atual sem uma tentativa SQL inválida.
- Corrige `/api/memberships/user-label` para usar `memberships.role` e `profiles.full_name`, eliminando consultas a colunas inexistentes.

## Alterações de banco versionadas

- Corrige grants necessários para módulos em produção, mantendo RLS como fronteira de autorização.
- Restringe tabelas internas e preferências de notificação.
- Remove listagem anônima de objetos do bucket de avatares sem alterar URLs públicas existentes.
- Move implementações privilegiadas de `accept_order` e `separate_label_for_order` para o schema `private`.
- Mantém as assinaturas públicas atuais como wrappers `SECURITY INVOKER`, evitando alteração no frontend.
- Substitui policies fiscais legadas por RLS derivada do pedido e do estabelecimento.
- Consolida policies duplicadas de notificações, preservando compatibilidade com `user_id` e `userId`.
- Otimiza RLS de preferências de notificação.
- Restringe `tenant_invitations` a leitura/gravação da empresa ativa por admin/operação.
- Remove leitura global de `profiles` e permite somente o próprio perfil ou perfis de empresas compartilhadas.
- Restringe tabelas de assinatura a leitura autenticada; gravações permanecem pelo servidor.
- Remove policies de leitura cruzada em `products`, dados/vínculos fiscais e histórico de fichas técnicas.
- Remove policies globais do catálogo de fornecedores e mantém apenas acesso por `establishment_id`.
- Retira privilégios anônimos/administrativos desnecessários da tabela `suppliers`.
- Versiona contratos mínimos/idempotentes que faltavam no histórico de migrations para previews limpos: perfis, memberships, pedidos, estoque, notificações, fiscal e histórico de fichas técnicas.

## Segurança operacional

- Nenhuma tabela operacional teve dados alterados ou removidos.
- Os 41 fornecedores existentes permaneceram intactos e já estavam vinculados à Santino.
- Todas as migrations foram executadas em transação.

- Supabase Security Advisor: resta somente habilitar manualmente `Leaked Password Protection` no Auth.
- As rotas atuais de importação, produtos, perdas, imagens e etiquetas foram revisadas e já validam empresa ativa/tenant.

- [x] Migrations aplicadas com sucesso no Supabase.
- [x] Advisories de funções `SECURITY DEFINER` públicas eliminados.
- [x] Policies globais de leitura multiempresa identificadas foram removidas.

- [ ] Habilitar `Leaked Password Protection` no painel do Supabase.

## Próxima etapa separada

O Performance Advisor ainda lista policies duplicadas e índices antigos em vários módulos. Não foram removidos em massa neste PR porque exigem testes de regressão por módulo para evitar impacto em pedidos, estoque e fiscal.

body:
## Summary

- Adds a `stremio/` package implementing the Stremio addon protocol in Go
- Adds `cmd/stremio/` entry point with a sample addon (catalog + streams)
- Zero new dependencies — uses only the standard library

## What's included

### `stremio/types.go`
All Stremio protocol types: `Manifest`, `Catalog`, `ExtraParam`, `MetaPreview`, `Meta`, `Video`, `Stream`, and the three response wrappers (`CatalogResponse`, `MetaResponse`, `StreamResponse`).

### `stremio/addon.go`
- `Handler` interface — implement this to supply your own content
- `Addon` struct — wraps a `Handler` and registers all routes
- Handles `/manifest.json`, `/catalog/{type}/{id}.json`, `/meta/{type}/{id}.json`, `/stream/{type}/{id}.json`
- CORS headers on every response (required for Stremio web/desktop)
- Extra parameters parsed from both the URL path segment and query string

### `cmd/stremio/main.go`
Sample `sampleAddon` implementation with two hard-coded movies (Big Buck Bunny, Elephants Dream) and direct MP4 stream URLs — works out of the box for testing.

## Running

```bash
go run ./cmd/stremio          # starts on :7000
go run ./cmd/stremio -addr :8080  # custom port
```

Then install in Stremio via `http://localhost:7000/manifest.json`.

## Extending

Implement the `stremio.Handler` interface in your own struct and pass it to `stremio.New(yourHandler)`:

```go
type Handler interface {
    GetManifest() stremio.Manifest
    GetCatalog(catalogType, catalogID string, extra map[string]string) ([]stremio.MetaPreview, error)
    GetMeta(metaType, id string) (*stremio.Meta, error)
    GetStreams(streamType, id string) ([]stremio.Stream, error)
}
```

author: eilandert
body:
Closes the runtime-regression follow-up the 2026-07-26 docs audit asked for in #110.

## Why

PHP front controllers run `try_files $uri /index.php`. nginx **replaces `r->uri`** on that internal redirect, so:

- **DOC-A1 (BLOCKER)** — the module default key `$host$uri$cache_turbo_normalized_args` collapses every clean URL onto `/index.php`. Unrelated pages share one cache entry.
- **DOC-A2 (MAJOR)** — preset URI rules and `cache_turbo_bypass_uri` both compare `r->uri`, so a route-only guard for a private path stops matching.

#110 fixed the published examples. This adds the regression that keeps them honest.

## What

Two locations model both halves:

| location | key | veto | proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/ctir/` | default `$uri` | — | DOC-A1: 2nd clean URL HITs the 1st entry and is served its body |
| `/ctir-fixed/` | `$host$request_uri` | `map $request_uri` → `cache_turbo_bypass` + `cache_turbo_no_store` | routes stay distinct; private route BYPASSes and is never stored |

`cache_turbo_bypass_uri` is deliberately **not** the fix — it reads the same rewritten `r->uri` (`ngx_http_cache_turbo_bypass_uri_match`, `module.c:4059`), so it cannot see the original route. The `map $request_uri` pattern is what `docs/xenforo.md` now prescribes.

The `/ctir/` half pins the defect on purpose. If the module default ever becomes original-path-based, its first assertion flips to MISS — that is intended, and the docstring says so.

## Negative controls

Both halves fail by their own discriminating assertion when the bug is restored:

- fixed key reverted to `$uri` → `got HIT` (routes collapsed)
- veto swapped to `bypass_uri` → `got MISS` (**private route gets cached**)

Status alone would not have been enough — the origin emits a unique `gen-<n>` body per hit, so body identity across two routes is what actually proves a shared entry. Both are asserted.

## Build change

Drops `--without-http_rewrite_module` from `ci-build.sh`. `try_files` and `map` are unavailable without it, so a front controller cannot be expressed at all — and that is the shape every affected deployment actually runs. The flag carried no comment or documented rationale. nginx now links `-lpcre2-8`.

## Validation

Werror build clean · unit 92/92 · full runtime suite green with `--redis-server` + `--memcached-server` · both negative controls verified failing.

author: kryota-dev
body:
## Summary

Adds a scheduled, **read-only** GitHub Actions workflow that runs
`anthropics/claude-code-action` to triage open Renovate PRs weekly and surface the
results where they are already looked at: the Renovate Dependency Dashboard (#12) plus a
per-PR comment on each analyzed PR.

Today `renovate-sweep` (`home/dot_agents/skills/renovate-sweep/SKILL.md`) is manual-only,
so Renovate PRs pile up. This automation does the collect → classify → analyze part on a
cadence; the merge decision stays local and human-approved via the skill.

Closes #362.

## What changed

- **`.github/workflows/renovate-triage.yml`** (new)
  - `on: schedule` `0 0 * * 1` (Mon 00:00 UTC = **Mon 09:00 JST**) + `workflow_dispatch`.
  - Runs `anthropics/claude-code-action@…be7b93b # v1` in automation mode (a `prompt`
    input, no `@claude` mention).
  - The inlined prompt collects Renovate PRs with `gh`, classifies each A/B/C by
    semver / CI state / mergeable / advisory (mirroring the `renovate-sweep` skill
    Phase 1–3), analyzes the risky ones, then posts a summary table to #12 and a per-PR
    comment on each analyzed PR.
- **`docs/contributing/ci-and-tests.{md,ja.md}`** — document the new workflow next to the
  existing CI inventory.

## Read-only guarantee (defense-in-depth)

1. **Least-privilege permissions**: `permissions: {}` at top level; the job grants only
   `contents: read` + `issues: write` + `pull-requests: write`. No `contents: write`, no
   `id-token: write`.
2. **Tool allowlist**: `claude_args: --allowedTools "…"` contains only read + comment `gh`
   subcommands (`gh pr list/view/diff/checks`, `gh search prs`, `gh issue comment`,
   `gh pr comment`) plus `Read`. `gh pr merge/close/review/edit`, `gh api`, `Write`,
   `Edit`, and `WebFetch` are absent, so "never merges" is structural, not just prompted.
3. The prompt treats all PR titles/bodies as untrusted **data**, never as instructions.

## Design notes (primary-source verified)

`claude-code-action`'s automation mode, input names (`claude_code_oauth_token`, `prompt`,
`claude_args`), and default tool gating were verified against the action's `action.yml`,
`docs/`, and `examples/`. Skill auto-discovery is **not** documented and our skills live at
a chezmoi-source path absent from the CI checkout, so the triage instructions are
**inlined** in the prompt rather than relying on discovery. No `--model` is pinned (the
action default is used) to avoid a stale model-ID knob.

## Prerequisite (manual, before first run)

- Set the **`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`** repository secret (generate with
  `claude setup-token`). Without it the action fails fast at auth. The workflow references
  the secret but cannot create it.

## Test plan

- [x] `actionlint` + `ghalint` pass on the new workflow.
- [x] `make lint` and `make test` (230 bats tests) pass.
- [x] `docs_facts.bats` passes (relative links resolve; EN/JA mirror intact).
- [ ] **Post-merge, human**: set the secret, then run `workflow_dispatch` once to confirm
  auth + comment posting to #12 and the analyzed PRs (needs the secret and write to real
  issues/PRs, so it cannot run pre-merge).

## Notes

- Model-fitness: this branch was implemented on Opus 4.8 after a `continue-anyway` at the
  standard-tier floor (Opus 5 @ high). Areas most sensitive to that gap are the design
  judgment (tool allowlist completeness, auth wiring) and the triage prompt's
  classification rules — worth a close review.

Summary

Implemented a per-wallet in-flight lock for the subscription endpoint to prevent concurrent requests for the same wallet from bypassing idempotency checks. This ensures only one subscription is processed at a time per wallet while allowing concurrent requests to receive the same result.

Changes Made
Added an in-memory Map to track in-flight subscription requests by wallet address
Implemented per-wallet request deduplication:
Reuse the existing in-flight promise when a concurrent request for the same wallet arrives
Return the same result to all concurrent callers
Created a new in-flight promise when no active request exists for the wallet
Ensured locks are removed after request completion
Added timeout handling using REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS to prevent stale locks
Guaranteed lock cleanup on both successful and failed subscription processing
Preserved existing database-backed idempotency behavior for multi-instance deployments
Concurrency Behavior
First request for a wallet acquires the in-flight lock and processes the subscription
Subsequent concurrent requests for the same wallet await the existing promise
All concurrent callers receive the same response
The lock is always released after completion or timeout
Cross-instance deduplication continues to rely on the existing database idempotency key
Acceptance Criteria Covered
 Two simultaneous subscription requests for the same wallet result in exactly one database row
 Concurrent requests receive the same response
 Lock is released after success or failure
 Tests in tests/routes/subscribeIdempotency.test.ts pass
 Existing idempotency key tests continue to pass
Testing
Added concurrency tests for simultaneous requests to the same wallet
Verified only one subscription transaction is executed
Confirmed concurrent requests return identical responses
Verified lock cleanup after successful completion
Verified lock cleanup after exceptions and timeout scenarios
Ran the complete test suite to ensure no regressions in subscription or idempotency behavior

Closes #837

Three difficulty levels selected after New Game: **Apprentice / Wizard / Archmage**.

| Knob | 🟢 Apprentice | 🟡 Wizard (baseline) | 🔴 Archmage |

author: llsilvas
body:
Fatia 2 de 3 da revisão semanal (F1 `add-weekly-review-consolidation` já em `develop`). A revisão da semana anterior ganha uma narrativa de foco (`nextWeekFocus`), passa a alimentar o prompt do próximo plano e registra o desfecho da decisão do coach.

Spec: `menthoros-product/openspec/changes/add-weekly-review-llm-focus/`

## Escopo entregue

- **Schema (V72):** `next_week_focus` + `focus_source` em `tb_revisao_semanal`; `consumed_review_id` + `consumed_review_outcome` em `tb_plano_semanal`; renames `dados_suficientes`→`sufficient_data` e `percentual_realizacao`→`completion_rate`.
- **Narrativa:** template determinístico derivado do `recommendationType` (nasce com `focusSource = TEMPLATE`), com upgrade opcional por LLM em executor dedicado (`@Async("weeklyFocusExecutor")` + `@Retryable` isolado no `WeeklyFocusModelClient`). Narrativa truncada em 280 chars antes de persistir.
- **Guarda de consistência:** `WeeklyFocusConsistencyChecker` reprova narrativa que sugere progressão sob RECOVERY/MAINTAIN e mantém o template.
- **Injeção no prompt:** `WeeklyReviewPromptFormatter`/`Provider` com janela de validade de 7 dias (D11), atrás de flag.
- **Loop de aprendizado:** `ConsumedReviewOutcomeResolver` grava o desfecho na aprovação/rejeição do plano; auto-approve registra `NO_COACH_IN_LOOP`, nunca `NO_ADJUSTMENT`.
- **Front:** renomeação do contrato (`sufficientData`, `completionRate`) no tipo, adapter, VM, card e testes.

## Flags — nasce desligado

- `menthoros.weekly-review.llm.enabled` = **false** (gate de custo A1 ainda aberto). Desligada, o comportamento é 100% determinístico e não há chamada ao LLM.
- `menthoros.weekly-review.injection.enabled` controla a entrada da revisão no prompt.

## Critérios de aceite

- **CA4** geração consome a revisão dentro da janela e ignora fora dela.
- **CA5** coach-in-the-loop: a revisão é contexto, não altera plano automaticamente nem é exposta ao atleta (asserções estruturais).
- **CA8** `consumedReviewOutcome` nos 5 desfechos, com desfechos independentes em consumo duplo.
- **CA-LLM** flag off ⇒ template sem LLM; falha do modelo ou reprovação do checker preserva o template.
- **CA-Fonte** `focusSource` grava a origem correta nos dois regimes.

## Validação

- Backend: `./mvnw clean test` — **2191 testes, 0 falhas**. Restam 6 erros de contexto Spring por checksum da migration V71 no Postgres local, **pré-existentes** e reproduzidos em árvore limpa (não ocorrem em base nova, como no CI).
- Front: `npm run lint && npm run build && npm run test:run` — **748/748**, lint limpo.
- Golden-master do prompt byte-idêntico nos 5 arquétipos.

## QA gate

Dois ciclos. O primeiro produziu as correções 6.1–6.4 (tenant no caminho `@Async`, `@Retryable` que o `try/catch` matava, evento publicado antes do save com `planoId` nulo, truncamento da saída do LLM). O segundo cobriu a 6.5 e adicionou:

- Resolução única da revisão consumida — era resolvida 2× por geração em leituras não-atômicas, então o LLM podia ver uma revisão e o plano gravar outra.
- `semanaInicio` unificada — o prompt era montado para uma semana e o plano salvo em outra quando o atleta já tinha plano futuro (**achado do `/codex:review`**, não visto pelos reviewers Claude).

Minors aceitos e registrados na task 6.6 da spec.

## Limitação conhecida

Sem timeout de resposta na chamada ao LLM — nenhum cliente LLM do módulo tem, e configurá-lo exige mexer no `MultiModelConfig`, afetando geração de plano e análise de treino. Fica para `add-external-call-resilience`. Mitigação: pool dedicado (core 1 / max 2), então uma chamada pendurada nunca consome a thread do coach.

## Merge coordenado

Depende do PR do front (renomeação do contrato). Mergear **backend primeiro, front em seguida** — a janela curta de campo `undefined` no card é aceita (task 4.2).

author: hazarustun-spec
body:
## Why

The configured model is dead for new API keys:

```
404 "This model models/gemini-2.5-flash is no longer available to new users."
```

Same for `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`. Every AI feature would have failed on first request in production. Fixing that surfaced two further problems — cost and latency — both addressed here.

## 1. Model is dead -> `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`

Gemini 3.x "flash" models **cannot be told to stop thinking**. Every documented switch was tried against the live API:

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| `thinkingConfig: { thinkingBudget: 0 }` | `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` |
| `generationConfig.thinkingLevel` (v1beta) | `400 ... Cannot find field` |
| `generationConfig.thinking_level` (v1alpha) | `400 ... Cannot find field` |
| `thinkingConfig: { includeThoughts: false }` | `200`, still spent 339 thinking tokens — hides, does not skip |

Thinking tokens bill as **output**. The lite models sidestep this entirely: they do not think at all.

Measured on the same daily-insight prompt (3291 input tokens), at published paid-tier rates:

| model | thinking | answer | time | cost/insight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gemini-3.6-flash` | 2737 | 1693 | 23.0s | $0.0382 |
| `gemini-3-flash-preview` | 1531 | 1812 | 20.5s | $0.0071 |
| **`gemini-3.1-flash-lite`** | **0** | 1901 | 10.0s | **$0.0037** |
| `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | 0 | 1948 | 9.1s | $0.0059 |

At 1000 daily insights that is **~$110/month instead of ~$1145/month**. It also lands *below* the `gemini-2.5-flash` setup this migration originally targeted ($0.0048).

No quality regression. Side by side on identical input, the lite model grounded its text in the actual chart — naming the Moon's transit through Cancer and Mars in its own house — where `gemini-3.6-flash` produced more generic prose.

## 2. Personality analysis was unusably slow

Asking for twelve planets at ten sentences each in one request ran anywhere from 18.7s to **over six minutes**. It blocks a user upgrading to premium, so the variance is the real defect.

Now split into four concurrent requests — three groups of four planets, plus summary/strengths/hiddenTraits — merged back into the identical object shape. Wall time is the slowest chunk, not the sum, and a chunk that fails to parse retries only its own quarter.

**Measured: 6.8s, 7.5s, 7.8s, and 14.0s on a run where one chunk retried.**

Per-chunk timeout is 90s, replacing a 300s whole-request timeout.

## 3. Truncation was silent

`safeJsonParse` repairs truncated JSON, so `finishReason: MAX_TOKENS` degraded an insight into half a sentence rather than raising. Now warned. `THINKING_HEADROOM` (default 3) is inert while thinking is zero but protects the budget if `GEMINI_MODEL` is ever pointed back at a flash model.

## Verification

Against the live API, not mocks:

- `generateDailyInsight` — **8.3s**, all seven sections populated, valid JSON
- `generatePersonalityAnalysis` — all 12 planet keys present, **zero** interpretations under 8 sentences, strengths and hiddenTraits populated
- `node test/basic.test.js` — **39/39**
- `node --check` clean across `src/` and `test/`

## Notes

`PERSONALITY_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is renamed `PERSONALITY_RULES` — it now holds only shared rules, with each chunk appending the output format it needs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: aceguru-mjh
body:
## Phase 3.2 + Phase 4 + PR10/PR11 consolidation

Three things in one PR:
1. **Consolidates PR10 + PR11** into main (they showed `merged:true` on GitHub but their content never reached main due to the stacked-branch issue — same problem we hit with P6/P7 earlier). Cherry-picked here.
2. **Phase 3.2** — Native Sandbox Enforcement (real Linux isolation, not stubs).
3. **Phase 4** — AstraDaemon Runtime Upgrade (daemon becomes a long-running service with heartbeat).

---

## Phase 3.2 — Native Sandbox Enforcement

`SandboxManager.create()` is no longer a stub. It chains four real Linux isolation primitives:

```
NamespaceManager → unshare(CLONE_NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWNET)
MountIsolation   → mount / MS_REC|MS_PRIVATE
SeccompManager   → libseccomp allowlist (read/write/exit)
LandlockManager  → PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS + Landlock ABI v1
```

**New files (daemon/sandbox/):**
- `sandbox_policy.hpp` — per-module policy struct (which isolation primitives to apply)
- `sandbox_state.hpp` — CREATED/ISOLATED/RUNNING/FAILED
- `namespace_manager.hpp/.cpp` — `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWNET)`, flag-gated
- `mount_isolation.hpp/.cpp` — `mount / MS_REC|MS_PRIVATE`
- `seccomp_manager.hpp/.cpp` — libseccomp allowlist (ASTRA_HAVE_LIBSECCOMP guard; gracefully degrades if libseccomp not linked)
- `landlock_manager.hpp/.cpp` — Landlock v1 + NO_NEW_PRIVS (path binding in Phase 3.3)

**Modified:** `sandbox_manager.cpp` — `create()` now chains all 4 layers.

## Phase 4 — AstraDaemon Runtime Upgrade

The daemon becomes a long-running service with liveness probing.

**New files:**
- `daemon/runtime/daemon_service.hpp/.cpp` — `start()/stop()/isRunning()` lifecycle primitive
- `daemon/ipc/message_router.hpp/.cpp` — single switch for request dispatch by type byte
- `daemon/ipc/protobuf_handler.hpp/.cpp` — decodes frame → MessageRouter
- `daemon/execution/execution_handler.hpp/.cpp` — post-decode entry point
- `core/ipc/DaemonState.kt` — OFFLINE/CONNECTING/ONLINE/FAILED
- `core/ipc/AstraDaemonClient.kt` — interface + DefaultAstraDaemonClient backed by DaemonClient; `StateFlow<DaemonState>` for UI; `connect()/execute(cap)/heartbeat()`

**Proto:** +`HeartbeatRequest { timestamp }`, +`HeartbeatResponse { alive, version }`, +`SandboxStatus { module_id, state, isolated }`

---

## Files: 23

**New (21):** SandboxPolicy, SandboxState, NamespaceManager, MountIsolation, SeccompManager, LandlockManager, DaemonService, MessageRouter, ProtobufHandler, ExecutionHandler, DaemonState.kt, AstraDaemonClient.kt
**Modified (2):** sandbox_manager.cpp (chains 4 layers), CMakeLists.txt (+8 sources), proto/astra.proto (+3 messages)

---

## What this enables

- **Real isolation:** modules run inside unshare + seccomp + landlock, not just an architecture interface
- **Long-running daemon:** DaemonService lifecycle + heartbeat so the UI can detect a dead daemon
- **App↔daemon closed loop:** AstraDaemonClient.connect → execute(capability) → result, with StateFlow for the dashboard

---

## Next: Phase 5 — MVP Integration & Release

Real-device testing, Magisk/KernelSU/APatch compat verification, crash fixes, CI, Release APK, first `.avm` sample module. AstraVeil goes from "engineering project" to "installable product".

author: neerajvipparla
body:
## Problem

`agentbridge sync` already detected divergence (both sides changed since the last fork/sync) via `timestamp` (auto-merge) and `abort` (refuse, report counts). Two things about `timestamp` didn't match what was actually wanted:

1. **Ordering** - it sorted merged turns by real wall-clock time, interleaving both sides. Wanted: each side's own new turns first, then the other side's, appended - grouped by origin, not interleaved.
2. **No way to pick a winner** - no way to say "keep only this side's continuation, drop the other's" when you don't want both divergent branches kept.

## Approach

Full design history is in this PR: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-sync-divergence-strategies-design.md` (approved via `superpowers:brainstorming`, section by section) and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-sync-divergence-strategies.md` (executed via `superpowers:subagent-driven-development` - a fresh implementer subagent per task, a spec+quality review after each, then a final whole-branch review).

**`--strategy` grows to four values**, each a small dispatched function in `src/sync/sync.js`:
- `timestamp` (default, **redefined**) - each side's own new turns first, then the other side's, appended - not interleaved.
- `abort` (unchanged) - refuses when both sides have new turns.
- `persist-claude` / `persist-opencode` (**new**) - keep only one side's divergent turns; the other side's are discarded entirely. `sync`-only, not available on `watch` (confirmed by `watch`'s pre-existing validation, plus a new test).

Four tasks, each with its own commit and passing task-scoped review:
1. Extract `mergeSync` into a strategy dispatcher - pure refactor, zero behavior change, verified by the existing suite passing unmodified.
2. Redefine `timestamp`'s ordering - delete the sort step (the pre-sort construction already produced the grouped-by-origin order); rewrote `T5` with a fixture that actually distinguishes old from new behavior, since the original fixture's timestamps happened to produce the same order under both.
3. Add `persist-claude`/`persist-opencode`, wire into `STRATEGIES` (the single source of truth for valid strategy names, used by both `mergeSync`'s dispatch and `syncSession`'s CLI-facing validation), update `sync`'s `--help` text.
4. Reorder `watch`'s existing strategy/interval validation ahead of its ledger-existence check (pure relocation) so a new subprocess test can confirm `persist-*` stays rejected there without needing a real ledger fixture; updated README.

**Final whole-branch review** (most capable model, after all 4 tasks passed individually) found 2 Critical issues a task-scoped review structurally couldn't see:
- README falsely claimed discarded `persist-*` turns were recoverable via the ledger - false by construction, since discarded turns are exactly the turns created *since* the last sync, so they were never in any ledger commit, and the live Claude JSONL is fully overwritten (not appended).
- The CLI printed "Syncing N Claude / M OpenCode turns" even under `persist-*`, at the exact moment one side's turns were being discarded rather than kept.

Both fixed in one fix wave (commit `4cd1885`), independently re-reviewed (scoped re-review confirmed all findings addressed, no new Critical/Important breakage), plus 4 Important findings (stale docs in `sync.js`'s header, `mergeAbort`'s error message, and two README sections that still described the old behavior).

## Verification

```
$ npm test
tests 4, pass 4, fail 0
```

Every example command in this feature (`fork`, `sync --dry-run`, `sync --strategy persist-claude`, etc.) was run against real sessions during hands-on testing after implementation, not just the automated suite.

## Blast radius

- No change to `fork`'s behavior.
- `timestamp`'s merge *ordering* changes for any session with turns diverging on both sides since the last sync - the turns themselves are unchanged, only their order in the merged output. Sessions where only one side changed are unaffected (that's the majority case).
- `persist-claude`/`persist-opencode` are new, opt-in, destructive by design (see the corrected README warning) - existing workflows using `timestamp`/`abort` are unaffected.
- `watch` gains no new accepted strategy values; its validation order changed (a pure relocation) but not its logic.

## Docs

`README.md` updated: the "Keeping both sides in sync" section, the top command block, the `watch` section, and "Known limitations" all describe the final behavior. `src/sync/sync.js`'s module header and `mergeAbort`'s error message were also brought in line with the redefinition.

author: saya6k
body:
`Kobo Sync failed: wantread` 재현 원인과 수정입니다.

## 원인

`wantread`는 KOReader가 정의한 **TLS 핸드셰이크/타임아웃 코드**입니다 (`frontend/socketutil.lua`):

```lua
socketutil.SSL_HANDSHAKE_CODE = "wantread"  -- from LuaSec's ssl.c
```

JSON 요청은 `LARGE_BLOCK_TIMEOUT`(10초)을 쓰는데, `/v1/library/sync`는 서버가 페이지 전체를 만든 뒤에야 첫 바이트를 보냅니다. 1376권 라이브러리 기준 실측:

```
tls=0.15s   ttfb=10.8~11.3s   total=11.0~11.4s   code=200   size=206KB
```

응답 자체는 정상 200인데 **첫 바이트가 10초 문턱을 간발로 넘겨** 매번 실패했습니다. TLS 핸드셰이크는 0.15초로 멀쩡하니 코드 이름과 달리 인증서·연결 문제가 아닙니다.

## 수정

- API(JSON) 요청에 30초/120초 부여
- `TIMEOUT_CODE` / `SSL_HANDSHAKE_CODE` / `SINK_TIMEOUT_CODE`를 "the server took too long to respond"로 번역해 노출

## 다운로드 경로는 그대로

같은 서버에서 책 다운로드 실측 `ttfb=0.73s total=0.80s` — 서버의 on-the-fly kepub 변환을 포함해도 1초 안에 스트리밍이 시작되므로 `FILE_*`(15초/60초)는 유지했습니다.

## 검증 한계

`main.lua`는 KOReader 의존 때문에 busted로 덮이지 않습니다(README에 명시된 구조). 문법 검사(`luac -p`)와 위 실측으로 확인했고, 실제 기기 동기화 성공 여부는 확인이 필요합니다.

author: brandonifco
body:
Phase 6 step 7, the last part. Phase 6 set out to make the engine *loadable* with any scenario rather than merely organised around one. This is the evidence.

## The Sunken Chapel

A second scenario sharing nothing with the Watchtower — its own progress vocabulary (`chapel.rumour-heard` → `chapel.charter-signed` → `chapel.seal-broken` → `chapel.relic-recovered`), locations, route, map and triggers, and **no combat at all**. No value in it derives from a Watchtower constant, so any rule still reaching for those would fail to run it.

**Registering it took two lines** — one in `ScenarioDefinitionRegistry`, one in `ScenarioSessionFactory.StartingParties` — and **no change to any rule**.

Both starting-party entries point at the same factory, which is the point rather than an oversight: party composition is campaign-declared (Priority 2 decision #12), so one campaign means one roster whichever of its scenarios is attempted.

It's deliberately small. Its job is to exercise the whole non-combat path — decide, travel, arrive, explore, act, finish — not to be an adventure worth playing. That's Phase 9.

## What the 11 tests prove

- the definition is valid authored content, with **zero** validation issues (not even warnings — unlike Watchtower, which has two unreachable markers)
- a new session starts where *this* scenario declares, on *its* initial marker
- the full traversal runs on generic entry points only: `OutpostMissionRules` → `RegionalTravelRules.CanBeginJourney`/`BeginJourney`/`Advance` → `ExplorationRules.CanEnterDestination`/`EnterDestination`/`MoveForward`/`Turn` → `ScenarioTriggerRules.CanActivate`/`Activate`
- the traversal consumes **no randomness**, because it never builds an encounter
- the two scenarios' progress vocabularies and location sets do not intersect
- a session **cannot** carry the other scenario's progress marker
- a chapel save round-trips at every saveable stage, re-serializing to a byte-identical document

## One gap this turned up

A trigger that starts no encounter left the session in exploration mode — so a scenario without combat could reach its final marker but **never its conclusion**, because session validation rejects a conclusion marker held outside conclusion mode. A trigger whose resulting marker is a declared conclusion now ends the scenario and clears exploration state, exactly as winning an encounter already did.

This is precisely the kind of thing authoring a second scenario exists to find: the content model allowed it, the validator allowed it, and execution didn't.

**It also closes the untested branch flagged in #106** — the encounterless trigger path is covered here, by the scenario it was added for.

## Also

Mid-journey saving stays refused for both scenarios alike. That's a limit of this phase of the save format, not something the first scenario is special about, and a test now says so rather than leaving the theory case quietly dropped.

## Gate

- Debug build: 0 warnings
- Full suite: **1863 passed**, 0 failed (+11) — including both golden-master combat transcripts and all three frozen V1 save fixtures
- Release build: clean
- `git diff --check`: clean
- The new provider contains no reference to any Watchtower type; the only two occurrences of the word are prose in its doc comment.

author: alexanderwagnerdev
body: ## Summary Fixes the four open review findings on #85 (proxy-trust rate-limit / secure-cookie work), building on top of that branch: - **P1 — Peer preservation ran after `ProxyFix`.** `_PreserveDirectRemoteAddr` was installed as the *inner* WSGI middleware, so `ProxyFix` rewrote `REMOTE_ADDR` from `X-Forwarded-For` before the direct peer was captured. If the panel port was directly reachable, an attacker could still spoof `X-Forwarded-For` and bypass the login/stats rate limiter. Now `_PreserveDirectRemoteAddr` wraps `app.wsgi_app` *after* `ProxyFix` is applied, so it always sees the real TCP peer first. - **P1 — `TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS` missing from Compose services.** Startup validation requires `TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS` whenever `TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT > 0`, but `docker-compose.yml` and `compose.quickstart.yml` only passed `TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT` into the container. A user who set `TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS` in `.env` would still hit a config-validation exit. Added the variable to both service environment mappings. - **P2 — Explicit `http://` `PANEL_PUBLIC_URL` ignored for cookie defaulting.** When `PANEL_PUBLIC_URL` was explicitly `http://...` and proxy trust was enabled, the secure-cookie default still fell through to the proxy-count fallback and returned `True`, causing browsers to drop the session cookie post-login. An explicit `http://` URL now short-circuits to `False`. - **Code quality — mixed `import`/`from...import` of `config`** in `tests/test_proxy_rate_limit_security.py`, flagged by static analysis. Switched the second usage to `importlib.import_module`. ## Test plan - [x] `python -m pytest tests/test_proxy_rate_limit_security.py -q` — 4 passed - [x] `python -m pytest -q` (full suite) — 114 passed, 5 skipped 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01665TmbhKQpZuCYy797oHEn)_ --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added trusted proxy IP/CIDR configuration for safer client IP detection and rate limiting. * Added configuration validation requiring trusted proxy addresses when proxy support is enabled. * Improved secure-cookie defaults when the application runs behind trusted proxies. * **Bug Fixes** * Prevented untrusted forwarded headers from spoofing client IP addresses and bypassing rate limits. * **Tests** * Added coverage for trusted and untrusted proxy behavior, configuration validation, and secure-cookie defaults.

author: ykunyao
body:
## What changed

- add one AbortController per active conversation in ChatService
- propagate AbortSignal through the provider-neutral stream API
- forward cancellation to Vercel AI SDK streamText and make Mock delays abort-aware
- add validated, trusted-frame chat cancellation IPC
- expose request-scoped cancellation through the preload client
- add a terminal cancelled stream event and listener cleanup
- replace Send with a guarded Stop button during generation
- preserve an already-saved user message while discarding incomplete assistant output
- document the design, implementation plan, usage, and roadmap status

## Why

Streaming chat could not be interrupted once generation started. This left users waiting on unwanted or costly provider output and left Phase 3's stop-generation acceptance criterion incomplete.

## User impact

During generation, the Send button becomes Stop Generation. Stopping ends the provider request, clears transient text, and enables another message. If the user message was already stored it remains in history; incomplete assistant output is never persisted.

## Safety and race handling

- only one active controller exists per conversation
- repeated or stale cancellation requests return false
- cancellation before provider resolution does not persist the user message
- cancellation after a partial delta preserves only the user message
- unexpected provider failures retain their existing error behavior
- cancellation emits a typed terminal event rather than exposing provider errors

## Validation

- `corepack pnpm typecheck`
- `corepack pnpm lint`
- `corepack pnpm test` — 66 tests passed
- `corepack pnpm format:check`
- `corepack pnpm build`
- `corepack pnpm package:win`
- packaged Windows smoke test: renderer loaded from app.asar and all SQLite tables initialized

No real model endpoint or API key was required for verification.

## Out of scope

Pause/resume, preserving partial assistant output, configurable timeouts, regeneration, and cancel-all behavior remain separate follow-up work.

author: johdanike
body:
## Summary
This PR resolves #44 by properly following the pagination cursor in the `getEvents` RPC call. Previously, the bot would silently drop any events beyond the initial 100-item limit, which structurally disadvantaged the bot during busy network periods by prioritizing stale tasks over fresh ones. This update ensures the bot fetches all events within the scan window up to a configurable safety limit.

## Changes Made
- **Cursor Pagination:** Rewrote the event fetching logic into `fetchPendingTasks`, which iterates using the `response.cursor` until the window is exhausted.
- **Request Safety:** Handled the API constraint by ensuring `startLedger` is only sent on the initial request, and `cursor` is strictly used on subsequent requests.
- **Configurable Limits:** Bounded the pagination with `MAX_PAGES` and `PAGE_SIZE` constants to prevent unbounded loops during extreme network spikes. These are configurable via environment variables and documented in `.env.example`.
- **Visibility:** Added a clear warning log (`⚠️ Stopped after X pages...`) if the `MAX_PAGES` limit is hit, ensuring truncation is never silent. Added an informational log detailing the total events fetched per round.
- **RPC Documentation:** Added a code comment specifying the Soroban RPC version this pagination behavior was tested and verified against.

## Acceptance Criteria Met
- [x] `fetchPendingTasks` follows the pagination cursor.
- [x] Page size and maximum page count are named constants, configurable via environment.
- [x] Reaching the page limit logs a warning naming the limit.
- [x] `startLedger` and `cursor` are not sent in the same request.
- [x] Total events fetched per round is logged.
- [x] The RPC version the pagination behaviour was verified against is noted in a comment.

Closes #44

author: shashankss1205
body:
Four fixes from the 0.5.2 audit — plus one bug found while verifying them that is **not** in the report and is arguably the most serious item here.

### 1. `<module>` was counted and reported as a real function (`U-M1`)

The Python parser adds a synthetic `<module>` frame per file as the attribution target for module-level calls. It was treated as an ordinary `Function`:

```
$ cgc analyze dead-code
⚠️  Potentially Unused Functions:
│ <module>  │ /home/…/cgc_entry.py:1  │     ← first row
```

On CGC's own repo, **264 of 5,501** `Function` nodes were these frames, so every function total a user saw was inflated by one per Python file. It is now marked `is_synthetic`, excluded from the index summary and excluded from the dead-code query.

```
before: 2 files -> Function nodes 3      (only_one + two <module> frames)
after:  2 files -> Function nodes 1
```

The name-based check is kept as a fallback so graphs indexed before the marker existed still count correctly without a re-index.

### 2. Incremental update duplicated CALLS on Neo4j (`I-M12`)

`affected_paths` = changed ∪ callers ∪ inheritors, and **all** of them are re-parsed and fed back through `link_function_calls` — but only `caller_paths` had their outgoing CALLS cleared:

```python
other_callers = list(caller_paths)          # ← missing the inheritance-only neighbours
```

On Neo4j/Nornic the writer uses `CREATE`, not `MERGE`, so those neighbours got their edges re-created on top of the existing ones and duplicates multiplied on every save. FalkorDB and Kùzu use `MERGE`, which is why this never surfaced locally.

### 3. 🔴 `cgc analyze dead-code` is completely broken on KùzuDB — not in the audit

Found while verifying #1. `writer.py:715` emits `HEURISTIC_CALLS` for resolution tier ≥ 8, but the rel table **was never declared in the Kùzu schema**. Reproduced on pristine `upstream/main`:

```
$ cgc analyze dead-code
RuntimeError: Binder exception: Table HEURISTIC_CALLS does not exist.
```

Two consequences: tier-8+ edges cannot be written on Kùzu at all, and *every* query matching `[:CALLS|HEURISTIC_CALLS]` fails outright — which includes `find_dead_code` and the inheritance re-resolution pass. KùzuDB is the **default on Windows** and the fallback backend everywhere else.

Declared with the same bindings as `CALLS`. After:

```
$ cgc analyze dead-code
│ only_one │ …/modtest/m.py:1 │
Total: 1 function(s)
EXIT=0
```

### 4. A comment that overstated FalkorDB's guarantees (`G-M11`)

```python
# Skip all CREATE CONSTRAINT statements for FalkorDB backends; the indices
# created below are sufficient for MERGE to perform correct deduplication.
```

Indexes do not enforce uniqueness — `CALL db.constraints()` returns `[]`. Deduplication holds because `MERGE` dedupes within an `UNWIND` and FalkorDB serialises writes per graph. That is an assumption worth stating plainly (it breaks with an external writer or concurrent write execution), not a guarantee the schema provides. No behaviour change; the audit was explicit that no duplicates could actually be produced today.

### Tests

7 new tests, **all 7 fail against unpatched `main`**.

Full unit suite: **739 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed** (excluding `test_cgcignore_patterns.py`, flaky on `main` independently — see #1408).

author: fbumann
body:
Stacked on #88 (which is stacked on #87) — the corrected examples only exist there. Retarget as those merge.

Three separate hand sweeps found three separate batches of broken examples. That is the argument for this PR: **an example nobody runs is a claim nobody checked.**

`tests/test_doc_examples.py` covers the fenced blocks in `README.md`, `SPEC.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `ROADMAP.md`, **plus the module docstrings** in `__init__.py`, `api.py` and `compat.py` — the docstrings matter, because that is where the last batch hid and where a markdown-only sweep would never have looked.

## What it checks

- **The README example runs end to end** against a temp copy of its own YAML block, and its objective must equal the value the README states in a trailing comment — so the prose and the run cannot disagree.
- **Every python block parses**, and every `ly.` / `sol.` / `ex.` / `compat.` name it shows must exist on the real object.
- **Every yaml block validates** — whole sections through `MathSchema`; a fragment against its own section model, since a fragment deliberately omits the declarations around it and only its *shape* is our claim.
- **No docstring example binds a live executor outside a `with`.**

## Verified against the real history

Each bug reintroduced, and the matching test watched to fail:

| reintroduced bug | test that caught it |
|---|---|
| `ly.write_lp(...)` — never existed | `test_python_block_uses_real_api` |
| `piecewise:` sign on three links | `test_yaml_block_validates` |
| bare `RangeIndex` in `sources` | `test_readme_example_runs` |
| objective comment drifted to a wrong value | `test_readme_example_runs` |
| docstring binding `sol = ly.solve(...)` unmanaged | `test_docstring_examples_close_the_solution` |

## Coverage cannot silently drop

A block that is neither a whole schema section nor annotated fails `test_every_block_is_covered` rather than being skipped. Annotations live in HTML comments, so they render as nothing:

```
<!-- doctest: wrap=constraints -->   nest the block under that schema key
<!-- doctest: skip -->               excluded, with the reason in a comment
```

Exactly one block needed one — SPEC's `storage_balance:` example, which shows a constraint entry without its `constraints:` wrapper.

## A bug the sweeps missed

Writing the harness turned up something four rounds of manual review did not: the elision idiom

```python
{"p_max": "p_max.parquet", ...}
```

**is not valid Python** — a dict literal cannot mix a key-value pair with a bare `Ellipsis`. Those examples could never have been pasted and run. Fixed in `__init__.py`, `api.py` and `CLAUDE.md` by naming a second source instead. Bare `{...}` is a *set* and parses fine, so the compat examples were already correct.

## Verification

`uv run pytest` — 257 passed, 1 xfailed (24 new) · ruff check + format clean · pyrefly 0 errors.

author: mateuszpuchalski
body:
Dwie zmiany na tej samej ścieżce — zapis lokalizacji z kolektora — w tej kolejności, bo pierwsza upraszcza drugą.

---

# 1. COFNIJ wychodzi (`30f44a3`)

Zapis lokalizacji z karty towaru miał **5-sekundową karencję** (`UNDO_GRACE_MS` → `next_attempt_at` w przyszłości), żeby pasek COFNIJ miał co anulować.

Ta funkcja nic nie dodawała: **pomyłkową lokalizację poprawia się po prostu skanując właściwą półkę** — ta sama liczba ruchów, zero mechanizmu do utrzymania. Koszt był za to realny i płacony przy **każdym** zapisie: pięć sekund, zanim worker w ogóle tknie zadanie.

Usunięte: `config.undoGraceMs` + `UNDO_GRACE_MS`, `EnqueueBase.graceMs`, `UndoManager.kt`, `UndoInfo`/`showUndo`/`hideUndo`, `UndoBar`, gałąź shake-to-COFNIJ w `MotionMonitor.kt` z ustawieniem `shakeUndo`, `OfflineQueue.remove()`.

**Zostaje** — mimo podobnej nazwy, to inne rzeczy: `POST /api/queue/:id/cancel` (używa go **ekran kolejki**, gdzie anulowanie jest świadomą decyzją przy podglądzie), log upadków w `MotionMonitor` (drugi, niezależny użytek akcelerometru) i cały bufor offline.

## Prawie-regresja, którą warto nazwać

Pasek COFNIJ niósł **trzy** role naraz: cofanie, **potwierdzenie zapisu** i **ostrzeżenie o kodzie spoza wykazu lokalizacji**. Wycięcie go w całości usunęłoby po cichu dwie ostatnie. Zastąpione `flashSuccess` + `toast`, więc magazynier nadal dostaje jedno i drugie.

---

# 2. Lokalizacja „w drodze” staje się widoczna (`561051e`)

Read-model `sgt_towar.lokalizacja` zmienia się **dopiero po udanym zapisie** przez workera. Do tego czasu karta pokazywała stan sprzed zmiany i **nie mówiła o tym słowa**:

- dodana lokalizacja nie widniała nigdzie → wygląda, jakby skan nie zadziałał (i kusi, żeby skanować drugi raz),
- usunięta nadal wisiała → wygląda, jakby nic się nie stało,
- **przy błędzie zapisu ten stan jest TRWAŁY**, a jedynym sygnałem zostawała czerwona pastylka Sfery w rogu — wspólna dla wszystkich zadań, więc nie mówiąca, **której lokalizacji** dotyczy.

Dla **stanów magazynowych** aplikacja rozwiązała to dawno: `pendingMmByTw` koryguje je o kolejkę i pokazuje `⏳ N szt w drodze`. Lokalizacje z tego wypadły — to ta sama odpowiedź dla drugiego pola.

## Serwer

`pendingLocChanges(twId, current)` wyprowadza zmianę **pojedynczych kodów** z payloadu, który niesie **całe** pole:

```
payload set_location:  { twId, newValue: "C04-06-02 D01-03-02" }   ← CAŁE pole
bieżące locs:          ["C04-06-02"]
                        ↓ różnica
                       [{ code: "D01-03-02", kind: "add", status: "pending", queueId: 1 }]
```

Dwie reguły, które nie są oczywiste i dlatego mają własne testy:

- **liczy się WYNIK, czyli ostatnie zadanie w toku** — wcześniejsze i tak zostanie nadpisane, więc pokazywanie go byłoby kłamstwem,
- **`error` wygrywa nad `pending`** — zadanie w błędzie się nie wykona bez PONÓW, więc niesie inny komunikat niż „czekaj”.

Karta dostaje `pendingLocs` **obok** `locs`, nie zamiast. `locs` zostaje prawdą z Subiekta — inaczej karta zaczęłaby kłamać w drugą stronę, pokazując niepotwierdzone jako pewne.

Zawartość regału (`GET /api/locations/:code/products`) dostaje `pendingHere` — **razem z towarami, które na tę półkę dopiero jadą** i nie ma ich jeszcze w read-modelu. Bez tego ekran regału pokazuje ten sam nieaktualny stan, tylko z drugiej strony.

## Kolektor

| stan | wygląd | znaczenie |
|---|---|---|
| potwierdzona | jak dotąd | jest w Subiekcie |
| dochodząca | przerywana ramka, przygaszona, `⏳` | zapis czeka w kolejce |
| schodząca | kod przekreślony, przygaszony | usunięcie czeka w kolejce |
| **błąd** | czerwony, ikona alertu, **pulsuje** | zapis się nie udał — czeka na PONÓW |

**Pulsuje wyłącznie błąd.** Ekran jest trzymany otwarty cały dzień, więc animacja kosztuje baterię i po godzinie staje się tłem — miga tylko to, co wymaga reakcji człowieka i tylko to, co jest stanem trwałym. Tap na czerwonym chipie prowadzi wprost do kolejki z PONÓW.

`LocationScreen` przechodzi z `produceState` na `pollFlow(2000)` — inaczej znacznik na regale nigdy by z niego nie zniknął.

Usunięcie karencji z etapu 1 skraca okno oczekiwania do jednego cyklu workera, więc chip-duch przestaje być stanem widzianym przy każdym skanie. Zostaje tam, gdzie naprawdę niesie treść: przy podróży do MSSQL i przy błędzie.

---

## Weryfikacja

- **`services/locations.test.ts` — 9 testów** samej reguły różnicy (dodanie, usunięcie do pustej wartości, zamiana = `add` + `remove`, dwa zadania w kolejce, status `error`, `error` bijący `pending`, izolacja innej kartoteki, zadania `done` ignorowane). Razem **27 testów serwera**.
- **Nowy e2e `lokalizacje-w-drodze` — 18 asercji, zero FAIL.** Sprawdza **obie strony przejścia** (przed i po przemieleniu kolejki przez workera) dla dodania i usunięcia, z obu ekranów — karty towaru i zawartości regału — oraz to, że po nieudanym zapisie chip **nie znika sam**.
- **Sens etapu 1 jako asercja**: świeże zadanie ma `next_attempt_at = null`, czyli worker bierze je w pierwszym cyklu.
- **Nic nie zostało po COFNIJ**: `grep` na `UNDO_GRACE_MS`, `undoGraceMs`, `graceMs`, `UndoManager`, `UndoInfo`, `showUndo`, `UndoBar`, `shakeUndo` — zero trafień. Osobno sprawdzone, że cięcie nie poszło za daleko: `POST /api/queue/:id/cancel` nadal zwraca `{"ok":true}` i nadal ma wywołanie w `QueueScreen.kt`.
- **Bez regresji**: `zwroty`, `tryba`, `tryba2`, `trybb`, `e2e2`, `flagi` — wszystkie zielone.
- `tsc --noEmit` czysty, `:core` **56 testów** (nowy pilnuje zgodności wstecznej: starszy serwer bez `pendingLocs`/`pendingHere` nie może wywrócić kolektora), `tools/docs_check.py` czysty.

> `:app` nie kompiluje się w tym środowisku (brak Android SDK) — sprawdza to CI, jak przy poprzednich zmianach UI.

## Do obejrzenia na sprzęcie

Zmiana jest wizualna, więc jedyny pełny dowód to kolektor: skan etykiety regału na karcie → chip-duch pojawia się i po ~1–2 s zamienia w zwykły (bez dawnych pięciu sekund czekania); z `WORKER_SIM_ERRORS=1` → chip czerwony, pulsuje, tap prowadzi do kolejki.

author: joshuaedwardcrowe
body:
## What

`.github/workflows/publish.yml` — a `workflow_dispatch`-only (manual)
release pipeline for all 9 KitCli packages, mirroring the design just
established for YnabSharp. Also documents the process in
CONTRIBUTING.md.

Flow: build → test → for each of the 9 packages, in dependency order,
read its own committed `<Version>` → pack → push (`--skip-duplicate`)
→ cut `CHANGELOG.md` → commit → tag (`KitCli`'s own version) → create a
GitHub Release.

## Why

Linked issue: n/a — builds on #55/#56 (publish order) directly

Same reasoning as YnabSharp's release workflow: manual trigger only
(publishing is external/hard-to-reverse, same category as a merge), no
in-workflow version mutation (that's exactly what made the old
`publish.rc` risky — see #13), bookkeeping ordered after the NuGet
pushes so a failure there doesn't require re-publishing anything.

One thing this PR does **not** do: force the 9 packages back into
version lockstep. Checked live NuGet history while building this —
they've already drifted (7 of 9 at `1.0.6`, one at `1.0.7`, `KitCli`
itself at `1.0.10`), and NuGet's own history has real gaps (`KitCli`
missing `1.0.7` entirely; three other packages missing `1.0.3`),
consistent with past `publish.rc` runs failing partway through. Filed
as #58 rather than quietly deciding what the "correct" synchronized
version should be — that's not a call I should make unilaterally.

## How

Extracted every project's current `<Version>` and cross-checked against
`api.nuget.org`'s flat-container index per package to see what's
actually live, before deciding how the workflow should read versions.

## Tested

- [ ] Unit tests
- [ ] `KitCli.Playground.Scenarios` scenario
- [x] Manual — validated workflow YAML with Ruby's parser (no `pyyaml`
      available in this environment). **Not** run end-to-end — no
      `NUGET_API_KEY` configured, and running it for real would
      actually publish packages. This is reviewed-and-reasoned-through,
      not empirically executed, same caveat as YnabSharp's equivalent
      PR.

## Kind of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Tech debt
- [ ] Docs / process

author: lemmonchess333
body:
Generalising the vacuity found in #1772 turned up a second instance.

## The sweep

A repo-wide search for "negative assertion under `waitFor`" gave **163** raw hits. Filtering to those with no positive anchor left **15**, and triage left **one** real case — this file.

The rest are legitimate, and the distinctions matter:
- `.not.toBeNull()` is a **positive** — waiting for a value to *appear*.
- The `Tooltip` cases open the tooltip synchronously first, so their negative is false at t=0.

*(My first detector found zero, because `block[:match.start()]` ends just before `waitFor(` — which includes that statement's own `await` keyword, making every hit look anchored. Fixed before drawing any conclusion.)*

## The real case

`useLastRunType` returns `repeatType`, which starts `null`. So:

```ts
await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toBeNull());
```

…was satisfied on its **first poll by the initial state**, and returned before the read resolved.

Mutating the hook to set `"easy"` *after* the read — a repeat row offered to every user, including signed-out ones:

| | result |
|---|---|
| before anchoring | 2 failed, **5 passed** |
| after anchoring | **5 failed**, 2 passed |

The two that still pass are correct: `stays silent when the read fails` throws at the SDK entry, and `offers nothing when signed out` issues no read at all — that mutation's `setState` is unreachable in both. They're left in their original form **with a note saying why**, rather than dressed up to look anchored.

The other three go through `renderAfterRead()`, which holds the read with `deferReads()` and releases it explicitly. The release *is* the anchor — this hook exposes no loading flag to wait on, which is precisely why the vacuity went unnoticed.

## The mutation shape that matters

Making the hook wrong **synchronously** (broken from first render) failed all 7 even *before* this change — which would have read as "the tests are fine." Only a mutation that goes wrong **after the read** distinguishes them: the same asynchronous shape the assertion was blind to.

That's the generalisable lesson, so it's now in CLAUDE.md's recurring-mistake list — two instances, both pinning documented security properties that nothing was holding.

## Verification

- `npm run test` — 5505 passed, 213 skipped, 0 failed
- `npx tsc -b` clean; `npm run lint` 0 errors

body:
## Summary

Scheduled maintenance pass: triaged the 30 open issues (6 already covered by in-flight PRs #364/#367/#370/#372), fixed 7 well-scoped, high-severity ones, and corrected README staleness found by a survey pass.

- **#341** — `--screening-levels` silently resolved `None` (or a raw `TypeError`) against the shipped matrix-nested `screening_levels.yaml`, making exceedances vanish silently in `build-max-result-dataset` and crashing `build-exceedance-event`. Adds `core.common.config.load_flat_screening_levels()`, routed through all 6 affected CLI commands. Raises a clear `ClickException` on a genuine cross-matrix value conflict instead of guessing.
- **#340** — `ND_QUALIFIERS` was copy-pasted into 7 report modules, none including `"UJ"` — a `UJ` result imported as nondetect (`result_parser.py`) but reported as a detect everywhere, producing false exceedances. Canonicalized to `core.common.config.ND_QUALIFIERS` (kept `"BDL"` too — see decision log).
- **#345** — `layout_manager.set_layer_visibility` took a `QACollector` param but never called it; a typo'd/renamed layer name silently failed to toggle visibility with a clean QA report.
- **#366** — `export_snapshot.build_where` interpolated `site_id`/`event_id` unescaped into a WHERE clause; the existing regression test only asserted `w is not None` (would pass on a fully-injected payload). Now escapes embedded quotes and the test verifies the actual escaped output.
- **#342** — `--compress` was accepted and documented ("ZIP the output GDB") but silently did nothing — no `zipfile` reference anywhere. Adds `compress_snapshot_gdb()` (stdlib `shutil.make_archive`, arcpy-free, independently testable).
- **#343** — `export_summary`'s `samples`/`site_id`/`event_id` were accepted but never read — the CLI help text promised metadata that never appeared. Wires them into new conditional "Metadata" and "Samples" sheets.
- **#369** — `import_to_gdb._delete_for_replace` applied `--matrix` only to `Env_Samples`/`Env_AnalyticalResults`; a `--matrix SOIL` replace wiped `Env_WaterLevels`/`Env_RPDResults` for every matrix at the site, including GW rows the run never touched. Neither table has a `Matrix` column, so this skips them (QA INFO, not silent) rather than guessing at a schema change.

**README fixes:** overstated roadmap gate status ("Phases 1–9 delivered" vs. CLAUDE.md's actual per-phase gate log showing Phase 5/7/8/9 legs still open), a Survey123 section not reflecting Phase 0 slice A having already shipped, 8 runtime-matrix rows mislabeled `HYBRID` when `capabilities.py` registers them `LOCAL` (guard-correctness reasons, verified before touching), a missing `notebook` extras-table row, and a missing DRAFT caveat on `manage-screening-levels`.

Judgment calls made along the way (screening-levels flattening semantics, the #369 skip-vs-guess direction, keeping `"BDL"` in the canonical set, the `export_summary` wiring approach) are recorded in `docs/adr/logs/2026-07-26-agent-decisions.md`.

## Not addressed in this pass

Deliberately left out — each needs a bigger design decision than fits a mechanical bug-fix batch:
- **#339** — report-family `--results-csv` vocabulary mismatch (canonical vs. report vocabulary); the issue itself frames the fix as an owner call between 3 architectural options.
- **#344** — RTK `site_id`/`batch_id` not stored — needs a `gdb_schema.py` column addition + arcpy `InsertCursor` field-list change (ADR-0077 doc-verification territory).
- **#220** — the zero-rows-parsed QA guard is already shipped (PR #363); the remaining half (whether it should ever block, and the SOIL-dropdown-vs-no-SOIL-profile question) is explicitly owner-gated per the issue's own comments.
- **#244**, **#272** — both explicitly need an owner design decision or are strategic/planning trackers, not discrete fixes.

A codebase-gap survey (TODOs, dead-ends, wiring gaps, dangling config keys) came back clean — nothing else rose to the bar for a new issue filing.

## Test plan

- [x] Full arcpy-free suite: `2551 passed, 20 skipped` (baseline was `2528 passed, 20 skipped`)
- [x] Each fix has new, targeted regression tests (screening-levels shape/flattening, ND_QUALIFIERS parity with `result_parser.py`, layer-visibility missing-layer warning, SQL-escaping, compress archive contents, export_summary Metadata/Samples sheets, matrix-scoped delete skip)
- [x] No new/changed arcpy call signatures — ADR-0077 doc-verification not triggered
- [x] `git diff --check`: clean

body:
## 概要

ADR の識別子に時刻部を導入し、並行ブランチでそれぞれ採番しても識別子が重複しない状態にする。Closes #587。

`ADR-20260726-06` が定めた `ADR-YYYYMMDD-NN-<slug>` と「対象日のファイルを配置ディレクトリから列挙し最大番号 + 1」という採番手順は、配置ディレクトリについて単一の直列化されたビューが存在することを前提とする。並行ブランチではこの前提が成立せず、実際に PR #575 と PR #576 がそれぞれ自分の base に対して手順を正しく実行した結果、`ADR-20260726-01` / `-02` / `-03` が2組ずつ存在する状態になった。drift-lint は識別子の重複を検査しないため exit 0 で通過する。

識別子を `ADR-YYYYMMDDHHMM-NN-<slug>` へ改め、**時刻部がブランチ間の一意性**を、**連番部が同一分内バーストの順序**を担う形にした。同一コミットで複数 ADR を起票するケース（多決定 ADR の分割による後継 N 本）は同一秒に作られるため時刻だけでは一意化できず、かつ分割後継の順序は決定クラスタ順であって時間順ではないため、両方が要る。

## 変更内容

### 発番スクリプトの追加（`feat` コミット）

- `plugins/adr/scripts/next-adr-id.sh` — 時刻部（分粒度・ローカル時刻）の取得と、同一時刻部内の連番決定を担う。列挙対象は**同一時刻部を持つ既存ファイルに限る**
- `plugins/adr/scripts/test-next-adr-id.sh` — 11ケース（連番の加算・ゼロ埋め・時刻部による分離・旧形式の読み飛ばし・上限99件・異常系）

スクリプト化したのは、実行時コンテキストが日付までしか持たず分粒度の時刻を取得できないためである。Issue の制約「時刻の取得に外部コマンドを実行しない」は現行規約の維持を意図したものだが、これを文字どおり守ると時刻部が取得できない。操作スキルに生シェル（`date`）を開く案と比較し、既存の `lint-adr.sh` / `gen-adr-index.sh` と同じ「同梱スクリプトのみ許可」の枠へ発番を1本足す形を採った（`allowed-tools` に `Bash(bash *scripts/next-adr-id.sh*)` を追加）。この選択は着手前に確認済み。

### 正典と規約の追随（`docs` コミット）

- `ADR-202607262019-01-adr-id-timestamp-numbering` を起票・承認し、`ADR-20260726-06` を上書き（core 反転）
- 退役に伴う inbound 参照の付け替え: `ADR-20260718` の `Related:` 行と `## Context` の現況参照を後継へ差し替え、注釈へ再反転の事実を反映（非core 編集として `## 変更履歴` に1行追記）
- `adr-model.md` — 採番方式節（形式・タイムゾーン・上限・時刻の取得方法）と採番衝突時の解消手順を書き替え
- `template.md` / `transitions.md` / `io-examples.md` / `SKILL.md` — 形式リテラルと発番手順の追随
- `index.md` の再生成
- #550 本文の分割方針を4段構成（#566 → #570 → #587 → #567）へ更新し、形式に依存する AC・遡及移行の番号割り当て規則を新形式へ改めた

## 検証

| AC | 内容 | 結果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 新規 ADR が `承認済み` / `有効` で `Supersedes:` を持つ | 充足 |
| 2 | `ADR-20260726-06` が `上書き済み` で `superseded-by` を持つ | 充足 |
| 3 | `adr-model.md` に形式・TZ・上限・取得方法の4点 | 充足（`adr-model.md:68,70,71,78`） |
| 4 | 衝突解消手順が配置ディレクトリ列挙に依存しない | 充足（`adr-model.md:90,96`） |
| 5 | `grep -rn 'ADR-YYYYMMDD-NN' plugins/adr` が0件 | 0件 |
| 6 | `lint-adr.sh docs/adr` が exit 0 | exit 0 |
| 7 | `test-lint-adr.sh` が 86/86 | 86/86 pass |
| 8 | #550 本文の分割方針が新形式を反映 | 更新済み |

新規テスト `test-next-adr-id.sh` は 11/11 pass。

## スコープに関する補足

Issue の IN に明記がないが、以下を含めた。いずれも追加的な変更であり既存の振る舞いを削っていない。

- **発番スクリプトとそのテストの追加** — 時刻取得方法の決定（確認済み）に伴う。配布物であるため回帰検知の手段を同時に置いた
- **`io-examples.md` の具体例の更新** — Issue の波及リストには挙がっていないが、具体例が旧形式のままだと規約と矛盾する
- **#550 の AC 群と遡及移行の番号割り当て規則の更新** — AC8 の対象は「分割方針」だが、形式リテラルを含む AC を据え置くと #567 が旧形式へ移行してしまう

## 残る作業（本PRの対象外）

- 既存 ADR の遡及リネームと、現に発生している `ADR-20260726-01` / `-02` / `-03` の重複解消 — #567
- ファイル名形式検査・識別子重複検査の `lint-adr.sh` への追加 — 別Issue

body:
## Description

See complete issue in [STR-4092](https://alpenlabs.atlassian.net/browse/STR-4092).

## Summary

Validate `bridge_pubkey` directly in the Alpen CLI instead of deserializing it through `shrex::Hex<[u8; 32]>`.

The `shrex` fixed-array deserializer reports oversized values from the destination-buffer perspective and silently zero-pads undersized values. This could produce confusing errors or allow an incorrectly sized configuration value to reach public-key validation.

## Changes

- Deserialize `bridge_pubkey` as a string.
- Require exactly 64 hexadecimal characters (32 bytes).
- Parse the value directly as an x-only secp256k1 public key.
- Return a clear configuration error containing the expected and supplied lengths.
- Add tests for short, long, malformed, and valid public keys.

## Example error

```text
bridge_pubkey must contain exactly 64 hexadecimal characters (32 bytes); got 66 characters
```

The entire code was written by Codex, Sol 5.6 model. I verified it.

body:
> Gestapelt auf #101 (braucht das Directory-Authority-Tier). Parallel zu #102.
> **Reihenfolge:** #102 idealerweise vor diesem PR mergen — siehe „Abhängigkeit" unten.

## Warum marktcom und nicht die anderen Verzeichnisse

Es ist das einzige Verzeichnis, dessen Suche gleichzeitig über **Radius um Koordinaten** und **Marktformat** adressierbar ist. Damit löst es dein Wochenmarkt-Problem strukturell statt per Keyword-Heuristik:

```
/termine/radius?lat=50.7374&lng=7.0982&radius=75
  &q[event_kategorie_eq]=<format>
```

Nie angefragt werden: `31 Wochenmarkt`, `43 Garten-/Pflanzenmarkt`, `16 Tiere`, `41 Weihnachtsmarkt`, `44 Mittelaltermarkt`, `3 Stadtfest`, `37 Messen`, `40 Stoffmarkt`, `12 Bambini` (haben wir über Kinderflohmarkt.com direkt), `4 Kunsthandwerk`.

Die IDs habe ich selbst gegen das Live-Select verifiziert. Korrektur zur Recherche: **`42` (Antik-Trödelmarkt) steht nicht im Dropdown**, ist aber live und genau on-target — wird deshalb explizit angefragt.

`robots.txt` ist `User-agent: * / Disallow:` — vollständig offen.

## Last

Bewusst minimal gehalten:

- **Nur Listenseiten**, keine Detailseiten. Die Liste trägt bereits Venue, PLZ+Ort, Veranstalter, Datum, Format und Beschreibung.
- **Paginierung endet bei der ersten Seite jenseits des Fensters.** Ergebnisse sind datумs­sortiert, also kostet ein 7-Tage-Fenster typisch *einen* Request pro Format. Kategorie 42 hätte sonst allein 6 Seiten à 30 Events.
- Das 12-Seiten-Sicherheitslimit wird **geloggt**, nicht still abgeschnitten.

## Dedup an der Quelle statt per Fuzzy-Titel

Der `eventname` der Liste ist der **Venue** („Hit-Markt", „ASV"), nicht der Marktname. Ein Verzeichnis-Datensatz lässt sich deshalb prinzipiell nicht per Titel gegen den Erstquellen-Datensatz matchen — der erste Treffer im Live-Test war ausgerechnet ein **Geide-Markt, den wir schon direkt lesen**.

Statt auf `SequenceMatcher` zu hoffen, werden Datensätze bereits integrierter Veranstalter verworfen: Geide, Grote & Hiller, Lampert, Okken, Cölln, Hofflohmärkte, HofFloh, Kinderflohmarkt, Rhein Antik, Brückenforum, Katharinenhof. Übrig bleibt das echte Neuangebot — laut Recherche 587 Wunschkategorie-Termine von nicht integrierten Veranstaltern (Melan, Nikolopoulos, Trödelfabrik Bonn u.a.).

## Titel-Design

Der Venue bleibt im Titel. Ein bloßes `<Format> <Stadt>` wäre kürzer, aber eine Stadt kann mehrere verschiedene Märkte am selben Tag haben — identische Titel würden echte Märkte wegdedupen. Ein Test pinnt, dass eine Serie vollständig überlebt.

Die Beschreibung ist **kein** Titel-Fallback: ihr erster Satz ist Marketing-Prosa (`Auf dem Antik- und Trödelmarkt ist der Name Programm`). Das war meine erste Fassung und sie hat genau solche Titel produziert.

## Abhängigkeit

`_INTEGRATED_ORGANIZERS` enthält `rhein antik`. Wenn dieser PR **vor** #102 gemergt wird, verwerfen wir Rhein-Antik-Termine ohne die Direktquelle zu haben. Der Verlust ist begrenzt (die Termine kommen weiter über den Bad-Godesberg-Kalender und Cölln Konzept), aber #102 zuerst ist saubererer. Im Code kommentiert.

## Tests

`373 Tests, OK` (vorher 366). Neu in `tests/test_marktcom.py`, Fixture spiegelt die echte Markup-Struktur inklusive Ad-Blöcken zwischen den Treffern:

- URL scopet auf Bonn-Radius und Format
- Produktmarkt-Formate sind nicht in `WANTED_CATEGORIES`
- Ad-Blöcke werden übersprungen
- Datensatz mit unerwünschtem Format-Badge fällt weg (Badge-Icon schlägt Query-Parameter)
- Märkte integrierter Veranstalter werden verworfen, neue behalten
- Skip-Marker matchen case- und whitespace-insensitiv
- unbekannte Orte werden nicht zu Bonn umgedeutet
- Venue bleibt im Titel, Marketing-Prosa nie
- **Verzeichnis verliert gegen den Stadtteil-Publisher** (Antikmarkt Bad Godesberg)
- Serientermine überleben Dedup vollständig
- Paginierung stoppt jenseits des Fensters

body:
## Summary

Implements SPEC-018 Harmony/gpt-oss response parsing for provider-side response synthesis:

- parses Harmony token IDs directly for final-channel content and `commentary to=functions.*` tool calls
- suppresses hidden `analysis` and non-tool `commentary` content from buyer-visible responses, streaming deltas, and logs/usage-facing accounting
- fails closed for malformed frames, undeclared functions, invalid JSON, wrong channel recipients, post-terminal content, and request stops in hidden or structural spans
- preserves Harmony return/call terminals through MLX generation so parser-owned synthesis sees the terminal token
- separates buyer API `usage.completion_tokens` from receipt/settlement `tokens_out`

## Root Cause

The prior response path operated on decoded text and legacy parser conventions. Harmony requires token-ID-aware parsing because structural tokens, hidden channels, and terminal call/return markers are semantically meaningful and can be stripped or misclassified by generic text/EOS handling.

author: alexgromer
body:
## Why

An audit on 2026-07-26 found the **living** docs six ADRs behind the code. Milestone contract docs (`M*_CONTRACT.md`) lag *legitimately* — they record their own milestones and rewriting them would make them lie about those milestones. These do not.

This commit updates the docs that were either **factually wrong** or **silent about a surface that already exists**. The rest is named in the backlog rather than quietly left behind.

## `docs/THREAT_MODEL` (+en) — new §4.12, two boundaries

**The first is genuinely new.** Since ADR-067 the product **systematically collects a foreign application's output**. Seven `app.*` codes carry into `runs/<id>/logs/run.jsonl` whatever the application printed itself:

- a `console.log` with a session token
- a URL with `?token=`
- dialog text containing personal data
- a 5xx response body inside an error message

We do not choose this — what the application prints is not Sentinel's decision. And `logsink.go` stores it **as received**: there is **no write-side filter** on secret shapes (`Bearer `, `eyJ`, `?token=`, long hex/base64) — unlike `brain`, which redacts its own logs. Only `0700` and the read token protect it, and **no TTL exists for `logs/`** while `trace.zip` has two (`SENTINEL_TRACE_KEEP`/`SENTINEL_TRACE_TTL_HOURS`). → **`GAP-SEC-005`, P1.**

**The second is not new surface but an invariant.** `cancel` signals a process **group** — without it, 2 orphans of 3 survive (measured). The group is created *at spawn*, so a run never inherits the caller's. But `cancel_test.go` checks cancellation behaviour and **never checks that the leader's PGID differs from control-API's**. A refactor of spawn would send SIGKILL to everything the operator started in that shell session. → **`GAP-OPS-007`.**

## `docs/OBSERVABILITY` (+en) — new §7

The two streams split by **audience** rather than severity, and why: AG-UI frames are **82% of a run's output** and are not noise — levelling a story destroys it. Plus the catalogue's five axes (level · category · source · audience · `degrades`), the read-side collapsing rule, and the reason writes are immediate:

> a stuck run emits nothing different, so holding a record back to count repeats kept the loop out of its own file for exactly as long as the loop lasted — the very case collapsing exists to expose.

Ends with what observability still does **not** have.

## `docs/OUTPUTS` (+en) — §11 and §12

`logs/` artefacts with their as-built limits: **`logs/*` are NOT in the artifact whitelist** (only reachable via the token-gated `GET /v1/runs/{id}/logs`), the application channel caps at **500** records with `app.log_capped` announcing truncation so a truncated capture cannot be mistaken for a complete one, `app.*` never reaches the verdict, no TTL. Plus §12, the ADR-069 store marker and why `501` would have been the wrong answer there.

## `docs/STATE_MACHINE` (+en)

`interactive_failed` was **missing from a table that explicitly promises to list ONLY fields really declared in `RunState`** — and whose own note records that an earlier version of that table got this wrong. Added, with the reason the field exists (one click 34 times until `max_steps` in a live log).

## `README` (+en)

The status table ended at **M9-LIVE-prep**, so eight shipped ADRs (063–070) were invisible on the project's front page. Added the fix wave and the product revision, plus a link to the regression map.

## Remaining, named honestly

`[DOCS-REFRESH-070]` is now `[~]` with the remainder listed: `ROADMAP`, `TESTING`, `DEVELOPMENT`, `SELF_HEALING`, `DISTRIBUTION` — **stale ADR references and incompleteness, not factual errors**. `SELF_HEALING` in particular does not lie about explore retries: it already states that the explore heal node is a stub.

## Gates

- bilingual parity holds: headings 20/20 (threat model), 12/12 (observability), 15/15 (outputs), 30/30 (state machine), 16/16 (README); `pairs_ok` unchanged at 46
- `gitleaks protect --staged` clean
- no code changed

author: vitala89
body:
## Problem

The toast in the bottom-right corner fired only on the pages that happened to inject `ToastService`. Settings, the Tracker and Interview Prep had it; most of the app did not. Saving a CV or a cover letter only flashed a small inline badge, saving the profile only changed a line of text under the button, and the cover-letter library said nothing at all.

Failures were worse. Deleting a job, importing a tracklist, adding or removing a Discover source, and saving a job from the Discover feed all failed silently, writing the error to the developer console only.

## What was actually wrong

The infrastructure was already correct. `ToastService`, `ToastErrorHandler` and `provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners()` mean an **uncaught** error toasts on its own. Every gap was a caught-and-swallowed error, or a success path with only inline feedback.

Audited all 38 desktop page components plus the five `core/` components against their mutation and `catch` sites.

## Changes

| Component | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `cover-letter-list` | zero toasts of any kind | load, duplicate, export, delete, generate - success and failure, matching its `cv-list` sibling |
| `cv-list` | errors only | + success on duplicate/delete/export/import/generate, + errors on duplicate/delete |
| `cv-detail` | inline badge only | toast on save; "save as template" also gained a `catch` it did not have |
| `cover-letter-detail` | inline badge only | toast on save |
| `profile` | text under the button | toast on save |
| `jobs` | errors into `actionMsg` | save-job, mark-applied, delete-job, plus four AI-generation and two portal-drafting failure paths. `markApplied` and `confirmDeleteJob` navigate away, so the inline text was never seen |
| `my-jobs` | silent | delete and import, success and failure |
| `discover` | seven actions to `console.error` only | save-row, add/remove source, toggle-source, dismiss, undo, scan |
| `quick-view-modal` | no `catch` on priority | + error on priority, + success on adding a comment |

All follow the pattern already used by `tracker` and `interview-prep`: `toast.success(t()('ns.key'))` on success, `toast.error(String(e))` on failure. Existing inline status text is kept - the toast is additive, not a replacement.

16 new i18n keys across all six locales.

## Deliberately left silent

JSON-parse fallbacks (`tracker-report`, `tracker-report-print`, `jobs` cache reads), best-effort background writes the code comments mark as non-fatal, and read-only page loads that already render an honest empty state (`dashboard`, `onboarding-banner`, `first-launch`). Toasting those would fire on page entry rather than on a user action.

## Validation

- `npm run type-check` - pass, 6 projects
- `npm test` - pass, 759 tests across 6 projects
- `npm run lint` - pass, 0 errors (11 pre-existing non-null-assertion warnings)
- `npm run format:check` - pass
- `git diff --check` - pass

`npm run desktop:build` was not run: no build-shape change, but that leaves the bundle-size budget unverified for this diff. **No on-screen check in the running Tauri app yet** - the toast markup and container are untouched, so this is unchanged rendering of an existing component, but it is unverified visually.

## Privacy and security

None. Error toasts render `String(e)`, the same text the affected pages already put into their inline status signals or the console. No new data source is read and nothing leaves the device.

## Risk

More toasts can read as noise where one user action triggers several writes. `TOAST_DEDUPE_MS` collapses identical repeats and `TOAST_MAX` caps the stack, so the failure mode is a briefly busier corner rather than a flood.

author: tkys
body:
## 概要

写真アプリ風の動画トリマーUIに刷新。現状の『掴めないスライダー + 表示専用 timelineBar』を撤去し、filmstrip + ドラッグ可能ハンドル + 30秒物理制限を実装。

## 実装内容

### `VideoTrimmerBar` (新規 View)
- AVAssetImageGenerator で filmstrip サムネイルを生成（`.task {}` で View 消滅時に自動キャンセル、`maximumSize` 指定でメモリ抑制）
- 選択範囲外を Dim 表示
- 左右ハンドルを `DragGesture(coordinateSpace: .named)` でドラッグ（バー座標系で位置→時間変換）
- 選択範囲内タップでスクラブ（その位置からプレビュー再生）
- ドラッグ開始時に `previewer.stop()` を呼ぶ（既存の停止処理を維持）

### `TrimRange` (新規 Model)
- 純粋関数として範囲クランプを実装
- `movingStart(to:)` / `movingEnd(to:)`: ジェスチャ中毎回適用
- **30秒制限は『そこで止める』挙動**: ハンドルを動かして上限を超える場合、もう一方のハンドルを押しのけず、上限ギリギリで停止（意図しない範囲移動を防止）
- 不正状態（duration <= 0）は no-op

### `VideoTrimView` 更新
- 2本の `Slider` と表示専用 `timelineBar` / `handleMark` を撤去
- `VideoTrimmerBar` に `@Binding` で startTime/endTime を渡す
- 30秒超過警告（`durationExceeds30s` / `duration_warning`）を削除（操作で防止するため不要）
- 既存の `TrimPreviewer` によるプレビュー再生はそのまま動作

## テスト

`TrimRangeTests`: 23件（全緑）
- 開始を終了より後にドラッグしても不正状態にならない
- 30秒を超える範囲を作れない
- 動画長 < 30秒のとき全範囲を選べる
- 動画長 0 / 極端に短い動画での境界
- ジェスチャ中の連続 onChanged シミュレート（30秒 cap が維持されること）

UI部分（ドラッグ操作、サムネイル表示、スクラブ）は実機/シミュレータでの目視確認が必要（Mac mini 環境では PhotosPicker の実動画選択が困難なため未実行）。
