author: jonahgabriel
body:
## Summary

Closes both halves of [OMN-15180](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-15180) (filed by the OMN-15159 build lane; blocks OMN-15170). Plan: `omni_home/docs/plans/2026-07-26-steel-node-dispatch-integration-plan.md`.

1. **Wire-model pin reachability.** `ModelDelegateSkillRequest` gains an optional `backend_id: str | None = None` field (additive; `frozen=True, extra="forbid"` preserved) and `HandlerDelegateSkill.handle()` threads it to `dispatch_port.dispatch(backend_id=...)`, reusing the OMN-15156 pin `LocalDelegationDispatchPort` already implements (`resolve_delegation_backend(task_type, backend_id=...)`, merged #1897). Before this PR the pin was unreachable from any wire-level caller (e.g. steel's `LlmBusDelegationClient`, OMN-15159).
   - `ProtocolDelegationDispatchPort` and `RuntimeDelegationDispatchPort` (the deployed-bus dispatch port) were updated to accept the new keyword so the shared handler call doesn't `TypeError` on the bus path.
   - The deployed bus path has no `backend_id` field on omnibase_core's `ModelDelegationRequest` and no pin support in `HandlerDelegationWorkflow` (`node_delegation_orchestrator`) — threading the pin across the bus boundary is a cross-repo change out of this ticket's scope. A non-None pin on that path now fails loudly with `NotImplementedError` instead of being silently dropped (the exact "pin drops at a hop" defect class this ticket exists to close).

2. **routing_tiers.yaml registration.** `local-coder-mlx` (registered as a `bifrost_delegation.yaml` backend by OMN-15155, merged omnimarket#1898) is added to the `local` tier's `models[]`, mirroring the sibling `local-coder`/`local-ds-v4-flash` entries, so task_type-based tier selection (`first_eligible_tier` → `backend_id_for_tier` → `_select_model_for_task`) can reach it too — not just the explicit `backend_id` pin. Declared after `local-coder` in file order so unpinned auto-selection is unchanged (verified by regression test).

Unblocks OMN-15170 (steel-side driver test proving a live call reaches `.200:8401`).

## Every hop the pin traverses

```
ModelDelegateSkillRequest.backend_id
  (src/omnimarket/models/delegation/wire/model_delegate_skill_request.py:126-141)
  -> HandlerDelegateSkill.handle() passes backend_id=request.backend_id
     (src/omnimarket/nodes/node_delegate_skill_orchestrator/handlers/handler_delegate_skill.py:318-323)
  -> ProtocolDelegationDispatchPort.dispatch(..., backend_id: str | None = None)
     (handler_delegate_skill.py:50-65, Protocol updated to match)
  -> LocalDelegationDispatchPort.dispatch(backend_id=...)  [bus-less local path, pre-existing OMN-15156 seam]
     (ports/port_local_delegation_dispatch.py:437-451)
     -> _resolve_initial_backend(task_type, backend_id=backend_id)
        (ports/port_local_delegation_dispatch.py:926-1004)
        -> resolve_delegation_backend(task_type, backend_id="local-coder-mlx")
           (routing/delegation_backend_resolution.py:319-330) -- resolves the EXACT
           pinned backend, bypassing tier_order selection entirely
  -> RuntimeDelegationDispatchPort.dispatch(backend_id=...)  [deployed-bus path]
     (ports/port_runtime_delegation_dispatch.py:81-104) -- a non-None pin raises
     NotImplementedError (fail-loud boundary; caught by HandlerDelegateSkill's
     existing except-Exception handler and surfaced as a "failed" response with
     the explicit reason, never a silent no-op)
```

Separately, routing_tiers.yaml half: `src/omnimarket/configs/routing_tiers.yaml` local tier `models[]` (new entry, mirrors `local-coder`) → parsed by `parse_delegation_config_yaml` → consumed by `first_eligible_tier`/`backend_id_for_tier`/`_select_model_for_task` in `node_delegation_routing_reducer`.

body:
## Summary
- Pi-hole's DHCP collector fetched active leases and static reservations as two independent lists, both appended to the same result. The poll engine persists one row per `(collector, ip)` via `INSERT OR IGNORE`, so whenever a reserved device was actually online, its active-lease entry landed first and the reservation entry was silently dropped — in-use static reservations showed up as `dhcp`, never `reserved`.
- Fixed by cross-referencing the static-host list against live leases before building the result, so a reserved IP always reports `state="reserved"` regardless of whether it currently holds a lease. Offline reservations (no current lease at all) now also surface correctly.
- Same class of bug fixed in the Infoblox collector: `binding_state STATIC` was mapped to `"active"` instead of `"reserved"`, and fixed addresses with no current lease transaction weren't queried at all (now also queries the `fixedaddress` WAPI object).
- Kea has the same underlying gap (no reservation query at all) but is left as a documented known limitation rather than an unverified fix, since it depends on the optional `host_cmds` hook and there's no live Kea server to verify the response shape against.

author: ulsklyc
body:
## Problem

`renderActivity()` in `public/pages/split-expenses.js` renders the label as
`` t(`splitExpenses.activityType.${item.type}`) `` with the raw type as fallback.
Two emitted types had no label, so the activity feed showed the bare key:

- `member_removed` (emitted by `server/routes/split-expenses.js` when a member is removed) was missing from every locale.
- The demo seed wrote `expense_added` and `settlement_added`, while the route emits `expense_created` and `payment_registered`, so the demo feed showed `splitExpenses.activityType.expense_added`.

## Changes

- **Locales (23 files):** add `member_removed` and `group_unarchived`. Wording is derived per locale from the existing `member_added` phrasing and the established restore vocabulary (`budget.unarchiveAccount`, `accountRestoredToast`), kept in the sentence shape of the neighbouring `group_archived` label. Inserted line-based with the surrounding indentation, no reserialization.
- **Seed:** `expense_added` -> `expense_created`, `settlement_added` -> `payment_registered`.
- **Test:** new guard in `test/test-frontend-audit.js` that extracts every activity type emitted by the route, the recurring scheduler and the demo seed, and asserts each has a label in all locales. Includes a `callArguments()` helper that splits calls into top-level arguments (nested calls and object literals keep their commas) and two safety nets: the type argument must be a string literal, and the extraction must yield at least 15 types so a broken signature match cannot make the assertion vacuous.

## Note for review

`group_unarchived` has no emitter on this branch yet; the key is added so the
in-flight unarchive endpoint does not land on a locale gap. The guard only
checks types that are actually emitted, so it stays green either way.

## Verification

- `npm run test:frontend-audit` 148/148
- `npm run test:split-expenses-routes` 58/58
- `npm run test:i18n-plural` 8/8
- Negative checks: removing `member_removed` from `de.json` or reverting the seed to `expense_added` makes the new guard fail.
- All 23 locales carry the same 16 activity types, no gaps and no extras.

author: erkjprz
body:
## Summary
- A signed-in auth user with no matching `members` row (e.g. from a partial signup failure) bounced forever between `/login` and `/dashboard`, since each blindly redirected to the other based on `user` presence alone. `/login` now also checks `member`, and shows a recoverable "account setup didn't finish" message with a Sign Out option instead of looping.
- Root cause: signup was two separate writes — `supabase.auth.signUp()` then a client-side `members` insert — with no rollback if the second failed. Signup now passes `name`/`role` through `signUp`'s `options.data` (stored in `auth.users.raw_user_meta_data`), and a new `on_auth_user_created` trigger (`handle_new_member_signup`) creates the matching `members` row in the same DB transaction. If that insert fails (e.g. a duplicate email), the whole `auth.users` insert rolls back with it — no orphaned auth user, no orphaned member row.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean

body: ## Summary Fixes a family membership limit bypass introduced in PR #803 and a related pre-existing gap in invite acceptance. ## Bug and impact Family memberships are capped at 10 sub-accounts. PR #803 changed `count_sub_accounts/1` to trust a preloaded `sub_accounts` association instead of querying the database. After #803 also began preloading `sub_accounts` on login, a primary user could keep a stale count and continue sending invites after the household was already at capacity. Separately, pending child invites were not counted toward the cap, so a primary with 0 linked members could send many invites and accept more than 10 sub-accounts over time. `accept_invite/2` also did not re-check the cap before creating the sub-account. Impact: unauthorized extra family members gaining member access (bookings, events, etc.) under a single family plan. ## Root cause - `FamilyInvites.count_sub_accounts/1` used `length(preloaded sub_accounts)` when loaded (#803 perf regression). - Invite validation only compared existing sub-accounts to `@max_sub_accounts`, ignoring pending child invites. - `accept_invite/2` never re-validated the cap inside its transaction. - `Accounts.admin_link_user_to_family/3` used `length(get_sub_accounts/1)`, which has the same stale-preload pattern. ## Fix - Always count sub-accounts from the database. - Count pending child invites toward reserved slots when creating invites. - Lock the primary user row and re-check the cap inside `accept_invite/2`. - Use a DB aggregate for the admin link cap check. ## Validation - Added regression tests for stale preload, pending-invite cap, and accept-time cap enforcement. - `mix test test/ysc/accounts/family_invites_test.exs` (new/updated cases) passes.

author: positonic
body:
## What

The `../mastra` half of exponential's **V2: Ideate features from chat** (ticket `crisp.vapor`). Adds an `ideate-features` tool that makes "ideate features from this meeting, focus on the ingestion parts" reachable from chat.

**No second write path.** The tool calls the same tRPC procedure the meeting-page button uses — `transcription.generateDraftFeatures` (shipped in exponential #429) — which runs the deterministic ideation service server-side and stores **DRAFT** rows only. Nothing reaches the product backlog until the human accepts in the review card. The tool never creates Features or Tickets itself.

## The registration trap

The tool is registered on **both** brains, which is the failure mode this work exists to avoid — a tool present in a tools map but absent from the agent's instruction tool-list is silently never called. So for each of `assistant-agent.ts` and `zoe-agent.ts`:

- added `ideateFeaturesTool` to the tools map (`assistantTools` / `zoeTools`),
- named it in the agent's instruction tool-list, and
- added a usage-pattern row so the model knows when to reach for it.

Plus the `index.ts` re-export.

## Contract with exponential

- Tool id is exactly **`ideate-features`** — the exponential client keys off this string to render the `draft-features` review card. Renaming it silently drops the card.
- Input: `transcriptionId` (required) + `focus` (optional free-text steer). The `focus` is threaded into the extraction prompt on the exponential side (fenced as untrusted data, not instructions).
- Access is authorized server-side; the procedure throws BAD_REQUEST / FORBIDDEN / NOT_FOUND, which surface as tool errors so the model reports the real reason.

Paired exponential PR: **#429 shipped V1**; the V2 client card + focus threading go in a separate exponential PR on branch `crisp.vapor-v2-ideate-features-from-chat-conversational-path`.

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: the new/changed files are clean. (6 pre-existing errors remain in `matrix-gateway.ts` / `matrix-format.ts` / `calendar-tools.test.ts` — missing `marked` / `matrix-js-sdk` deps, unrelated to this change.)

author: antstanley
body:
> Stacked on #64.

Rust 1.97.0 → **1.97.1** (the current stable, a point release), and the end of the pin duplication that made bumping it a five-file chore.

## The drift

The channel was written in **six** places: `rust-toolchain.toml`, the workspace `rust-version`, and five workflow steps. One of those five carried the comment *"channel comes from rust-toolchain.toml"* directly above a hardcoded `1.97.0`.

It never did. Nothing would have noticed if they disagreed, and a deploy building on a different compiler than CI tested is the kind of thing you find out about afterwards.

## One place, parsed

`.github/actions/rust` is now the only place CI sets up Rust. It **parses** the channel out of `rust-toolchain.toml`, adds the wasm32 target, installs `wasm-pack`, and restores the cargo cache. Callers pass only the extras they need:

```yaml
      - name: Rust toolchain (wasm32), wasm-pack and the cargo cache
        uses: ./.github/actions/rust
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt
          tools: just,nextest
```

Five copies of a ten-line block collapse to five one-line `uses:`. `wasm-pack@0.15.0` was also copied five times and is now pinned once, in that action, since it is the only thing that installs it.

## The half a parse cannot fix

`rust-version` in `server/Cargo.toml` declares the MSRV separately, and can quietly fall a minor behind the channel while promising support for a compiler nobody builds with. `just guard-toolchain` asserts the two agree and joins `check`.

Falsified before committing, because a guard that cannot fail is worse than none:

```
$ sed -i 's/rust-version = "1.97"/rust-version = "1.96"/' server/Cargo.toml
$ just guard-toolchain
guard-toolchain: rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.97.1 but server/Cargo.toml declares MSRV 1.96
error: recipe `guard-toolchain` failed with exit code 1
```

## Local tools

Drifting the other way: local `wasm-pack` was 0.13.1 against CI's 0.15.0, which is why every `just wasm` printed an upgrade warning. Now 0.15.0 here too, and `rustup` picks up 1.97.1 straight from the toml.

`wasm-pack` 0.15.0 is already the latest release, and `just`/`nextest` are installed unpinned in CI, so neither had a version to bump.

## Verification

On 1.97.1: `just check` (all six gates), a fresh `just wasm`, the Playwright smoke, `cargo metadata --locked`, and every workflow plus the new action parsed as YAML. Pushed with `just push`.

## Still broken, and not the toolchain

`just test-wasm` fails locally. The driver starts, gets `SIGKILL`, and the runner sees a 404 on the session handshake: `wasm-bindgen-test-runner` 0.2.126 against a ChromeDriver **151** newer than the installed Chrome **150**. The repo pins none of those three, so there is nothing here to fix. Recorded as an open question in `10-build-release-deploy.md` instead, because it means the browser-only Rust paths are CI-only coverage for anyone in that state. CI runs the lane green.

No changeset: nothing a visitor can see.

author: ghackett
body:
## Summary

Adds a second terminal panel to every terminal tab: a plain shell with **no agent auto-launched**, sitting either **below** or **to the right** of the agent terminal.

- **Two small OSD buttons** float in the bottom-right corner of the window (visible whenever a terminal tab is selected):
  - 🖥 toggles the panel (same as **Ctrl+J**),
  - ↻ swaps it between the bottom and the right edge — shown **only while a panel is open**.
- **The shell survives a swap**: the panel and the agent terminal live in a `Gtk.Paned` (wide handle in both layouts), and swapping just flips the paned's orientation — no reparenting, no respawn.
- **Last-used mode is the app-wide default**: the chosen position (bottom/right) persists in settings, and any panel opened next — in any tab, new or existing — starts in the last-swapped mode.
- **Panel sizes**: each layout's panel size is remembered per tab while the app runs (swapping back and forth always returns to the same two spots; hide/show restores them). The last-*set* size per layout (`panel_size_bottom` / `panel_size_right`, stored as the panel's px size so it transfers across window sizes) persists app-wide: dragging a divider updates it (debounced, only the dragged mode is written), and every panel opened afterwards — any tab, or after a restart — defaults to it, falling back to ~1/3 of the paned when unset.
- **Worktree-aware working directory**: when the panel is shown, the agent terminal's *current* cwd is resolved best-effort — foreground process via `tcgetpgrp` + `/proc/<pid>/cwd` (catches an agent that moved into a worktree), falling back to the shell's cwd, then the tab's starting directory. The panel's shell spawns there; on later shows, if the shell is sitting idle at a prompt and the agent has moved, a `cd` is fed in (prefixed with kill-line so half-typed input isn't corrupted). A busy panel is never interrupted.
- The panel spawns **lazily** on first show; hiding it keeps the shell alive. Typing `exit` in the panel hides it, and the next show spawns a fresh shell.
- **Close protection (tab)**: closing a tab while a command runs in its panel shell (even a hidden panel) reveals the panel and asks for confirmation before the job is killed — there's no graceful exit for an arbitrary command, unlike the agent's `/exit`. Confirming continues with the normal graceful agent close.
- **Close protection (window)**: closing the window via the titlebar X with busy sessions shows a **single confirmation** covering all of them, then drains every tab through the existing graceful-close flow (`/exit` per agent, 12s force fallback each) and closes the window once the last tab is gone. Pressing X again mid-drain force-closes. With nothing running, the window closes immediately as before.

## Notes

- Ctrl+J is intercepted at the window level (capture phase), so it works while the terminal has focus; the raw Ctrl+J byte no longer reaches the agent CLI — same trade-off as the existing window shortcuts.
- cwd detection uses Linux `/proc`; on other platforms it degrades to the tab's starting directory.
- `dialogs.confirm_dialog` gains an optional `on_dismiss` hook (and now sets `close_response`, so Esc cancels).
- Per-session divider persistence was tried and replaced by the app-wide last-set sizes above; stale `panel_positions` keys in existing `state.json` files are ignored.

## Testing

- `ruff check claude_session_manager/ tests/` clean (pre-existing E501s in `po/generate.py` / `scripts/` untouched).
- `python3 -m pytest` — 88 passed, including new tests for the panel-size settings.
- Modules import cleanly against GTK4/VTE.

author: 0-jake-0
body:
## Summary

Closes the **Gate 2 `graph_node` tail** — the last open item in the node catalog — by porting classic `graph_node`'s thread-offload combinators. Getting the map form to work in historical mode required fixing the channel source's historical read first, which is a worthwhile change on its own.

### 1. Incremental historical channel read (replaces block-collect)

The channel source's historical path previously **block-collected the entire feed into memory at `start()`** (a documented deviation: unbounded memory, and it deadlocked any producer that depends on the receiving graph's own output). It's replaced with an incremental, timestamp-gated **one-ahead** read — classic `ChannelReceiverStream`'s "block-while-behind / non-block-once-caught-up" loop (`interp.rs::pump_historical`).

- Every channel now has **bounded (one-ahead) decode memory** instead of a second full copy.
- A concurrent producer↔consumer no longer deadlocks — which is exactly what makes historical `spawn_map` possible.
- Results stay **byte-identical**: guarded by the existing channel / `produce_async` / `consume_async` / csv parity suites (all green).

### 2. `graph_node` → `spawn` / `spawn_map`

next's ergonomic twins of classic `producer()` / `mapper()`:

- **`SourceOps::spawn`** — run a producer sub-graph on a worker thread. The worker builds and runs its own graph at run start (under the driving run's inherited mode + bound) and forwards timestamped values over the channel layer.
- **`StreamOps::spawn_map`** — map an input stream through a worker sub-graph. The two graphs run concurrently, lock-step by graph time.

Both run in **both** run modes. Historical replay is deterministic — values **and** tick times match classic's `graph_node_works` oracle.

### 3. Opt-in bounded buffer / back-pressure

The transport was hardwired to an unbounded std mpsc (a fast producer could queue an unbounded backlog). Added an opt-in bound following the `produce_async_bounded` precedent — `Option<usize>`: `None` = unbounded (default), `Some(n)` = `sync_channel(n)`, so a producer outrunning the graph **blocks** on `send`.

- New surface: `SourceOps::channel_bounded` / `spawn_bounded` / `StreamOps::spawn_map_bounded` (the latter bounds both worker channels). The plain `channel`/`spawn`/`spawn_map` are now thin `None`-delegates.
- `ChannelSender` holds either an unbounded `Sender` or a bounded `SyncSender` (private `Tx` enum); the receive side and the incremental read are untouched.
- **Caveat (documented):** a bounded transport must not be used by a producer that fills the buffer *before the run starts* (`replay_results`, csv, `postgres_read`) — with no running consumer to drain it, a bounded send blocks at wiring. Those keep the unbounded path.

### Engine plumbing

- `channel_triggered` / `channel_lockstep` receiver variants (read-ahead decoupled from the drive mode) for the `spawn_map` output and worker-input channels.
- `Kernel::run_for()` accessor + `Builder::source_at_start_with_params` / `compose_spawn_at_start`, so a worker learns the run params at start (they don't exist at wiring).

## Test plan

- `tests/spawn.rs`: spawn / spawn_map × historical / realtime (historical asserts exact values **and** tick times), plus a bounded spawn+spawn_map test that matches the unbounded result.
- `tests/channel.rs`: a concurrent producer exceeding the bound back-pressures yet replays losslessly and deterministically.
- `wingfoil-next` default + `async` suites: green (58 test binaries). Classic `wingfoil` kernel tests: green.
- `cargo clippy` clean on every feature path this touches (default, `async`, `csv`); `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- `examples/spawn.rs` runs and prints the expected deterministic output.

> Note: `cargo lint-all` can't complete in the CI sandbox without CMake/clang (the aeron/iceoryx2/fluvio adapters) — unrelated to this change, which is all default-feature engine code plus the shared kernel.

## Docs

- `port-plan.md`: Phase 2 `graph_node` entry marked ✅; Phase 3 threading note updated.
- `deviation-register.md`: new **B6** (`spawn_map` lock-step caveat) + a **Resolved** note for the block-collect → incremental read, including the new opt-in back-pressure surface.

author: arutemu64
body:
## What & why

A review of the agent-skills setup, plus three things it surfaced along the way: the app addressed users two different ways, a policy line was deciding something it should have been asking, and several doc claims had gone stale.

### Skills

`npx skills update -p` across all 28 lock-managed skills, then a pass over whether each still earns its place.

Removed two:

* **`tailwind-css-patterns`** — written against Tailwind v3 (`tailwind.config.js` for tokens; we are CSS-first `@theme` on v4.3.3), illustrated with React `className`, and its sample card is `rounded-lg shadow-lg` with a `bg-indigo-600` button — indigo, over-rounding and an oversized shadow, three tells `kill-ai-slop` hunts and PRODUCT.md's anti-references rule out.
* **`pwa-development`** — auto-loaded via its `paths:` globs on every touch of `service-worker.ts` or `manifest.json`, then injected 960 Workbox-centric lines with no mention of `$service-worker`. Our SW is SvelteKit's own.

Added three: **`sqlalchemy-alembic-expert-best-practices-code-review`** (the async SQLAlchemy + Alembic half of the backend had no skill at all — the half AGENTS.md already warns about), plus **`accessibility`** (WCAG 2.2) and **`core-web-vitals`** for a mobile-first PWA used on venue wifi. All three are markdown-only, no scripts.

Kept `test-driven-development`, `using-git-worktrees` and `finishing-a-development-branch` despite each contradicting this repo's workflow: they are required sub-skills of `executing-plans`, `writing-plans` and `subagent-driven-development`, so removing them would leave dangling sub-skill calls. AGENTS.md now states that it wins where a vendored skill disagrees.

Two project-local skills for what upstream cannot know: **`fanfan-migrations`** and **`fanfan-russian-copy`**. A third, `fanfan-pwa`, was written and then dropped — `docs/frontend.md` §2 already documented the caching split in more depth, so it was a third copy of the same knowledge and the one least likely to be in the diff when the SW changes. Its three genuinely-absent facts moved into §2 instead.

### Doc accuracy

Four claims turned out to be stale. Each was true when written, which is the point — none were careless, and review had passed them all:

* **`docs/backend.md`** documented ORM enum columns as native `postgresql.ENUM(...)`. There are none in this schema — `str_enum_column()` maps every StrEnum to VARCHAR + CHECK with `native_enum=False`.
* **`docs/backend.md`** gave the reason autogenerate misses enum-member changes as ENUM label changes. The real mechanism is that Alembic does not diff CHECK constraint *bodies*, which is why such a migration comes out **empty** rather than wrong — a meaningfully different failure mode, since nothing looks broken.
* **`AGENTS.md`** said "Tests are not a gate", but `.github/workflows/ci.yml:125` runs `uv run pytest tests`. The existing suite has always been a merge gate.
* **`AGENTS.md`**'s codebase map put the outbox relay under `presentation/scheduler/`. It is registered in `main/scheduler.py:41`, deliberately apart from the cron definitions in `presentation/scheduler/jobs.py` because it runs on an `IntervalTrigger` — "so delivery latency is seconds, not minutes" — which the cron-only `get_job_definitions` cannot express. The map sent readers to the wrong file for the one job whose timing is load-bearing.

Also adds `just backend-check-migrations` to the command table; it is a gate and was the only one missing.

The rest of AGENTS.md was audited and holds — see "How tested".

### Testing policy

`docs/testing.md` opened with "Tests are optional, not mandatory on every change", which answered the question before it was asked, and answered it *no*. That is now a decision to make per change, with criteria concrete enough to make it: write a test when the change encodes a rule that can break silently (a permission, a state transition, an ordering or time calculation, a parser, a bug just fixed); skip it for copy, styling, config, and refactors an existing test covers; on a close call, write it. Adding a *new* test is discretionary; keeping the current suite green is not.

### Copy

The skill work surfaced that the app addressed the user two ways. `frontend/src/` was overwhelmingly «ты» with nine «вы» strings across four files, including a whole formal block on the feedback screen; the four email templates were uniformly «вы». Both are now «ты», and email greets with `Привет`. `Расписание` → `Программа` removes the last competing word for the programme (it was 1 against 11).

One line could not convert word-for-word: `Если вы не запрашивали это письмо` is gender-neutral only because «вы» past tense is. «ты» forces `запрашивал`/`запрашивала` on a mixed-gender audience, so it was rephrased out of the past tense — `Если это письмо пришло по ошибке, просто проигнорируй его.`

## Type of change
- [x] Backend
- [x] Frontend
- [x] Docs / infra

## How tested

* `just frontend-lint` and `just frontend-check` after the frontend copy changes — 2832 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
* `just backend-lint` (incl. import-linter: 2 contracts kept) and `just backend-typecheck` after the email templates.
* All four email templates rendered through the real `create_jinja_env` + `JinjaTemplateRenderer` with the interactors' own context dicts, covering both branches of the `{% if username %}` conditional — layout inheritance and autoescape unaffected, output correct at both TTLs (15 and 60 минут).
* Verified no dangling references: nothing names a removed skill, every skill named in AGENTS.md / rules / docs exists, `skills-lock.json` and `.agents/skills/` agree, no broken symlinks in `.claude/skills/`.
* AGENTS.md claims checked against the codebase: all 21 named `just` recipes exist, every path in the map exists (incl. the six `lib/` submodules), all eight linked docs and both named sections resolve, `secrets/` PEMs are gitignored and mounted `:ro` in all three compose services, `uv.lock` records the project version (so the bump procedure is right), `frontend/package.json` is at `0.0.0`, `v*` tags publish GHCR images, and `just ci` is step-for-step what `ci.yml` runs.
* Confirmed nothing in tests or docs asserted on the old copy.

No new tests here, by the criterion this PR introduces: the changes are copy, docs and skill files, with no rule that can break silently.

## Checklist
- [x] User-facing copy in Russian; code comments in English
- [x] Lint & types pass (`just backend-lint` / `just frontend-lint`, `just backend-typecheck` / `just frontend-check`)
- [ ] UI checked on a narrow screen (mobile-first)
- [x] Docs updated (AGENTS.md / docs/) if paths or architecture changed

**On the unchecked box:** no visual check was run. The frontend changes are text-only substitutions inside existing components, and every «ты» form is shorter than the «вы» form it replaced (`Введи` < `Введите`, `Выбери` < `Выберите`, `Напиши` < `Напишите`), as is `Программа` < `Расписание` — so no string grew. Worth a glance at the feedback and broadcast forms anyway, since those changed most.

## Two gaps found but not changed

Both are CI coverage, not doc bugs, and closing them is your call:

* **`just backend-import-lint` does not run in CI.** It is what enforces the first "Never" in AGENTS.md — the layering rule. `ci.yml` runs ruff, ty, pytest, the frontend trio and hadolint; no import-linter. The rule is enforced only by a developer running `just backend-lint` locally, so nothing blocks a violating merge.
* **`just backend-check-migrations` does not run in CI either**, so ORM/migration drift is not caught automatically.

Adding both to `ci.yml` is a small change if you want it in this PR or a follow-up.

## Note on versioning

No version bump here — `backend/pyproject.toml` is untouched, per AGENTS.md. If you want one, **PATCH** is the right call: no manual deploy steps, no schema or contract changes, and the only runtime-visible difference is user-facing copy.

author: jdc9111
body:
## Summary
On mobile, result cards were rendering ~8px narrower per side than the search bar and example chips above them (343px vs 351px), making the cards look inset/shrunk rather than filling the width.

Root cause: `body` is a column flex container, and `main` had `margin: 24px auto`. In flexbox, auto side-margins on the cross axis override the default `align-items: stretch` behavior — so instead of stretching to fill available width, `main` was shrink-fitting to content and centering itself, while `.search-bar` (a plain sibling, not affected by this) stretched normally.

Fix: on mobile only, override `main`'s side margins to 0 and match its padding to the search bar's 12px, so `main` (and the cards inside it) stretch to the same width as everything else. Desktop centering via `max-width: 960px` is unaffected since the override is scoped to the `max-width: 640px` media query.

## Test plan
- [x] Verified card width now exactly matches the search bar's content width (351px) and shares the same left edge on a 375px viewport
- [x] Verified desktop table/layout centering is unchanged at 1200px width

author: wtomas
body:
## Why

Agents authoring prompt templates via the `sufleur skill` markdown regularly omit `{{@type}}`/`{{@doc}}`/`{{@optional}}` unless explicitly asked. The directives were only mentioned in the render step's notes — framed as "render to empty strings", i.e. ignorable metadata — and there was no correct authoring pattern to copy, so even agents that remembered them misplaced section directives or invented invalid types like `string[]`.

## What

- New subsection under **step 2 (Edit files locally)** — the point where files are actually written — making annotations part of authoring: the stakes (a bare `{{variable}}` generates `unknown` in TS / `Any` in Python), placement rules (directives immediately after a variable; opening the section body for sections), the valid type set, one worked example, and a pre-push self-check.
- Slimmed the render-step note to cross-reference the new section, keeping the caveat that `{{@doc}}` never reaches the rendered prompt.

## Verification

- The example in the new section renders cleanly through `sufleur prompt render` (directives strip from output).
- Tested with 5 fresh-context agent runs on the same authoring task (annotations never mentioned): both old-skill baseline runs produced untyped array items, one with invalid `string[]` and directives placed outside the section; all three amended-skill runs produced fully and correctly annotated templates.

body:
## 摘要

2026-07-26 防御系统全链路审计落案，docs-only，新增两份 skeleton plan（`docs/plans-skeleton/`）：

### 1. plan-bughunt-guangbo-defense-accum-v1（潜伏 critical，供 bugfix loop 认领）

广播体操四肢防御加成每 tick 向 `DerivedAttrs.defense_profile` 做 `+=`（`body_conditioning.rs:169-181`），唯一重置点是 `Changed<PlayerInventory>` 护甲重扫——不换装即无限叠加直到撞 `ARMOR_MITIGATION_CAP=0.85`。设计上限 +0.5%（`LIMB_DEFENSE_BONUS_MAX=0.005`），实际 85% 全伤型减伤，偏差 170 倍。对照组铁证：同函数 move_speed/jump 因 `attribute_aggregate_tick` 重置清单（`status.rs:171-175`）而幂等，`defense_profile` 是清单唯一漏项。**当前被 r10-findings P1 熟练度断裂掩盖（生产 prof 恒 0），r10 P1 修复即引爆——两者有落地顺序硬约束，已写入 plan。**

### 2. plan-defense-hardening-v1（六阶段结构性加固）

| 阶段 | 主题 |
|------|------|
| P0 | 跨源全局减伤 cap：剑格 0.95×盾格 0.95×护甲 0.85×丹药 0.95 自由叠乘，理论残余 1.875e-5 = 事实免疫；减伤后无 severity floor |
| P1 | 统一旁路伤害入口：17 处绕过 `resolve_attack_intents` 直写 `health_current`（13 处无 GameMode 门，创造模式照样被天劫/阵法反噬/炸炉扣血）；`resolve_attack_intents` 已 12842 行 + 16/16 SystemParam 顶满，旁路是被单体逼出来的 |
| P2 | 攻击侧真元守恒：`qi_invest` 扣费无 zone 归还（同文件截脉/锻体/天劫都做了回灌，唯独最大流量路径没做）+ `NpcMelee` 反作弊白名单纯豁免无预扣 = 凭空铸造 |
| P3 | 防御失败反馈闭环：`DefenseKind` 只有成功变体；`ParrySuccessEvent` 施法瞬间假 emit（真实成功点 `resolve.rs:1150` 不发）；举盾吞截脉零提示。A/V 规格已按实施精度内联 |
| P4 | 护甲客户端数据同源化：straw 材质缺注册（新手第一件甲隐形+tooltip 空白，根因 PR #250 一行 Java 没碰）；iron 8/200↔12/280 漂移（tooltip 骗人 33%）；CrossCheck 单向抓不到 |
| P5 | 旋钮与死参数收口：damage_mul 全 1.0 且 qi 分支不乘、dash iframe 死参数、木盾污染削减数值复核 |

## 核验方法

全部锚点经两轮独立 read-only Explore agent 对抗核验（very thorough），含四处对审计初稿的**证伪/订正**并已写入 plan：截脉不削 severity 只削污染（`resolve.rs:1442-1443` 自证）、NPC 截脉不对称真因是 `qi_current=0` 双真元门而非 client 通道依赖、woliu 扣血真实位置 `woliu_v2/skills.rs:650`（初稿 `:459` 证伪）、木盾削污染有 worldview §五 L432 正典背书非 bug。

## 去重

与既有 9 项 plan 显式划界（plan 内有专节）：r10-findings P0 破盾泄漏、npc-combat-gear-v2（NPC 穿甲 B 路线已拍板）、module-wiring-gaps-v2 T13（armor OBJ 渲染）、neardeath-ux-v1、combat-event-juice、shield-feedback-network-thread-ui、layered-equip-v1（护甲域 cap owner）、npc-daily-life-qi-mint、远端护甲 wire 字段（无人认领，登记 §8 #6 建议独立 plan）。`plan-defense-*` 命名全 docs 零冲突。

## 模型署名

主导 + 两轮核验 Explore agent：claude-fable-5

author: asheshgoplani
body:
## Summary

Closes the incident class where a leaked tmux control client took down the whole session fleet. Three linked defects, all reproduced and pinned by tests that fail on `main`.

**The defect.** `OpenKeySender` spawned a **bare** `tmux -C`. A control-mode client with no command falls back to `new-session`, so every insert-mode entry minted an extra session with a live shell pane — one pty apiece — that `Close()` never killed. Verified on an isolated socket:

```
sessions before                    tgt
sessions after bare `tmux -C`      1, tgt      <- implicit session created
sessions after killing the client  1, tgt      <- and it outlives the client
```

That is the accumulation failure: these orphans, alongside leaked test servers, drove a host to 507/511 ptys, after which every attach failed with `fork failed: Device not configured`.

It is also an **identity** failure. On macOS a process keeps the argv it was exec'd with, so the default socket's server — auto-started by one of these bare clients — was itself named exactly `tmux -C`. A maintenance job matching `pgrep -fx "tmux -C"` hit that server and every live session on it died at once. **Argv is not identity.**

## Changes

**`internal/tmux/keysender.go` — attach explicitly**

```go
cmd := tmuxExec(socket, "-C", "attach-session", "-t", target)
```

Nothing is created, and the argv names its command. Mirrors `controlpipe.go:113`, the existing sanctioned control-client spawn. Attaching imposes no resize on the target (confirmed 200x50 before, during, and after attach on tmux 3.7b) — control-mode clients only take a size if they ask via `refresh-client -C`, which this one never does.

Two changes fall out. The attach can now fail, so `Open` reads tmux's `%begin`/`%end` handshake and errors on `%error`/`%exit`, letting callers degrade to the per-call `send-keys` path instead of holding a dead client. And the child runs in its own process group so `Close` tears down the whole subtree, reusing the existing `reapWithEOFGrace` EOF-then-signal escalation rather than an unconditional `Kill`.

**Teardown: kill through the socket you spawned on**

Two teardown paths reported success while leaving a live server behind, which is why both went unnoticed.

- `testutil.IsolateTmuxSocket` / `ShortTmuxSocket` went straight to `RemoveAll`, under a comment claiming the kernel cleaned up after the server. It does not. Unlinking a Unix socket never signals its listener: the server keeps running, keeps its panes and their ptys, and is now unreachable by every socket path in existence. Both now kill first via a shared `KillTmuxServersUnder`, addressing each server by absolute `-S <path>` with a `TMUX*`-scrubbed env.
- The `#1031` launch-race teardown had the mirror-image bug: its subprocesses strip `TMUX*`, so their `-L <socket>` lands under tmux's default base, while teardown inherited the package `TestMain`'s isolated `TMUX_TMPDIR` and looked elsewhere. `kill-server` found nothing, said so, and the error was dropped with `_ =`. **Measured before this change: a passing run left 2 servers and 6 live panes behind.** Teardown now shares the subprocesses' exact env, checks the error, and fails the test if a server outlives it.
- `issue1031_socket_leak_test.go` seeded its simulated leak with the test process's own env, so it rehearsed a reap on a socket path production never uses — it would have kept passing while real leaks piled up.

**`scripts/reap-stale-tmux.sh` — socket path only, now in the repo**

Candidates are socket paths from the two conventions only tests produce (`ad1031-*`, and the `ad-tmux-*` / `ad-sock-*` per-run dirs). Each is probed with `tmux -S <sock> list-sessions` — the call that identifies the server also proves it is reachable — and killed through that same path. No `pgrep`, no `pkill`, no pid, no name match anywhere. The default socket is excluded explicitly and by construction; the high-pty warning is kept; `DRY_RUN=1` is supported.

**Closing the class structurally: tests can no longer reach the default socket at all**

The three isolation layers that existed all reason about `$TMUX`, and the guard treated "`$TMUX` is unset" as safe — *"there's no inherited socket to leak onto"*. tmux does not need `$TMUX`: with no `-S`, no `-L` and no `TMUX_TMPDIR` it resolves to `<tmpdir>/tmux-<uid>/default` on its own. So a package whose `TestMain` forgot to isolate, or a test that scrubs `TMUX*` from an env to simulate a detached child, reached the real server while every existing check reported success — and one `kill-server` on that path ends every live session on the machine. That is the same fleet-death class as the argv bug above, arrived at from the other direction, and it is the one a future contributor is most likely to reintroduce.

`tmuxExec` / `tmuxExecContext` now mirror tmux's own socket resolution (`-S` > `-L` > `$TMUX` > default, resolved under `TMUX_TMPDIR`) and panic — before the subprocess exists — when a test binary's spawn would target the user's default server. The panic names the offending argv and the fix. It runs at the argv factory, so it covers every socket-aware spawn in the package; `TestNoRawTmuxExec_OutsideAllowlist` is what keeps call sites funnelled through there. There is deliberately no opt-out env var: a test that believes it needs the user's default server is the exact thing this refuses.

Scope is drawn at the socket whose loss is unrecoverable:

- Name-keyed servers in the same directory (the `-L ad1031-*` launch-race servers) are **allowed** — a distinct server, wasting a pty at worst, with its own teardown.
- The default-socket shape check does **not** require the socket to exist: a spawn that would *create* the user's default server must be refused too.
- The `$TMUX` branch **does** require a real listening socket, because `$TMUX` is also a value tests fabricate to exercise parsing (`/tmp/tmux-1000/default`, `/tmp/tmux-test.sock`). A path with no listener cannot be a live server.
- Command-level `-S` is not a socket path. `capture-pane -p -S -2000` and `refresh-client -S` would otherwise resolve a socket named `-2000`, so flag scanning stops at the tmux command.
- Inert outside `go test` binaries. Production is entitled to the default socket — that is the point of the empty-socket default (#697).

`testutil.IsolateTmuxSocket` additionally asserts its own post-condition: it refuses to hand back a `TMUX_TMPDIR` that is tmux's default base (or a `tmux-<uid>` dir inside it). Isolation that silently fails to isolate is worse than none, because cleanup then runs `kill-server` against whatever it finds under the "isolated" dir — making the isolation helper itself the thing that kills the fleet.

The guard's tests drive it through an injected env lookup instead of mutating `TMUX_TMPDIR` process-wide, since mutating it to rehearse a leak is itself a way to cause one. `TestTmuxExecUnderPackageIsolationDoesNotPanic` is the wiring canary: a false positive in the factory would not fail one test, it would panic every tmux-touching test in the repo.

**The isolation teardown window — found by the guard above, on CI**

Adding the guard turned up a live instance of the very thing it looks for. After the `internal/session` suite printed `PASS`, a leaked `Instance.watchForFastDeath` goroutine ran `tmux has-session` against `/tmp/tmux-<uid>/default`.

The window is `IsolateTmuxSocket`'s own cleanup. It restored `TMUX` / `TMUX_PANE` / `TMUX_TMPDIR`, on the reasoning that `go test` should not leave the developer's shell env altered. It never could — a child process cannot change its parent shell's environment — so the restore protected nothing, while the only reader of the restored values, the *still-running* test binary, got its tmux resolution pointed back at the live fleet for the rest of the process. `watchForFastDeath` polls for 15s at 250ms; the suite that starts it finishes in under 3s, and `t.Cleanup`'s `tmuxSession.Kill()` does not bump the spawn generation the watcher ch

author: kiyoaki
body:
## Summary

Closes the last two lifecycle follow-ups deferred by the 2026-07-26 refactor review, plus the
VSTest session-hook question. All three needed a decision rather than a drive-by fix; the owner
delegated those decisions and the rulings recorded below are what this PR implements.

## 1. Session-scoped hook parity

Session hooks were the only lifecycle scope whose exceptions escaped unwrapped:
`ExecuteSessionSetupAsync` and `ExecuteSessionTeardownAsync` in `NextUnitFramework` let a user
hook's throw propagate out of the Microsoft.Testing.Platform callback, while assembly and class
scopes catch, classify, and report it.

The hooks move into a new `SessionLifecycleRunner`. Ruling on the reported shape, per phase:

- A setup hook throwing `TestSkippedException` records a session skip reason, and every test in
  the session is reported skipped with it. This mirrors `_assemblySkipReason` in
  `TestExecutionEngine`. The skip is swallowed inside the `AsyncOnceGate` operation, so the gate
  records setup as completed and no later caller re-runs the user's hooks -- retrying a hook that
  already decided to skip would be wrong. `AsyncOnceGate`'s publish-on-success-only contract is
  unchanged and still directly tested.
- Any other setup failure is caught outside the gate, which leaves the gate open exactly as before,
  and is surfaced through `CreateTestSessionResult` (`IsSuccess=false` plus `ErrorMessage`) instead
  of crashing the host.
- Teardown catches per hook, so a failing hook no longer skips the remaining ones. Multiple
  failures are aggregated into an `AggregateException` and surfaced through
  `CloseTestSessionResult`. There is no per-test sink at session close, so the result object is the
  reporting channel; a synthetic node like assembly teardown's `[AssemblyTeardown]` is not
  available there.
- Both phases classify `OperationCanceledException` with `RunCancellationClassifier`, matching
  assembly teardown. Genuine run cancellation propagates as the exception the platform expects --
  in teardown only after the remaining hooks have run. A hook's own unrelated OCE is wrapped in a
  non-OCE and reported as a failure, so adapters cannot swallow it as cancellation. When a hook
  failure and run cancellation coexist at close, the failure wins the reporting channel.

## 2. RunAsync non-reentrancy guard

Ruling: keep the sequential-only execution model and upgrade the documented caller constraint on
`TestExecutionEngine.RunAsync` to an enforced precondition. Overlapping-run support is declined --
no evidence shows Microsoft.Testing.Platform issuing overlapping run requests, and both
alternatives (serializing runs per engine, or making assembly state run-local) change the
execution model.

`RunAsync` now claims a private `Interlocked` flag before it touches its arguments -- a claim taken
after the `testCases.ToList()` could be stranded by a throwing enumerable -- and throws
`InvalidOperationException` on overlap. The claim is released in a `finally` that wraps argument
enumeration, graph building, the run, and cleanup. `_assemblySetupLock` is deliberately not reused:
it is held only for the brief windows that touch the assembly flags. Parallelism within a single
run (`ParallelScheduler`, `Parallel.ForEachAsync`) is unaffected. No public API change;
`PublicAPI.*.txt` untouched.

## 3. VSTest session hooks

Ruling: session hooks stay Microsoft.Testing.Platform-only. VSTest executes per assembly with no
session boundary to attach them to, so wiring stays declined and the documented limitation on
`NextUnitTestExecutor` stands. Revisit only if a concrete need arises. No code change.

## Testing note

`SessionLifecycleRunner` is the test seam rather than `NextUnitFramework` itself: the framework's
session callbacks take platform context types with no public constructors, and driving them would
require overwriting the process-wide `GeneratedTestRegistryStore.Current` that the running test
host is itself using. The mapping from runner outcome to session result is a two-line ternary in
each callback.

## Validation

- `dotnet build NextUnit.slnx --configuration Release` -- 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `dotnet format NextUnit.slnx --verify-no-changes` -- clean
- `dotnet test --solution NextUnit.slnx --configuration Release --no-restore` --
  1104 total / 1094 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped (baseline on main: 1086 / 1076 / 0 / 10; this PR
  only adds tests)
- `markdownlint --config .markdownlint.json PLANS.md` -- clean

Codex reviewed the branch pre-push and converged. Its one finding (P2: session teardown dropped a
hook's genuine run cancellation, unlike assembly teardown which hands it back to `RunAsync`) is
fixed in the second commit and covered by tests.

<!-- 日本語でレビューをしてください -->

## 概要

ローカル開発用 Postgres（docker-compose.yml）が起動不能になっていたのを修正。

## 問題

- Renovate の digest 自動更新（直近 #392）で `postgres@sha256:…` が **PostgreSQL 18系** に到達
- 18系はデータ格納場所が変更されており、compose の `./postgres_dev:/var/lib/postgresql/data` マウントと非互換 → コンテナが即停止
- さらに既存ローカルデータは `PG_VERSION=16` のため、18系バイナリではそもそも動かない（メジャー間データ形式非互換）

## 修正

- `image: "postgres:16"` にタグ固定
- Renovate（config:best-practices の pinDigests）は今後16系タグ内で digest を pin するため、勝手にメジャーが上がる再発はなくなる。17/18系へのメジャー更新は別PRとして提示されるので、データ移行と合わせて手動判断できる

## 確認済み

- postgres:16 で既存データ（./postgres_dev）のままコンテナ起動 → `pg_isready` OK
- `/liver_register` からのライバー登録動作を確認（#418 の作業時）

author: sousuke0422
body:
## 背景

Argos は全 story を毎 build 撮影するため、月次のスクリーンショット枠を使い切った。
Chromatic の TurboSnap に相当する変更 story の自動検出が Argos には無い。
この PR は、変更のあった story だけを選んで撮影する仕組みを入れる。

議論の経緯は #449 にある。

## 何を入れたか

変更ファイルから影響を受ける story を算出する selector を追加した。
Storybook の index.json と、build 時に生成される preview-stats.json の依存グラフを突き合わせる方式である。
Chromatic の TurboSnap と同じ考え方に沿っている。

判定は FULL、PARTIAL、NONE の3値とした。
グラフの生成に失敗した場合、seed が解決できない場合、到達数を安全に算出できない場合は FULL へ倒す。
判断がつかないときに撮影を省くのではなく、全て撮る側へ倒れるため、見落としたまま緑になることはない。

依存更新の PR も selector を通す。
到達が 0 件であれば撮影しないが、その根拠を manifest に残す。
到達が 1 件でもあれば撮影し、VRT の結果を automerge の判断材料として残す。

## 構成

selector の中核はプロバイダに依存しない module として実装した。
Argos への出力は薄いアダプタに分離してある。
将来 self-host の VRT へ移す場合も、中核はそのまま再利用できる。

## baseline の解決

Argos が実際に比較した baseline commit は、公開 GraphQL の baseBuild と baseScreenshotBucket.commit から取得できる。
build 44 と build 43 の実データで確認した。
subset build が baseline 候補から除外される仕様であることも確認している。

この確証が取れるまで PARTIAL は無効にしていた。
baseline を推測で仮定すると比較対象がずれ、撮らなかった story の回帰が無音で通るためである。

## 検証

selector と adapter の contract テストが 9 件通る。
skip は 0 件である。

frontend の unit スイートは exit 0 で、skip は無い。
lint は frontend 3 ファイルと scripts 5 ファイルで warning 0、error 0 である。

build-storybook で 4467 module の依存グラフを生成し、story を 117 件へ正規化した。
docs entry は対象から除外される。
password-input を seed としたとき 16 story へ到達し、期待した集合と一致した。

撮影対象が 0 件になる経路も実際に動かし、manifest の記録と gate の通過を確認した。

## 今回のスコープ外

main への push は従来どおり全 story を撮影する。
PR 側の selector が取り落としたものを拾う最終防線として残した。
このため月次の消費は依然として枠を超える見込みである。

枠そのものの解消は別途扱う。
この PR は TurboSnap と同等の機能を入れるところまでを目的とする。

Part of #449

author: equationstratos
body:
Correction des écarts signalés entre `build.html` et `drone_viewer.html`.

## Cause

Le simulateur d'assemblage était un fichier **écrit à la main** (`gen_build.py`) où j'avais **ressaisi les coordonnées** au lieu de les reprendre du visualisateur. D'où :

- supports caméra mal placés (le viewer les monte sur un **pivot**, pas à une position brute) ;
- bumpers mal orientés (le viewer en fait **4 miroirs par signe d'échelle** + un back bumper, pas 4 copies positionnées) ;
- hélices sans le sens **CW/CCW** ni la translucidité ;
- antenne VTX non accrochée à son pivot arrière ;
- batterie = ancien maillage STL au lieu de la boîte procédurale **DOGCOM** (étiquette sur le dessus + bords arrondis) ;
- rendu et couleurs différents.

## Correction à la racine

`build.html` est désormais **la même page** que `viz/drone_viewer.html`, générée par **le même script**, avec le panneau d'assemblage activé par défaut. Le mode assemblage **réutilise les groupes déjà construits** par le viewer (leur `userData.home` = le vrai siège) : plus aucune pièce ni position n'est redéfinie, donc **la divergence est structurellement impossible**.

`gen_build.py` est supprimé (c'était la source du problème).

## Ce que ça apporte, comme demandé

- **Pièces, cotes, matériaux, couleurs et rendu identiques** au visualisateur.
- **Sélecteur de caméra** (O4 Lite / nano) et **sélecteur d'antenne VTX** (5 modèles) disponibles dans le simulateur.
- **21 sélecteurs de couleur** par pièce.
- Liste de gauche : **un clic surligne** la pièce en 3-D, **un double-clic l'emboîte** toute seule.
- Glisser-déposer, **Tout assembler**, **Éparpiller**, fantômes translucides conservés.

## Vérifié en navigateur

21 pièces · 0 → 1 au double-clic → 21 via « Tout assembler » · sélecteurs caméra + VTX présents · 21 color pickers · **0 erreur JS**.

## Variantes d'URL

| URL | Effet |
|---|---|
| `build/build.html` | simulateur d'assemblage (par défaut) |
| `build/build.html?nobuild=1` | même page, panneau masqué |
| `viz/drone_viewer.html?build=1` | le visualisateur avec le panneau d'assemblage |

author: shishir435
body:
Follow-up to #206. Four defects found reviewing the 0.12.4 error-reporting work end to end, plus the release notes it left behind. All are report-quality or cost, none block the release. ## Cost: one self-test run instead of one per bubble `getBundle` ran the full self-test suite unconditionally, and the error panel prepares a bundle on mount. The message list is virtualized, so a screenful of failures meant one repository transaction, two storage round-trips, one provider network probe, and one recorded diagnostic event **per visible failure** — the displayed errors diluted the ring buffer that exists to explain them. Results are now shared for 60s with in-flight join, and only a real execution records an event. Cancellation is preserved rather than traded away: the shared run owns its own `AbortController`, an aborting caller stops waiting immediately, and the underlying work is cancelled only once every interested caller has abandoned it. One client's RPC timeout can no longer kill another client's in-flight suite. `diagnostics.run` passes `force` — it is only reachable from pressing **Run self-tests**, which means measure now. ## Reports no longer contradict themselves `checks.providerEnabled` was inferred from a successful `listModels`. That is a different claim: discovery runs with `enabledOnly: false`, so it succeeds against a *disabled* provider. Real reports asserted `Provider enabled: yes` directly above a diagnostics line reading `disabled`. Now read from provider config via `providers.list`. Failure-path latency is kept — an instant refusal and a 30s timeout are different bugs — but labelled `(time to failure)` so it cannot be misread beside `reachable: no`. ## One draft composer, one entry point There were **four** issue-draft builders: the error panel, the footer's bare duplicate for the same message, the generic help draft, and a hand-rolled one in `diagnostics-settings.tsx` with no diagnostics paste block, no privacy statement, and no URL-length clamp — missing in the one place a reporter arrives already holding a bundle. All now share `REPORT_TAIL` and a `composeReportUrl` that keeps the length guarantee. `buildDiagnosticIssueUrl` moves into `error-report.ts` with its fields clamped, and its test moves with it. The footer's link is deleted. It rendered for exactly the messages that already show the panel, two rows below it, with no bundle and no local checks — the more discoverable button produced the weaker report. ## Stale recovery actions expire A week-old failure still offered a button that would flip a provider setting and drop a fresh response into the middle of that conversation. Actions that mutate config or append a turn now declare `maxAgeMs` (1h); read-only navigation declares none. Because resolution is first-match-wins, a stale in-place fix degrades to the settings deep link rather than to nothing. ## Release notes The 0.12.4 entry was written in #202, before #204 and #205/#206 landed, so the uninstall flow and the entire error-reporting feature were absent from it while sitting under `Unreleased`. Folded into one 0.12.4 entry and condensed to summary bullets. Process note: a release-notes commit that lands mid-line cannot describe the rest of the line. Worth a final pass at tag time. ## Verification - 271 test files / 2,220 tests pass - Biome check, format check, typecheck clean - New coverage: shared-run dedupe and abort isolation, config-read `providerEnabled`, stale vs fresh recovery resolution, labelled failure latency, diagnostics draft carrying the shared tail and staying inside the URL limit

Greptile Summary

This follow-up improves diagnostic accuracy, report consistency, and stale-action handling. - Forced self-test requests now start a fresh execution while automatic bundle requests share recent or in-flight results. - Diagnostic cache publication is sequence-guarded so older executions cannot replace newer measurements. - Provider state and failure latency are reported more accurately. - Issue-report entry points now share privacy, diagnostics, and URL-length safeguards. - Recovery actions that mutate state or append turns expire after one hour. - Release notes consolidate the completed 0.12.4 work.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge. No blocking failure remains; the forced diagnostics path starts its own execution, and sequence ordering prevents an older overlapping run from replacing its results.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/lib/diagnostics/diagnostics-service.ts | Adds TTL and in-flight sharing, isolated cancellation, unconditional fresh forced executions, and sequence-guarded cache publication. | | src/background/rpc-server.ts | Routes the user-triggered diagnostics run through the forced execution path. | | src/lib/error-report.ts | Consolidates report composition and adds diagnostic draft clamping and clearer failure-latency labeling. | | src/features/chat/lib/error-recovery-actions.ts | Expires state-changing recovery actions while preserving read-only settings navigation. | | src/features/chat/components/chat-error-report-action.tsx | Reads provider enabled state from configuration and supplies message age to recovery resolution. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant RPC as Diagnostics RPC participant S as DiagnosticsService participant A as Automatic bundle run participant F as Forced self-test run U->>RPC: Run self-tests RPC->>S: "run(signal, force=true)" S->>F: Start new sequenced execution Note over S,A: Existing automatic execution may continue F-->>S: Publish only if sequence is newest S-->>RPC: Fresh test results RPC-->>U: Display results A-->>S: Older result ignored for cache publication ```
Reviews (4): Last reviewed commit: ["docs(diagnostics): record why forced run..."](https://github.com/shishir435/ollama-client/commit/c8df2f7fa6d8b50b8c19dc008551f3d234159f5a) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=47361341)

author: shulu0523
body:
## Problem

`CameraFrameSource` is a process-lifetime singleton on Android, so a frame left over from a previous capture session survives across sessions. On the next `start()`, that stale frame is the first one the pipeline pops, which anchors `SharedVideoSource`'s PTS pacing on an old timestamp. The pacing loop then sleeps for the stale frame's age on *every* subsequent frame, throttling the encode path to ~1 fps for the rest of the session.

### Reproduction
Android ↔ macOS video call. The first call is smooth (30 fps). Hang up and immediately start a second call: the second (and every later) call is stuck at ~1 fps on the Android sender, while CameraX itself keeps delivering 30 fps. The throttle magnitude equals the gap between hang-up and re-dial.

## Fix

- Clear `pending_frame` in both `start()` and `stop()` so no frame leaks between sessions. `stop()` clears eagerly; `start()` clears defensively because the camera callback may still push frames after `stop()` (app-side capture stops asynchronously).
- Route `SharedCameraSource::start`/`stop` through the inner source's methods instead of poking the `started` flag directly, so the cleanup is not bypassed.

author: renanaugustomacena-ux
body:
## Summary

Six defects across two themes, all found by cross-checking what the system *claims* against what is actually on disk. The suite was green throughout — none of these had a failing test.

### Dataset split integrity

**1 · Shard presence is not match completeness.** HLTV publishes some maps as two `-p1`/`-p2` files. Each half ingests as an independent match and writes its own shard, so the P4-A gate from #41 accepted both. Five fragments of 2, 5, 6, 7 and 9 rounds sat in TRAIN, and `…furia-vs-mouz-m1-nuke-p1` carried `avg_kills`/`avg_adr` at `0.0` for all ten players — the last-tick scoreboard read added in #41 is *correct* for a fragment that never reaches a populated scoreboard, so nothing downstream caught it. `_build_eligibility_gates` now composes shard completeness, a round floor, and nonzero per-demo aggregates. `MIN_COMPLETE_MAP_ROUNDS = 13` because a decided MR12 map cannot end sooner; whole maps in this corpus start at 14.

**2 · Matches straddled split boundaries (train/test leak).** `temporal_assign` sliced the flat `PlayerMatchStats` row list, and `match_date` carries per-row microsecond spread, so a demo whose ten rows crossed an index landed in two splits. Live: `…natus-vincere-vs-g2-m1-dust2` had one player in TRAIN and nine in VAL; `…natus-vincere-vs-furia-m2-dust2` spanned VAL/TEST. Splits are now assigned over matches, ordered by each match's earliest row with the demo key breaking ties.

**3 · One unreadable shard erased the whole completeness signal.** Enumeration sat in a single `try/except`, so the first failure returned `None` — "signal unavailable" — which drops the gate and readmits the 259 permanently-incomplete historical demos. Four legacy-schema shards predating `match_complete` were enough. Measured: 314 shards, 310 readable, 96 complete, 4 raising, `None` returned in 0.1 s. An individual shard that fails is now counted as *not complete*; only a total failure returns `None`. For a safety gate the degraded state must be restrictive.

### Storage paths that silently relocated data

**4 · `PRO_DEMO_PATH` defaulted to `$HOME`.** It doubles as the shard root via `_resolve_match_data_path`, and `$HOME` always exists, so the `isdir()` check could never reject it. Every process on stock settings resolved `MATCH_DATA_PATH` to `~/match_data`. Now defaults to `""`, and a bare home directory is refused as a shard root even when configured explicitly.

**5 · Singleton construction moved the shard corpus.** `get_match_data_manager()` ran a "one-time migration" that `shutil.move`d every shard to wherever `MATCH_DATA_PATH` had resolved. Neither one-time nor safe — the trigger was a path comparison, not a persisted marker. Combined with 4 it fired inside `pytest` twice in one afternoon: 45 shards off an external volume, where the copy ran the root disk out of space and killed the run with ENOSPC mid-move, then 313 shards off `/data`, taking `/` from 42 GB to 2 GB free. Construction now only reports; relocation is explicit via `migrate_match_data()`, unchanged and still tested.

**6 · A dangling `match_data` symlink was self-repaired by deleting it.** `MatchDataManager.__init__` `os.unlink`d the dead link and created an empty directory. On a second machine, or with a drive unplugged, the app came up with zero shards, no error, and the only record of where the data lived destroyed. Now raises `MatchDataUnavailableError` naming the link, the dead target and three remedies, touching nothing on disk. A merely *absent* path is still created, so fresh installs are unaffected. It derives from `RuntimeError`, not `OSError`, so defect 3's handler cannot swallow it.

## Effect on the live DB

| | |
|---|---|
| evicted | exactly the 5 `-p1`/`-p2` fragments |
| admitted | exactly the 3 IEM Atlanta demos whose shards were recovered from a fallback path |
| eligible | 93 → 91 demos, **TRAIN 63 / VAL 14 / TEST 14** |

No unintended evictions or admissions.

## Test plan

- [x] 29 new tests, each written before its fix and confirmed RED first. The migration one asserts the invariant rather than a directory layout — *construction never calls `migrate_match_data`* — and fails against the old code inside `match_data_manager.py:1002`, where it read `result["moved"]` after invoking the migration
- [x] Full fast suite: **2362 passed, 5 skipped**. 8 failures are environmental — the monolith is on a read-only mount; a direct read-write `sqlite3.connect` raises the same `unable to open database file`, and a pristine `origin/main` worktree fails the identical tests identically
- [x] Acceptance over the live 314-shard directory: **314 before, 314 after, root disk untouched, no `~/match_data` recreated.** Suite runtime also fell 272 s → 141 s, the difference being 40 GB it used to copy
- [x] `tools/headless_validator.py`: PASS 318/319, exit 0 (sole warning: pre-existing optional `shap`)
- [x] Integrity manifest synced; pre-commit clean on all four commits

## Also

`.gitignore` now covers the artifacts a relocated monolith leaves behind: `*.db.old_*`, the `match_data` symlink and its `.old_*` sibling, and the `pre_rating_repair` CSV.

author: thomasryu1992-commits
body:
**main is red right now**, on both runners, for every open PR — including the other session's. Not a code regression: a test fixture reached its own expiry date.

## What happened

`_seed_candidate` dated the working-memory candidate from the file's fixed `NOW = "2026-07-19T12:00:00Z"` with a 7-day TTL:

```python
"created_at": NOW, "expires_at": timeutil.plus_minutes(NOW, 7 * 24 * 60),
```

which is exactly `2026-07-26T12:00:00Z`. And `approval_cli.main` takes no `now` — the fixture's own docstring says *"the CLI has no injection seam"* — so it validates candidate expiry against `timeutil.utc_now_iso()`.

For seven days the fixture was live. At 12:00Z today it was not:

```
BLOCKED CANDIDATE_EXPIRED: working-memory candidate memcand_f0713d... expired at
2026-07-26T12:00:00Z; an expired candidate cannot be promoted
```

and the two consume tests began asserting against the wrong stderr (`assert 'CONSUMPTION_DISABLED' in ...`, `assert 2 == 0`). My local runs passed because they ran before 12:00Z; CI at 12:03Z failed on ubuntu and windows identically — which is the tell that it is a clock, not a platform.

## Fix

The expiry is derived from the real clock, because the real clock is what the code under test reads. A fixture may pin a fake `NOW` for everything it *constructs* — the task, the binding, `created_at` — but **liveness has to be expressed against the clock that judges it**.

Plus a loud guard at the seam: `_seed_candidate` now asserts the candidate it just built is live, so a future absolute expiry fails right there with that sentence rather than surfacing as an unrelated stderr mismatch two functions away.

## Same pattern elsewhere — checked, not guessed

| fixture | expiry | exposed? |
|---|---|---|
| `approval_cli` | NOW + 7d = **2026-07-26T12:00Z** | **yes — this PR** |
| `approval_consumption` | NOW + 7d = 2026-07-23 (already past) | no — passes an explicit `now` |
| `audit_gaps` | NOW + 7d = 2026-07-27 (tomorrow) | no — passes an explicit `now` |
| `memory_retention` | — | no — asserts a computed value, not liveness |
| `crypto_analytics` | hard-coded, one is 2026-07-28 | **flagged, not touched** — crypto is another session's track |

The two that share the arithmetic are safe precisely because they inject `now`; `approval_cli` was the one exercising a real-clock entry point.

## Verification

- `tests/test_mvp_runtime_approval_cli.py`: 7 passed (was 2 failed / 5 passed).
- Full suite: **2374 passed**, 14 subtests.

Merging this unblocks every open PR, so it should go in ahead of mine (#230).

author: ohdearquant
body:
## What

A terminal record belongs to whichever writer won the terminal transition. Six
sites in the scheduler broke that: each wrote the run's outcome columns on their
own, immediately before the guarded transition, so a path that lost the race
landed its values over the winner's while its status change was correctly
refused.

The clearest case is the cancellation branch. `"Scheduler shutdown"` is a
placeholder rather than a measured cause, so a shutdown arriving after the
deadline reaper had already finalized a run replaced the reaper's real cause
with text that names nothing — and the guarded transition then declined, so the
status stayed correct while the explanation beside it did not.

The completion path had the same shape, and there it is easier to miss because
the overwriting values are genuinely measured: a nonzero exit does not entitle
that path to stamp its exit code, end time and stderr onto a row another writer
finalized.

## Change

All six sites now pass those columns through the guarded write, so losing the
race writes nothing at all rather than writing partially. `exit_code` joins the
`schedule_run` extra-field allowlist for the completion path.

The one remaining standalone `update_schedule_run` is a dispatch marker on a
still-running row. That is not a terminal write and is left alone.

## Tests

Two race tests against a real state database cover the cancellation and
completion paths: a run finalized first as `timed_out` keeps its status, its
cause, and an unset exit code. Both fail without the change, on the overwrite
itself — the cancellation one on `"Scheduler shutdown"` replacing the recorded
`TimeoutError`, the completion one on the loser's stderr replacing it.

One of those tests was initially written with a fixture that could not run
against the unpatched tree at all, so it failed there for its own
incompatibility rather than for the defect. That is noted in the test and the
fixture was narrowed until the base failure is the overwrite and nothing else.

Three existing tests asserted the standalone write had happened, which was the
defect itself; they now assert the fields ride the guarded call together with
its running precondition. The notify test that injected a database failure on
the abandonment path now injects it where that write lives.

`tests/studio tests/state tests/apps_studio_server` reports the same seven
failures as the base commit, all of them an absent PostgreSQL driver, with no
new ones.

author: danmotive
body:
## What

Adds `scripts/i18n-space-phrases.mjs`, which upserts the three dynamic phrases of the Spaces screen into **all 13 base locales** and normalises them to a single house rule:

> **First part. Second part** — state first, then what to do next or what happens next.

Run it locally:

```
node scripts/i18n-space-phrases.mjs          # rewrite
node scripts/i18n-space-phrases.mjs --check  # verify only, exit 1 on drift
cd web && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build
```

## Why

`spaces.empty`, `spaces.lists_empty` and `spaces.archive_confirm` existed **only** in `en-US` and `ru-RU`. The other eleven base locales — `uk-UA`, `be-BY`, `kk-KZ`, `es-ES`, `pt-BR`, `tr-TR`, `zh-CN`, `hi-IN`, `bn-BD`, `ja-JP`, `ko-KR` — resolved these keys through the `[locale, lang, "en-US"]` fallback chain in `web/src/i18n.ts`, so an otherwise fully translated Spaces screen printed English empty-states and an English archive confirmation dialog.

This was the **only** structural key-set gap between the locales. Every other group (`confirm.*`, `notif.*`, `profile.*`, `task.*`, `templates.*`, `timeline.*`, `totp.*`, `workload.*`) already matches across all 13 files.

## Format

`en-US` already followed the rule for two of the three keys; `spaces.archive_confirm` was a bare question and now carries a second part too:

| key | before (en-US) | after (en-US) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spaces.empty` | No spaces yet. Create your first space below. | No spaces yet. Create your first one below. |
| `spaces.lists_empty` | No lists yet. Create one below. | No lists yet. Create your first one below. |
| `spaces.archive_confirm` | Archive “{name}”? | Archive “{name}”? You can restore it from the archive later. |

The script refuses to write anything unless **every** phrase in its table splits into at least two parts, and it checks that `{name}` survived in `spaces.archive_confirm`. Terminators recognised: `.` `!` `?` `。` `！` `？` and the Devanagari danda `।`, so the CJK and Hindi phrases are validated by the same rule rather than being exempted.

## Notes

- Output is re-serialised with sorted keys and two-space indent, which is the existing file style — the diff stays limited to the touched keys.
- The slang overlays `ru-RU-it` / `en-US-it` are **not** rewritten. They inherit from their base locale, and `scripts/check_i18n.py` already exempts them via `OVERLAYS`. If one of them ever overrides these keys the script prints a notice instead of guessing the slang wording.
- The second part promises restore-from-archive, which the existing archive/restore flow already supports. It deliberately says nothing about cascading to lists inside the space — I have not verified that behaviour in `internal/api/archive.go`.

Part 1 of 3. Sibling PRs: `fix/members-i18n-keys` (raw keys on the Members screen) and `fix/locale-wording` (per-language wording errors).

author: cyrex562
body:
Stage 1 of per-building labour. This adds the **data model and the allocation algorithm**; it deliberately changes no behaviour, so all 14 balance bundles are unmoved. Rewiring `process_production_scaled` to consume the plan — which *will* move balance numbers — is a separate change, so the retuning is visible on its own rather than buried in a refactor.

## What this adds

**`BuildingDef.default_priority: u8`** — ordering policy lives in content, not as a category table in the kernel. A greenhouse ships ahead of an ore mine; a pack author retunes without touching Rust. `#[serde(default)]` to the middle of the range, so existing packs load unchanged.

**`PlacedBuilding.priority` and `.labour_lock`** — priority seeded from the def at placement, then player-adjustable. A lock pins an allocation the allocator hands out first and never reclaims. Both serde-defaulted, so a pre-#307 save loads with every building on exactly the footing it already had implicitly.

**`colony::labour::allocate_labour`** — a pure function returning a `LabourPlan`:

1. **Locked buildings first**, in priority order among themselves.
2. **Then everything else in priority order**, `1` before `9`.
3. **Partial fill, not all-or-nothing** — a building that can only be half staffed gets half, so labour degrades smoothly instead of falling off a cliff at each boundary.
4. **Deterministic** — ties break on `(priority, building_type, id)`, so the same colony always yields the same plan. Replays and save-resumption depend on that.

Two clamps on locks, both documented: to the building's own demand (pinning 50 workers to a 5-slot greenhouse would waste 45), and to whatever workforce remains when its turn comes. If the player over-pins, the *lower-priority* locks come up short — the same rule the automatic pass follows, rather than a separate failure mode.

Buildings with no recipe offer **no jobs**, mirroring the filter the old colony-wide `labor_demanded` used, so a silo or habitat doesn't soak up staff it can't use. `LabourAllocation::ratio()` returns `1.0` for zero demand — a silo must not be reported as labour-starved.

## No category ranking

An earlier draft ranked `BuildingCategory` first with priority as a tiebreak. Dropped, and the module doc records why: categories cut across intent. A farm and an ore mine are both `Extraction`, so a food crisis would have competed with a metal shortage on equal footing. Authored per-building defaults express the same thing directly and more flexibly.

## The tests were vacuous, and I'd have shipped them

Worth stating plainly. My first version named the fixtures `farm` (better priority) and `mine` (worse) — which happen to sort alphabetically in the *same order* as their priorities. So the `(priority, building_type, id)` tiebreak alone produced every expected result. I checked by deleting the priority comparison entirely: **all 19 tests still passed.**

The fixtures now deliberately **oppose** the orderings — the alphabetically-later name carries the better priority — and three tests fail without the priority comparison:

```
FAILED a_shortage_starves_the_worse_priority_first
FAILED a_building_that_can_only_be_partly_staffed_gets_what_is_left
FAILED locks_beyond_the_workforce_starve_the_worse_priority_lock
```

19 tests cover: full staffing with idle remainder, priority-ordered starvation, partial fill, no-recipe buildings, locks beating a better unlocked priority, locks clamped to demand, over-locking, zero workforce, unknown building types, order independence, tiebreak determinism, and authored-default seeding.

## Definition of Done

| Tier | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace` | 765 + 37 + 81 passed, 0 failed (19 new) |
| `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo fmt --check --all` | clean |
| Balance harness | 14/14 pass, **all unmoved** — confirming this stage is behaviour-neutral |
| Frontend tiers | not applicable — no frontend change |
| `outpost_tauri` | not verified (no WebKit2GTK here); no host code changed |

42 test fixtures across 7 files needed the new `BuildingDef` field. Patched by brace-matching each initializer rather than regex, after a regex pass on an earlier issue wrongly caught function parameters and a closure signature.

## Next stages

1. **Wire the plan into the sol pipeline** and gate `process_production_scaled` on per-building labour instead of the colony-wide ratio. This is the invasive part; expect balance bundles to move, and I'll report the deltas rather than nudging assertions until they pass.
2. **Commands** — `SetBuildingPriority`, lock/unlock, and `AssignLabour` becoming the real override path.
3. **UI** — labour, priority selector, and lock in the building details page.
4. **Content** — author defaults across the roster.

Two open questions from #307 remain and don't block stage 2: whether a paused building should be skipped, and whether priority is per-instance or per-building-type (recipe selection is per type, so matching that is consistent and much less UI, but loses prioritising one of three mines).

Refs #307
