body:
## Summary

- add a non-throwing at-source URL error-detail sanitizer that removes userinfo, query strings, fragments, and sensitive invalid-port text before repr/interpolation
- normalize parser-ignored tab/CR/LF and leading WHATWG C0/space before locating the authority
- inspect and suppress malformed NFKC-equivalent authorities before cutting query/fragment tails
- fail closed on ambiguous scheme names/slash-runs and locate only the first tail delimiter without proportional allocation
- apply redaction across bean-sourcing fetch, redirect, decode, validation, extraction, timeout, and transport failures
- replace raw parser, `urljoin`, `httpx`, Pydantic, and malformed-port exception text that can itself echo URLs
- handle malformed parse failures at the API boundary, including unclosed IPv6 and NFKC-invalid authorities
- reject URLs over 4,096 characters with a constant secret-free response before redaction, admission, fetch, or provider work
- pre-read at most 64 KiB in route-scoped ASGI middleware and invoke FastAPI only after the complete body fits, including missing or understated lengths
- keep the frontend display helper unchanged as defence in depth

## Why

Error details previously interpolated raw operator-supplied URLs. A query containing both quote characters can escape repr's chosen delimiter and defeat quote-span display redaction; malformed URLs can also fail before userinfo/fragment checks. Sanitizing structurally before message construction prevents those sensitive components from entering any client response.

Closes #656

## Scope and cap accounting

Merge-base: `origin/main` at `72c12f5`.

- runtime logic: `api.py` 112 changed lines + `bean_sourcing.py` 228 changed lines = **340 logic lines**
- tests: `test_api.py` 153 + `test_bean_sourcing.py` 443 = **596 test lines**
- total summed insertions + deletions: **936**
- no deletion credit claimed; no data, fixture, generated, or frontend files changed
- test diff is below the 600-line QA trigger

The runtime size is above the kickoff's rough 30-70 estimate because the complete error-constructor inventory included redirect, decompression, resolver, timeout, transport, extraction, validation, malformed Unicode delimiter composition, lazy port parsing, ambiguous authority prefixes, bounded API validation, and a pre-parser route body cap. It remains one coherent 340-line untrusted-input/error-detail boundary and is below the 400-line cap.

## Local validation

Final head `47bbf3fce8bbbd0e3448fd6977422edb353e45ed`:

- `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .` — passed

## Shift-left and review

This touches untrusted URL parsing, so the security-reviewer route normally applies. Claude Code is unavailable/suspended for this session per operator direction; I instead completed the repository untrusted-input checklist and an adversarial local audit before commit. The audit explicitly checked malformed/unclosed IPv6 input, both-quote queries, userinfo, fragments, redirect `Location`, transport exception text, Pydantic validation text, SSRF behavior, resource admission order, NFKC-equivalent reserved delimiters and their composition/order, lazy malformed ports, ambiguous scheme/authority prefixes, and raw URL interpolation inventory.

GitHub Codex review rounds found fifteen actionable URL-redaction/resource variants, all fixed with exact regressions:

- credential-bearing `urlsplit()` exception text
- parser-ignored tab/CR/LF hiding authority syntax
- NFKC-equivalent `＠` userinfo delimiters
- leading WHATWG C0/space before scheme-relative authorities
- credential-bearing `urljoin()` exception text
- NFKC-equivalent `？` / `＃` tail delimiters
- sensitive invalid-port text echoed through both the URL and lazy parser exception
- fullwidth tail truncation occurring before later userinfo redaction
- malformed zero/one/three-slash scheme separators exposing userinfo-like text
- proportional allocation from materializing every tail-delimiter position
- NFKC-equivalent scheme colons bounded as path text before authority redaction
- bare three-or-more-slash scheme-relative prefixes exposing userinfo-like text
- invalid apparent schemes with compatibility colons and authority syntax exposing userinfo-like text
- unbounded malformed-URL redaction synchronously blocking controller ticks before admission
- framework buffering/JSON-decoding an unbounded body before the URL field limit

The author's final adversarial pass also covered the literal-colon sibling (`1https://...`) of the ambiguous-scheme finding. The bounded-input regressions verify that oversized malformed URLs invoke none of redaction, semaphore admission, fetch, or provider work; declared, missing, and understated body lengths fail at the ASGI receive boundary with a constant 413; a complete valid JSON prefix cannot trigger downstream work when later bytes overflow; exact-cap bodies pass the middleware; worst-case escaped 4,096-character URLs reach normal processing; and other routes remain unaffected.

No fetch semantics, SSRF policy, provider path, roast-control logic, safety/controller/enums, data, or frontend behavior changed.

## Temporary Claude status

Per operator direction, the suspended Claude review is optional for today. `review-gate` has been removed from required branch-protection contexts while all CI, web, Playwright, and `codecov/patch` protections remain enforced. Claude workflow failures are ignored until the App is restored.

## D23 handoff

Independent D23 triage verified and resolved all fifteen actionable fixes on their corresponding heads. It adjudicated the ordinary-path observation as real but outside #656's explicit query/userinfo/fragment scope, replied with the diagnostic-policy rationale, and resolved that thread without requesting a change. On head `3104e621daab88ab872397bdbecf7154af5cdc94`, it ran 49 focused helper/backend/API regressions and verified the two ambiguous-prefix fixes plus the proactive literal-colon sibling. On head `a9f4d68cc0aa96c2c37ce3afbdbb5c82b865f3df`, it verified the constant oversized URL response, no pre-admission work, the exact character boundary, and unchanged default validation with four focused tests. It correctly kept the pre-parser P1 open on `7ab5bb88245dab07197b1efcd634674e2b748e7e` after proving a valid first chunk could still trigger service work before later overflow. On final head `47bbf3fce8bbbd0e3448fd6977422edb353e45ed`, five focused tests plus direct middleware probes proved zero sanitizer, semaphore, service, receive, or downstream calls on the relevant overflow paths; it then resolved only that P1 thread. The author did not self-resolve or dismiss review feedback.

author: thierryvm
body:
Plan complet produit par 14 agents : 5 audits du code réel, 4 études de marché, une synthèse, puis **3 critiques adversariales chargées de le détruire** — pas de le valider. Ceci est la version qui leur a survécu.

Documentation uniquement, aucun code.

## Trois prémisses de la demande initiale, réfutées sur pièces

**« On ne peut pas modifier une dépense »** — faux. `ExpenseEditDrawer.tsx` fait 217 lignes, est monté ligne 337, appelle `updateExpenseAction`, et a 4 blocs de tests. Le déclencheur est un crayon gris collé à une corbeille rouge qui capte l'œil. Défaut d'**affordance**, pas de code manquant.

**« Il n'y a pas de vraies catégories »** — faux aussi. La table existe depuis le schéma initial, **8 catégories sont semées à chaque inscription**, `expenses.category_id` existe, le schéma Zod le porte, le Server Action l'écrit. **Deux lignes d'UI débranchent tout** : `categoryId: null` en dur, et un mapping RSC qui perd le champ avant le composant.

**« Les menus sont confus »** — le symptôme est réel, la cause n'est pas les menus. La nav expose **six noms de tables** en 7 destinations de rang égal, dont **trois décrivent le même geste mental** : de l'argent qui sort. Aucune refonte visuelle ne répare ça — c'est pourquoi le polish est délibérément la **dernière** étape.

## Ce que l'étude de marché change

Les banques belges (BNP Fortis, KBC, Beobank) livrent déjà la catégorisation automatique **gratuitement**. En saisie manuelle sur ce terrain, Ankora perd d'avance.

Mais aucune ne sait ce qui est **déjà engagé** — et ce chiffre ne se déduit pas d'un historique, il se **déclare**. C'est la seule donnée que PSD2 ne fournira jamais, ce qui retourne l'absence d'agrégation en positionnement plutôt qu'en handicap.

## Ce que les critiques ont tué

- Une clause `ON DELETE SET NULL` sans liste de colonnes qui aurait rendu **impossible la suppression d'une catégorie** sur trois tables (violation NOT NULL sur `workspace_id`)
- L'absence de tout chemin de retour arrière sur 4 migrations — **un seul projet Supabase, plan Free, pas de PITR, un utilisateur réel**. Gate obligatoire désormais : dump + down.sql testé + push par @thierry
- La seule migration restante a été **sortie du chemin critique**

## Structure

17 étapes, une branche par étape, ordonnées pour qu'aucune ne dépende d'une suivante. L'étape 1 est petite et livrable seule, conformément à la règle « tant qu'elle n'est pas finie, on ne continue pas ».

body:
## Summary
This PR addresses critical issues with customer account re-entry and adds project quota visibility for retailers. It ensures customers always have valid entitlements when signing in via access codes, and provides retailers with accurate project usage tracking.

## Key Changes

### Customer Entitlement Repair on Re-entry
- Added `ensureEntitlementForCode()` method to guarantee redeemed customers have an entitlement row, fixing the "Your access is not set up" 403 error that occurred when accounts existed but entitlements were missing
- Handles both new entitlements (created from code) and existing ones (only fills gaps without resetting usage)
- Called during both initial redemption and re-entry flows to handle partial redemption failures

### Project Quota Tracking
- Added `projectsUsed` and `projectsRemaining` fields to `AccessCodeResponse` to show retailers how many projects have been created against each code
- Implemented `countByAccessCodeIds()` query in `ProjectRepository` for efficient batch counting across multiple codes (single query per page instead of per-code)
- Updated `listCodes()` to populate usage metrics without N+1 query problems

### Access Control Refinement
- Modified `assertAccessValid()` to allow customers with no entitlement row to view projects (returns empty list instead of 403), while still enforcing expiry checks for existing entitlements
- This prevents the dashboard from becoming unusable when a customer re-enters without an entitlement

### New Endpoints
- Added `GET /api/access-codes/{codeId}/projects` to view all projects created against a code with real shade codes, supporting multi-project orders

### Re-entry Robustness
- Enhanced `redeemAsNewCustomer()` to handle orphaned accounts (account exists but code wasn't consumed) by completing the redemption and ensuring entitlement exists
- Uses compare-and-set on code consumption to handle concurrent re-entries safely

## Notable Implementation Details
- Entitlement repair is idempotent: re-entry never resets usage or shortens the access window
- Code expiry can only extend (never shorten) an existing entitlement's expiry
- Empty code lists short-circuit the batch count query to avoid JPQL `IN ()` syntax errors
- All changes maintain backward compatibility with existing entitlements

author: apnex-greg
body:
Director-ratified: pause = set suspended + stop both clocks + notify the holder **and the author**. The holder half existed; this is the other half.

## Why the author channel is not cosmetic

**A row suspended from `ready` has no holder**, so the holder channel notified *nobody* and nothing said so. The author is the only party who can be told — that is the case the Director asked for.

## 🔴 The notice mechanism was structurally single-recipient, and only a delivery test found it

`historyFor` linked intent→history via `candidate.holderNoticeIntentId === intent.intentId`, and a history entry records exactly **one** such id — the holder's. The author intent matched nothing, threw *"no exact before-state history"*, and **was never delivered**. The intents existed and looked correct on the row; only the messages were missing.

> **A test asserting on `pendingRecallIntents` would have passed while nobody was notified.**

These tests drive the **real projector** and assert on **messages actually delivered**, which is the only reason the defect surfaced. Now matched on `operationId` + `beforeStateHash`. The exactness guarantee is unchanged — operation and exact before-state must both match, and a mismatch still throws. What is dropped is the assumption that one pause produces one notice, which was never a property of the pause, only of the code that read it.

## Also caught, and it would have failed open

`recallNoticePending` was keyed on the **holder** notice alone. An author-only notice — the no-holder case, i.e. the whole point — would have sat unprojected while the flag said nothing was pending, so the projector's own trigger would never fire. Now keyed on `notices.length > 0`.

## De-dupe is structural, not a check

Recipients collect into a `Map` keyed by agentId, so a duplicate **cannot** be added — rather than remembering to test before pushing. Two notices for one pause read as two pauses to anyone counting them.

## Field naming, stated rather than glossed

`exactHolderAgentId` is the recipient **routing** key, and for an author notice it carries the author. The name predates the author channel and is now narrower than the field. Renaming touches a required, indexed storage field for cosmetic gain, so the name stays and the ambiguity is resolved by an explicit `recipientKind: "holder" | "author"` discriminator — optional, so every already-persisted intent still decodes.

## Tests — all three required cases, through the production path

| case | expected |
|---|---|
| no holder | **author** notified (holder channel covers nobody) |
| holder ≠ author | both, exactly once each |
| holder == author | one notice, one message (de-dupe) |

Plus distinct `intentId`s — a shared id would let one notice overwrite the other's projection state. The pre-existing projector idempotency test is now author==holder **deliberately**: its subject is per-intent crash-gap behaviour, and that fixture now doubles as a de-dupe proof — it reds on `toHaveLength(1)` before the projector is even reached.

243 files / 2928 passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped; `tsc` exit 0.

author: tanzerine
body:
## Why

Nothing in the codebase tracked LLM spend. `lib/pipeline/capacity` measures wall-clock — enough to size a tick, useless for pricing. So every question about plan margin could only be answered by guessing.

What we *do* know is revenue per post, and it falls sharply as the tier rises:

| plan | price | posts | **$/post** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $29 | 12 | **$2.42** |
| Growth | $79 | 40 | **$1.98** |
| Agency | $199 | 150 | **$1.33** |

Cost per post is roughly flat across tiers, which means Agency plausibly carries the thinnest unit margin *while* being sold "priority pipeline". Whether that's fine or alarming needs a number.

## The approach

A generation spends across six modules — site-profile, topic-refiner, writer (often twice), manager (often twice), the cover art-director, inline images — none of which should know anything about billing.

Threading a usage value out of six return types would mean changing those signatures, their callers, and their tests, and coupling the whole pipeline to a concern none of it owns. So `llmCall` reports into an `AsyncLocalStorage` meter and `generatePost` opens one. **Nothing in between changes.**

`AsyncLocalStorage` specifically, not a module-level array: ticks overlap once the cron runs more often than a generation takes, and a global would bill one post for another's tokens.

Each run appends one costed line to `generation_log`:

```
persist · done · "cost · $0.0182 · 6 calls · 14.2k in / 5.1k out"
```

## The invariant worth reviewing

**An unknown cost is `null`, never `0`.** An unlisted model, or a provider that reports no token counts, is counted as `unpriced` and excluded from the total rather than silently priced at $0.

A table that does the latter produces totals that look precise and are wrong — which is worse than having no totals, because you'd act on them. `describeCost` surfaces the unpriced count in the log line so an undercount announces itself.

Prices are provider list prices and will drift. They're an indicator to act on, not accounting.

## Scope

Instrumentation only — **no pricing decision follows from this yet.** That needs a month of real data, which now starts accumulating. Outside a metered scope the meter is a no-op, so the assistant and plan-chat paths are unaffected.

## Verification

`npm test` — 893 pass (22 new), `npm run build` green.

Extends the song-model PoC with a note-lifecycle **automaton** over the lifted control flow, covering doc items 4 (control transitions) and 5 (AD/SR selection).

Each store to `control` (`$D404`), `attack_decay`, or `sustain_release` becomes a `Transition(role, action, to, source, guards)`:
- **guards** — the conjunction of enclosing branch conditions on the path (rendered, e.g. `(m_5523 & $01)`, `(m_54F5 & $20) == $00`).
- **action** — classifies the `$D404` value: `gate_off` (mask clears bit 0), `gate_on` (OR bit 0), else `waveform`.
- **to** — note-lifecycle state (`off`/`on`); **source** — backtraced waveform/AD-SR table base.

Commando recovers 7 edges: note-on waveform under the `m_5523 & $01` flag bit, note-off `gate_off` under `(m_54F5 & $20)==$00 & (m_54F2==$00)`, and the note-on AD/SR selections — the *when* (guards) and *what* (action + table) together.

body:
## Summary
This PR adds the ability to filter colour matches by paint company/brand across the colour matching tools (Color Finder and Color Match). It also includes infrastructure improvements for API path validation and route protection.

## Key Changes

### Colour Matching Company Filter
- **New `CompanyFilter` component** (`src/components/catalogue/company-filter.tsx`): A dropdown selector that filters matches to a single paint company, hidden when only one company is available
- **New `useShadeBrands` hook** (`src/hooks/use-shade-brands.ts`): Fetches the live list of paint companies from the backend with a fallback to companies present in the catalogue for offline/demo mode
- **Enhanced `useShadeMatch` hook**: Now accepts an optional `brand` parameter to restrict matching to a specific company. Both the backend matcher (via `?brand=<slug>` query param) and offline fallback respect this filter, ensuring results never silently widen when the backend is unavailable
- **Updated Color Finder and Color Match components**: Integrated the company filter UI and pass the selected brand to the matching hook

### API Infrastructure & Validation
- **New `bff-paths.ts` module** (`src/lib/bff-paths.ts`): Extracted the BFF allow-list to a shared location so it can be tested against actual API client calls
- **New `bff-paths.test.ts`** (`src/lib/__tests__/bff-paths.test.ts`): Validates that every path the API client calls is in the BFF allow-list, preventing silent 403 failures like the `api/me/assigned-products` regression
- **New `protected-routes.test.ts`** (`src/lib/__tests__/protected-routes.test.ts`): Ensures every `(app)` route group page is protected by middleware so access tokens stay refreshed
- **Updated BFF route handler**: Now uses the extracted `isBffPathAllowed()` function

### Access Codes & Projects Management
- **Updated `AccessCodes` component**: Changed from single "room" to multiple "rooms" per code; now displays `projectsUsed / projectQuota` instead of just quota; calls `listProjectsForCode()` instead of `getGuestProjectForCode()`
- **Updated `CustomerAccessBanner`**: Shows project usage as "X of Y projects used" to clarify the deduction, not just remaining count
- **New API method**: `listProjectsForCode()` to fetch all projects created against a code
- **Updated types**: Added `projectsUsed` and `projectsRemaining` fields to `AccessCode`

### Tests
- **New `use-shade-match.test.tsx`**: Comprehensive tests for the company filter functionality, including backend integration, offline fallback, and edge cases (empty results, unreachable backend)
- **Updated `access-codes.test.tsx`**: Updated assertions to reflect "Rooms" plural and new project quota display format

## Implementation Details
- The `brandSlug()` utility converts company names to URL-safe slugs (lowercase, non-alphanumerics collapsed to dashes) matching the backend's convention
- Company filtering is applied consistently across both matching paths: the backend receives the slug via query parameter, while the offline matcher filters the catalogue by the company's display name
- The BFF allow-list is now a single source of truth that can be validated against actual client usage, preventing future regressions where new API paths are added without updating the proxy
- Route protection tests ensure the middleware refresh mechanism works for all protected pages, preventing access token expiration issues for redeemed customers

author: franko1260
body:
## The bug

All repos vanished from the app sidebar; every deep link returned "Workspace not found".

The daemon task was replaced 2026-07-26 08:43 UTC. Its boot logs:

```
msg="Workspace registries bootstrapped from existing agent storage"
  reconstruction="cloud-durable"
  materializedProjects=43 materializedWorkspaces=43 reconstructedFromDurableProjects=30
module=workspace-reconciliation changeCount=42
  changes=[{kind:"workspace_archived", directory:"/workspace/ws_3ea432ff/Nuvo-Software-Pty-Ltd__agora", reason:"directory_missing"}, ...]
```

`bootstrapWorkspaceRegistries` correctly rehydrated 43 workspace records from the durable project store. ~13ms later `WorkspaceReconciliationService` swept them with an `existsSync` check — and in cloud `/workspace` is tmpfs and empty that early in boot. 42 of 43 archived, including all four real repos.

Nothing was lost: the cloud workspace is `active`, 35 durable project rows survive unarchived, and the cloud workspace registry is `InMemoryWorkspaceRegistry` so the archive isn't even persisted. But the list was destroyed on **every** recycle.

## The fix

The lazy repair from #61 already re-clones a missing path on open. The only defect was that reconciliation deleted the entry before the user could click it. So defer the archive — don't pre-clone at boot, since cold start is already over budget and eager cloning would make it worse.

`isCloudRepairableMissingWorkspace` answers "can the lazy repair restore this?" against the project list `reconcile()` has already loaded, so it adds no I/O and no cold-start time. It reuses `selectProjectRepairClone` and the repair's own path regex, so the deferral set and the repair set cannot drift.

Injected as an optional predicate rather than imported directly by the reconciliation service: that file is byte-identical to upstream and worth keeping so ahead of the pending merge, and a direct import would drag `@aws-sdk/client-secrets-manager` into a core desktop service's module graph. Absent the predicate, behavior is exactly upstream's — desktop is untouched.

**Both construction sites are wired** (`bootstrap.ts` and `Session.reconcileActiveWorkspaceRecords`). Fixing only bootstrap would let the first `fetch_workspaces_request` re-archive everything, and that pass also tears each workspace down.

The deferral is self-bounding: recomputed from the live durable list every pass, so once a project row is archived the next pass archives its workspace normally. No TTL or counter — and none would survive the session site, which builds a fresh service per call.

## Deliberate limitations

- **Stale routine worktrees** (`/var/lib/paseo/worktrees/routine-*`, 38 of them) still archive. Correct — they're genuinely unrecoverable.
- **Nested paseo worktrees below a repairable clone still archive.** Re-cloning the parent does not restore their branch state. Repos come back after a recycle; worktrees inside them do not. Restoring those needs the S3 git-delta snapshot path — follow-up, not an extension of this predicate.
- A relic `.git-canonical` row from *another* workspace also defers, because the predicate derives the ws id from the path exactly as the repair does. Deliberate: one definition of "restorable" beats two that can drift. A deferral the repair can't honor surfaces as a visible error on open.

## Tests

- `workspace-reconciliation-service.test.ts` — deferral honored / declined / omitted (upstream parity), and the predicate gets the full project list from a single registry call.
- `cloud-workspace-repair.test.ts` — 8 predicate cases including the agora repro, stale worktrees, nested worktrees, archived rows, and the off-cloud control.
- **New `workspace-reconciliation-boot.test.ts`** — covers the composed boot sequence, which nothing tested before. Each half was individually tested and individually correct; only their composition was broken. **Verified this test fails without the fix.**

Full server suite: 3414 passed, 0 failed. Typecheck and oxlint clean.

author: eyalbenari99-star
body:
Root cause of "not sync from computer": the pull loop only applied 6
whitelisted operational keys (users, perms, calls, issues, role defaults,
tombstones) plus today's daily report on every pull. Every other
hydroPro_* key — employees, HR memos & positions, CRM leads, fleet
drivers/vehicles, IT/GH cameras & DVRs, GPS reports & attendance, QC
inspections, security patrols, seed studies, R&D items, past daily
reports, accounting maps & journals, monitor/wall/camera-stream configs,
drum/pool state, and the rest — was only applied on the FIRST pull of
the session. That's why edits on computer A never reached computer B
until B refreshed the page.

Fix: generic pull-merge for every synced key that isn't already covered
by the OP whitelist or today's-day merge.
 · arrays of id-like objects → __hnxMergeById (newer wins per id)
 · JSON objects → __hnxDeepMerge (field union, empty never overwrites filled)
 · non-JSON scalars → adopt cloud copy (last-write-wins)

To keep an in-flight local edit from being clobbered by a stale cloud
value during the ~4s push-debounce window, every localStorage write to a
synced key sets a per-key dirty flag; keys with the flag are left alone
during pulls and the flag clears the moment the next push succeeds.
Writes performed BY the pull itself run under __HNX_SUPPRESS so they
don't self-flag.

Also bumped: APP_VERSION 12.88→12.90, APP_BUILD_DATE, cloud popup label.

author: thalida
body:
Closes #122
Closes #143

Timeline renders the **union** manifest — every path that ever existed — but every content read went to HEAD. The reported symptom was a console full of `/api/file … 404` for media that no longer exists.

The 404s were the visible half. The quiet half: media that *did* survive rendered its **current** bytes no matter how far back you scrubbed. Gating the fetch on presence, as the issue suggested, would have silenced the console and left that in place. So this makes Timeline actually period-correct instead.

## Content follows the commit

The bundle already knew each path's blob sha at each commit, so the replay carries it and `/api/file` takes an optional `sha`: absent reads the working tree, present reads that blob. The file preview, README pane, ad panels, binary fingerprints and the font/waveform facades all pin their version while scrubbing and fall through to the path in Live. `POST /api/files` takes a path→sha map so Timeline keeps the batching that exists to spare the connection pool.

**One endpoint, not two.** This first shipped as a separate `GET /api/blob`, which was wrong: "blob" is git's word for stored content, not a different resource. It's the same file at a different point in time, so it's one endpoint with a version selector — matching how the batch sibling already worked. The old cache-buster is renamed `v` → `mtime`, since that is what it holds and the server never declares it.

**Absent is not the same as versioned.** A file gone at the scrubbed commit has no blob to name, so the sha resolves null and the loader used to fall through to a by-path read of HEAD — the original 404, by a new route. Media, data facades and the README now skip the fetch entirely when a path has no content at that commit.

## Panes follow the scrub

Period-correct content that resolves once isn't much use: the preview and README kept whatever they fetched when selected, so scrubbing moved the city and not the panes. Both read the history manifest now, a file absent at the scrubbed commit reads as deleted rather than quietly showing HEAD's version, and the preview refetches when its blob changes.

Fetches key on a new `SETTLED_COMMIT`, not the live position — dragging a long history would otherwise refetch once per commit crossed. The tree and search stay live, since filtering the union is cheap and watching it change under the drag is the point.

## Numbers describe the blob being served

The footer read "42 lines" over a 36-line body. `linesAt` interpolates between **change entries** so building heights can tween, and the display path was reading that curve: with edits at commit 0 (36) and commit 3 (46), commit 2 reads `36 + 10×2/3 = 42.67`.

`entryAt()` returns the entry actually in effect — a step lookup — and both the sha and the displayed lines/bytes come from it, so a number and the bytes beside it cannot describe different blobs.

An audit of the rest found one more of the same kind: `scrubFile`'s lerped count fed both the height curve **and** `isEmptyFile()`, so a file that was empty at this commit but big later lost its flat empty slab. Emptiness is a fact about the blob; it reads the step entry now. Everything else checked out — `presenceAt` drives opacity, `lastModifiedIndexAt` is already a step, `statsAtDeletion` reads entries directly, and `scrubFile` never escapes to the picker or tooltip. `bytesAt` had no production caller left and is gone.

## Folder stats (#143)

The street pane's numbers are subtree rollups, so no blob endpoint reaches them. #143 assumed a per-commit-per-directory replay with the payload cost that implies — unnecessary, as it turns out: `/api/manifest?ref=` already reconstructs a whole repo at any commit using the same code a live scan runs, so the rollups match by construction.

Fetched lazily and cached per `(src, sha, excludes)`: only when a street pane is open to read it, only once the scrub settles, and a revisited commit is free since a reconstruction can't change. A superseded scan aborts when you scrub past it; a failed one keeps the last good manifest rather than blanking the pane.

**All three `TimelineStaleNote`s are gone** in the steady state — the street pane's now shows only while its scan is in flight, when the union rollups genuinely are all-time.

## Security

`/api/file` resolves its path **non-strict** when a sha is given, because a historical path legitimately may not exist. That isn't a traversal hole: `resolve()` still normalizes `..`, and a path that doesn't exist has no symlink of its own to redirect through. A test pins the escape attempt at 403, and `assert_inside` keeps `must_exist=True` by default so every existing caller is unchanged. git-lfs pointers resolve like the live scan, so LFS media isn't served as a pointer file.

## Worth watching

Reconstructing a commit is a real scan. It's lazy and cached, but the first visit to each commit with a folder selected does the work. If that drags on a large repo, the fallback (union stats plus the note) is intact.

Full gate green via the pre-push hook: 369 pytest, ruff, 2838 vitest, eslint, prettier, typecheck. Verified against mounted local repos.

author: fabn
body:
Everything a SolidQueue app needs to autoscale its job executor to zero. All opt-in — requiring the gem alone changes nothing.

Closes #6
Closes #7

## Scope

#6's body covers three pieces, but a later comment narrowed it to the scheduler thread and split the observability half into #7. This PR does both: they are one coherent feature (the always-on pod hosts the scheduler *and* publishes the gauges), and the gauges are what the metric-naming decision below is about. Easy to split into two PRs if you'd rather review them separately — the code is in separate files.

## 1. Supervised scheduler thread (#6)

`RailsPodKit::SolidQueue::SchedulerRunner` runs a scheduler-only `SolidQueue::Scheduler` in `:async` mode, supervised by a `Concurrent::TimerTask` that (re)starts it whenever its thread has died.

Deliberately **not** `plugin :solid_queue`: the full supervisor forks, and its Puma watchdog takes the host process down when the supervisor exits — which a transient Postgres disconnect is enough to cause ([rails/solid_queue#512](https://github.com/rails/solid_queue/issues/512)). Here a DB blip at worst kills the scheduler thread; the next tick brings it back and the host process never notices.

```ruby
# config/puma.rb — after_booted only runs in the real Puma process
after_booted { RailsPodKit::SolidQueue.start_scheduler! }
at_exit      { RailsPodKit::SolidQueue.stop_scheduler! }
```

Static tasks come from `config/recurring.yml` (honouring `SOLID_QUEUE_RECURRING_SCHEDULE`) via the public `RecurringTask.from_configuration`, since `Configuration#recurring_tasks` is private; dynamic ones from the DB. Multiple replicas stay exactly-once via the unique index on `solid_queue_recurring_executions (task_key, run_at)`.

Tunables: `polling_interval`, `supervision_interval`, `recurring_schedule_file`.

`start_scheduler!` is **not** gated on `enabled` — that switch owns the metrics exporter, and an app may want the scheduler with metrics off. What keeps it out of consoles and specs is *where* you call it from.

## 2. Queue gauges (#7)

Two gauges, computed at scrape time from a yabeda `collect` block — no background thread, no cached snapshot:

| series | meaning | Datadog |
|---|---|---|
| `solid_queue_backlog` | jobs claimable right now, per `queue` | `solid_queue.backlog` |
| `solid_queue_latency_seconds` | how long the oldest of them has waited, per `queue` | `solid_queue.latency_seconds` |

Renamed from the `solid_queue.ready_size` / `oldest_ready_age_seconds` sketch in the issue: **backlog** and **latency** say what they are, and Prometheus names can't carry dots anyway. The `_seconds` suffix comes from yabeda's `unit:`, so it lands on the exposition but not on the registry key.

"Claimable right now" is ready executions **plus** scheduled ones whose time has come — the dispatcher has only to move those across. A scheduled execution's wait is measured from its `scheduled_at`, not `created_at`: enqueuing a week ahead of the slot doesn't make it a week late.

Both matter and neither alone is enough — backlog misses a small-but-stalled queue, latency misses a large-but-moving one.

### An idle system reads 0, not no-data

A queue that drains is explicitly zeroed rather than left pinned at its final backlog — the exact reading that keeps an alert firing on an idle system. The zeroing starts from a **baseline** of every queue the app is known to use, discovered once per process from the jobs table or pinned by the host:

```ruby
RailsPodKit::SolidQueue.install_metrics!(queues: %w[default mailers])
```

Without that baseline a process booting while the queue is empty — the steady state of a scale-to-zero deployment — publishes no series at all, since a yabeda gauge only exists once it has been set. Discovery is best-effort by construction: the jobs table is bounded by `clear_finished_jobs_after`, so a queue idle longer than the retention window leaves no trace in it. Pin `queues:` where the zero has to be guaranteed.

### A collection error is always reported, then swallowed or raised

Reported means logged **and** handed to `Rails.error` — `Rails.error.report` only fans out to subscribers, so on an app with none the failure would otherwise leave no trace and the only symptom would be a gauge quietly serving a stale value. What happens next depends on who owns the endpoint:

| | |
|---|---|
| `fail_scrape_on_error: false` (default) | serve the last reading. Right on an endpoint shared with the Puma or Sidekiq series, where failing the response would lose those too — at the cost of a stale gauge a consumer can't tell apart from a live one. |
| `fail_scrape_on_error: true` (`run_exporter!`'s default) | fail the scrape. Right on the dedicated pod, where there's nothing else to protect: the gauges go to no-data and the failure shows up in the scraper's own `up` series. |

Per-series removal isn't an option — prometheus-client-mmap keeps a value once written.

Declaration is one-shot but the options are merged across calls, which matters more than it looks: the pod's entrypoint boots `config/environment`, so the app's own initializer has normally already declared the gauges by the time `run_exporter!` asks for `fail_scrape_on_error: true`. An option given on any call wins; one left out keeps what an earlier call set.

## 3. The always-on pod

`run_exporter!` declares the gauges, starts the scheduler, serves `/metrics` and blocks until SIGTERM (winding the scheduler down so it deregisters rather than expiring). Unlike `GlobalExporter` it is **not** Rails-free — SolidQueue is ActiveRecord-backed and reads the app's own tables — so the host entrypoint boots the environment first. The gem still ships no executable.

```ruby
#!/usr/bin/env ruby
require_relative '../config/environment'
RailsPodKit::SolidQueue.run_exporter!
```

`scheduler: false` serves the gauges only (an app whose web process already hosts the scheduler); `metrics:` overrides the gauge options.

## The invariant needed widening

The "prefix-pure endpoint" rule doesn't hold on its own any more. The Datadog check uses `metrics: [".*"]`, which ingests everything on the endpoint, so a web pod exposing both `puma_*` and `solid_queue_*` would have the `puma` instance swallow the SolidQueue series un-stripped. The spec now allows the three group prefixes, and the README documents the rule: **one prefix per endpoint**, or an explicit `metrics:` filter on *every* instance sharing it. That's the main reason the docs point the gauges at their own pod, which keeps the published check config unchanged for existing adopters.

## Incidental

- `RailsPodKit::Exporter` extracts the WEBrick `/metrics` server shared by the non-Puma entry points (Sidekiq, `GlobalExporter`, the SolidQueue pod). One start latch per process instead of one per entry point — with three entry points that started to matter. `Sidekiq.start_metrics_server!` stays as a delegating alias.
- `.github/release-drafter.yml`: dropped the `files: ['*.md']` rule from the `chore` autolabeler. It matched on documentation being *touched*, not on the change *being* documentation, so any feature that updates the README — which every user-facing feature here does — landed under Maintenance. The `docs/*` and `chore/*` branch rules already cover the real case.

## Testing

- 75 examples, 0 failures, stable across seeds; RuboCop clean.
- Specs stay isolated per the repo convention: `solid_queue` is not a dependency, so the models and the scheduler are stubbed and the suite still needs no database.
- Because that leaves the query shapes and the boot order unverified, both were exercised against real ActiveRecord models on SQLite outside the suite: backlog 3 (2 ready + 1 due scheduled, the future-scheduled queue absent) and latency 120s from the oldest ready row, 0/0 after draining; an idle system with an empty ready table still publishing 0 for every queue in the baseline; and, in the pod's real initializer-then-`run_exporter!` order, a broken connection raising out of

author: chrishayuk
body:
`/mathonly` swapped the weights but left `self.broker` set, so the next `/broker` saw the flag, returned early and never reloaded. Act 4 then ran the **maths** checkpoint in broker mode and emitted no call at all — both the 4c pumpkin beat and the 4d closing shot produced nothing.

That isn't a corner case, it's the running order:

```
cold open   /broker
3b          /mathonly
4c          /broker     ← no-op, wrong model still loaded
4d          /broker     ← same
```

Every take would have hit it.

## Fix

- `load()` clears the broker flag — leaving broker mode is part of loading something else.
- `load_broker()` rebuilds the weights on re-entry but keeps the `CellHost` and its compiled cells. Compiling a cell is the slow part, and the second `/broker` is thirty seconds from the closing shot.

## Verified

The exact failing sequence now works end to end:

```
  [cell] safe_div(157, 16) → 9      ← cold open
>   7 + 5 = 12                       ← 3b, maths checkpoint
  [cell] add_sat(412, 355) → 767    ← 4c
  [cell] safe_div(157, 16) → 9      ← 4d
```

Plus a full 20-command runthrough in shoot order: 0 failures, no leftover process.

## How it was found

By running the script rather than reading it — and specifically by the empty-generation notice from `a24c509`, which printed *"belongs to a different checkpoint than the one loaded (model_mathonly.pt)"* under the pumpkin prompt. Four lines of diagnostics naming a real bug on their first outing.

body:
## Summary

Improve the `no-loss-of-precision` rule's hot paths without changing the rule framework or its diagnostics:

- Reuse the raw numeric token range and report it directly, avoiding duplicate scanner work.
- Add a zero-allocation fast path for decimal integers through `2^53`.
- Replace regular-expression dispatch and `big.Float` round trips for non-decimal integers with exact IEEE-754 bit checks.
- Lazily cache exact decimal powers while retaining the existing `big.Rat` rounding semantics.

### Performance

Measured on Apple M1 Max (`darwin/arm64`):

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Single-rule repository timing | 18.5 ms / 804 files | 0.8 ms / 819 files |
| Safe small integer | 1.09 µs, 929 B, 39 allocs | 18 ns, 0 B, 0 allocs |
| Decimal fraction | 1.24 µs, 1,089 B, 44 allocs | 0.71 µs, 472 B, 21 allocs |
| Hexadecimal integer | 0.5–1 µs, 6–7 allocs | 0.14–0.15 µs, 2 allocs |
| Smallest subnormal | 22 µs, 6,162 B, 64 allocs | 19.7 µs, 2,819 B, 24 allocs |

The repository timing comparison is indicative rather than file-for-file identical; the post-change run covered 15 additional files. Rule timing is summed across parallel workers.

Validation completed before rebasing onto the latest `main`:

- `go test -count=1 ./internal/rules/no_loss_of_precision`
- Targeted `go test -race` for differential and concurrent-cache cases
- 35,444 fuzz executions against the previous algorithm with no divergence

EvidenceEngine.source_paths was referenced via getattr(engine, 'source_paths', {}) at edf_collector.py:9938 but never initialised or populated. author: bluetoothbot
body:
**What**: `stop_notify()` now writes `0x0000` to the CCCD on connection-v3 proxies, so the peripheral actually stops notifying.

**Why**: On proxies advertising `REMOTE_CACHING`, the esp32 wipes the resolved descriptors to save memory, so `start_notify()` writes the CCCD itself — that branch is already in the code and documented. Nothing ever undid it. The firmware's `notify_characteristic()` only calls `esp_ble_gattc_register_for_notify` / `esp_ble_gattc_unregister_for_notify`, and neither touches the CCCD. So `stop_notify()` dropped the proxy-side subscription while the peripheral kept sending notifications for the life of the connection: battery drain on the peripheral, wasted airtime on the proxy, and devices that gate behaviour on subscription state left stuck in streaming mode.

**How**: Mirror the `start_notify` branch — same `REMOTE_CACHING` guard, same `get_descriptor(CCCD_UUID)` lookup. The CCCD write goes first so the peripheral is quiet before the subscription is released, and the release sits in a `finally` so a failing write cannot leave the local bookkeeping drifted from the already-popped handle. Non-`REMOTE_CACHING` firmware resolves descriptors itself and is left alone.

**Testing**: 176 pass, 100% line + branch coverage retained. Three new cases: CCCD cleared under `REMOTE_CACHING`, skipped without it, and the proxy subscription still released when the CCCD write raises.

author: nosen-nvt
body:
`capabilities.docker` を持つ job が sandbox の中から **volume 名を指定するだけで daemon の永続状態を丸ごと読めた**。

`build/container/compose.yml` は daemon の状態を `boid_state` named volume 1 本に集約し `/home/boid` (daemon の $HOME) 全体に mount している。compose の `name: boid` により実際の volume 名は `boid_boid_state`。中身は `boid.db` / **`secret.key`** (シークレット暗号化鍵) / `web_secret` / `tls/ca.key` / `install_id` / `~/.config/boid/` 一式。

dockerproxy policy の予約判定は `boid-ws-` prefix のみだったので、次が素通りしていた:

```json
{"HostConfig":{"Mounts":[{"Type":"volume","Source":"boid_boid_state","Target":"/state"}]}}
```

この露出は volume-only cutover 以前から存在し、#839 が「boid 所有の volume は sandbox から触らせない」原則を立てた際に、**いちばん価値の高い volume が対象外のまま残っていた**。

## 方式

daemon が起動時に `/proc/self/mountinfo` (fallback: `/proc/self/cgroup`) から自分の container ID を特定し、`ContainerInspect` で自分にマウントされた named volume 名を列挙、dockerproxy policy の予約集合に動的に載せる。#839 で作った 3 経路 (`volumes/create` の Name、`DELETE /volumes/{name}`、`containers/create` の `Mounts[].Source`) の判定機構をそのまま再利用する。

却下した代案: `boid_`/`boid-` prefix の一律 deny (ユーザ volume の誤爆 + compose project 名の変更で破綻)、ledger 所有でない volume の mount 全 deny (挙動変化が大きすぎる)。

予約するのは「**自分にマウントされている named volume 全部**」で dataHome を含むものだけではない。`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (config.yaml / host_commands.yaml / `workspaces/<slug>/init.sh`) は `filepath.Dir(cfg.DBPath)` の外にあり、今は同じ `/home/boid` mount に載っているという偶然でしか覆われていない。over-reserve の代償は job にとって説明可能な損失が無く、under-reserve の代償は `secret.key`。

## 「守れていないのに黙っている」経路を構造的に潰した

self-inspect は失敗しうるので fail-open (WARN + 続行) にしたが、それは「失敗したことを必ず伝える」が成り立って初めて許容できる。**codex レビュー 3 巡で、黙って無防備になる経路が 4 つ見つかり全部塞いだ**:

| # | 経路 | 対応 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | container 内判定を engine 固有の sentinel ファイルで行っていたため、containerd / Kubernetes 等で「container 外」と誤分類し**無警告で containment 無効** | 判定を「daemon の永続領域が mountinfo 上で `/` 以外の mount に覆われているか」に変更。engine 種別にも sentinel にも依存せず、保護対象そのものに直結する |
| 2 | `dataHome` が相対パスや symlink 経由だと root mount と誤判定 | 判定前に `filepath.Abs` + `filepath.EvalSymlinks` で正規化。「hung filesystem で stat したくない」という当初の回避理由は、daemon がそもそも同じパスで `boid.db` を開く以上成立しないので撤回 |
| 3 | docker client の構築が deadline の外にあり、その失敗が `StateVolumeExpected == false` として無警告で捨てられた | client を `buildRuntime` で 1 個だけ構築して container backend と**共有**。呼び出し側は error を先に読む。結果 **「error != nil ⇒ StateVolumeExpected == true」** が構造的に成立し、false を返すのは「root mount 上のただの dir と肯定的に確認した」経路のみになった |
| 4 | cgroup fallback が最初の 64 hex を無条件に採るため、ネストした形で**親 container を inspect しえた**。親にも同じ宛先の volume があれば「守れているように見えて実際は守っていない」最悪の形になる | distinct な ID が 2 個以上なら曖昧として推測せず WARN + fail-open |

`ContainerInspect` には deadline を付けた (engine が接続を受けたまま無応答なら起動が永久に止まっていた)。

正規化だけ失敗して ID 特定と inspect が成功した経路は、error ではなく `DataHomeUnresolved` フィールドで伝える。error にすると呼び出し側が「containment INACTIVE」と警告してしまい実態と食い違う (volume は実際に予約されている)。この場合 `data_home_covered` は信用できないので、**それを事実として述べる方の WARN は抑制する** (両方出すと矛盾した log になり operator は行動できない)。

## 実機での検証

実際の `/proc/self/mountinfo` を live な rootless podman deploy と bare host の両方から取得し、判定ロジックを実データに当てて確認した (読み取り専用):

| 環境 | dataHome | 覆っている mount | 判定 |
|---|---|---|---|
| live `boid_daemon_1` (rootless podman 4.9.3) | `/home/boid/.local/share/boid` | `/home/boid` | **true** → `boid_boid_state` を予約 |
| bare host | `/home/nosen/.local/share/boid` | `/` | **false** → 無言の no-op、engine を呼ばない |

mountinfo の形式は podman (`/containers/overlay-containers/<64hex>/userdata/hostname`) と docker (`/var/lib/docker/containers/<64hex>/hostname`) の両方を fixture にしてある。実機で `/proc/self/cgroup` が `0::/` (cgroup v2、ID なし) を返すことも確認済みで、これが cgroup を主判定にできない根拠。

## 副次的な発見 (本 PR では未対応)

live な rootless podman deploy では **`HOSTNAME` 環境変数が空**で、`ContainerBackendOptions.SelfContainerID: os.Getenv("HOSTNAME")` が inert になっている。`ensureWorkspaceNetwork` の daemon self-connect が silent に行われていない疑いがある。本 PR の mountinfo ベースの container ID 取得が流用できる。

## 検証

`go build` / `go vet` / `go test ./...` / `go test -race` / `check-internal-architecture.sh` / `golangci-lint` すべて green。実ユーザ領域は 165,315 エントリの find 比較で無変化。

codex 静的レビュー 3 巡: 1 巡目 Major 3 + Minor 1、2 巡目 Major 2、3 巡目 Blocker 0 / Major 0 / Minor 2 → 全対応。配線 seam と警告契約は mutation proof (実装をわざと壊して赤を確認) で pin してある。

author: lmpeixoto
body:
## Summary

Implements backlog #21 (Define SLOs and alerting rules) and #21c (wire
Alertmanager to a real notification channel), per ADR 0020.

- `alertmanager.enabled` flips `false` → `true` in `argocd/apps/prometheus.yaml`.
- One Prometheus alert rule per row in ADR 0020's SLO table, added via
  `server.serverFiles.alerting_rules.yml` (no Operator/`PrometheusRule` CRD,
  consistent with ADR 0014's stance):
  - `GatewayHighErrorRate` / `ApiHighErrorRate`: non-5xx rate (`outcome="SERVER_ERROR"`)
    > 5% over 5m — matches the threshold ADR 0017's dashboard already uses.
  - `ApiVariantsLookupHighErrorRate`: same signal scoped to `uri="/variants/lookup"`
    (api's external dependency on clinvar-service), 10% threshold — lower per-endpoint
    traffic in this dev cluster is noisier, so a slightly higher bar avoids paging on
    one or two failed manual test calls.
  - `WorkersListenerErrorRate`: the listener timer's own `error!="none"` tag, >5%/5m.
  - `WorkersConsumerLagHigh`: `sum(kafka_consumer_fetch_manager_records_lag)` > 500,
    sustained 10m — this dev cluster's real traffic is a handful of messages per
    session, so 500 un-consumed records is already orders of magnitude past jitter.
  - `ClinVarIngestionFreshnessBreach`: no completed ingestion attempt in 8 days
    (weekly cadence + 1 day grace).
  - `ClinVarIngestionDurationAnomaly`: latest observed ingestion duration > 360s
    (4x the ~90s real-data baseline, "several multiples" per ADR 0020's wording).
- **Stated gap, not silently skipped**: clinvar-service's `GET /internal/clinvar/lookup`
  non-5xx-rate alert (also in ADR 0020's table) is *not* included — its shipped metric
  (`clinvar_lookup_duration_seconds`) has no status/outcome label, so there's no real
  signal to alert against yet. Tracked as new adamastorx backlog #21e, not faked here.
- **Also fixes a real gap found while writing these rules**: clinvar-service was never
  actually added to Prometheus's scrape config when its `/metrics` endpoint shipped
  (#21a) — confirmed missing from a live `/api/v1/targets` call before writing any
  clinvar-service alert rule (an unscraped metric's rule would silently never fire,
  not error). Added as a fifth static scrape target.
- **#21c**: Alertmanager's own `config` wired to one real receiver — `webhook_configs`
  pointed at a randomly-generated-once `ntfy.sh` topic. Chosen over
  Slack/Discord/Telegram/PagerDuty for needing zero account/credential setup (verified
  live: POSTing an Alertmanager-shaped JSON blob to a topic-suffixed ntfy URL returns
  200 and delivers a real push notification — readable but not prettified, a nicer
  template/relay is real follow-on work, not needed for this bar). A minimal severity
  routing tree exists (`critical` gets a faster `group_wait`/`repeat_interval`,
  everything else shares the same receiver on a slower cadence) — deliberately not
  over-built, per #21c's own AC ("#21b's future burn-rate work will refine later").
  Alertmanager's persistence is disabled (`emptyDir`) for v1 — its first-ever deploy,
  nothing to lose yet.

## Verification done

- All 7 alert expressions confirmed syntactically valid and evaluable against the
  live cluster's actual running Prometheus (`kubectl -n prometheus port-forward
  svc/prometheus-server`), each returning `status: success` (empty result sets are
  expected — none of the breach conditions are currently true, and clinvar-service
  isn't scraped yet pre-merge).
- Confirmed live that clinvar-service is genuinely absent from `/api/v1/targets`
  today (the scrape-config gap this PR also fixes).
- Full chart render reproduced locally exactly as CI's `helm-render` job does
  (`scripts/render-helm-charts.sh` + `kubeconform -strict -ignore-missing-schemas`)
  — all 12 rendered Applications valid, including this one (Alertmanager's
  `ConfigMap`/`StatefulSet` and Prometheus's rule `ConfigMap` all render as expected).
  Also ran the plain `manifests` job's kubeconform invocation against `argocd/` —
  clean.

## Left for post-merge (explicit, not silently skipped)

This PR is **not deployed to the live cluster**. ArgoCD's `prometheus` Application
has `syncPolicy.automated: {prune: true, selfHeal: true}` under the app-of-apps
pattern (ADR 0003) — a pre-merge manual trial (e.g. pointing the live Application's
`targetRevision` at this branch) would fight that same `selfHeal` reverting it back
to `main`, so the safer, correct point to verify live is after merge, when ArgoCD
picks this up through its normal GitOps flow.

Post-merge verification checklist for a human (or a follow-up agent run) to do:
1. Confirm ArgoCD synced `prometheus` (`kubectl -n argocd get application prometheus`).
2. Confirm all 7 rules loaded: `kubectl -n prometheus port-forward svc/prometheus-server 9090:80`,
   then `curl localhost:9090/api/v1/rules`.
3. Confirm the Alertmanager UI shows the same 7 rules with the ntfy receiver attached
   (`kubectl -n prometheus port-forward svc/prometheus-alertmanager 9093:9093`).
4. Trigger one real alert condition and confirm it reaches the ntfy topic — e.g.
   `kubectl -n workers scale deployment/workers --replicas=0` for a few minutes to
   build `WorkersConsumerLagHigh` backlog (if `work-items` traffic is flowing), or any
   other reversible fault matching one of the 7 rules above, then scale back up.
5. Subscribe to the ntfy topic (value committed in `argocd/apps/prometheus.yaml`,
   `alertmanager.config.receivers[0].webhook_configs[0].url`) via the ntfy Android/iOS
   app or `curl -s https://ntfy.sh/<topic>/json` to confirm the notification actually
   arrived.

## Test plan

- [x] `helm template` render + `kubeconform -strict` clean (both the rendered chart
      output and the raw `argocd/`/`kubernetes/` manifests).
- [x] All 7 PromQL expressions validated against a real, live Prometheus instance.
- [ ] Post-merge: rules loaded in `/api/v1/rules`, one alert fired and confirmed
      reaching the ntfy topic (see checklist above).

Related: adamastorx#21, adamastorx#21c, adamastorx#21e (new, tracks the
clinvar-service metric gap this PR states rather than fakes).

author: juanmahidalgo
body:
Stacked on #179, which left an explicit `TODO(ops)`: dev held a placeholder address (`0x1111…1111`) with the flag off. This resolves it so the flow can be validated end-to-end on Amoy.

- `dev.json`: `PROCEEDS_TO_TREASURY` → `"true"`, `TREASURY_ADDRESS` → the real Amoy treasury `0x3EEdEceaFA4797D36819C1d9f8e3b0071285AD69` (funded with test MANA/POL).
- `stg.json` / `prod.json`: unchanged — flag off, address empty.
- Replaced the TODO with the ordering constraint below, so this cannot be re-enabled from scratch in the wrong sequence.

## Deploy ordering — this must go LAST

With the flag on here and credits-server's consumer not yet live, listings route their MANA to the treasury and nobody credits the seller. Recoverable on a testnet; not on mainnet. So:

1. credits-server #527 + #528, deployed to dev with `PROCEEDS_TO_TREASURY=true` and `TREASURY_ADDRESS` set (env scaffolded in definitions #1620, flag currently off there).
2. **then** this.

shop-server (#14 + #16) is NOT a prerequisite — it only reconciles and alerts, it is not in the money path. It is blocked on DevOps granting the repo access to `QUAY_USERNAME`/`QUAY_TOKEN`, and that block does not hold up this test. The trade-off while it is missing: the payout path runs unmonitored, so the first runs should be watched by hand.

The Amoy trades-squid is already reindexed onto trades-squid-core#38 — I verified the promoted `squid_trades` schema in the dev `dapps` DB has `log_index` and `received_beneficiaries`, so credits-server's capability probe will pass and it will start observing immediately.

## Verification

`tsc -b` clean, eslint clean on `src/config`, 82 suites / 999 tests green. The 4 pre-existing eslint errors in `src/lib/names.ts` are untouched by this diff.

Worth noting what the flag does NOT change: `proceedsBeneficiary()` still guards on a non-empty address, so a future misconfiguration falls back to the seller/creator rather than routing proceeds to nowhere.

author: adamisrael
body:
Closes #203.

## What

An operator picks a theme and the SSH TUI honours it; the browser frontend shipped fixed colours. An amber board served a `#1e5f74` teal login button, grey-blue links, and — since #201 — header/footer bars in `#0a0a0a`. `[theme]` quietly meant "SSH only".

`theme_css` renders the resolved `Theme` as CSS custom properties, injected into the page #201 already builds per request. The stylesheet's own values remain the defaults, so a role the theme can't express changes nothing.

## Scope — and a correction to the issue

I framed #203 as "the browser terminal is always black". Reading the rendering code properly, **that was overstated**, and I [corrected it on the issue](https://github.com/AdamIsrael/bbs-rs/issues/203#issuecomment-5084293021) before starting.

The TUI sets a background on exactly two things — the title bar and the warning line. Everything else inherits the terminal's, and `Theme` has **no background colour at all**. Black isn't a bug; it's the assumption every preset and every shipped ANSI art file is designed around. So the terminal stays as it was, and this changes the page furniture, which is what's actually wrong:

| Theme role | Drives |
|---|---|
| `title_bg` | login button, header/footer bar background |
| `title_fg` | button text, bar text |
| `accent` | links |
| `warning_fg` / `warning_bg` | login error text |
| `dim` | secondary text |

Note `title_fg` for the **button text**: it was hardcoded `#fff`, which fails on a light accent like amber. Using the theme's own contrast partner is both correct and self-maintaining.

## Colour mapping

Colours map through **xterm.js's default palette**, not an invented one. The same theme drives the TUI *inside* that terminal, so a private mapping would have the chrome and the terminal content disagreeing about what "cyan" is on a single screen.

- `Rgb` passes through as its own hex — an operator's `#ffb000` is never snapped to a palette entry
- `Indexed` walks the 256-colour cube, including its **uneven** `0/95/135/175/215/255` step table
- `Reset` yields no hex — it means "the terminal's default" — so those roles keep the built-in

## Verification

- `cargo fmt` / `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean; full `cargo test` green.
- Colour-mapping unit tests: named → palette, RGB passthrough, the 256 cube's boundaries and grey ramp, `Reset` → `None`.
- Four HTTP tests: classic's cyan/black/yellow reach the page as palette hexes and `#1e5f74` is gone; a preset changes them; a per-colour override wins; and `Color::Reset` emits no declaration, so exactly one `--bbs-dim` survives.
- **Live against a real amber board**: the served page carries a second `:root` block overriding the defaults with `#ffb000`, winning by cascade order.

#204 (custom CSS) is the remaining half, and now has theme-derived custom properties to define precedence against.

body:
Adds Apple Watch screenshots to the App Store listing (which currently has none). Rebased onto `main` after #237 + #238 landed (supersedes the auto-closed #239, which GitHub closed when its stacked base branch was deleted on merge).

## Why simctl, not XCUITest
watchOS ships no `XCTest.framework` in the simulator SDK → no `XCUIApplication`, no UI automation. So the watch app takes both roles: a DEBUG-only `--screenshot-screen <slug>` launch arg boots it straight into one screen, and `simctl launch` + `simctl io screenshot` captures it. Language rides in via `-AppleLanguages`/`-AppleLocale` launch args, same as the iOS path.

## What
- **DEBUG-only screenshot mode** (`WatchScreenshotMode.swift`, whole file `#if DEBUG` + flag-gated): throwaway in-memory `DemoData` store, renders one of 5 screens (live dive, summary, dive profile, session list, start). `DemoData` moved to `Persistence` (shared, DEBUG-only, absent from Release).
- **Device:** Apple Watch Ultra 3 (49mm) → 422×514 → `APP_WATCH_ULTRA`.
- **Fail-closed throughout:** slug-stamped "screen ready" handshake (no render → timeout → no PNG); resolved-vs-requested language verified per capture; unknown slug / blank summary/profile → `fatalError` (DEBUG); PNGs flattened to RGB with an alpha assertion.
- **Upload safety:** `stage_screenshots` validates against an expected-devices manifest and **refuses to stage if any device class is missing from every locale** — `deliver` deletes a locale's screenshots across all display types under `overwrite_screenshots`, so an iOS-only or watch-failed run would otherwise wipe the live Watch set.

## Verification
- `DiveFreeWatch` builds (debug + Release); screenshot symbols only in the debug dylib, absent from Release.
- Watch capture run for ja + uk: correct language + number formats, RGB 422×514, cross-locale check fires, list/summary/profile are one story.
- Completeness guard tested against full / iOS-only / per-locale-gap / no-manifest fixtures — aborts on the last three.
- Rebased cleanly onto main (3 watch commits, no conflicts); A's purge lane + B's localization both present underneath.

Reviewed three times (8 findings round 1, 4 round 3, all fixed).

## Summary

- Discovers and verifies the rival-battle trigger (it happens inside Oak's Lab, not outside as originally assumed) and adds `create_rival_battle_state.py` to reproduce `rival_battle.state` reliably.
- Adds and empirically verifies battle memory addresses (HP, moves, PP, in-battle flag), sourced from the public pret/pokered disassembly and cross-checked against real gameplay before being trusted.
- Adds a Gymnasium battle environment (`envs/battle_env.py`) with PP-aware move masking and proportional HP-based reward shaping, and trains a Stable-Baselines3 DQN that wins **100/100** evaluation battles.
- Adds a tabular Q-learning agent for the leave-house task (`agents/q_learning_agent.py`) that wins **30/30** evaluation episodes, a 19-step path every time.

## Notable bugs found and fixed along the way

- The move-select cursor in battle is sticky (remembers the last move used) and the move list wraps around instead of clamping — a fixed navigation sequence was silently selecting the wrong move most of the time. Fixed by reading the cursor's actual screen position.
- Clearing a battle turn's dialogue with a fixed press-count was unreliable since different moves produce different amounts of text. Fixed with `advance_battle_dialogue()`, which checks real game state instead of guessing a count (same idea as the existing `walk_tile()`).

- Moving `config.py` into `core/` broke its hardcoded parent-directory count for `PROJECT_ROOT` — caught immediately by re-running the environments after the move, not just checking that imports resolved.

author: aalonx
body:
Follow-up to #56, from the machine it was verified on: after that merge the user logged out, logged back in — and the keyring was still locked.

## What #56 got wrong

It masked `gnome-keyring-daemon.socket` and deliberately stopped nothing, on the reasoning that *"the running daemon keeps serving this session and the change lands at the next login."*

`mask` only refuses **future** starts. It never touches a unit that is already running, and `user@$UID.service` outlives the session whenever lingering is on (`loginctl enable-linger`, which plenty of tooling sets). So the daemon that the socket started *before* the mask survives logout after logout, still owning `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/keyring/control`:

```
pid 1473  gnome-keyring-daemon.service   started 16:19:19, still alive at 18:07
Linger=yes                               user manager pid 718 from 16:18:21, survives logout
18:05:46  gnome-keyring-daemon[30580]: discover_other_daemon: 1   ← PAM's daemon gives up again
```

The survivor does receive the password over the control socket (it recreates `login.keyring` and `user.keystore`), but its Secret Service is already initialized, so the collection never gets exposed — `gkm_object_expose_full: assertion 'GKM_IS_OBJECT (self)' failed` — and you get a `login` collection that is **listed but not loaded**. That fails asymmetrically, which is what sends people looking in the wrong place: reads answer "not found" instantly, so Settings → AI happily enables its buttons, while the first write blocks on a `gcr-prompter` that times out after 10 s without answering. The Save button dies and nothing is logged.

Net effect: the fix appeared inert until a full **reboot**.

## The change

- `nidara-setup` stops what it masks — **socket first**, because the `.service` `Requires=` it and follows it down, whereas stopping the service alone leaves the socket listening for the next probe to re-activate it.
- No session is left without a Secret Service: `org.freedesktop.secrets` stays D-Bus activatable (unchanged, and argued in the existing comment). That is also how a fresh rival can appear behind our back, so if a daemon is still running after the stop, the script now says the machine needs a **reboot** instead of reporting success.
- `hyprland.lua`: the comment said the socket must "stay disabled" — masked-but-running is just as fatal, so it now says masked **and not running**.

## Skill

- `dev-workflow.md` — the mask/stop rule with the lingering explanation, and a corrected verification recipe. The old one checked the service's `Collections` property, which **lists `/collection/login` even when it was never loaded**: a false positive for exactly the broken state. The real probe is the collection object; `Object does not exist at path` is the signature. Also documents the other cause of the same signature (a stale `user.keystore` whose password isn't the login one) and its fix.
- `tech-debt.md` #41 — Settings → AI cannot tell a hung keyring write from a working one: `storeKey()` re-enables the button only from a callback that never runs, and `keyringAvailable()` probes service liveness rather than collection writability.

## Testing

Not reachable from `Super+Shift+R` and not covered by the CI smoke (the headless boot has no PAM login) — same limitation as #56. The failure mode this fixes was reproduced first-hand: journal, D-Bus probes and unit states above all come from the affected session. The `stop` semantics are the safe direction regardless (systemd permits `JOB_STOP` on masked units; `Requires=` propagation from the socket is in the shipped unit file).

author: quadseven
body:
Fixes #1345.

## Why

`getTorrentStatusFromState` derives `active`/`inactive` for the qBittorrent backend from the state string alone. That works for most states, but not for the two forced ones.

qBittorrent resolves `isForced()` **before** it tests the payload rate in `TorrentImpl::updateState`, so `Uploading`/`StalledUploading` and `Downloading`/`StalledDownloading` are unreachable for a force-started torrent — `forcedUP` and `forcedDL` each cover both the transferring and the idle case. The state string does not carry the information, so no mapping from it alone can be correct.

The result is that a force-seeding torrent is reported `inactive` while it is uploading (and never matches the `Active` filter), and an idle force-started download is reported `active`. `upRate`/`downRate` are correct throughout, which is what makes `status` visibly inconsistent with the rest of the record.

Size: XS

## Acceptance criteria

- `forcedUP` reports `active` when the torrent is transferring and `inactive` when it is not, and stays in the `seeding` taxonomy either way.
- `forcedDL` reports `active` when transferring and `inactive` when not, and stays in the `downloading` taxonomy either way.
- States that already encode their own activity are unchanged: `uploading`, `stalledUP`, `downloading`, `stalledDL`, `queuedUP`, `queuedDL`, `stoppedUP`, `stoppedDL`, `checkingUP`, `checkingDL`, `metaDL`, `forcedMetaDL`, `error`, `missingFiles`, `moving`, `checkingResumeData`, `unknown`.
- The `warning` status from a tracker message is still appended independently of the activity flag.
- Behaviour matches the rTorrent backend, which already derives the flag from observed rates.

## What changed

- `getTorrentStatusFromState` takes an `isTransferring` argument (defaulting to `false`, so existing callers keep their current behaviour) and uses it for `forcedUP` and `forcedDL` only. `forcedUP` is split out of the `queuedUP`/`stalledUP` case, and `forcedDL` out of the `metaDL`/`forcedMetaDL`/`downloading` case.
- The call site in `clientGatewayService.ts` hoists the `info.dlspeed > 0 || info.upspeed > 0` predicate it already computed for `dateActive` into a local `isTransferring` and passes it through, so no extra request or field is needed.
- New unit tests for the mapping.

## Test plan

- `pnpm run check-types` — clean
- `pnpm run lint` — clean (`--max-warnings 0`)
- `pnpm exec prettier -c` on the touched files — clean
- 13 new unit tests in `server/services/qBittorrent/util/torrentPropertiesUtil.test.ts`, covering both forced states in both directions, the states that must stay rate-independent, the `warning` append, and the default argument. All pass.
- Verified against a real qBittorrent 5.2.1 instance: captured a live `/api/v2/torrents/info` payload of 67 force-seeding torrents, 2 of which were uploading at the time (84,682 B/s and 1,318 B/s), and replayed it through the old and new mapping. Exactly those 2 flipped `[complete,inactive,seeding]` to `[complete,active,seeding]`; the other 65 were untouched.

The pre-existing integration projects spawn real torrent-client binaries, so I was not able to run them locally — the new tests are pure unit tests over the mapping function and need no client.

## Out of scope

- The `active`/`inactive` derivation for the other backends.
- Any change to how the `Active`/`Inactive` sidebar filters are computed from `status`.
- `metaDL`/`forcedMetaDL`, which are a metadata fetch rather than a payload transfer and keep reporting `active`.

body:
## What
On mobile, the project list loads but **opening a session** fails with the service worker's `{"error":"network-unreachable","detail":"Load failed"}`. The stale worker serves the cached landing page while its `fetch()` for `/session/<project>` rejects. Bumps `public/sw.js` `CACHE_NAME` **v3-56 → v3-57** so an existing worker installs the current one on next navigation (`skipWaiting()` + `clients.claim()` already make it take over live).

## Why it's the stale worker, not #380's PTY exhaustion
#380 attributes this exact mobile symptom to ttyd PTY-pool exhaustion. But when diagnosed **2026-07-26** the pool was **healthy** — 36 ttys / 14 procs / 0 leaked children, vs #380's 230/153 exhaustion baseline — and a Safari **Private tab** (which runs no service worker) loaded sessions fine. So this instance was a stale service worker, a distinct trigger from PTY exhaustion. #380's durable PTY fix and a durable stale-worker auto-bump both remain open follow-ups.

## Test plan
- The three `CACHE_NAME` monotone-floor guards (`bridge-port-input`, `master-drawer-frontend`, `openclaw-cache`) pass unchanged (57 > their floors).
- Live-served `sw.js` confirmed serving `v3-57`; operator to verify a normal-tab mobile session-open now succeeds.

Animating `100%`, `24/7` and `A–Z` from zero meant the trust band opened by showing `5%`, `1/7` and a partial `A–Z`.
