## Summary

- add the unified `stable-lifecycle` certification command, closed versioned lifecycle policy and schemas, authenticated published-build inventory, append-only transition ledger, deterministic descriptor artifacts, and protected publication verification
- integrate the separately versioned `support-lifecycle` update-key document with CoreUpdater using exact trust-scope binding, sequential editions, persisted last-known-good state, future-effective transition handling, replay/fork protection, and crash-durable compromise invalidation
- enforce effective build revocation at package download, installer launch, and store handoff boundaries without conflating it with update-signing-key compromise or disabling non-destructive node operation
- expose a redacted host/operator-only lifecycle snapshot through the detached runtime SPI, Platform API, Web Shell, diagnostics, and support bundles while keeping the app-readable core-update contract unchanged
- bind Stable maintenance, Platform API deprecation clocks, first-party app/catalog state, content-profile governance, security advisories, and hotfix follow-up obligations to authenticated lifecycle state
- add protected lifecycle input, authorization, publication-backend, publication, and independent-verification workflows with exact provenance, protected-ref checks, idempotency, conflict detection, and no publication from tests or pull requests
- preserve immutable historical GA/maintenance receipts, baselines, history entries, release assets, and `core-info.json`; support status changes only through the separate authenticated lifecycle descriptor
- update project documentation and repository skills to describe the finalized activation, trust-scope, persistence, package-selection, security, and operator behavior

## Lifecycle policy

The closed build vocabulary is:

- `current-stable`
- `supported-maintenance`
- `security-fixes-only`
- `deprecated`
- `end-of-support`
- `revoked`

Normal transitions are monotonic. Revocation is an explicit terminal security path requiring protected authorization, advisory or incident linkage, and authenticated replacement or recovery guidance. Policy durations and freshness windows are data-driven in the versioned policy rather than hard-coded into Java or Python.

## Security and compatibility boundaries

- build revocation remains distinct from update-key compromise
- update-key compromise stops update-key-derived activity before durable marker persistence and restores the critical alert and revocation propagation after restart
- descriptor replay, rollback, fork, wrong scope/docname/key identity, stale editions, unexpected fields, and release-identity substitution fail closed
- future-effective editions do not skip intermediate lifecycle or recovery-guidance intervals
- `supported-maintenance` receives optional `recommendedBuild` guidance rather than a false mandatory replacement
- unsupported or revoked state does not delete data, uninstall apps, shut down the node, disable FProxy browse, or introduce forced-update semantics
- the operator-only lifecycle route does not advance or leak through the app-facing Platform API contract
- no centralized telemetry, installation counting, or background reporting is introduced

## How to test

- [x] `./gradlew spotlessApply`
- [x] `./gradlew test`
- [x] `python3 tools/release-certification/certify.py stable-lifecycle --self-test` — 120 tests passed
- [x] `python3 tools/release-certification/certify.py stable-maintenance --self-test` — 182 tests passed, including the fixed canonical GitHub Release destination and configurable-target fail-closed coverage
- [x] `python3 tools/release-certification/certify.py app-platform-docs --self-test`
- [x] `./gradlew :runtime-node:test --tests '*CoreSupportLifecycleParserTest' --tests '*CoreSupportLifecycleStateTest' --tests '*CoreSupportLifecycleStoreTest' --tests '*CoreSupportLifecycleTransitionTest'`
- [x] `./gradlew :test --tests '*CoreSupportLifecycleUpdaterTest' --tests '*CoreUpdaterTest' --tests '*NodeUpdateManagerTest' --tests '*NodeUpdaterTest' --tests '*RevocationCheckerTest' --tests '*UpdateOverMandatoryManagerTest'`
- [x] `./gradlew :runtime-spi:test :adapter-http-legacy-admin:test`
- [x] `./gradlew :test --tests '*LegacyCoreUpdateActionPortTest' --tests '*CoreActionToadletTest'`
- [x] `git diff --check origin/develop...HEAD`

## Publication note

No lifecycle descriptor, update-key edition, tag, GitHub Release, catalog, or package was published while developing or testing this change. Activating lifecycle state still requires the protected release-manager/security-manager authorization and publication environments, private insert material supplied only through protected secret indirection, and independent exact-byte verification.

author: oferchen
body:
## The bug

Protocol 28 and older carry no iflags on the wire. Upstream synthesises a value
instead:

```c
/* rsync.c:383-384 */
iflags = protocol_version >= 29 ? read_shortint(f_in)
           : ITEM_TRANSFER | ITEM_MISSING_DATA;
```

`ITEM_MISSING_DATA` makes `log.c:736-737` fill itemize columns 2..10 with `?`,
so a proto-28 transfer renders `>f?????????` - "the peer did not tell me what
changed".

We synthesised a bare `ITEM_TRANSFER`, which rendered `>f.........` and
asserted "nothing changed" - a claim neither side ever made. We support
protocol 28-32, so this is reachable against any pre-29 peer.

## The fix

`ITEM_MISSING_DATA` is bit 16. Upstream deliberately keeps it off the wire
(`iflags &= 0xffff`, generator.c:581) and synthesises it only at the
decode-to-display site. Only one of our four pre-29 fallbacks reaches a
renderer, so only that one gains the bit - making all four agree with each
other would make them disagree with upstream.

| Site | Change |
|---|---|
| `generator/item_flags.rs` `ItemFlags::read` | now `ITEM_TRANSFER \| ITEM_MISSING_DATA`. Its sole caller feeds `write_iflags_into`; the echo path already masks `& 0xFFFF`, so the log-only bit cannot leak onto the wire. |
| `receiver/wire.rs` (x2) | unchanged - `SenderAttrs.iflags` is a u16 that only selects which trailing fields to parse and is echoed back, never rendered. A display bit would be dead state. Comments now record why. |
| `batch/replay/dispatch.rs` | returned `0x8000 \| 0x0400`. `0x0400` is `1<<10` = `ITEM_REPORT_CRTIME` (rsync.h:247), **not** `ITEM_MISSING_DATA` (`1<<16`, rsync.h:254) - it set an unrelated flag. Dropped; the named constant now carries its rsync.h citation. |

`itemize.rs` already gives `ITEM_IS_NEW` priority over `ITEM_MISSING_DATA`
(mirroring log.c:735-737), so a newly created file still renders `+++++++++`.
Confirmed rather than assumed, and pinned by a test.

## A test encoded the bug

`generator/tests.rs::item_flags_read_protocol_28` asserted the bare
`ITEM_TRANSFER` and its comment stated that behaviour as though intended. It is
updated to the upstream contract (and extended to cover proto 20) rather than
the code being bent to keep it green.

## Verification

Compared against a genuine upstream 3.4.4 (`rsync version 3.4.4 protocol
version 32`, confirmed from the `--version` banner), with the peer advertising
protocol 28 so the negotiated version is genuinely 28. Push rows, byte-for-byte:

```
before   <f......... changed.txt     <f......... new.txt
after    <f????????? changed.txt     <f????????? new.txt     <f????????? sub/deep.txt
upstream <f????????? changed.txt     <f????????? new.txt     <f????????? sub/deep.txt
```

Tests: `-p transfer -p batch -p protocol --all-features` 8678 passed; the same
crates with default features (incremental-flist off) 2732 passed. fmt + clippy
`--workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean.

## Out of scope (filed as observations, not fixed here)

Two adjacent divergences surfaced during verification and are **not** addressed:

1. **`--protocol=N` is a no-op on the client's SSH path.** `oc-rsync -ai
   --protocol=28 <src> h:<dst>` produces argv and output identical to omitting
   the flag, and still sends the proto-32 capability suffix
   (`-logDtpre.iLsfxCIvu` where upstream at 28 sends `-logDtpr`). Clamping only
   happens when the *peer* advertises the lower version. This is why
   verification above forces 28 from the peer side.
2. **Pull-side itemize at proto 28** still renders locally-computed flags
   (`>f+++++++++` / row ordering) where upstream renders `>f?????????` after a
   leading `cd+++++++++`. That is a structural difference in where the receiver
   sources its itemize row, not a fallback-value bug.

author: gilbert09
body:
## Problem

`apple_search_ads` was a scaffolded stub in the data warehouse source registry.
It appeared in the enum and the catalog but had no `get_schemas`, no client and no tests, so it could not actually be connected.

Apple Search Ads spend is required for mobile acquisition reporting alongside the other ad networks.

## Changes

Implements the `apple_search_ads` source end to end.

- Transport: hand-rolled. Apple Search Ads needs an ES256-signed JWT client-secret assertion minted per token exchange, an `X-AP-Context: orgId=` header, and POST report requests whose date window/pagination live in a nested `selector` body with rows nested under `data.reportingDataResponse.row[].granularity[]`; none of that is expressible in the declarative rest_source config. All HTTP rides `make_tracked_session()` (custom `Retry` that adds POST to the retryable methods, since urllib3's default refuses POST retries and every read path except `/campaigns` and `/acls` is a POST); no tenacity layer
- Base class: `ResumableSource[AppleSearchAdsSourceConfig, AppleSearchAdsResumeConfig]`
- Credentials the customer supplies: Customer-supplied config fields: `org_id`, `client_id`, `apple_team_id` (Apple's teamId, JWT `iss`), `key_id` (JWT `kid`), `private_key` (unencrypted EC P-256 PEM, TEXTAREA + secret), plus optional `start_date` for the report backfill floor. PostHog signs a 30-minute ES256 assertion with PyJWT (already a repo dep, as is cryptography) and exchanges it for a 1-hour access token at `https://appleid.apple.com/auth/oauth2/token` (`grant_type=client_credentials`, `scope=searchadsorg`); re-minted once on a 401 mid-sync. No Integration kind, no OAuth app, no new env var, no new dependency
- Tables exposed (7): `acls`, `campaigns`, `ad_groups`, `keywords`, `campaign_report`, `ad_group_report`, `keyword_report`
- Incremental sync: yes, the three `*_report` tables are incremental on `date` (Apple's server-side `startTime`/`endTime` report filter, YYYY-MM-DD). Entity tables (`acls`, `campaigns`, `ad_groups`, `keywords`) are full refresh: Apple's entity list/find endpoints expose no updated-since filter. Report tables are `merge_only` (append is not offered) with `default_incremental_lookback_seconds = 7 days`

Shipped as `releaseStatus=ReleaseStatus.ALPHA`.
The diff is limited to this source's own directory, its generated config and its icon, plus a one line move in `SOURCES.md` from the scaffolded list to the implemented table.

### Notes for review

- `frontend/public/services/apple_search_ads.png` was ALREADY committed (128x128 Apple mark). I fetched the Logo.dev 512px version, compared them, found it the same logo, and reverted to the committed file so the diff carries no icon churn. Nothing under `frontend/` is in this commit.
- Ordering / watermark design (the load-bearing decision, please sanity-check): report rows within one request window arrive grouped by entity, not by date, so `date` is not strictly ascending inside a batch. Windows are walked oldest-first and capped at `REPORT_WINDOW_DAYS = 7`, and the schema's `default_incremental_lookback_seconds` is set to exactly the same 7 days, so the most the per-batch...
- Resume: state is `(offset, window_start, campaign_id)`, saved after each yielded batch and again pointing at the next (window, campaign) task on task completion. On resume the checkpoint is matched by VALUE against a freshly built task list, not by index, so a changed campaign list restarts the window range (duplicates merge) rather than skipping a campaign. Campaign ids are sorted for a...
- Org-wide find endpoints `POST /adgroups/find` and `POST /targetingkeywords/find` (used instead of 2-level per-campaign fan-out). If `/targetingkeywords/find` turns out to be campaign-scoped only, the `keywords` table needs fan-out.
- Ad-group and keyword reports exist only per campaign (`/reports/campaigns/{id}/adgroups`, `/reports/campaigns/{id}/keywords`), so those two tables fan out over campaign ids; `campaign_report` does not.
- `selector.orderBy` is deliberately omitted from report and find bodies: Apple's sortable-field enum differs per report level and rejects unknown fields, so sending a guessed field risks a hard 400. Offset pagination over a stable entity set is used instead; noted in a code comment.
- Report `startTime`/`endTime` use `YYYY-MM-DD` (v5), not the `MM-DD-YYYY` the research bundle claimed.

## How did you test this code?

Automated tests only, at both levels the source skill asks for.
`tests/test_apple_search_ads_source.py` covers the source class: the schemas it exposes, credential validation and error classification.
`tests/test_apple_search_ads.py` covers the transport: authentication, pagination or windowing termination, and row normalization.
All HTTP calls are mocked, so the suite makes no live vendor calls.
84 tests pass, 0 failing.

Repo wide mypy and the full `sources/` pytest suite were run across the whole batch this source was built in, not just this directory.

I have not exercised this against a live vendor account, so credential handling and endpoint behavior are verified against the vendor's published API documentation rather than a real sync. That is the main thing worth a careful review.

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

The posthog.com source doc is not written yet and is tracked separately, per the documenting-warehouse-sources guide.

author: yochze
body:
read_file picks its source by whether connection_id is set: empty means the
report's own file space (uploads / attach_file results). An agent that ran
list_files and then called read_file with only the returned id — a Graph
driveItem id like '01LZCX…' — hit the session lookup, missed, and failed with
"is not a file attached to this conversation". The id was fine; only the source
was unnamed. Worse, the error reads as "your id is wrong", so the model re-ran
list_files, got the same id back, and looped.

When the session lookup misses and the agent has exactly one attached file
connection, read from it. The fallback goes through resolve_file_client, so the
per-user data-source access check, the active-connection filter and the
capability check all apply exactly as they do for an explicitly named
connection — it picks the source, it does not grant reach to it. With two or
more connections nothing is guessed, and a uuid4 id (a conversation attachment
by construction) never probes a connector, so a stale or foreign attachment
still reports precisely instead of returning a provider 404.

The unresolved-id error now names the attached connections with their ids and
spells out the retry, so the next call sets connection_id instead of re-listing.

author: nishujangra
body:
## Summary

Adds regression coverage for the observability and request/response contracts consolidated on this branch. The bulk is tests; two commits change behavior and are called out below.

The recurring theme is **cross-plane parity** — the QUIC data path and the bootstrap TLS path must resolve equivalent requests to the same routing decision, emit the same request shape upstream, normalize responses identically, and record the same canonical outcome reason and metric labels. Those invariants were previously implicit.

**84 new tests** across 4 crates, 33 files, +4494/-114.

## Behavior changes

Two commits are not test-only:

- **`3d7c7a0` — `fix(config)`: iterate upstreams in name order.** `normalize_upstreams` iterated a `HashMap`, so which upstream got named in a `DuplicateRouteAmbiguity` error depended on hash order — the same config could produce different error text run to run. Now sorted by name. `duplicate_route_ambiguity_is_reported_deterministically` asserts both insertion orders yield an identical error and fails without this fix.
- **`ef94ceb` — `refactor(edge)`: extract local response builders.** Pulls inline header construction out of the H3 send paths into pure functions (`simple_response_headers`, `overload_response_headers`, `admission_rejection_headers`, `response_headers_with_defaults`, `bootstrap_response_constraints`). Behavior-preserving — verified the pre-existing suite passes on the extraction alone before any tests were added — and it makes the local-response wire shape assertable without a live listener.

## Coverage by area

| Area | What's now pinned |
|---|---|
| Admission | Overload reason -> metrics label -> response body mapping; each rejection path (brownout, adaptive, route cap, global cap, global/upstream inflight) resolves to a distinct reason |
| Routing | Method/host tie-breaks in overlapping routes; stable unrouted errors; CONNECT gated on `allow_connect` |
| Request build | Host policy (pass-through / rewrite / upstream), forwarded-header append without duplicate drift, auth mutations applied after configured headers, invalid headers rejected before dispatch |
| Response | Local wire shape (status, framing, challenge metadata); hop-header stripping; HEAD and 204 stay bodyless |
| External auth | Response-header allowlists enforced per outcome; state transitions for every decision variant; fail-open vs fail-closed; config-time precedence rejection |
| Retry / hedge | Denial precedence order, retryable vs terminal classes, budget accounting not consumed by denials, telemetry outcome distinctness |
| Outcomes | Status-class and backend labels aligned with latency buckets; canonical reason mapping for admission and backend failures |
| Metrics | Retry, hedge, and overload-shed label vocabularies asserted against rendered Prometheus output |
| Backend lifecycle | Failed DNS refresh preserves prior resolution and generation; removed pool members counted correctly; stale bundle views unaffected by reload |
| Cross-plane parity | Route resolution, API-key denial, and gRPC trailer/content-type handling produce identical results over QUIC and bootstrap |

## Known gap — not fixed here

**Bootstrap and QUIC disagree on upstream-timeout status.** Bootstrap returns **504** `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT` (`crates/edge/src/quic_listener/bootstrap/dispatch.rs:41`); QUIC returns **503** `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (`crates/edge/src/quic_listener/forwarding/response.rs:1249`). Bodies are identical (`upstream timeout\n`).

A parity test written for this branch caught it. It is **deliberately not included** — reconciling the two is an outward-facing behavior change that deserves its own review and a decision on which status is canonical. Flagging it explicitly so the parity coverage here isn't read as covering timeouts.

## Test ergonomics

Helpers are local to the owning module; no shared fixture DSL was introduced. Two follow-ups applied after review of the tests themselves:

- `6d6504e` — consolidated four near-duplicate `PendingForward` fixtures onto one `#[cfg(test)]` constructor colocated with the struct. Verified by adding a throwaway field and counting breakage: **5 sites -> 2**, and the 2 remaining are correct (the constructor itself, and the production constructor that must name every field). Zero test modules break on a field addition.
- `36251a5` — split two tests that bundled independent contracts (12 asserts each) into 5 per-contract cases. Verified by sabotage: breaking the Deny path now fails only the Deny test while Redirect and Challenge still pass; previously the first failed assert masked the rest. The outcome tests also each get their own `Metrics` registry, so one outcome's counters can't hide another's.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` — zero warnings
- `cargo test --workspace` — all targets pass, 0 failures

## Summary
No-go map (IV): **can a bosonic condensate yield fermions at all?** Bare SSV **fails** (firm negative, computed pointwise); the minimal repair is **derived** — a multi-component condensate.

## The mechanism (grounded in real sources)
**Finkelstein–Rubinstein / Skyrme / Witten:** a soliton is a fermion iff a `2π` rotation of it is a non-contractible loop (`π₁(Q_B)=Z₂`, double cover, FR sign `−1`). For target `SU(2)≅S³`: `π₃=Z` (solitons exist) and `π₄=Z₂` (fermionic option, WZ term).

## Computed admissibility split (`B = (1/2π²)∫det[n,∂ₓn,∂ᵧn,∂azn]`)
| test | value | target | |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1** bare SSV (`U(1)`) density | max `\|ρ\| = 0.0` **exactly** | pointwise zero | ✓ |
| **C1** SU(2) hedgehog, 1 turn | `\|B\| = 0.994` | 1 | ✓ |
| **C2** hedgehog, 2 turns | `\|B\| = 1.965` | 2 | ✓ |
| **C3** deformed profile | shift `0.002` | topological | ✓ |
| **C5** grid convergence | `0.907→0.977→0.994` | → integer | ✓ |

**T1 is the strong form of the negative:** the `U(1)` winding density vanishes **identically at every point** (great-circle image → parallel tangents) — structural, not a numerical cancellation. So `B=0` for *any* bare-SSV configuration → **no solitons to quantize, a fortiori none fermionic.** The paper-I `U(1)` vortex rings cannot be fermions by the FR mechanism as they stand.

## Verdict
- **Bare SSV FAILS** the statistics question (proof-carrying negative).
- **Derived constraint:** fermionic solitons demand a **multi-component (SU(2)-valued/spinor) condensate** — previously a free modelling choice, now a requirement. `π₄(S³)=Z₂` (cited) then supplies the FR fermionic option.

## Honesty (rule 1)
Admissibility, not existence — whether **log-GPE dynamics stabilizes** a Skyrme-like soliton (Derrick) is open, flagged not solved. `π₄=Z₂` cited, not computed (loop homotopy beyond these numerics). The **holographic route** (no-go III's bulk fermion) remains the container alternative.

author: ouvill
body:
## Summary

- derive registration and resend timestamps from PostgreSQL's transaction clock
- keep durable challenge/outbox state and encrypted replay responses on the same microsecond-precision instant
- pass that canonical instant through the delivery cooldown claim instead of sampling a separate process clock

## Root cause

Rust `Utc::now()` retained nanoseconds in API/replay responses, while PostgreSQL `TIMESTAMPTZ` persisted microseconds. The same logical deadline could therefore compare unequal, and main CI reproduced this twice in `email_request_resend_budget_and_delivery_retry_are_atomic`.

Using one database transaction instant also keeps lock/rate-limit decisions and stored timestamps consistent. A transaction delayed by lock contention can only shorten TTL relative to wall time, which remains fail-closed.

## Evidence

- exact head `98c88cc8d010e504d41f8aacecacc1f3a4088bcd`
- failing test reproduced on main runs [30214408331](https://github.com/ouvill/taskveil/actions/runs/30214408331) and [30215058160](https://github.com/ouvill/taskveil/actions/runs/30215058160)

author: umut-polat
body:
## Purpose

Fix a crash in the realtime speech-to-text WebSocket that silently kills the session when a client sends a binary frame.

`RealtimeConnection.handle_connection` reads every frame with `websocket.receive_text()`:

```python
while True:
    message = await self.websocket.receive_text()
    try:
        event = json.loads(message)
        await self.handle_event(event)
    ...
```

Starlette's `receive_text` does `return cast(str, message["text"])`. For a binary frame the ASGI message is `{"type": "websocket.receive", "bytes": b"..."}` — there is no `"text"` key, so it raises `KeyError`. That `KeyError` is raised **outside** the inner `try`, so it propagates to the connection-level `except Exception` (`connection.py:80`), which logs and runs `cleanup()` — the session is torn down and the socket closes with a bare `1000`, with **no error event ever sent to the client**.

Sending raw PCM as a binary frame instead of base64-in-JSON is the natural mistake on a realtime **audio** endpoint (every OpenAI-realtime-style client exposes `ws.send(bytes)`), so this is easy to trigger by accident.

### Fix

Receive frames via `websocket.receive()` and reject non-text frames with a clean `invalid_frame` error event, keeping the session open. Disconnects are still surfaced as `WebSocketDisconnect` so the existing handling is unchanged:

```python
async def _receive_text_frame(self) -> str | None:
    message = await self.websocket.receive()
    if message["type"] == "websocket.disconnect":
        raise WebSocketDisconnect(message.get("code", 1000))
    return message.get("text")
```

## Test Plan

New unit tests in `tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/realtime/test_realtime_connection_unit.py` drive `handle_connection` with a fake WebSocket that mirrors Starlette's frame semantics (so `receive_text` really raises `KeyError` on a binary frame):

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/realtime/test_realtime_connection_unit.py
```

- `test_binary_frame_reports_error_and_keeps_session_open` — a binary frame yields an `invalid_frame` error event instead of crashing.
- `test_text_frame_is_routed_to_handle_event` — normal text frames still dispatch.
- `test_disconnect_frame_ends_loop_cleanly` — disconnect ends the loop with no error event.

## Test Result

With the fix: `3 passed`. Against the current code the binary-frame test fails with the original `KeyError: 'text'` logged at `connection.py` (session dies, no `invalid_frame` emitted), confirming the test reproduces the bug. `pre-commit run` passes on both files (ruff, ruff-format, typos, mypy).

author: gilbert09
body:
## Problem

`applovin` was a scaffolded stub in the data warehouse source registry.
It appeared in the enum and the catalog but had no `get_schemas`, no client and no tests, so it could not actually be connected.

AppLovin is a major mobile user acquisition network, needed for blended mobile acquisition cost.

## Changes

Implements the `applovin` source end to end.

- Transport: hand-rolled (report-style API: the requested `columns` list defines both the row shape and the aggregate grain, plus a hard 45-day date-window walk with per-window limit/offset paging and a restatement lookback, none of which the declarative rest_source config can express; all HTTP rides `make_tracked_session(redact_values=(api_key,))`)
- Base class: `ResumableSource[AppLovinSourceConfig, AppLovinResumeConfig]`
- Credentials the customer supplies: single customer-supplied field: `api_key` (the AppLovin Report Key, password/secret). No OAuth, no Integration kind, no new env var. Sent as the `api_key` query param, so the session is created with `redact_values=(api_key,)` and every raised error message is redacted before it can reach `latest_error`
- Tables: max_ad_revenue (/maxReport, network grain); max_ad_unit_revenue (/maxReport, ad-unit grain, the only grain where AppLovin returns `requests`); publisher_report (/report?report_type=publisher); advertiser_report (/report?report_type=advertiser); max_cohort_ad_revenue (/maxCohort); max_cohort_impressions (/maxCohort/imp); max_cohort_sessions (/maxCohort/session)
- Incremental sync: yes. `day` (DateTime) on all 7 tables, filtered server-side via `start`/`end`. `merge_only` (append is not offered) because aggregate rows restate; incremental runs re-pull `REPORT_LOOKBACK_DAYS=7` before the watermark and clamp the start to today-44 so a stale watermark can't send an out-of-window date. `sort_mode="asc"`: windows walk oldest-first and every request pins `sort_day=ASC`

Shipped as `releaseStatus=ReleaseStatus.ALPHA`.
The diff is limited to this source's own directory, its generated config and its icon, plus a one line move in `SOURCES.md` from the scaffolded list to the implemented table.

### Notes for review

- `frontend/public/services/applovin.png` was ALREADY committed on master and is the correct AppLovin logo (512x512), so I fetched the Logo.dev PNG, compared both visually, and reverted to the committed one rather than committing pointless binary churn. No icon file is in the diff.
- `unreleasedSource=True` deleted, `releaseStatus=ReleaseStatus.ALPHA` set. No test asserts unreleasedSource is True (one asserts it is None). No `supported_versions`/`default_version`, r.applovin.com carries no version token anywhere, only `api_docs_url`.
- Endpoint paths, every column name, the `{code, count, results}` JSON envelope, limit/offset semantics ("returns an empty set once offset passes the total"), the 45-day request window, and the documented maxReport constraint that `requests` is unavailable whenever `network`/`network_placement` is requested while `attempts`/`responses`/`fill_rate` are only available when it is (encoded in...
- NOT VERIFIED (no live Report Key available): (1) whether every requested column COMBINATION is accepted: AppLovin checks auth before params, so a 403 masks any column error. If a combination is rejected in production it surfaces as a fast, clearly-messaged non-retryable "AppLovin rejected the report request" carrying the response body, which is the intended failure mode. (2) `sort_day=ASC` on...
- (a) the Axon Campaign Management API (campaign/creative-set dimension tables) needs a SECOND, different key type plus `account_id` and carries a 1000-req/60s limit with a 10-minute 429 lockout, mixing it in would mean optional credential fields and schemas that appear in the picker but can't sync, so it is out. (b) `/max/userAdRevenueReport` is out: it needs per-app...
- 45 days is a hard API limit, not a choice. History older than that is unobtainable, and the source caption says so.
- (1) the Report Key rides in a query param, so `requests`/`urllib3` transport errors (which quote the full URL) are caught and re-raised redacted with `from None` so the unredacted original can't leak through `__cause__`, two tests pin this. (2) 429/5xx raise a `TRANSIENT_ERROR_PREFIX` that is deliberately NOT in `get_non_retryable_errors()`; I initially bucketed them with 4xx and caught it in...

## How did you test this code?

Automated tests only, at both levels the source skill asks for.
`tests/test_applovin_source.py` covers the source class: the schemas it exposes, credential validation and error classification.
`tests/test_applovin.py` covers the transport: authentication, pagination or windowing termination, and row normalization.
All HTTP calls are mocked, so the suite makes no live vendor calls.
123 tests pass, 0 failing.

Repo wide mypy and the full `sources/` pytest suite were run across the whole batch this source was built in, not just this directory.

I have not exercised this against a live vendor account, so credential handling and endpoint behavior are verified against the vendor's published API documentation rather than a real sync. That is the main thing worth a careful review.

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

The posthog.com source doc is not written yet and is tracked separately, per the documenting-warehouse-sources guide.

author: rainboy105
body:
## Summary
Fixes the failed deploy at https://github.com/vabsgoyal/Gurukul_bk/actions/runs/30215695995/job/89829459599.

**Root cause theory** (can't confirm from here - no server/DB log access): `PrincipalPhoneBackfillSeeder` (#13) very likely already created a `Credential` row for `(school_id=demo school, username=9999999999)` on an earlier app restart. V17 (#14) then tried to `INSERT` the exact same combo unconditionally, hit the `credential` table's unique constraint, and failed. Flyway migration failures are fatal to Spring Boot startup by default - that's why the app never came up for its health check, producing the SSM deploy script's `exit status 7`.

**This also creates a second problem**: a failed migration gets recorded in `flyway_schema_history` and by default **blocks every future startup** until it's manually repaired - so without addressing that too, every subsequent deploy would keep failing at the same spot regardless of what else changes.

**Fix:**
1. `V17` rewritten as `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (...)`, guarding both the `employee` and `credential` inserts on whether a credential for that `(school_id, username)` already exists. All-or-nothing - won't create an orphan duplicate "Principal" employee if a credential already exists under a different employee row.
2. Added `spring.flyway.repair-on-migrate=true` - Flyway will auto-clear the stale failed `V17` entry and retry with the current (now-idempotent) content on the next deploy, with no manual DB intervention needed.

**What I can't rule out:** if the app is still down after this redeploys, that points to something needing direct DB/server access to diagnose further (confirming `repair-on-migrate` actually fired, or inspecting `flyway_schema_history` directly) - I have no credentials or log access to check that myself.

## Test plan
- [x] `./mvnw -q -DskipTests compile`
- [x] `./mvnw test` — full suite passes on a fresh H2 database (guard condition is true there, so behavior is unchanged for tests); the existing `DemoPrincipalSeedIntegrationTest` (password login) and `PrincipalPhoneOtpIntegrationTest` (OTP login) both still pass against the same seeded row

author: alies-dev
body:
## Issue to Solve

`docs/contributing/taint-analysis.md` listed six taint annotations and documented none of the conditional `@psalm-taint-escape` form, `@psalm-assert-untainted`, or `@psalm-taint-specialize` on a class docblock. It also gave no signal about which analyzers actually consume each tag, so a stub could carry an annotation that parses, stores, and silently never fires.

## Solution Description

Documented the full tag surface from Psalm source, verified against both majors this repo targets (7.0.0-beta19 on `master`, 6.16.1 behind `3.x`), with fixtures executed against built binaries rather than source reading alone.

- Added the conditional escape form: leading-`(` selection, the `TConditional` requirement, the per-parameter template rewrite, literal-string kind resolution, and why `@psalm-flow` stays mandatory.
- Documented the limitation that matters most: only `FunctionCallReturnTypeFetcher` and `StaticCallAnalyzer` consume `conditionally_removed_taints`. On an instance method or `new`, a conditional escape parses and never applies. Since nearly every stub in this repo is an instance method, that closes off the form here and points at a `RemoveTaintsInterface` handler instead.
- Added `@psalm-assert-untainted` (severs every taint kind, not one) and class-level `@psalm-taint-specialize`.
- Added a scope column, because a tag on the wrong scope is ignored rather than reported.
- Recorded the fail direction with an executed three-case `filter_var()` fixture: an argument that cannot be resolved to a literal reports rather than silently passing.

Cross-major handling: the doc calls out behavioral differences only, at the point of use, and stays silent where the majors agree. Two differences are documented. Psalm 6 has no `getOrRegisterTaint()` and resolves conditional-escape literals directly, and Psalm 6 reports type or taint issues per invocation but never both, which is the one that bites when testing.

## Checklist
- [x] Documentation is updated

author: pmcfadin
body:
Docs-only. Records a real dup-work near-miss from this session so the pickup rule closes the gap.

**What happened.** A lead working #2043 read #1883 at session start — genuinely OPEN, board `Status=In Progress`, Seam 1 approved, spec-only branch on origin. Hours later, on finishing #2043, it claimed #1883 and built a worktree. But a **different session had already delivered #1883** in the meantime: PR #2904 merged 17:35:47Z, issue CLOSED COMPLETED, OpenSpec change archived at `openspec/changes/archive/2026-07-26-rust-per-row-alloc-budget`, telemetry stamped via #2929.

**Why the claim protocol didn't catch it.** Every signal it checks was clean, and all of them read as *"abandoned claim, go adopt it"*:
- no `refs/claims/issue-1883` — the finishing session correctly released it on completion;
- no `issue-1883-*` branch — correctly deleted on merge;
- board `Status=In Progress` — stale, left behind by the finishing session.

The near-miss surfaced only incidentally: `git rebase origin/main` replayed the stale spec commit and printed its new parent, `chore(#1883): archive rust-per-row-alloc-budget …`.

**The lesson.** Absence of a claim ref + absence of a branch is **ambiguous** — it means EITHER "abandoned, adopt it" OR "finished, stay away." The disambiguator is the issue's own state, and nothing in the current pickup rule re-reads it at claim time. So: run `gh issue view <N> --json state,stateReason` **immediately before** `claim.sh claim`, and treat `CLOSED` as a hard stop regardless of board Status — the board mirror lags, and a completed issue's board item is routinely left stale by the session that finished it. Branch-absence is itself weak evidence of completion (a finished 1:1:1:1 cycle deletes its branch), so **branch-absent + issue-CLOSED is the already-shipped signature**.

Cost this time: one wasted claim/worktree cycle and a duplicate spec commit, discarded before any implementation. Cost if unnoticed: a second PR re-implementing merged work.

No code changes; appends lesson 25 to `process_improvements.md`.

author: italofelipe
body:
## Contexto

Existiam só checkout novo (`POST /subscriptions/checkout`) e cancel — **não havia troca de plano**. Trocar mensal↔anual disparava um **novo checkout**, que no AbacatePay cria uma **segunda assinatura paralela** → risco de **cobrança dupla**.

## O que muda

Novo `change_subscription_plan` (serviço) + endpoint **REST** `POST /subscriptions/change-plan` e **mutation GraphQL** `changeSubscriptionPlan` (paridade; deprecated→REST no mesmo padrão dos demais, ADR-0004).

### Invariante de segurança (nunca cobra duas vezes)
A ordem é a garantia: **cancela a assinatura atual no gateway ANTES de criar o novo checkout**. Se o cancel falhar → o novo checkout **nunca** é criado (aborta) → sem cobrança dupla. Nunca há duas assinaturas ativas faturando.

### Continuidade de entitlements (sem flicker)
`status`, `plan_code` e `current_period_end` locais ficam **intocados** — o usuário mantém premium no período que já pagou; o **novo plano entra pelo webhook `subscription.completed`**. O registro local aponta para o novo placeholder `bill_`, então o **job de reconciliação (#1600) o ignora** até a promoção. Se o usuário abandonar o novo checkout, os entitlements simplesmente **expiram no fim do período** (via `expires_at`) — sem premium grátis indefinido.

### Decisão de proration (registrada)
**Sem crédito de proration.** O AbacatePay não expõe proration nem troca agendada (só create-checkout + cancel), então o modelo correto é cancelar o atual e emitir um checkout novo para o plano novo; o novo plano fatura na conclusão. Documentado no docstring do serviço.

### Auditoria
`record_entity_change(action="plan_change", extra="to=<offer>")` — novo helper de auditoria (irmão do `record_entity_delete`) para não mislabelar a troca como delete.

## Validação

- `run_ci_quality_local.sh --local` — **verde** (coverage ~91%, ruff+mypy+bandit+pip-audit + hooks de arquitetura GraphQL).
- 7 testes: ordem cancel→checkout (nunca 2 ativas); placeholder `bill_` pula o cancel; **falha no cancel aborta sem criar checkout**; continuidade (status/plano intocados); auditoria registrada; REST happy-path (201) + já-no-plano (409) + plano inválido (400).
- `test_graphql_auth_everywhere` verde → a nova mutation exige auth.

## Risco residual
Médio-baixo. Mexe em cobrança real, mas a ordem cancel-antes-de-checkout elimina o double-charge e a continuidade via `expires_at` evita leak. **Edge documentado como follow-up**: se o usuário trocar e abandonar o novo checkout, fica um `bill_` placeholder no registro (premium expira no período; sem cobrança) — o reconcile poderia futuramente expirar placeholders `bill_` velhos. Nomes de evento/estado do gateway seguem pendentes de confirmação (platform#891).

Closes #1597

## What

Raises the three aggregate literals in `src/test/test-idor.ts` from `6 / 6 / 12` to `9 / 9 / 18`, replaces a stale file header, and records two CORRECTION blocks in `docs/REMEDIATION-PROGRESS.md`.

## Why

`test-idor.ts` has carried `positivesMinPassing: 6` / `negativesMinPassing: 6` / `combinedMinPassing: 12` since `07fe2d3` (#52, 2026-05-15), calibrated when `fixtures/idor` held 8 positives and 8 negatives. `ff3c364` (2026-05-28) added a ninth positive and a ninth negative without touching the constants, decaying both bars to 6 of 9, a 67 percent bar. The gate could pass with three positives missed AND three negatives leaking.

This is the same decay defect PR #116 fixed for four sibling tests. idor was skipped there because it was ALREADY routed through `runStabilityHarness` and so fell outside that step's scope, not because it was clean.

## The two CORRECTIONs

Both name `f62921e` (#116, 2026-07-22) as the entry point of the error, and both were false when written rather than overtaken by later events. Neither rewrites a historical fact; both are appended, and both sit in NOT-DONE / DEFERRED, never in DONE.

1. The six-item stage-3 inventory claimed all six harness-routed entry points were "corpus-relative and all-passing". Five were. `test:idor` was not, and never had been.
2. The "Decayed absolute thresholds" ledger item named `test-secrets-exposure.ts` as the SOLE remaining instance of the defect. idor was a second instance, at a looser bar than the env-exposure 64 percent that item does list. `test-secrets-exposure.ts` remains open at 7/9/16 and is unchanged by this PR.

## THE NEW BAR IS UNVERIFIED AT ITS NEW HEIGHT

Raising these aggregates is a POLICY change, not a measurement. **No live n=5 run of `fixtures/idor` has ever been taken at 9/9/18.** Stage 3 has never executed, so this is true of ALL SIX harness bars at their current heights, not only idor's. The frozen replay recordings are n=1 and establish no stability. This is stated in the file header and in the CORRECTION, deliberately, so the bar is not mistaken for a verified result.

## Zero spend

No live entry point was run to produce this PR. Verified with `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint:no-console` only, both exit 0. The pre-commit secret scan ran and reported clean over both files.

**Strictly tightening.** The change can only make a gate harder to pass, never manufacture a false green.

The only consumer of these literals is `.github/workflows/stage3-live-detection.yml`, which is `workflow_dispatch` only. This PR tightens that gate and nothing else.

author: dallenpyrah
body:
## Root cause of the "stranded child run"

There is no Relay stranding defect and there never was a forever-stuck child. The `recovered-delayed` fixture serves two instant model turns and four five-minute turns strictly by request arrival order, while the phase-2 settle poll pinned alpha and beta as the two children that must complete and gamma as the one still pending. Whichever child loses the scheduling race for the second instant turn parks on a five-minute scripted model turn — `(execution running, child run queued)` is the normal steady state of an in-flight child — and the ~100 s poll can never settle, failing with exactly the reported `recovery state did not settle` snapshot.

Evidence, gathered on a 2-vCPU Linux VM (colima, `oven/bun:1.3.14`, matching the Blacksmith runner shape):

- The identical failure signature reproduces with Relay **0.7.21** (2 of 8 full-suite runs): alpha and gamma completed, beta `running`/`queued` — same second-child shape CI showed on 0.7.22/0.7.23. The race predates the suspected versions.
- A diagnostic run that re-queried 340 s after the poll gave up found beta **cancelled** in both tables: the 5-minute `recoveryChildSettlementGrace` cancelled the root and Relay cascaded to the parked child. Self-healing, not stranded.
- Gamma completed within the poll window, which is only possible by consuming one of the two instant positional turns — a delayed turn takes 300 s.
- Phase 2 appends no new child events (idempotent replay), confirming the recovered children race to the scripted model directly.
- Eliminated by direct code analysis of 0.7.21..0.7.23: the reconciliation memo (success-only key set — no joining, no stored values, cannot hang or go stale), the archive-observability and MySQL-migration commits (no SQLite runtime lines), and the producer settle window (archive publication timing only, bounded at 30 s, never on the child dispatch or notify path).

Append-latency differences between 0.7.21 and 0.7.22/0.7.23 only re-weighted which child loses the race on given hardware — that is why CI read it as a version regression and why the earlier macOS variant builds (snapshot-before-append etc.) appeared to "fix" it.

## The fix

The poll now accepts any two completed children plus one still-pending child agreed by both projections, and the final assertions derive the cancelled child from the observed race loser. Every behavior the test proves is unchanged: recovery without re-running the root turn, idempotent replay, two preserved delegated outcomes, settlement-grace cancellation of the root, and the cascade to the late child.

## Adoption

Second commit takes Relay 0.7.23: 76% smaller durable events (5,529 → 1,319 bytes) with flat append cost — the storage win this failure was blocking.

Validation so far: fixed test green on 0.7.23 in the reproducing VM (runs continuing), full `bun run typecheck`, diagnostics lane, and `bun run test` green on 0.7.23. This PR's proc lane is the authoritative gate.

Relay-side coverage and the corrected tradeoff doc: In-Time-Tec/relayfx#361.

author: lindkvis
body:
Fixes the four blockers raised by the independent security and engineering reviews of `develop` for v1.8.0rc1. Both reviews returned **GO-WITH-CONDITIONS**; reports are in `docs/reviews/` (gitignored, local only).

## Commits

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `6c714ee7` | Shard the release-prep sweep (6 contiguous blocks, ~45 -> ~15 min) and move the seven behavioural authz suites onto the blocking gate |
| `dfe73269` | Stop authz tests passing vacuously via the SPA fallback |
| `9892ad14` | Server-side confirm token on delete-forever; purge safe against concurrent restore |
| `fb4ac88a` | Pin a loose `!= 403` assertion to the status it means |
| `facdb253` | Record the invalidation suite as load-sensitive rather than as a false failure count |
| `f7efdfbb` | Drive scrapheap file removal from what the DELETE actually deleted (F1) |

## The four blockers

1. **Vacuous authz test.** `pixlstash/server.py:1244` is an SPA catch-all returning 200 for any unmatched GET, so `assert status == 200` against a nonexistent route proved nothing. The test claimed to cover `/stacks/{id}/pictures`, one of three historical whole-library BOLA leaks, and never requested it. Now exercises all three `_LIST_AWARE` stack routes, both directions, proven load-bearing by mutation.
2. **Authz suites did not block CI.** Gate goes 42 -> 49 files, 533 -> 684 tests; measured cost ~3.3 min spread over 8 shards, so PR turnaround stays ~13.5 min. A `MUST_BLOCK_ON_EVERY_PR` guard prevents silent re-deferral.
3. **No server-side confirmation on delete-forever.** A bodyless DELETE destroyed the entire scrapheap. Now requires a single-use, TTL-bounded, selection-bound confirm token minted by the preview endpoint. Intent control, not an authz control - `ROUTE_POLICIES` unchanged, both routes stay `OWNER_ONLY`.
4. **Purge could destroy a picture restored mid-purge.** Selection, locks and deletion now run in one DB submission (closing a lock lookup that ran outside the write queue), and the removed set is derived from the DELETE itself, so a spared row keeps its file and gets no ledger row.

## Sign-off status

CSO cleared `6c714ee7` and `fb4ac88a`; `dfe73269` and `9892ad14` are CLEARED-WITH-CHANGES with the remaining items targeted at 1.8.0 final. **F1 (`f7efdfbb`) is pending independent sign-off** - it introduces a fail-closed rollback path that has not yet been adversarially reviewed.

## Deferred to 1.8.0 final

F3 (`include_protected` outside the confirm fingerprint), F4 (`total_count` not enforced), three frontend `.data`/`skipped_restored` one-liners including a privacy notice that never fires, an Origin check for the residual CSRF vector, a 404 for unmatched `/api/` paths, and batching the uncapped manual purge.

Does not address the Principal's release-bookkeeping blockers (setuptools pin, changelog, version bump), which gate the tag rather than this branch.

author: kachkaev
body:
Moves everything under `pages/` to `app/`. Mostly renames, so `git log --follow` still works; net −30 lines.

## What changed

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `pages/_app.page.tsx` + `pages/_document.page.tsx` | `app/layout.tsx` |
| `pages/index.page.tsx` | `app/page.tsx` (`"use client"`) |
| `pages/404.page.tsx` | `app/not-found.tsx` |
| `pages/_error.page.tsx` | `app/error.tsx` |
| `pages/api/jump.handler.ts` | `app/jump/route.ts` |
| `pages/shared/page-metadata.tsx` | deleted → metadata API |

Colocation folders keep the existing convention, so `index.page.tsx` + `index.page/` became `page.tsx` + `page/`, and `_app.page/` became `layout/`.

Two `next.config.ts` entries are now obsolete:

- `pageExtensions: ["page.tsx", "handler.ts"]` — only existed to allow colocation inside `pages/`, which the app router does natively. It also *had* to go: `pageExtensions` applies to `app/` too, so `page.tsx` would otherwise have needed to be `page.page.tsx`.
- the `/jump` → `/api/jump` rewrite — `/jump` is a real route now.

## Worth a look during review

- **`/api/jump` no longer resolves.** Every documented interface (CLI, `opensearch.xml`, Chrome, Alfred) posts to `/jump`, which is unchanged, and `/api/jump` was only ever the rewrite target rather than a documented endpoint. Happy to add a compatibility rewrite if you'd rather not break it for anyone who hardcoded it.
- **`app/error.tsx` no longer sets a document title.** Error boundaries must be client components, which rules out both `metadata` and a plain `<title>` — the latter *adds* to the layout's title instead of replacing it, which I confirmed renders two `<title>` tags. The on-page “500 / unknown error” is unchanged; only the tab title falls back to the site default. `not-found.tsx` was not affected: Next 16 does honour a `metadata` export there, despite the docs listing only `layout` and `page`.
- **Two tags stayed hand-written in the layout** because the metadata API cannot express them: the opensearch `<link>` (`icons.other` drops `title`, which browsers show as the search engine name) and `vk:image` (`other` emits `name=` rather than `property=`, and skips `metadataBase` resolution — the URL came out relative).
- **`app/layout/js-class-switcher.tsx` carries an eslint-disable.** `unicorn/no-null` and `unicorn/no-useless-undefined` contradict each other for a render-nothing component, and a bare `return;` fails `tsc`. The `no-js` → `js` swap still happens in an effect after hydration, exactly as `_app.page.tsx` did.

Incidental app-router wins: the 404 now gets `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` automatically, and `og:image` / `twitter:image` are made absolute by `metadataBase` rather than by hand.

## Verification

`pnpm lint` (eslint, markdownlint, dedupe, prettier, tsc) and `pnpm build` pass. Beyond that, against a production build and a dev server:

- `/jump` redirects are byte-identical to before across `prettier`, `prettier s`, `prettier r`, `react h`, `lodash y`, an unknown package, an empty `to=`, and no query string at all. The fallback still sends a relative `/` in `Location`, hence a plain `Response` rather than `NextResponse.redirect()`, which only accepts absolute URLs.
- Rendered `<head>` on `/` checked tag by tag against the old `_document` output.
- Hydration verified in a browser: `<body>` flips to `js`, the hidden `from` field becomes `bookmark`, clickable code gets `cursor: pointer`, and clicking a destination keyword fills the input, focuses it, and highlights the matching row.
- `/nope` returns 404 with the right title and renders inside the shared layout.
- Dev server log is free of errors and hydration warnings.

author: jzabroski
body:
Follow-up to #2326.

## Problem

Central Package Management made NuGet start warning **NU1507** on every restore:

> There are 2 package sources defined in your configuration. When using central package management, please map your package sources with package source mapping … The following sources are defined: NuGet Feed, fluentmigrator

The warning is well-founded rather than noise. Without a mapping, NuGet searches *every* configured feed for *every* package. That is the shape dependency-confusion attacks exploit: anyone able to publish to the Azure Artifacts feed could shadow a package we expect to come from nuget.org, and restore would happily take it.

## Fix

I checked what the Azure Artifacts feed actually serves. Its search endpoint returns only our own CI-built packages — `FluentMigrator`, `FluentMigrator.Abstractions`, `FluentMigrator.Runner.*`, `FluentMigrator.Extensions.*`, `FluentMigrator.MSBuild`, `FluentMigrator.Tools`, and so on. Nothing third-party. So the mapping writes down exactly that:

```xml
<packageSourceMapping>
    <packageSource key="NuGet Feed">
        <package pattern="*" />
        <package pattern="FluentMigrator*" />
    </packageSource>
    <packageSource key="fluentmigrator">
        <package pattern="FluentMigrator*" />
    </packageSource>
</packageSourceMapping>
```

Two things follow from this:

- **`FluentMigrator*` still resolves from both feeds.** NuGet picks the longest matching pattern, and both sources declare `FluentMigrator*`, so both stay eligible. This preserves today's behaviour for the samples that consume released FluentMigrator packages (`FluentMigrator.MSBuild 7.1.0`) and for anyone restoring a CI prerelease.
- **Everything else is locked to nuget.org.** `Npgsql`, `Testcontainers.*`, `Oracle.*` and friends match only the `*` pattern, which only "NuGet Feed" declares. The private feed can no longer serve them. That is the actual security win, and it costs nothing because the private feed never had them.

I deliberately did *not* use the stricter form (`FluentMigrator*` on the Azure feed only). It reads cleaner, but it makes restore depend on every FluentMigrator package version we consume being present on the private feed — a footgun for a sample that pins a public release.

The `nuget.config` comment explains the reasoning and notes the one maintenance obligation this creates: a package from a genuinely new source needs a pattern here, or restore will not find it.

## Verification

- `dotnet restore FluentMigrator.sln --force` — **NU1507 is gone**, exit 0.
- `dotnet restore FluentMigrator.sln --packages <empty-dir> --no-cache` — restores from an empty package folder with the HTTP cache bypassed, so every package is resolved through the mapping against the live feeds rather than served from `~/.nuget/packages`. Exit 0, no NU1101/NU1102 (package-not-found), and `FluentMigrator.MSBuild 7.1.0` downloads as expected.

The only warnings left on restore are the pre-existing `log4net 2.0.12` (moderate, via `Snowflake.Data`) and `SQLitePCLRaw.lib.e_sqlite3 2.1.11` (high) advisories, unchanged from `main`.

author: emrahbaysal
body:
## What UAT row 165 asks for

> On a failed `cutover-step-*` row, a Re-run button is present (per-row, gated to Failed) — the sovereign-admin can re-drive a failed cutover step from the browser.

## Which surface renders `cutover-step-*` rows, and how that was proven

`products/catalyst/bootstrap/ui` — the React/TSX operator console. A walker reaches it at **`https://console.<sovereign-fqdn>/jobs`** (`consoleJobsRoute`, `src/app/router.tsx:1380-1383` → `JobsPage` → `JobsTable`); the mothership-scoped twin is `/provision/$deploymentId/jobs` (`router.tsx:878-881`).

Evidence chain:

- `internal/handler/cutover_activity_bridge.go` projects the 11-step cutover execution through `jobs.ActivityBridge`, which mints one leaf per step with `Kind: jobs.KindStep` and `JobName = ActivityStepJobName("cutover", slug)` → `cutover-step-<slug>` (`internal/jobs/activity_bridge.go:276`, `:96`).
- `JobsPage.tsx` reads exactly one backend list — `GET /api/v1/deployments/{depId}/jobs` via `useLiveJobsBackfill` — and threads `deploymentId` into `<JobsTable>`; its own header comment names cutover steps as rows it lists.
- `JobsTable.tsx:810-822` renders the Actions cell whenever `deploymentId` is present, and the control inside it whenever `isJobRetryable(job.status)`.

Note for anyone repeating the search: this is *not* `core/console` (that is the per-Organization portal — `getMyOrgs`, "No jobs yet for this organization") nor `products/catalyst/console`. A grep restricted to those two trees finds nothing and reads as "no UI exists".

## The actual gap — not a missing button, a button that always failed

The control already rendered on a failed cutover-step row and was already gated to Failed. What was missing was the backend leg: `dispatchRetry` had no `case jobs.KindStep`, so every click fell through to `default:` and returned

```
422 {"error":"not-directly-retryable","detail":"kind \"step\" does not support retry: …"}
```

Reproduced before the fix by `TestRetryJob_CutoverStep_Failed_RedrivesEngine`. So the row-165 assertion was false in the way that matters: the sovereign-admin could see the control and could not re-drive the step. The label was wrong too — `step` fell to the default `"Retry reconcile"`, which describes an annotation bump, not what a cutover step re-run does.

## Which backend path the button calls, and why that one

`POST /api/v1/deployments/{depId}/jobs/{jobId}/retry` — the existing generic remediation endpoint (`cmd/api/main.go:1475`), extended with a `KindStep` case rather than given a new sibling endpoint. That case calls `runCutover(ctx, deps, steps, operatorRetry=true)` — the same engine entry `HandleCutoverStart` spawns at `cutover.go:2306`.

Why not have the UI call `POST /api/v1/sovereign/cutover/start` directly:

- The retry route already carries the four properties this action needs — session gate (registered inside the `RequireSession` group), operator-tier RBAC (`jobRetryCallerAuthorized`, 403 otherwise), the ownership gate (404 on cross-tenant), and an Execution recorded on the row with the operator identity in its first LogLine. `/cutover/start` has the session gate but none of the per-row audit or ownership plumbing.
- It keeps one remediation write surface for the jobs canvas, which is what `jobs_retry.go` was built to be.

Why re-driving the whole engine is the correct per-row semantic: the chain is sequential and halts at its first failure, so at most one step is `failed` at any time. `runCutover` skips steps whose durable per-step status is already `success`, so it resumes exactly at the failed step, deletes its stale Job, re-runs it, and continues. "Re-run this row" and "resume the chain" are the same operation here.

No new endpoint. No chart change. `jobFailedTransiently`'s fail-closed design is untouched — the auto-resume and in-cluster trigger still pass `operatorRetry=false`, so an unattended genuine failure still never auto-loops; only the deliberate human CTA re-runs it.

## Changes

**Backend** — `products/catalyst/bootstrap/api`

- `internal/handler/jobs_retry_cutover_step.go` (new): `retryActivityStep` / `retryCutoverStep`. Resolves the step slug from the leaf's JobName, verifies it against the installed step ConfigMaps, claims the engine's single-run flag, spawns `runCutover(..., true)` on a background context so a closed browser cannot cancel a multi-step cutover.
- `internal/handler/jobs_retry.go`: the `KindStep` dispatch case, plus `errCutoverRunInFlight` → **409** so a Re-run fired during an in-flight run cannot race a second engine goroutine.

Failure mapping is honest rather than uniform: unknown/foreign step slug, cutover chart absent, or a step leaf from a future non-cutover activity group → **422** with an actionable detail; engine busy → **409**; non-failed row → **409** (the pre-existing `jobRetryableStatus` gate, which independently enforces "gated to Failed" server-side).

**Frontend** — `products/catalyst/bootstrap/ui`

- `retryJobFeedback.ts` (new): `retryLabel` gains `case 'step' → "Re-run"`; `errorMessageFor` surfaces the server's own `detail` for any non-2xx, falling back to `Not permitted` (403) / `Not retryable` (409, detail-less) / `Failed (<status>)`. Extracted to its own module so both ladders are unit-testable and the component file exports only a component.
- `RetryJobButton.tsx`: uses those, adds `aria-busy` on the in-flight state and a step-specific tooltip. The success state now reads "Request accepted — the live state refreshes on the next poll" rather than implying the step itself succeeded.

The Failed-only gate is unchanged (`isJobRetryable`) — this PR locks it down with tests rather than touching it.

## Honest feedback, no optimistic green

Pending state while the POST is in flight ("Requesting…", button disabled + `aria-busy`, no success element rendered). Success claims only "Requested" on a real 2xx — the request was accepted; the live `/jobs` backfill reports the actual outcome on its next poll. Every non-2xx renders the server's reason verbatim in the error slot. A rejected re-run can never render as green.

## Tests, including the negative direction

Backend — `jobs_retry_cutover_step_test.go` (5 cases): failed step re-drives the engine (stale failed Job deleted, fresh Job created, both steps end `success`, Execution recorded); succeeded/running/pending each → 409; viewer → 403; engine busy → 409; unknown slug → 422 naming the slug.

Frontend — `JobsTable.cutoverRerun.test.tsx`: control present and labelled "Re-run" on a failed `cutover-step-*` row; absent for succeeded/running/pending (with the Actions cell still rendering its empty marker, so absence is the gate firing and not the column vanishing); in a two-row chain only the failed row offers it. `RetryJobButton.test.tsx` adds the step label, the pending state, and 422/409/detail-less-409/status-fallback rendering.

Each half was reverted and the matching tests confirmed failing:

| Reverted | Result |
|---|---|
| `case jobs.KindStep` in `dispatchRetry` | 3 backend tests fail — `got 422 … kind "step" does not support retry` |
| `case 'step'` in `retryLabel` | `expected "Re-run", received "Retry reconcile"` |
| `isJobRetryable(job.status)` gate → always render | 4 of 5 row-165 render tests fail |

## Gates

Backend: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./...` all green; `gofmt` clean on every touched file.

Frontend: `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) green; `tsc -b --noEmit` green; `eslint` clean on all four touched files (it also clears two pre-existing unused-arg errors in `RetryJobButton.test.tsx`).

Full `vitest run`: 9 files / 68 tests fail — **identical on `origin/main` with this change stashed** (same 9 files, same 68 count), so they are pre-existing and unrelated. The four files in this PR's blast radius (`RetryJobButton`, `JobsTable.cutoverRerun`, `JobsTable`, `jobs.types`) are 76/76 green.

No chart touched, so no `Chart.yaml` bump or lockstep script applies. No cluster was touched — repo-only.

author: flamarion
body:
End-session doc refresh. Three drifts, two introduced by today's convention changes and one long-standing.

**CONTRIBUTING.md was actively contradicting reality.** It said branch naming is `feat/<name>` / `fix/<name>` / `chore/<name>`, which no longer links anything to Jira, and that the PR title is what semantic-release reads "if you squash-merge" — the conditional is obsolete now that squash is the only merge method available. Corrected to lead with `TBD-<number>-<slug>`, to require the key in commit messages (which is what makes CI runs appear as Jira builds), and to state squash-only plainly. Also notes the squash body is now the PR description, so descriptions land in permanent history.

**CLAUDE.md had no record of either convention.** Added two Key Conventions bullets: squash-only merging and why that makes the PR title the release gate; and the Jira linkage rules, covering the three places the key belongs, smart commits going in the commit body rather than the subject, the `#word`-terminates-`#comment` gotcha, and the repo-local `user.email` requirement that smart commits fail silently without.

**CONTRIBUTING.md Quickstart still cloned the old repo path** (`flamarion/pfv`, then `cd pfv`), so step 1 of the 30-minute Quickstart failed outright. PR #582 fixed this in README.md but missed CONTRIBUTING.md.

Checked and deliberately left unchanged:

- CLAUDE.md's reference to the K8s init container is accurate. `k8s/` still holds a Helm chart with one.
- README.md needed nothing. It points at CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md rather than restating conventions.
- **DEPLOYMENT.md's remaining `flamarion/pfv` references are out of scope on purpose**, filed as TBD-231. Two of them are not links: they document the live AWS OIDC trust-policy `sub` claim, pinned with `StringEquals` on the `github-actions-apex-deploy` role. If the deployed IAM policy still carries the old path then the doc is correct as written, and editing it would make the doc lie about security infrastructure. That needs the policy verified first, which is Terraform territory.

author: nedseb
body:
Première étape du lot 2 (#2358) : la maquette du compte rendu, refaite de zéro. Doc-only, aucun code.

## Pourquoi refaire et non amender

La maquette précédente **violait deux des trois règles qu'elle proclamait**, mesures prises sur son propre SVG :

| Ce qu'elle affirmait | Ce qu'elle dessinait |
|---|---|
| « les proportions sont à l'échelle » | barre « Carte SD » : 640 px pour 5,0 Go (**128 px/Go**) ; barre « Écrit » : 470 px pour 5,0 Go (**94 px/Go**) - deux échelles dans le bloc qui invite à comparer |
| « la somme des segments fait le total » | barre empilée : le segment majoritaire (583/612) occupait **toute** la largeur, les deux autres peints **par-dessus** |

Pour ce composant-là, c'est le défaut le plus grave possible : une vue fausse avec l'autorité du visuel.

Sa **forme** est écartée aussi : 620 px et quatre sections titrées reposent l'exigence des puces qu'elles remplacent - lire pour savoir si l'on peut continuer.

## Ce que la nouvelle maquette propose

Une bande dense d'environ **250 px** : verdict chiffré, barre du devenir, coût disque en deux barres **à échelle commune**, ce qui reste vrai, action suivante. Les noms des fichiers rejetés sont derrière un accès - la ligne de pied les résume déjà par motif (« 8 rejetés : 6 déjà expansés, 2 en-tête illisible »), et c'est le seul détail dont la réponse aux trois questions ne dépend pas.

La variante en deux colonnes est documentée comme **écartée**, avec sa raison : plus large, plus haute (donc une modale), et sa colonne de droite est vide dans le cas courant.

Deux variantes ajoutées, qui manquaient :

- **« rien à signaler »** - le cas courant : sans rejet ni avertissement, les blocs disparaissent au lieu d'afficher des cadres vides (180 px) ;
- **« en échec »** - même structure, proportions inversées, reprise proposée plutôt qu'un acquittement.

## La preuve d'échelle est publiée dans la maquette

Chaque largeur est calculée, et sa vérification figure dans le document :

```
Devenir (612 sur 840 px) : 583 → 800,2 · 21 → 28,8 · 8 → 11,0   somme 840,0 / 840
Lu (5,0 Go)              : 441,2 px                              88,2 px/Go
Écrit (6,8 Go)           : bruts 441,2 · séquences 158,8         88,2 px/Go, même échelle
Légende                  : 95,3 % + 3,4 % + 1,3 %                100,0 %
```

Les pourcentages sont arrondis **au dixième** : à l'unité, cet import se lirait « 95 + 3 + 1 = 99 % », et un compte rendu qui ne fait pas 100 % laisse chercher le point manquant.

## Deux constats notés pour la suite

- **Un modèle distinct de `CompteRendu`** : celui-ci (ADR 0031) porte des **phrases** et sert déjà quatre écrans et la CLI. Le compte rendu chiffré porte des **quantités** : les deux coexistent, le lot 2 ne refait pas l'existant.
- **Les octets écrits n'existent pas** dans le modèle (`RapportImport` = comptes par statut, `ResultatImport` = nombres d'originaux et de séquences). Les barres de volume supposent d'ajouter cette mesure au moteur d'import : c'est la seule donnée que ce lot ajoutera, et elle viendra avec le branchement.

## Vérifications

`mkdocs build --strict -f mkdocs-brief.yml` vert · `DocumentationAJourTest` 19 gardes vertes (indexation des maquettes, liens, réciprocité) · arithmétique des échelles vérifiée par script.

Avance #2358. Suivent : le modèle et ses invariants, le composant et ses captures, puis les branchements.

author: marmeladema
body:
Fixes a way to silently lose a first message, and the long-standing `thread-selection` suite flake.

## The bug

The project `+` action calls `newThread`, which awaited a network round-trip before switching to the draft:

```js
async function newThread(pid) {
  const project = await api("GET", `/api/projects/${pid}`);   // round-trip
  openDraftThread(pid, project && project.default_model);      // resets the composer
}
```

For the length of that fetch the previously selected thread is still on screen, composer visible and editable. Text typed in that window goes into a composer that is about to be reset: `openDraftThread` runs, calls `restoreComposerDraft()`, and the text is gone.

The send that follows hits `sendInput`'s early return, which issues no notice:

```js
if ((!text && attachments.length === 0) || ...) return;
```

No request, no error, no message. It gets more likely the slower the server.

Observed with temporary instrumentation:

```
PROBE restoreComposerDraft was="probe iteration 4"   // clears what was typed
PROBE sendInput text="" threadId=null draft=true      // returns without sending
```

## The change

Drawing a draft does not need the project record; only the model default does, and `normalizeDraftModel` already falls back when none is given. The draft opens synchronously and the default is applied when it arrives.

That leaves the draft interactive before its model is known, which needs three rules (spec **LT7**):

1. **Same draft only** — the default applies only to the draft it was requested for, not one the user has since sent, switched away from, or replaced.
2. **An explicit choice wins** — a model or reasoning effort picked in that window pins the draft, so the default does not replace it.
3. **The first send waits** — `startDraftThread` awaits the pending default before issuing `threads/start` and reads the model afterwards. Without this the turn would start on `fallbackDraftModel()` (`openai/gpt-5.5`, not present in the replay config), which is what the picker holds until the default lands. The optimistic user row is drawn before the wait, so the click keeps its immediate feedback.

## The suite flake

`thread-selection.spec.ts` has been failing intermittently for a while. It was not a WebSocket problem — the surrounding logs are full of connection resets and cookie warnings, and those were unrelated.

The test clicks `+`, waits for `#input` to be visible, and types. That wait passed instantly against the *previous* thread's composer, so the test typed into the composer that was about to be reset. It surfaced two steps later as "agent reply never appeared", with the page still on the draft placeholder and an empty composer.

## Tests

`tests/e2e/tests/draft-composer.spec.ts` holds the project `GET` open with a route interceptor, so the window is wide and deterministic rather than a rare timing loss, and waits for the response to be delivered before asserting.

- `keeps a message typed while the new thread is still opening` — the draft is usable before the fetch returns, the typed text survives it, and the message sends.
- `sends the first message on the project's model, not the placeholder` — asserts `model_ref` in the intercepted `threads/start` body.

Each guard was verified by removing it and observing the corresponding failure.

One gap, stated plainly: rule 2 is not reachable through the UI in this harness, because `#modelSel` and `#effortSel` are both empty until `loadProjectModels` completes, so there is nothing to pick during the window. The guard is kept because that is a second independent fetch whose ordering is not guaranteed, but it is code without a test.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace` | 487 passed |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | clean |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` | clean |
| Full Playwright suite | 40/40, repeated runs — `thread-selection` included, no longer excluded |
| 40-iteration create-thread loop (natural timing) | before: fails at iteration 39 · after: completes |

Spec bumped to 1.63 with **LT6** (synchronous open) and **LT7** (the three model rules); the §13 *Composer drafts* bullet now states that a view switch must not discard text typed while it is in progress.

## Follow-up, not included

`openThread` has the same shape — `saveComposerDraft()` → `await` → `restoreComposerDraft()` — so text typed during a thread switch is lost the same way. It is a narrower case, so it is left out of this change rather than widening it.

author: realcodywburns
body:
Running the spec-067 quickstart end to end (**T148**) found that much of it doesn't work as written — including the three gates it calls merge-blocking. Also closes the T136–T143 / T147 ledger entries, which shipped in #967 but were never marked.

## Credential leak — the reason this isn't just a docs commit

`scripts/ops/verify-protocol-addresses.js` printed the resolved RPC endpoint **verbatim** in its per-network header and again in its HTTP error path. QuickNode and Alchemy embed the API key in the URL *path*, and this script's output goes to stdout, into CI logs, and into terminal transcripts people paste into issues — so **every run against a keyed endpoint published a live key**.

Now redacted to protocol + host, with `/…` marking that a credential existed:

```
https://my-node.quiknode.pro/abc123secretkey/     -> https://my-node.quiknode.pro/…
https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/SUPERSECRET  -> https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/…
https://rpc.example.com/?apikey=hunter2           -> https://rpc.example.com/…
https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com               -> https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com
```

## The safety gates did not run

All three commands in quickstart §1 were stale, and two failed in the worst available way: **`--grep` with no match exits 0 reporting "0 passing"**, so 1a and 1b read as green merge gates while asserting nothing. 1c passed *directories* to `hardhat test`, which takes files, so it crashed.

| Gate | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| 1a | `--grep "expiry refund"` → 0 passing | `--grep "MEMBER as depositor"` → **2 passing** |
| 1b | `--grep "NFT owner\|exit without router"` → 0 passing | actual test titles → **5 passing** |
| 1c | directories → `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` | the two test files → **8 passing** |

1a's pattern was stale because the expiry test was deliberately rescoped — an Across refund needs an off-chain dataworker root bundle, a dispute window and a merkle-proved leaf, so staging it would mostly test Across. Each gate gained a note to **check the passing count, not just the exit code**, since that's the failure mode that hid this.

**This also closes T150 blocker 6.** `depositor == member` had only ever been proven against a mock written by the same authors; it has now run green against the real Polygon SpokePool's own event encoding.

## Two more real defects

- **`deploy-bridge-liquidity.js` printed `Wrapped`** while registering `ConfigOnly` — contradicting the paragraph at the top of the same file explaining why these services must *not* be Wrapped. That's the line an operator pastes into a deployment record, and the distinction is what stops `depositToVaultWithFee` being pointed at them. The label map now lives beside `ServiceKind` in `lib/feeServices`; both scripts read it, removing the private copy that let them drift.
- **`AssetDetailSheet` gated Trade on raw `net.dex`** instead of `capabilities.dex`, bypassing the FR-016a `SWAP_CHAIN_IDS` allow-list. Latent under today's config; live the moment a network's DEX addresses land.

## Verified

Contracts 979 passing / 2 known environmental fork failures. Frontend 4,487 passing / the same 4 known pre-existing failures. An intermediate run showed 978/3 — the mainnet-fork staking test flaking on a public RPC, confirmed not a regression by running it in isolation on both trees.

## Found but not fixed here

Filed separately rather than scope-creeping this PR — see the issue comment on #966:

- **SC-020 is broken on the Trade surface.** `TradePanel`/`TradeTokenSelect` are still strictly active-chain — no cross-network list, no pin, no search. Bridge and Supply were converted; Trade was not.
- `ineligibleReason` in `networkPin.js` has **no production caller**, so "an ineligible asset shows its disabled reason rather than vanishing" doesn't happen — `UniversalAssetSelect` filters them out.
- `check:storage-layout` fails after a local §3 deploy: it matches records by `chain<id>`, and hardhat's default 1337 collides with the local node's.
- §2 names `npm run slither` and `npx medusa fuzz`, neither of which exists.
- CI never runs `npm run test:fork`, and `oracle-fork-tests.yml` supplies only Amoy + Polygon RPCs — so the base forks and the mainnet HubPool test silently skip while the job reports green.
