author: drizki
body:
## Outcome

This replaces the four application-chrome wrappers with one context-aware `ApplicationMasthead`, while retaining the existing declarative `MenuBar`, menu model, and controller primitives. Menus and the command palette now project the same typed command registries, so a command has one label, visibility rule, enabled rule, disabled reason, shortcut, and handler.

## Parts A–F

- **A — one application menu bar:** `ApplicationMasthead` resolves dashboard, screenplay, breakdown, and setup contexts. The old `ApplicationMastheads` and `ScreenplayMenuBar` implementations and their dead CSS are deleted. Start- and end-aligned menus now share one physical and accessible menubar.
- **B — truthful commands:** capability-absent commands are omitted; capability-present but unavailable commands are visibly disabled with inline, tooltip, and accessible explanations. Find and Find/Replace now open genuinely different CodeMirror modes. Reset and Publish require explicit `ConfirmationDialog` confirmation.
- **C — one palette everywhere:** the existing `CommandPalette` remains the sole implementation and retains `useDialogStackEntry`. Dashboard, screenplay, breakdown, and `/breakdowns/new` feed it their real command registry; the trigger and Ctrl/Cmd+K work on each surface.
- **D — universal Help and credits:** Help is declared once and reused everywhere. `OpenSourceCreditsModal` uses `ModalShell`, search, internal scrolling, initial focus, stable focus restoration, and shared-stack Escape ordering. `pnpm credits:generate` derives a deterministic 285-entry manifest.
- **E — no application-chrome logo:** auth and invitations retain branding. Dashboard uses the requested minimal initials identity; breakdown, screenplay, and setup use navigable breadcrumbs, preserving the navigation previously hidden behind each logo. Identity/avatar consolidation remains for #180.
- **F — host capabilities:** `HostWindowCapabilities` is resolved once at the renderer boundary from an optional preload bridge. Components consume named `applicationMenu`, `windowControls`, and `titleBarDrag` capabilities and never inspect a platform or runtime-profile name. A native-menu host suppresses only in-app menus; breadcrumb/identity and the palette remain.

### Structural reasoning

The consolidation is a registry-and-projection design rather than one giant conditional menu tree. Each surface still declares menu composition as data, but every actionable row is an `ApplicationCommand<Context>` shared by menus, shortcuts, and the palette. This keeps surface-specific behavior explicit while preventing the three command surfaces from drifting.

The host seam is a small renderer capability provider, mirroring `library-target.tsx`: preload integration stays at one boundary, while components remain portable. The browser default is the current in-app bar; a future native-menu host can inject capabilities without editing application components.

Credits cover the host-neutral production dependency closure of `@coda/web` and `@coda/api` plus font files bundled by the web client. These are the renderer and local service shipped to users. Development-only dependencies and the separately operated MCP service are excluded. Environment-selected native optional packages are represented by their portable parents, preventing generator-host artifacts from changing the manifest. Fresh macOS and Linux installs produced the same SHA-256 (`cd814aa7528079470d487933b2eebb8f482b7324db56a0e31de101760cd61bc3`). Entries are de-duplicated and sorted by license, package, and version, with no timestamp or local path. The checked artifact is enforced by `pnpm quality`.

## Part B running-app audit

| Surface / command group | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| Dashboard File/Edit/View/Go and dashboard palette | **PASS — binding audit retained.** The issue's running-app audit already verified these; their handlers were not re-tested. They are now projections of the shared registry. |
| Dashboard on `/breakdowns` | **PASS — running app.** Export Screenplay, generic Rename/Find/Refresh, and other capability-absent object actions are absent instead of misleadingly disabled. Supported empty-library actions retain their surface label and state a reason. |
| Screenplay `Edit > Find…` vs `Find and Replace…` | **PASS — running e2e.** Find sets `data-coda-search-mode="find"` and hides replacement controls; Find/Replace sets `"replace"` and shows them. |
| Screenplay command layer fixed by #183 and management fixed by #185 | **PASS — binding audit retained.** No reimplementation or redundant running-app retest. The existing real handlers are projected into the common registry. |
| Breakdown `Workspace > Reset Workspace…` | **PASS — running e2e.** Confirmation is visible; confirming completes the `/workspace-layout/reset` POST successfully. |
| Breakdown `Workspace > Publish Default…` | **PASS — running e2e.** Confirmation is visible; confirming completes the `/workspace-layout/publish` POST successfully. |
| Breakdown end-aligned project chip | **PASS — running DOM + focused test.** It is a descendant of the single `role="menubar"` and project navigation still works. |
| `/breakdowns/new` chrome | **PASS — running e2e.** Menubar, Help, palette trigger, Ctrl/Cmd+K, account actions, and Library breadcrumb are present. |
| Screenplay and breakdown palettes | **PASS — running e2e.** Both expose their contextual commands; screenplay has editor commands and breakdown has workspace commands and project objects. |
| Help / dialog stack | **PASS — running e2e.** Credits receives search focus; Ctrl/Cmd+K opens above it; first Escape closes the palette, second closes credits, and focus returns to Help. |
| Full Screen | **Not chased, per binding audit.** The standard browser API does not settle in the automation webview; no new defect was found. |

### Help destinations

| Item | Before | After / verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Documentation | `https://kinetik-gg.github.io/coda-docs/` (already corrected by #183; historical `https://coda.github.io` was 404) | unchanged, HTTP 200 |
| GitHub | `https://github.com/kinetik-gg/coda` | unchanged, HTTP 200 |
| Report an Issue | `https://github.com/kinetik-gg/coda/issues` | unchanged, HTTP 200 |

The generator emitted 295 unique project/license destinations across 285 credits; a concurrent curl audit found no failing URL after project links were normalized to stable, versioned npm pages.

## Verification — verbatim terminal results

```text
$ pnpm format && pnpm format:check
$ prettier --check .
Checking formatting...
All matched files use Prettier code style!

$ pnpm lint
$ eslint . --max-warnings=0
[exit 0]

$ pnpm typecheck
apps/api typecheck: Done
apps/web typecheck: Done

$ pnpm quality
Open-source credits manifest is current.
Found 58 clones.
Total duplicated lines: 1016 (1.04%)
✔ No circular dependency found!
check-db-portability: 341 files clean — no dialect-specific SQL outside the adapter.
check-runtime-profile-portability: 196 files clean — no profile branching outside the capability module.
[exit 0]
```

author: mabrig1
body:
## The evidence

Production logs from the ten-agent deployment show the model ids are finally correct — **no 404s** — and every call still failing:

```
openai/gpt-oss-120b returned nothing within 14s
nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5 returned nothing within 8s
qwen/qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct — no response within 37s
Node.js process exited with exit status: 128
```

Three defects behind that, plus the reason a finished build still doesn't look like an app.

### 1. Budgets too small to reach first token

Ten steps split 240s (~24s each), then the provider chain split *that* again across three tiers at 60/40 — leaving **8–15s per model**. A free inference tier routinely needs 20s+ before it starts streaming, so every model "failed" while working normally.

- The first tier now gets the **whole** step budget. Reserving time for later tiers only pays off when failures are fast (404, 401) — and those cost no time, leaving the budget intact anyway. Holding time back from the first attempt is what turned "slow" into "failed".
- `MIN_ATTEMPT_MS` 8s → **25s**.
- A **timeout stops the chain**: another model on the same slow endpoint won't answer faster, so falling back to the scaffold immediately beats burning the rest of the step.

### 2. Budget spread too thin

Weights now concentrate on the three steps that write the app — planner 2, ui 3.5, coding 3.5 — and the **Architect Agent is deterministic by design**: its file map is fully derived from the plan, so a model call there bought nothing and cost a slice the generating steps needed.

### 3. Unhandled rejection crashed the function

The stream's completion promise was handled with `.then(...).catch(...)`, which leaves the promise returned by `.then()` unhandled when `completion` itself rejects — exactly what an aborted request does. Now handled with two-argument `then()` at the point of creation. **This is what took the build down with `exit status 128`.**

### 4. The preview was a poster, not an app

The UI Agent was asked for *"a static preview of the app's home page"* and dutifully produced landing pages; the scaffold did the same. Both now produce a **working prototype**: the app's primary interface, seeded with sample records, with inline script so add/toggle/delete actually respond. The scaffold derives its list from the plan's first table (label column, status column), so even a degraded build shows something app-shaped.

## Verification

Against a stub that mimics the real free tier (**20s to first token**, then streams):

```
planner     | Manage projects and tasks on a Kanban board.
ui          | Generated 6 UI files          ← no fallback note
database    | Schema ready: tasks
coding      | Wrote 3 code files            ← no fallback note
repair      | Applied 1 fix(es) — all checks now pass
deployment  | Deployed and verified
110s · 12 files · 7/8 verification (auth warns in demo mode)
```

**The first run where nothing degrades to a scaffold.** Under the old budgets every one of those steps timed out.

Scaffold preview renders at HTTP 200 with a working add form, live list, checkbox toggle, delete actions, and nav to the planned pages — verified by fetching `/api/preview/<id>` and asserting on the markup.

`tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` all clean.

## What

Add the already-live public canon MCP endpoint to AgentTool's RFC 9727 API catalog:

- one catalog `item` for `https://api.agenttool.dev/v1/mcp/canon`
- one per-API context with the public discovery document, experimental compatibility locator, and service health
- no media-type guess for the content-negotiated MCP endpoint
- no `service-desc`, OpenAPI-coverage implication, payment relation, write path, provider claim, or authority claim

The item says the exact useful contract: MCP Streamable HTTP over POST, no authentication, and exactly two read-only tools (`search` and `fetch`). The experimental card remains `service-meta`, not a standardized MCP discovery record.

## Why

The canonical three-road compass sends an `inspect` visitor to this API catalog. Before this change, that catalog listed no MCP endpoint even though AgentTool's first-party origin index, `agent.txt`, docs, and compatibility locator already exposed the live public MCP surfaces.

This closes that first-party discovery break without changing the three roads or the MCP runtime.

## Verified

- 83 focused discovery/MCP/Telescope round-trip tests passed, 2,794 assertions
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `git diff-tree --check`
- exact committed output inspected: no `service-desc` or payment relation on the MCP context
- independent read-only standards review found no blocker against RFC 9727, RFC 9264, or RFC 8631
- GitHub CI: all 11 jobs passed on exact head `5a3dc189`

The first CI run caught the old seven-context count in the real producer-to-Telescope-consumer round trip. The follow-up commit updates that contract and now asserts that Telescope receives both the canon MCP membership item and its context; the second full CI run is green.

I also attempted the unfiltered API suite locally. It reached unrelated database-backed tests and failed because no PostgreSQL service is running at localhost:5432; it also reached a cross-workspace SDK test whose workspace dependency is not installed in this isolated worktree. I stopped the noisy run rather than start services or install the wider estate. GitHub's hermetic API, protocol, database, package, and SDK gates all passed afterward.

## Fase 7 — módulo clínico-financeiro

Quando um **procedimento vinculado a um orçamento/pacote já pago** utiliza **produtos com valor de venda**, o modal de procedimento agora:

1. Mostra um checkbox **"Os produtos utilizados já estavam previstos no orçamento/pacote pago?"** — padrão **marcado (sim)**, opção conservadora (não propõe nada por padrão).

author: cmadd123
body:
Security audit found two ways one tenant can reach another's data. Both are Firestore-rules fixes (+ one query refactor).

## 1. org_ref self-assignment → cross-tenant takeover (CRITICAL)
`users/{uid}` allowed unconstrained `write`, and org membership = `users/{uid}.org_ref`. org_ref values leak via public link docs, so an attacker could read a victim's org_ref, set their own, and get full access to that tenant. **Fix:** org_ref may only be set to your own uid (personal org) or an org that invited your email (verified via `invites/{email}`, matching the existing invites-rule pattern). Signup and normal profile edits unaffected.

## 2. Public link collections allowed `list` → mass exfiltration (HIGH)
`client_sign_links` / `sub_schedule_links` / `designer_links` used `allow read: if true`. In rules v2 `read` = `get` **+ `list`**, so anyone could `getDocs()` the whole collection and dump every org's signed proposals, sub schedules/addresses, designer links. **Fix:** `allow get: if true` + deny `list` (designer_links keeps an org-scoped list for the builder; `createOrGetDesignerLink` now queries by org_ref so that's satisfiable).

## ⚠️ Deploy required
Rules are inert until `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules`. Could not emulator-test locally (no Java in this env) — please run rules-unit-testing / a staged deploy before prod. Logic was reviewed against existing working patterns; typecheck clean.

author: officialabhinavsingh
body:
## LLM generated content, by Claude Opus 5

Drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by me. I have read every line of this
change, run the full test suite locally, and can explain each decision. Local
test output is included below.

#### Reference Issues/PRs

Part of #3429. Addresses the `PaddingTransformer` entry.

#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.

`PaddingTransformer` did not implement `get_test_params`, so it fell back to the
base class default of a single empty parameter set. It was therefore listed in
`EXCLUDED_TESTS_BY_TEST["test_get_test_params_coverage"]`.

This PR adds two test parameter sets and removes the exclusion entry.

**1. `sktime/transformations/padder.py`** — adds `get_test_params` returning:

```python
params = [
    {"pad_length": None, "fill_value": 0},
    {"pad_length": 120, "fill_value": -1.0},
]
```

The first set restates the `__init__` defaults. This is deliberate:
`create_test_instance` uses the first dictionary, and `PaddingTransformer` is
used as a pipeline component in `test_compose.py`, `test_base.py`, and the
classification/clustering `test_pipeline.py` modules. Keeping the first entry at
the defaults means `create_test_instance()` is unchanged by this PR and those
tests continue to exercise the same configuration as before.

The second set is substantially different, and reaches code the first set cannot:

- `pad_length=120` takes the `else` branch of `_fit` (user-specified fixed
  length). Previously only the `pad_length is None` branch, which infers the max
  length from the data, was reachable from the general test suite.
- `fill_value=-1.0` makes padding visible in the output. With the default
  `fill_value=0`, an implementation that ignored `fill_value` and hardcoded a
  zero fill would produce identical output and go undetected. A negative float
  also sits outside the range of the generated test data and exercises the
  `float` coercion in `np.full(self.pad_length_, self.fill_value, float)`.

`pad_length=120` is the value already used in this estimator's own tests
(`sktime/transformations/tests/test_Padder.py`, lines 38 and 56), so no new
magic number is introduced. The value must be at least the longest series in the
test data, since `_transform` raises `ValueError` when
`max_length > self.pad_length_`.

**2. `sktime/tests/_config.py`** — removes `"PaddingTransformer"` from
`EXCLUDED_TESTS_BY_TEST["test_get_test_params_coverage"]`.

Both changes are required together. `test_excluded_tests_by_test` in
`sktime/tests/tests/test_test_utils.py` asserts that the exclusion list is a
subset of the estimators that genuinely have fewer than two test parameter sets,
so leaving the entry in place while adding the parameters fails that test
(verified locally, output below).

`PaddingTransformer` is not present in `EXCLUDE_SOFT_DEPS`, so no change is
needed there.

#### Does your contribution introduce a new dependency? If yes, which one?

No. `pyproject.toml` is untouched.

#### What should a reviewer concentrate their feedback on?

* The choice of `pad_length=120` for the second parameter set. It is the value
  already used in `test_Padder.py`, and the `_transform` guard is one-sided
  (larger is safe, smaller raises), but a smaller value would also work if
  preferred for speed.
* Whether the first parameter set should be spelled out as
  `{"pad_length": None, "fill_value": 0}` or left implicit. I made it explicit
  to keep `create_test_instance` behaviour identical for the composition tests
  that use this transformer.

#### Did you add any tests for the change?

No new test file. This PR enables an existing framework test,
`test_get_test_params_coverage`, which was previously not collected for this
estimator, and adds a second parameter set that is then exercised across the
whole standard estimator suite.

Local test output, on Python 3.14.6, pandas 2.3.3, numpy 2.4.6,
scikit-learn 1.7.2:

Before the change, the test is not collected at all, because the estimator is
in the exclusion list:

```
$ pytest sktime/tests/test_all_estimators.py \
    -k "test_get_test_params_coverage and PaddingTransformer"
53305 deselected in 150.89s
```

After removing the exclusion entry only, without adding `get_test_params`:

```
>           assert len(param_list) > 1, msg
E           AssertionError: PaddingTransformer.get_test_params should return at
E           least two test parameter sets, but only 1 found.
E           assert 1 > 1
E            +  where 1 = len([{}])

FAILED sktime/tests/test_all_estimators.py::TestAllObjects::test_get_test_params_coverage[PaddingTransformer]
1 failed, 53305 deselected
```

With both changes applied:

```
$ pytest sktime/tests/test_all_estimators.py \
    -k "test_get_test_params_coverage and PaddingTransformer"
1 passed, 53433 deselected in 153.85s
```

The deselected count rises from 53305 to 53433. The additional 128 collected
tests are the second parameter set being exercised across the standard suite.

Full standard suite for this estimator, both parameter sets:

```
$ pytest sktime/tests/test_all_estimators.py -k "PaddingTransformer"
270 passed, 53164 deselected in 153.98s
```

Guard test, this estimator's own tests, and every module that uses
`PaddingTransformer` as a pipeline component:

```
$ pytest sktime/tests/tests/test_test_utils.py \
         sktime/transformations/tests/test_Padder.py \
         sktime/transformations/tests/test_base.py \
         sktime/transformations/tests/test_compose.py \
         sktime/classification/compose/tests/test_pipeline.py \
         sktime/clustering/compose/tests/test_pipeline.py
108 passed, 3 skipped in 9.54s
```

Confirming the estimator's own tests and the guard test actually ran rather
than being skipped:

```
test_Padder.py::test_padding_transformer PASSED
test_Padder.py::test_padding_parameterised_transformer PASSED
test_Padder.py::test_padding_fill_value_transformer PASSED
test_test_utils.py::test_excluded_tests_by_test PASSED
4 passed
```

To confirm the two changes are coupled, I temporarily restored the exclusion
entry while keeping `get_test_params`, which fails as expected:

```
E         Extra items in the left set:
E         'PaddingTransformer'
FAILED sktime/tests/tests/test_test_utils.py::test_excluded_tests_by_test
```

`pre-commit run --files sktime/transformations/padder.py sktime/tests/_config.py`
passes, including `ruff format` and `ruff check`.

#### Any other comments?

The class docstring documents `pad_length` but not `fill_value`. I have left
that out of scope to keep this PR to a single concern, and am happy to open a
separate `[DOC]` PR for it if useful.

#### PR checklist

##### For all contributions
- [x] I've added myself to the [list of contributors](https://github.com/sktime/sktime/blob/main/CONTRIBUTORS.md) with any new badges I've earned :-)
- [x] The PR title starts with either [ENH], [MNT], [DOC], or [BUG].

The 4th finding (discussion fetch firing on every detail-page view rather than only on thread-expand) was left as-is — it's an intentional tradeoff, not a bug: net bandwidth is still strongly positive, and gating it further would lose the wrong-attempt/participant tooltips without a clear win.

## Motivation

The trainer previously had distributed configuration support but lacked complete integration between distributed strategies and the training phase execution flow. This change enables proper distributed model handling while preserving existing single-device training behavior.

Closes #371 

## Changes

- Added distributed phase strategy integration in `nightmarenet/distributed/strategies.py` to apply appropriate wrapping based on training phase.
- Updated `nightmarenet/training/trainer.py` to route phase execution through distributed-aware model strategies.
- Updated `configs/default.yaml` with distributed training configuration compatibility.

body:
## 요약

- 에픽 #77, 이슈 #83 의 첫 PR. `src/core/games-composer.ts` 의 순수 리듀서(게임 추가 컴포저의
  단계 전이)를 XState 머신(`src/core/composer.machine.ts`)으로 그대로 옮긴다.
- **사용처는 아직 0이다.** `game-composer.tsx` 배선과 `games-composer.ts`·그 테스트 삭제는
  다음 PR(14).

## 무엇이 바뀌는가

- 9종 액션의 전이표가 계층 상태로 읽힌다: `search`(`beforeResults`/`hasResults`) / `detail`.
  - 늦게 온 검색 응답을 버리는 옛 `isStaleSearch`(`selected!==null || query!==state.query`)의
    앞 조건은 이제 `detail` 상태 자체가 구조로 걸러 준다(그 이벤트를 받는 핸들러가
    `search` 아래에만 있다) — 남는 건 검색어 대조뿐이다.
  - `searchError`(검색 실패)와 `addError`(추가 실패)가 다른 단계에 속한다는 사실이 구조로
    드러난다.
- `activeIndex`(콤보박스 키보드 커서) 접힘은 상태 재진입에 기대지 않고 각 케이스에서 손으로
  -1 을 다시 쓴다 — XState 의 `assign` 은 같은 값을 넣어도 매번 새 context 객체를 만들어서
  (실측), 재진입에 기대면 "같은 자리를 다시 가리키면 같은 context 다"(mousemove 바일아웃)
  불변식이 깨진다. `activeMoved`·`activeSet` 은 가드로 "바뀌는 게 없으면 액션 자체를 안 문다"를
  직접 챙긴다.

## 테스트

- `games-composer.test.ts` 의 48케이스를 `composer.machine.test.ts` 로 전부 이관했다(케이스가
  줄지 않았다 — 오히려 계층 상태값 전이를 확인하는 케이스 1개를 더해 49개).
- 순수 함수 호출 자리는 XState 의 `initialTransition`/`transition`(부수효과 없는 pure API)으로
  옮겼다 — 원본의 `run(...actions)` 폴드·`composerReducer(state, action)` 직접 호출과 같은
  사용법이다.
- "같은 자리를 다시 가리키면 같은 상태 객체다" 테스트는 원본이 보던 리듀서 상태 전체 참조
  대신, 컴포넌트가 실제로 구독할 `context` 의 참조 동일성으로 옮겼다(둘 다 XState 에서
  assign 이 안 돌면 참조가 그대로라는 실측 위에 있다).

## 검증

- `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run boundaries && npm test && npm run build` 전부

author: dbelokursky
body:
**Фаза 6.** Список из сорока серверов из подписки листался только скроллом, а единственный показатель, по которому его имеет смысл упорядочить, жил в другой вкладке.

## Поиск — одно поле, а не четыре

Фильтр смотрит на всё, что видно в строке: имя, адрес, порт, протокол. Пользователь, набирающий `de-3`, `vless` или `443`, хочет одного и того же — спрашивать его, в каком это было поле, значит задавать вопрос, на который он не обязан отвечать.

## Сортировка

Мой порядок (по умолчанию — единственный предсказуемый), по имени, по протоколу, сначала быстрые.

**Незамеренные и недоступные — всегда внизу.** Ни то, ни другое не является скоростью, которую наблюдали; поднять их наверх в списке «сначала быстрые» было бы враньём.

## Откуда берётся задержка

Последний результат теперь хранится в `LatencyTester`. **Только в памяти**: задержка верна для момента и сети, и запись её в `servers.json` подавала бы цифру из прошлой сессии как текущий факт.

Кнопка «Замерить» наполняет её для **видимых сейчас** серверов — отфильтрованные пропускаются: мерить сорок, когда пользователь сузил до трёх, это работа, о которой не просили.

## Активацию пришлось перестроить первой

Она была привязана к модели выделения. Это работало ровно пока список не пересобирался под ней — а `FilteredList` пересобирает его на каждое нажатие клавиши и сам двигает выделение. **Поиск молча переключал бы сервер, через который приложение подключается.**

Та же правка чинит два дефекта, которые были и раньше:
- навигация стрелками писала конфиг и перезапускала живой туннель на каждое нажатие;
- множественный выбор был невозможен — любая строка, задетая при его наборе, становилась активной.

Теперь активирует обычный клик или Enter; клик с модификатором набирает выделение. Это и делает возможным массовое удаление — ошибочно импортированная подписка требовала сорока подтверждений.

## Что не сделано и почему

**Группировка по подписке снята, а не отложена.** `SubscriptionService.applyNamePrefix` уже добавляет каждому импортированному серверу префикс `[Имя]`, так что группировка видна в строке и — что полезнее — доступна через тот же поиск. Настоящие заголовки групп к тому же противоречат сортировке: список не может быть одновременно сгруппирован по источнику и упорядочен глобально по задержке, а пришли именно за задержкой.

## Проверка

`mvn clean verify` — **591/591** зелёные (+8 новых). Вёрстка проверена рендером вида в PNG, а не чтением FXML.

author: sinity
body:
## Summary

`devtools verify --quick` (and its `render all --check`/lint/mypy components) currently fails on `master` HEAD itself.

## Problem

The tracker-authority PR that merged earlier today added `docs/tracker-authority.md` and `devtools/reconcile_tracker_authority.py` without ever registering the doc in `devtools/docs_surface.py`'s registry, and the script fails both `ruff check` (SIM115: unpaired `NamedTemporaryFile` open/close) and `mypy --strict` (`_load_manifest` returns `Any` from a `dict[str, Any]`-typed function). None of this was caught pre-merge — GitHub's squash-merge button doesn't run the local pre-push hook, so nothing exercised the quick gate against the final merged tree. Discovered while rebasing an unrelated worktree onto master and finding `devtools verify --quick` red at HEAD with no local changes.

## Solution

- Registered "Tracker Authority" in `docs_surface.py`'s operations tier and regenerated `docs/README.md`.
- `_write_candidate` now opens its temp file with a context manager instead of an unpaired open/finally-close.
- `_load_manifest` narrows `json.loads()`'s result with an `isinstance(payload, dict)` check before returning it as `dict[str, Any]`.

## Verification

- `devtools test tests/unit/devtools/test_render_docs_surface.py` — 5 passed.
- `devtools verify --quick` — pass (confirmed failing at HEAD before this change, exit 1 via `render all` reporting the unindexed doc, plus the ruff/mypy findings).

author: devdesai444
body:
Keeps the free-tier Supabase project from auto-pausing (the thing that broke login before).

**How it works:** the project pauses after ~7 days without database activity — and dashboard visits / auth-only calls don't count, it has to be a real query against a table. `scripts/supabase-keepalive.mjs` does a PostgREST select against `profiles`; the query runs in Postgres even though RLS returns no rows, which is what keeps the project marked active. The GitHub Action runs it daily at 06:17 UTC in GitHub's cloud, so nothing needs to stay on locally.

**Note:** scheduled Actions only run from the default branch, so this starts firing once merged to main. You can trigger it manually any time from Actions → supabase-keepalive → Run workflow to confirm it's green.

URL + anon key default to the public values already in `supabase-config.js`; set `SUPABASE_URL` / `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` repo secrets to override if the project ever moves.

author: fdiazinoa
body:
## Qué cambia

- Agrega `get_dashboard_kpis_v2`, una RPC que calcula el contrato completo del Dashboard BI dentro de PostgreSQL en una sola consulta agregada.
- Sustituye la descarga paginada de todas las ventas por un servicio con modos de activación `legacy`, `shadow` y `v2`.
- Mantiene fallback automático al cálculo actual si la RPC falla.
- Evita solicitudes duplicadas concurrentes con single-flight y limpia la caché al importar o reiniciar ventas.
- Reduce la consulta de locales del frontend a los cinco campos que realmente necesita.
- Conserva los KPI visibles durante una actualización y aplica el período solo al pulsar `Aplicar`, evitando dos cargas sucesivas al editar las fechas.

## Por qué

El endpoint actual descarga bloques de 1,000 ventas desde Supabase hacia Railway y agrega todo en Python. Para Ágora, del 1 al 26 de julio, esto implicaba 107,018 registros, aproximadamente 107 solicitudes y varios megabytes transferidos por cada caché fría.

## Impacto y compatibilidad

- El modo predeterminado continúa siendo `legacy`, por lo que desplegar el código no cambia inmediatamente el resultado operativo.
- `shadow` compara ambos resultados y responde todavía con legacy.
- `v2` activa el camino optimizado; ante cualquier error vuelve automáticamente a legacy.
- La función SQL solo puede ejecutarse con `service_role`; `anon` y `authenticated` no tienen permiso.
- La migración ya fue registrada de forma aditiva; no modifica ni elimina datos.

## Validación

- Suite completa: `139 passed`.
- Pruebas enfocadas finales: `15 passed`.
- Build de producción Vite: exitoso (`2147 modules transformed`).
- Paridad con datos reales de Ágora: `difference_count = 0` para los 107,018 registros del período.
- Benchmark sin caché: legacy `22,335.5 ms`; v2 `393.7 ms` (~57x más rápido).
- `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`: `261.854 ms`, sin lecturas físicas en la ejecución observada.
- Permisos verificados: `anon=false`, `authenticated=false`, `service_role=true`.

## Activación recomendada en Railway

1. Desplegar manteniendo `DASHBOARD_KPI_MODE=legacy`.
2. Cambiar a `shadow` y revisar registros de paridad.
3. Cambiar a `v2` cuando la comparación permanezca limpia.

author: nolte
body:
## Summary

The nightly E2E matrix ran **five** profiles while the declared in-scope set is **seven**. `full-tablet` was covered by neither the nightly nor any other workflow, so it had **no CI coverage at all** — and it was missing from the `workflow_dispatch` choice list too, so it could not even be dispatched by name.

That matters beyond the missing profile: *"the nightly is green"* did not mean the declared matrix was green, and nothing in the workflow said so. During the #768 campaign `full-tablet` surfaced defects no other profile could — it combines the `md`-and-above sidebar behaviour with full auth mode — but that evidence stayed local, and PR #759 recorded the limitation explicitly because it could not be closed at the time.

The infrastructure was never missing: the compose service `e2e-tests-full-tablet` exists and `scripts/run-e2e.sh` maps the profile correctly. This was purely a workflow-configuration gap.

## Changes

One file: `.github/workflows/e2e-nightly.yml` (1 file changed, 203 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-), after the rebase onto #805).

**The profile list is derived, not restated.** A `registry` step parses the `case "$PROFILE" in` block of `scripts/run-e2e.sh` at run time. That block *is* the registry: every matrix cell is literally the argument to `./scripts/run-e2e.sh --profile <cell>`, so deriving from it makes it impossible for the matrix and the runner to disagree about what a profile name means.

**Compose was evaluated as the source and rejected, with evidence.** `docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml config --profiles` reports:

```
core-crud  full  full-mobile  full-tablet  mobile  smoke  tablet  timescaledb
```

`light` is **absent** (its runner `e2e-tests` has no `profiles:` key — it is the default service) and three names are present that are not `--profile` values. Deriving from that would need a hard-coded *addition* plus a hard-coded *subtraction*, i.e. the literal back again. The mapping is also demonstrably not the identity: `core-crud` exists as a compose profile but has no `--profile` branch.

**The parse is narrow and loud**: the anchor `^case "[$]PROFILE" in$` must appear exactly once or the step fails; every parsed token must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`. A formatting change that breaks the parse produces a red run, not silent coverage loss — verified, see mutation E below.

**`smoke` is excluded from the nightly matrix, deliberately and visibly.** It is a marker subset of the light suite and already runs per PR and per push to `develop` as the required `E2E smoke (compose, light)` check, so nightly it would add no coverage `light` does not already give. The decision is recorded in three places so the next reader does not have to re-derive it: the file header comment, a named job env `NIGHTLY_EXCLUDE: smoke`, and the dispatch description (`all = full matrix, minus smoke`). It stays in the choice list so a one-off re-run of just that subset remains dispatchable — which also keeps the guard invariant as the clean "choice list == registry" rather than "registry minus an exception".

**A four-way drift guard** runs as a shell step in the existing `matrix` job — no new workflow — and **before** the fan-out, so a mismatch costs one runner-minute instead of six jobs. It checks: the dispatch choice list against the registry; every registry profile has a compose profile (with `light` exempted and the reason stated); **every compose profile is reachable through the run script** — the direction that hid this bug; and every `NIGHTLY_EXCLUDE` entry is a real registry profile, so a rename cannot silently turn the exclusion into a no-op.

**A failing guard turns the run red**, and that is the whole notification story. This PR originally extended the `report` job so a drift failure could not go unannounced; #805 has since removed that job entirely, establishing the run status and the per-profile check runs as the single reporting channel and dropping the auto-filed failure issues. The extension was therefore obsolete on rebase and has been dropped — a skipped matrix makes the run red on its own, which is exactly the signal #805 intends.

## Linked issues

Closes #794

## Testing

**The guard was mutation-tested against itself** in a sandbox copy, running the real step scripts (the original file untouched):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| **A** — `full-tablet` removed from the choice list (the original defect) | exit 1, side-by-side diff shows `> full-tablet` |
| **B** — new compose profile `desktop` with no script branch | exit 1: `Compose profile 'desktop' has no '--profile desktop' branch, so nothing in CI can run it.` |
| **C** — registry entry renamed `full-tablet` → `full-desktop` | exit 1, all three checks fire |
| **D** — `NIGHTLY_EXCLUDE: smoke-tests` | exit 1: `… is not a scripts/run-e2e.sh profile.` |
| **E** — case condition quoted, so the parse silently loses it | registry shrinks to 6 → exit 1 instead of silent coverage loss |
| Baseline, unmutated | exit 0: `No drift: matrix, scripts/run-e2e.sh and docker-compose.e2e.yml agree.` |

**Matrix resolution was executed, not reasoned about** — the `run:` blocks were extracted from the YAML with the `${{ }}` expressions substituted and `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` wired up:

```
Input 'all'            → profiles=["light","mobile","tablet","full","full-mobile","full-tablet"]
Input ''  (schedule)   → profiles=["light","mobile","tablet","full","full-mobile","full-tablet"]
Input 'full-tablet'    → profiles=["full-tablet"]
Input 'smoke'          → profiles=["smoke"]
Input 'light'          → profiles=["light"]
Input 'bogus-profile'  → (no output, exit 1)
                         ::error::Unknown profile 'bogus-profile'. Known profiles: light smoke mobile tablet full full-mobile full-tablet
```

**actionlint**: `docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/repo -w /repo rhysd/actionlint:latest` → **exit 0** on `e2e-nightly.yml`, verified independently of the implementing agent. (A whole-repo run exits 1 on three pre-existing findings in `docker-publish.yml` — SC2193 and 2× SC2086 — untouched here.) Two initial SC2016 infos on the new step were resolved **without a suppression**, by writing the pattern as `"[$]PROFILE"` (a bracket expression matching a literal dollar); equivalence for `grep -E` and `sed` BRE was verified separately. PyYAML parses the file; the `github-script` body passes `node --check`.

## Risk / rollout notes

- **Issue reference**: #794
- **Issue classification**: `chore` / `test`
- **Specialist**: `nolte-engineering:fullstack-developer`; orchestrator verified actionlint, the single-file territory boundary, and resolved the #805 rebase conflict

**Cost**: `all` goes from 5 to 6 parallel jobs — one more runner at 35–50 minutes. `fail-fast: false` and the matrix structure are unchanged, so the critical path does not lengthen. The guard adds one checkout plus a `docker compose config --profiles` call to the `matrix` job.

**Scope is larger than the issue's "keep it cheap"**: 135 code lines for a registry parse plus a four-way guard, where the issue suggested one shell step. The extra checks are what make the guard cover the direction that hid this bug (compose profile with no script branch) rather than only the direction that was visible. Worth a reviewer's judgement on whether that trade is right.

**The most fragile part** is the guard parsing the `options:` list out of this workflow file with `awk` — YAML by regex. It is anchored by an exact `options:` occurrence count that fails loudly if the shape changes, but it is the piece most likely to need attention when the file is restructured. GitHub requires a static literal there, so there is no way to derive it.

**Rebased onto #805**, which landed while this PR was open and rewrote the same file. Exactly one conflict hunk: the `report` job, deleted on develop's side and extended on this branch. Resolved in develop's favour — the job is gone, so the extension had nothing to attach to. Every other part of this change (matrix entry

author: 0xward
body:
A pass over the app against MiniPay's listing requirements (Stage 1 + Stage 2), since that is what this project is being built for. Five things were wrong. None were visible to a build, a type-check, or the asset audit — all five live either in copy or in a page nobody navigates to.

## Fixed

**1. The Add Cash deeplink pointed at a host MiniPay does not publish.**
`MINIPAY_ADD_CASH_URL` was `https://minipay.opera.com/add_cash`. The canonical reference (`docs.minipay.xyz/technical-references/deeplinks.html`, fetched today) states *"All deep links use the host link.minipay.xyz"* and documents Add Cash as `link.minipay.xyz/add_cash[?tokens=…]`. It lists no `minipay.opera.com` host at all. The comment defending the old value claimed `link.minipay.xyz` was the unrelated P2P "Cash Links" feature — that was wrong.

Now `https://link.minipay.xyz/add_cash?tokens=USDT,USDC,USDM`. **Caveat:** that docs page is still titled *"Deeplinks (available soon)"*, so this remains a device-verified item, not a settled one.

**2. "Add Cash" was our own button label** in seven places (Navbar ×4, Marketplace, Crafting, Season Pass). The copy rules map this action to **Deposit**. "Add Cash" now survives only in code comments, where it correctly names MiniPay's own screen.

**3. "Connect your wallet to mint a pass." / "Connect to claim daily perks."** — connect prompts inside the Mini App, which the zero-click-connect rule forbids. The whole premise is that the address is already there.

**4. `/profile` was worse than non-compliant — it was dead.** The page rendered `<PlayerProfileCard />` with no `walletAddress`, and nothing ever passed one, so it could never leave the "Connect wallet to load profile." branch. It now reads the wallet its own route already provides (`app/profile/layout.tsx` already wraps it in `Web3Providers`).

**5. `/profile` printed a full raw `0x…` address.** The phone-first identity rule bans a raw address as the primary identifier. It now goes through `maskAddress()`. A sweep confirms this was the only unmasked address left anywhere in the app.

Wiring the wallet up in (4) introduced a hydration mismatch — caught by the 360×640 check rather than by me. `useWallet()` falls back to a guest address in `localStorage`, which does not exist while Next prerenders that static route. The address is now read after mount so both sides start from the same state.

## Verified clean, no change needed

- **No message signing** — no `personal_sign` / `eth_signTypedData` / `signMessage` / `signTypedData` in `app`, `components`, `lib`, `hooks`, or the engine.
- **No CELO shown** — `celoBalance` is read by `WagmiIsland` and passed through the bridge, but no component renders it.
- **No banned vocabulary** in any user-facing string. The only repo matches are skill reference docs, an internal architecture note, and a script comment.
- **360 × 640** — `/profile`, `/stats`, `/terms`, `/privacy` all render with no horizontal overflow; `/game` is covered by the existing browser suite.
- **ToS, Privacy and support** are all reachable in-app from Settings.

## The guard

`scripts/check-minipay-copy.js` (`npm run check:copy`, wired into CI) enforces the three rules that live in copy: banned vocabulary, connect-wallet prompts, and message signing. It scans only text a user can actually read — JSX text nodes and text-bearing props — so `feeCurrency` and `eth_gasPrice` are left alone.

`/terms` is exempt from the vocabulary rule, and **only** that rule: a disclaimer saying NullState Point "is not a cryptocurrency" has to name the category to mean anything, and rewriting it to "not a stablecoin" would be both softer and false. The connect-wallet and signing rules still apply there.

Each of the three rules was verified by reintroducing a real violation and confirming the check goes red.

## Verification

- Full CI suite locally: market sync, engine parses, engine minifies (14/14, no skips), icons match masters, weapon sheets match icons, reference audit, copy check, `tsc` — all green.
- Browser suite on a production build: **20/20**.
- New 360×640 pass over `/profile`, `/stats`, `/terms`, `/privacy`: 13/14. The one failure is a 503 from `/api/player/profile` because this container has no Firebase Admin credentials — an environment artifact, and itself evidence that `/profile` now actually attempts the load it never used to.

## Still open

- **SEC-1** — reward endpoints remain unauthenticated (task #26). Revisit with ODIS phone verification before the reward pools grow.
- Submission screenshots (≥3, ≤500 KB each) not yet captured.
- The on-device checklist in `MINIPAY-COMPLIANCE-CHECKLIST.md`, including proving the corrected deeplink actually opens the Add Cash screen.

author: bogdaniel
body:
Refs #88

> **Stacked on #268** (→ #267 → #224 → #191 → #143). Merge order: #143 → #191 → #224 → #267 → #268 → this PR. Only the last commit belongs to this PR.

## Verified root cause

`docs/product-contract.md` §3 states: *"No cross-workflow artifact discovery. The release gate consumes summaries produced in the same run; cross-run handoff is deliberately not automated."* `.github/workflows/ci-release-gate.yml` says the same in its header, and `actions/download-artifact` retrieves artifacts from the **current run** only.

That default is correct — but it means an organisation whose scanner workflow is separate from a **protected** release/deploy workflow cannot use the gate at all: the standalone gate finds no summary and fails closed. Every such adopter had to build artifact discovery, and its trust rules, themselves. This PR closes the product gap **without** relaxing the default.

**"Download the latest successful artifact" is not a trust rule.** That run can be a fork pull request, a different branch, a different commit, a re-run of an older commit, a cancelled run, or a workflow nobody meant to trust — and the artifact contents can be substituted.

## Implementation

**`scripts/verify-evidence-handoff.sh`** (new) consumes explicit producer metadata and rejects everything else. 14 mandatory rules, printable from the implementation via `verify-evidence-handoff.sh explain`:

repository · fork head · workflow allowlist · run id · status · conclusion · event allowlist · trusted ref · **exact commit** · freshness · **ambiguity** · artifact identity · **checksum manifest** · the summary's own `source.commit`/`source.branch`/`source.workflow`.

Two design points worth review:

* **Ambiguity is a rejection.** If more than one supplied producer run satisfies every rule, the verifier refuses and tells the caller to name one with `--expected-run-id`. It never picks "latest".
* **Per-run mismatches are diagnostic while a candidate is still standing.** When several runs are supplied (a rerun, a superseded run, a decoy), a mismatch on a non-selected run is reported as a note; it becomes a rejection only when **no** run survives. That keeps the verdict honest without making a legitimate multi-candidate query impossible.

**`scripts/build-evidence-manifest.sh`** (new) is the producer half: it records repository, run id, commit, artifact name and a SHA-256 for every evidence file, deterministically (sorted). Without it the handoff is rejected — an artifact *name* proves nothing, because names are not unique across runs and contents are not bound to a commit.

**`templates/workflows/sentinel-shield-evidence-handoff.yml`** (new) ships **disabled** (`workflow_run` commented out). It runs in default-branch context, never checks out or executes the producer's head code, requests `contents: read` + `actions: read` and no write scope, **verifies before it enforces**, and does not fall back to the example summary.

## Affected contracts and files

| Contract | Files |
| --- | --- |
| **New**: handoff verifier (0 verified / 1 rejected / 2 invocation / 3 tool) | `scripts/verify-evidence-handoff.sh` |
| **New**: producer evidence manifest | `scripts/build-evidence-manifest.sh` |
| **New**: opt-in consumer template (ships disabled) | `templates/workflows/sentinel-shield-evidence-handoff.yml` |
| Product contract wording | `docs/product-contract.md` |
| **New** runbook + docs hub entry | `docs/cross-workflow-evidence-handoff.md`, `docs/index.md`, `docs/workflow-template-inventory.md` |
| Tests | **new** `tests/prod/287-cross-workflow-handoff.sh` |

Nothing existing changed behaviour: no gate, exit code, schema, environment variable or shipped default was modified. This is purely additive and opt-in.

## Why this stays fail-closed

* Every trust input is **mandatory** — no `--expected-repository`, `--expected-workflow` or `--expected-ref` means exit 2. There is no "any workflow" or "any ref" mode.
* A missing manifest, an empty manifest, a digest mismatch, a listed-but-absent file, or **any file the manifest does not cover** is a rejection.
* Unparseable run timestamps are rejected (freshness must be *provable*, not assumed).
* The consumer template does **not** wire `select-security-summary.sh`, so the example-summary fallback cannot be reached on this path.
* Missing or unverifiable evidence remains fail-closed: verification runs before enforcement, and a failed verification fails the job.
* The verifier is read-only — asserted by a test that the artifact directory is byte-identical afterwards.

## Compatibility and migration

* Additive and opt-in: the template ships with its trigger commented out, and no existing workflow, script or contract changed.
* Same-run `needs:` remains the documented default; a test asserts the managed workflow still uses it.
* Migration for split pipelines is a documented five-step path (add the manifest step → install the template → dispatch once against a known-good run → read the verification record → only then make it a required check).
* Retention, replay, duplicate producers, reruns and superseded runs each have an explicit documented policy, tabulated in the runbook.

## Validation executed

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `make validate` | **PASS** |
| `sh scripts/self-test.sh syntax` | **PASS** |
| `sh scripts/self-test.sh workflow-sanity` | **PASS** |
| `sh tests/prod/287-cross-workflow-handoff.sh` | **PASS** (all checks) |
| `sh tests/prod/110-workflows.sh`, `111-workflow-timeouts.sh`, `220-workflow-runtime-audit.sh` | **PASS** |
| `sh tests/prod/268-documentation-accuracy.sh` | **PASS** (pin-count literal updated for the new template's pinned actions) |
| `sh tests/prod/271-doc-reference-integrity.sh` | **PASS** |

**Test coverage added** — one happy path as the control, then each trust dimension broken **individually**: wrong repository; **fork head**; `pull_request` and `pull_request_target` events; non-allowlisted workflow; untrusted branch; wrong commit; failed / cancelled / skipped / unfinished runs; wrong run id; stale, future and unparseable timestamps; unreadable run metadata; **two equally valid producers rejected as ambiguous** and resolved by naming one; **naming a run that did not produce the artifact rejected** (manifest/run cross-binding); substituted artifact content; an uncovered extra file; a manifest-listed file that is absent; manifests from another run / commit / repository; **path traversal** in a manifest entry; an empty manifest; a non-allowlisted artifact name; summaries bound to the wrong commit / branch / workflow; missing summary; every invocation-contract error; read-only and idempotency checks; and template assertions (ships disabled, no `pull_request_target` trigger, no write scope, verification ordered before enforcement, no example-summary fallback, every action SHA-pinned).

## Skipped tests / environmental limitations

* **No live GitHub Actions run was executed.** The verifier is exercised against recorded `gh api repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}` response shapes, and the template is validated statically (YAML sanity, permissions, pinning, step ordering). This PR does **not** claim a live cross-workflow adoption run; the template is marked `template-only` in the inventory accordingly.
* The `workflow_run` trigger cannot be exercised from a fork or a branch by design, so its behaviour is asserted through the verifier's rules rather than a live event.
* `sh scripts/self-test.sh e2e` remains red in this environment for the pre-existing Docker-daemon reason documented in #267 (identical on `origin/master`).

## Security considerations

* The whole point of the change is to make an unsafe pattern **unnecessary**: adopters no longer need to hand-roll artifact discovery, and the supported path refuses fork evidence, wrong-commit evidence and substituted artifacts.
* The privileged consumer never checks out or executes producer head code, and holds **no write scope** — `contents: read` + `actions: rea

body:
## What

The palette grows **25 → 43 components**, covering the Salesforce / Tableau / Power BI / Grafana catalogs (per the vendor synthesis in `docs/leap-dashboard-rehaul.md`).

**Goal & Progress family:**
- **Speedometer Gauge** — the classic gas gauge: needle + anchor over colored segment bands (sky below the low breakpoint, amber between, emerald at/above the high one — no red, per the design system). Breakpoints come from the widget's conditional-color settings and default to thirds of the scale; tick marks and axis labels included.
- **Bullet / Linear Gauge** — qualitative bands + measure bar + target tick (Tableau bullet / Salesforce flat gauge), DOM-rendered for crispness.
- **Progress Ring** — percent-to-goal donut with the % in the hole.
- **Rating** — the aggregate as partially-filled stars out of a configurable max.

**Charts:** **Combo** (bars + line, two measures merged by label, opt-in second axis), **Pareto** (ranked bars + cumulative-% line), **Rose** (Nightingale), **Radar** (series polygons over group axes), **Sunburst** (group → series two-ring hierarchy), **Sankey Flow** (group → series volumes), **Calendar Heatmap** (daily density on a real calendar), **Box Plot** (min/Q1/median/Q3/max per category, client-side quartiles).

**Tables:** **Matrix / Pivot** — rows × columns × measure with row/column/grand totals and value-shaded cells (highlight-table behavior, toggleable), cell click drills.

**Metrics:** **Multi-Row Card** — one compact stat block per group value.

**Filters & Navigation (new category):**
- **Picklist / Toggle / Date Range filter widgets** — placed on the canvas like any component; changing one immediately re-filters every widget on the dashboard (Power BI slicer behavior). Options load from the data via the existing `dashboard_filter_distinct_values` RPC; values ride the same extraFilters + override-fields path as the header filter bar, so a widget filter also overrides a report's own saved filter on that column. State lives in `DashboardRunner`; the builder renders them inert.
- **Link** — a navigation card to a record page, module, report, or external URL.

**Plumbing:** `runWidgetData` gains `combo` and `filter` shapes; the ECharts core registers sankey/boxplot/radar/sunburst charts + calendar/radar components (still one isolated lazy `vendor-echarts` chunk).

**Deliberately not built, with reasons (documented in the rehaul doc):** geo map (needs a bundled US-states GeoJSON + `registerMap` — queued), state timeline (LEAP doesn't store per-record status interval history yet), packed bubbles (no native ECharts type), decomposition tree / smart narrative / Q&A (AI-class → the LEAP AI assistant workstream).

HA-00113 updated to the 43-type list. No DDL in this PR (round-1 RPCs cover every new widget).

## Verification

- `npm run build:safe` passes (preflight + Vite + runtime smoke); registry has 43 unique entries.
- Rebased onto latest master (#225/#231) before push.

author: copilot
body:
Autoscaled worker exits dropped the local runner record without removing the runner's JIT registration, so GitHub could hold registrations for containers that no longer exist (Genesis capture: 2 live workers, 8 registered runners against a target maximum of 4), and a replacement could be admitted immediately for the same lost capacity.

Exit cleanup now removes the exact persisted runner ID, and any failure becomes a durable retry obligation instead of an untracked ghost. Manager contract 10 wire behavior is unchanged; nothing is added to `observed-state.json`.

### Durable cleanup-pending record (`manager/autoscaler/registration_cleanup.go`, new)
- Per-target document at `<stateDirectory>/registration-cleanup/<target>-<hash>.json`, written with the existing atomic writer and deleted once the backlog empties.
- Carries only what cleanup needs — target key, slot key, runner ID/name, container identity fence, attempt counters, retry schedule. No JIT config, credentials, or job output.
- Bounded at 64 records; load rejects malformed documents, foreign target keys, duplicate slots, incomplete identities, and out-of-range schema/contract versions.

### Exit and retry lifecycle (`manager/autoscaler/scaler.go`)
- `handleContainerExit` write-ahead persists the identity, then removes that exact runner ID before the local record is gone. `RunnerNotFound` is already-clean; exit code and container absence are never treated as proof.
- Failures (including `JobStillRunning`) keep the record pending with a 15s retry schedule, report through `onError` so status stays degraded, and are retried on every reconciliation.
- Records are reloaded at scaler construction, so a manager restart resumes cleanup without losing or duplicating work.
- Scale-down, stale-fence, retirement, and shutdown paths are untouched: exits skip removal when `registrationRemoved` is set or the scaler is shutting down, and the operation gate keeps duplicate exit callbacks to one removal.
- A live-identity fence drops (never removes) a pending record whose runner ID or container ID is still held by a live worker.

### Replacement admission
Unresolved cleanups hold the capacity they lost, so a permanently failing removal cannot loop into new runners:

```go
if target > current {
	missing := target - current
	if blocked := s.pendingRegistrationCount(); blocked > 0 {
		if blocked > missing {
			blocked = missing
		}
		missing -= blocked
		s.logger.Warn("Deferring replacement capacity until registration cleanup completes", ...)
	}
	for ; missing > 0; missing-- {
		s.startRunner(ctx)
	}
}
```

### Tests
Exit ordering (durable record precedes removal), `RunnerNotFound`, `JobStillRunning`, generic API failure with blocked-then-restored replacement, duplicate exit callbacks, scale-down exits not repeating removal, busy-runner safety, restart recovery asserting the persisted record carries no JIT payload, plus store round-trip and document validation.

Reviewer note: the scaler now takes a `*slog.Logger` for bounded pending/success/failure logging, which changed `newRunnerScaler`'s signature and its two call sites.

- Fixes #32

author: adamblum
body:
Closes #302. PHR-S FM R2 **TI.1.1 (Entity Authentication)** hardening for local (email/password) accounts — the next WS0 conformance increment.

## Changes
- **#03 Lockout** — `EmailBackend` counts consecutive failed logins and locks the account (`AUTH_LOCKOUT_THRESHOLD`, default 5 / `AUTH_LOCKOUT_SECONDS`, default 900s). Locked accounts are refused regardless of password, with no lockout disclosure (preserves #10 limited feedback). Counters reset on success.
- **#04 / #05 No-reuse** — new `PasswordHistory` model + `password_reuse_error()` reject the current password and any used within the last `PASSWORD_HISTORY_SIZE` (default 5) **or** `PASSWORD_REUSE_DAYS` (default 180).
- **#09 Force-change** — `Identity.must_change_password` (exposed **read-only** via `/api/v1/user/`), cleared by the new **`POST /api/v1/auth/change-password/`** (verifies current password, runs validators + no-reuse, keeps the session valid via `update_session_auth_hash`).
- **#08 Admin reset** — `IdentityAdmin` action **emails a single-use reset link** (Django signed token tied to the password hash → invalidated on use/expiry; **no password is emailed**) via the configured **Mailgun/anymail** backend. Completed by public **`POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password/`** + a public **`/reset-password`** SPA page.

Shared helpers live in `services.py` (`record_password`, `password_reuse_error`, `set_new_password`); signup/invite now record initial passwords into history. All thresholds are env-configurable per org policy. Migration `0010` is additive.

## Tests
- Backend `AuthControlsTest` (10): lockout after threshold, refused-while-locked, reset-on-success, lockout expiry; reuse-of-current/recent rejected, unique accepted; change-password guards (wrong current, validators, auth required); force-change flag set/cleared.
- Backend `PasswordResetFlowTest` (5): admin email sends a reset link; valid link resets; **single-use**; invalid token rejected; validators enforced.
- Frontend `ResetPassword.test.tsx` (4) + `App.test.tsx` route mock.
- **Full suites: 941 backend / 116 frontend; `tsc` clean.**

## Notes
- **Email delivery is unchanged** — still Mailgun/anymail (`MAILGUN_API_KEY` / `MAILGUN_SENDER_DOMAIN`). The edited `EmailBackend` is the **authentication** backend, not the email-sending one.
- Global request-blocking on `must_change_password` (hard-stop all writes until changed) is intentionally **not** included — the flag is surfaced + a change-password flow provided; hard-blocking is a larger, riskier change left for follow-up.

body:
Пакет опубликован — [`@trdlabs/engine@0.1.1`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@trdlabs/engine), с провенансом, — поэтому обходной путь Ф3 больше не нужен.

## Что убрано

Submodule `vendor/engine` и вся его обвязка: из `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `Dockerfile` (COPY манифеста до install + сборка dist), четырёх воркфлоу (`submodules: true`) и скриптов `pretypecheck`/`pretest`. Зависимость — **точный пин `"0.1.1"` без каретки**, как требует карточка для engine v0.

## Голдены не сдвинулись

`ENGINE_VERSION` остался `0.0.0`: это версия **семантики** исполнения, отвязанная от версии пакета (решение владельца 2026-07-26). Пруф извлечения перепроверен против npm-версии — откат добавленных Ф3 ключей формы по-прежнему воспроизводит `7149703e` / `4c7a2303` / `e49fd70e` побайтово.

## Исправлено утверждение, ставшее ловушкой

В Ф3-тесте стояла сверка `ENGINE_VERSION` с версией `package.json` ядра. Она была верна ровно пока два числа случайно совпадали, и сработала бы на первом же релизе: выпуск, ничего не меняющий в исполнении, «доказывал» бы смену идентичности прогона — при том что вся суть развязки в обратном.

Теперь тест пинует то, что обязано держаться: голдены доказаны под **этой** генерацией семантики, записанной в пруф-карте. Сменится она — падение здесь, а не молчаливое расхождение.

Пруф-карта сохраняет коммит, против которого эквивалентность была доказана (`provenOnEngineCommit`), и отдельно фиксирует, чем пакет потребляется сегодня — переезд с пина на релиз не отменяет доказательство и не переписывает его задним числом.

## Прогон

Полный набор локально: **250 файлов, 1405 тестов, 0 падений** (Docker-sandbox-тесты исполнялись, не скипались).

author: jbernavaprah
body:
Deletes the API-coherence machinery end to end. The exact framework train plus the train-selected `phoxal::api` facade is the API compatibility boundary; nothing needs a second, generated description of it.

Tracked by organization#957.

## What goes

- The `Coherence gate` workflow and its `coherence-check` job, plus the live ruleset requirement for that status.
- `cargo xtask coherence-check`, `xtask/src/coherence.rs`, and the coherence-only object-file metadata extraction.
- `phoxal::check::check_coherence`, `ParticipantContractSurface`, `CoherenceReport`, `CoherenceMismatch`.
- The embedded per-participant contract inventories: `ParticipantApi::CONTRACTS`, `ParticipantLifecycle::SERVER_CONTRACTS`, `ApiContractUse`, `ContractRole`. Every consumer was inside a `#[cfg(test)]` module. The `Declares*` marker impls that provide the real compile-time handle gating are untouched.
- `#[phoxal(external)]` and the `attributes(phoxal)` helper, so a stale field attribute now fails to compile.
- `check_plan`, which discarded its input and always succeeded, and `check_graph`, which did the same.

Embedded participant metadata becomes `{id, config_schema}` with `deny_unknown_fields`, so a binary from an older train is a hard parse error rather than something silently half-understood. The `id` is the participant's own declared identity, which phoxal-cli now checks against the identity that selected the binary before trusting its config schema.

## The world clock is no longer enforced by a doc comment

`TimelineAuthority` claimed only a simulator could mint world steps. Nothing enforced it: any participant could declare a `StatePublisher<simulation::Clock>` and build it through the ordinary builder.

`simulation::Clock` now uses a `world_clock` topic role that generates a disjoint `WorldClockContract`, so the ordinary `state_publisher` bound cannot name it. `timeline_authority()` and `world_clock_publisher()` live on a `SetupContextSimulatorExt` gated on `IsSimulator`, which is sealed behind a supertrait the role macros emit. Both types are off `phoxal::bus` and `phoxal::prelude`, reachable only through the explicit `phoxal::raw` opt-in.

This closes the accidental route, and the docs say exactly that rather than claiming a seal. The sealing path is `#[doc(hidden)]` rather than private, because the macro expands in downstream crates and Rust has no visibility level between "this crate" and "the world". Deliberately naming that path, or reaching through `phoxal::raw`, remains possible. Cross-process uniqueness stays a selection-time property phoxal-cli enforces. A trybuild case covers all three routes.

## Also

- Participant IDs are restricted to `[a-z0-9_-]+`, whether written explicitly or derived from the type name. They were spliced unescaped into the metadata JSON and used as Zenoh key segments, so an id containing a quote produced an unreadable section.
- The ELF metadata section is renamed `.phoxal_api_meta` to `.phoxal_meta`; it carries no API metadata anymore.
- `API_CONTRACT_MANIFEST` is `cfg(test)`-gated rather than deleted. It backs a real curation guard - every command topic must carry a delivery classification - that cannot be written without enumerating the tree, and the shipped rlib now carries no contract inventory at all.
- `xtask` becomes `workspace-policy`. The name promised a command runner whose last verb was the coherence gate. The `.cargo` alias pointing at a package with no binary is deleted.

## Verification

`fmt`, `clippy -D warnings` and 486 workspace tests pass, and were reproduced independently by the reviewing agent. Three rounds of independent review; every finding resolved or answered.

body: ## Summary Sets up a reproducible development environment for `gus` (a Go user-auth/account library) so lint, tests, and a consumer flow all run cleanly. The repo previously had **no `go.mod`**, so it could not build in module mode, and modern dependency resolution breaks the test suite. author: davidbudnick
body:
## Summary

Makes `FuzzySearchKeys` and `SearchByValue` scale better on large keyspaces by avoiding full-keyspace materialization and unbounded value fetches.

### FuzzySearchKeys
- Keeps a **bounded min-heap of size `maxKeys`** while scanning so memory is O(maxKeys), not O(matches)
- Still scans the full keyspace for correct global top-N ranking
- After scan, sorts the final top-N by score descending and pipelines Type/TTL as before
- `maxKeys <= 0` falls back to a default of 100

### SearchByValue
- **Streams** via `scanEach` instead of `scanAll` (no full key list in memory)
- **Early-stops** once `len(matches) >= maxKeys`
- Bounds value fetches used only for substring matching:
  - strings: `GETRANGE` first 64KB (`searchMaxStringBytes`)
  - lists: `LRANGE 0..searchMaxItems-1` (100)
  - hashes/sets: single `HSCAN`/`SSCAN` with COUNT 100
  - ReJSON: still full `JSON.GET` (no bounded Redis API)
- Final TTL pipeline runs only for matched keys
- `maxKeys <= 0` / empty pattern defaults applied

### Trade-off (intentional)
Value search only inspects a **prefix window** of each value. Matches that exist only outside that window (deep in a large string/list/hash/set) may be missed. Acceptable for interactive TUI search; full materialization was the previous cost.

## Test plan
- [x] `go test -race ./internal/redis/...`
- [x] Fuzzy top-N on large synthetic keyspace (500+ noise keys)
- [x] SearchByValue early-stops at maxKeys
- [x] Large string GETRANGE prefix match when needle is near start
- [x] Bounded list/hash/set match paths
- [x] Empty DB / missing pattern / nil cmd branches do not panic
- [x] ReJSON match + JSON.GET error path
- [x] 100% statement coverage on changed functions

## Out of scope
- GetValue detail path (owned by parallel work)
- UI debounce (owned by parallel work)

author: karlkfi
body:
## What

`scripts/dogfood/stop.sh` now waits for in-flight worker pods to drain before it
scales the system pool to 0, and fails the stop rather than scaling down if the
drain doesn't finish.

## Why

The system pool carries the tenant AGCs, and **an AGC is the only thing that
reaps its worker pods.** `stop.sh` resized that pool to 0 unconditionally, so a
stop issued mid-flight evicted the AGC with nowhere to reschedule:

- its worker pods kept running on the `workers` pool, with no controller left to
  delete them;
- those pods carry `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"`
  deliberately (a worker mid-job has no replacement), so the autoscaler wouldn't
  reclaim their nodes either;
- the nodes billed until a human noticed. One incident stranded 82 spot
  node-hours.

Resetting `GAG_RUNNER` first stops *new* dispatches routing at the cluster, but
already-queued dispatches are still assigned to the scale set — which is why an
explicit wait is needed rather than a glance.

## How

- `stop.sh`: reset `GAG_RUNNER` → verify the kubectl context → **drain** →
  resize. Knobs: `DRAIN_TIMEOUT` (default 1500s, the longest dispatched job's
  `timeout-minutes: 20` plus reap time), `DRAIN_INTERVAL` (15s), `SKIP_DRAIN=1`.
- On timeout the script exits 1 **and leaves the pool up** — the cheaper failure,
  and the one that keeps the AGC alive to finish reaping. The error names the
  pods still in flight, the node each pins, and the four ways out (wait and
  re-run, bounce a wedged AGC, delete genuine orphans, or `SKIP_DRAIN=1`).
- New `scripts/dogfood/lib/workers.sh` holds the occupancy probes so the teardown
  scripts read worker state one way. It selects on the `app.kubernetes.io/*`
  labels the AGC stamps on **both** tiers (not the `runner-` name prefix
  `delete.sh` was matching), counts **non-terminal** phases rather than `Running`
  only (a `Pending` worker means the job is already acquired), and reports an
  unreadable cluster as `unknown` rather than `0` — an unreachable cluster must
  never read as an idle one.
- `delete.sh` now uses the same probe; its confirmation reads "Worker pods in
  flight" accordingly. It deliberately does *not* wait — deleting the cluster
  takes the worker nodes with it, so there's nothing left to strand.
- `validate-release.sh`'s teardown comment records why its guarded `stop.sh` call
  may now leave the system pool up.

## Testing

- New `scripts/dogfood/workers-test.sh`, wired into `make scripts-test` (and so
  `make check` + the CI shellcheck job). kubectl and `sleep` are stubbed, so no
  network, no cluster, no wall-clock wait. Covers the unknown-not-zero property,
  `Pending` counting as in-flight, the settle window, a mid-drain read failure
  resetting that window, timeout on a cluster that never drains, and the exact
  label + field selector.
- Mutation-checked: flipping the field selector to `status.phase=Running` and the
  settle window to 1 both fail the suite.
- Smoke-tested end to end against stubbed `gcloud`/`gh`/`kubectl` — idle cluster
  scales down, busy cluster refuses with the guidance and exits 1, and
  `SKIP_DRAIN=1` scales down anyway.
- `make check` green.

Docs: `docs/plan/gke-dogfood.md` Part D's "Stop dogfooding" recipe (which carried
the same hand-typed footgun) now points at the script and explains the ordering,
the knobs, and the failure mode; Part E's teardown table gains an in-flight-jobs
row.

## Summary

- add authenticated, post-setup Schemathesis response validation against the published OpenAPI contract using only the disposable integration stack
- make the contract-response job advisory while failing the harness if route coverage is incomplete or more than 20% of responses are `401`/`423`

The authenticated sweep exercises all 282 selected operations. It currently reports 274 passing operations and eight pre-existing violations:

1. two setup problem codes missing from the `Problem.code` enum
2. an empty record-upload SHA reaching S3 as an invalid empty key

The CI job is intentionally advisory until those mismatches are resolved; incomplete operation coverage or an auth/setup regression still fails the harness itself.

author: asasher
body:
Closes #109

Work-type: `enhancement`

## Summary

Installing these skills is two jobs, and only the first is a command. `install` mounts the skills; the
setups are what bind them to the repository they landed in — they read the repo, write and reconcile the
playbooks under `docs/agents/`, and sometimes have to ask. A checklist a human sequences after the CLI
returns is exactly the step that gets skipped, and a skipped `staffing setup` leaves a project with no
roster at all.

So the README's install section leads with one copy-pasteable prompt. It runs the install, reads the
setup requirements the install reports and runs them in the reported order, reviews the resulting diff,
and commits. It names no harness-specific tool, command, or path, and needs nothing from this repo
installed first — it carries the `npx` invocation itself. The CLI moves beneath it under **Driving the
installer yourself**, retained whole: the three commands, the mount/variant/prune behaviour, the
`setup_report` paragraph from #117, the state file and `check`, the from-a-checkout form, and the
`npx skills add` warning.

Scope discovery, and the reason this is longer than "move a prompt to the top": three ways the prompt
could send an agent somewhere the CLI would not, all found by review and all confirmed against the code
before fixing. They are described under **Changes**.

## Changes

**`README.md`** — the `## Install` section only; nothing else in the repo is touched.

- The prompt is one fenced block, shown once rather than per scenario, with the branch a consuming repo
  actually faces folded into step 1. Two prompts would have duplicated five steps to vary one line.
- It is written in the operator's voice ("the skills I want", "ask me"), so the agent has a principal to
  return to when a setup needs a decision. Setups reconcile repo-owned playbooks and sometimes ask; a
  prompt that let an agent guess there would defeat the point of handing it to an agent at all.
- **`setup_order` is necessary but not sufficient, so the prompt sweeps past it.** The report lists
  skills declaring `metadata.setup`. Resolving the prompt's own default set gives a 17-skill closure in
  which exactly two — `diagnosing-bugs` and `staffing` — declare one. `backlog` *describes* a setup in
  its `SKILL.md` and declares none, so the setup that writes `platform.md`, `backlog-policy.md`,
  `environment.md`, `codebase.md`, `evidence.md` and `change-description.md` never reaches the report: a
  fresh consuming repo would arrive at `backlog groom` with no playbooks, which is the silent
  missing-setup failure this ticket exists to close. Step 3 runs the reported setups in the reported
  order; step 4 then skims the remaining `installed` entries for a setup the report could not name.
- **No mount path is named**, because for a skill with `metadata.variants` the two mounts hold materially
  different files — `.agents/skills/staffing/` is the Codex-compiled tree, and a Claude session following
  a hard-coded path would run `staffing setup` out of Codex mechanics and seed the wrong roster. The
  prompt asks for the copy belonging to the harness in use, which is also what keeps AC-3 honest.
- **Step 1 stops on a pre-#106 consumer.** `_recorded` migrates from `skills-lock.json`, so `previously`
  is populated from it and `removed = previously - closure` prunes whatever a `--skill` set leaves out.
  A repo with a `skills-lock.json` and no `install.json` gets a question, not a guess.
- Concreteness elsewhere came from the cold-reader probes below, each addition closing something a reader
  had to invent: `install.json` as the marker for an existing install, and `docs/agents/` as where
  playbooks live.
- Step 5 asks for the diff to be judged, not just displayed — a playbook naming a command or branch the
  repository does not use is the characteristic failure of an unattended setup, and it is invisible
  unless someone looks.
- The CLI section keeps the refresh-versus-name-the-set distinction in both places it was already made:
  the inline comments on the two commands, and the sentence that a bare `install` never silently widens a
  curated selection.

## Plan

None — #109 routed **direct** (its dispatch block: strategic decisions settled by #107's spec, revision
1; the prompt-over-checklist call was already made, with wording, length and CLI retention delegated).
There is no committed plan document to pin.

## Checks run

Per `docs/agents/codebase.md` § Checks. This change touches no skill source and no script, so no probe
eval applies; the prose checks are the cold-reader probes recorded under **Verification**.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH python3 site/check.py` | exit 0 — 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| `PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH python3 tools/test_catalog.py` | exit 0 — 22 tests |
| `PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH python3 tools/test_install.py` | exit 0 |

## CI status

This repo has **no CI** — readiness is the checks above, the cold-reader verdicts, and review `LGTM`, not
a status check.

## Verification

The proof that catches this failing is a cold reader's: an agent given **only** the fenced prompt, with
no knowledge of this repo, asked what sequence it would run and what it would have to invent. Four
rounds through gpt-5.6-sol (`codex exec -s read-only`) — the fourth against the shipped text, after the
last review fix — plus an independent fresh-eyes pass on the diff and three adversarial reviewer passes
that checked every factual claim against the installer and catalog.

| Criterion | Outcome |
|---|---|
| AC-1 — leads with one self-contained prompt, nothing pre-installed | Pass. The section opens with the block; the reader's first command is the `npx` line, needing only node and network. |
| AC-2 — install → reported setups in reported order → review diff → commit | Pass. The cold reader produced exactly that sequence, resolving `setup_report.setup_order` and stopping to ask before undefined setup decisions. The ordered run is the primary path; the step-4 sweep is additive, and exists because the report structurally cannot name an undeclared setup. |
| AC-3 — harness-neutral, no harness-specific tool or command | Pass. The prompt names no harness, tool, slash command, or mount path; `.claude/skills` appears only in the CLI section below it, as an installer-created path. |
| AC-4 — CLI documented beneath, refresh vs. change-the-set intact | Pass. Retained in full under **Driving the installer yourself**, distinction stated twice. |
| AC-5 — no manual post-install setup checklist as the primary path | Pass. No checklist anywhere; the prompt is the lead. |

Caveats and named gaps, disclosed rather than claimed away:

- **Not demonstrated end to end.** The prompt was verified by cold reading and by checking each claim
  against `tools/install.py` and `tools/catalog.py` — not by pasting it into a fresh agent in a real
  consuming repo and watching an install plus setups land. That demo is the honest remaining gap, and it
  is what #109's "demoable end to end" line asks for.
- **`backlog` describing a setup it does not declare is a repo defect this prose works around.** Step 4
  exists to cover it. The clean fix is to move `backlog`'s `## setup` into `reference/setup.md` and
  declare `metadata.setup`, which is a skill-source change with a catalog regeneration and a probe eval
  behind it — out of scope for a README ticket, and unfiled: tracker writes beyond this PR are not this
  session's to make.
- **The empty-`setup_order` case is unreachable on the npx path.** The packed package ships no `.git`, so
  `basis` degrades to `unknown-revision` and every setup-declaring skill is listed. Setups reconcile
  rather than overwrite, so re-running is safe.
- Residual ambiguities the cold reader still names — which files count as playbooks in an unfamiliar
  repo, what counts as a decision worth asking about — are resolved by reading the repo and the setup,
  which is what the prompt tells it to do. They are
