body:
## Summary
Teachers previously had no way to remove a student from their section — only a bare admin-only `DELETE /sections/:id/students/:student_id` endpoint existed, with zero frontend button anywhere. This adds a request/approval workflow mirroring the existing `ClassRequest` (teacher requests → admin approves) and `EnrollmentRequest` (student requests → teacher approves) patterns already in the codebase.

- **New `unenroll_requests` table** + `UnenrollRequest` model/schemas, following the `ClassRequest`/`EnrollmentRequest` conventions.
- **New endpoints**: create (teacher, section owner only), list (per-section for the teacher's roster UI, global for the admin inbox), approve/reject (admin), cancel (teacher, own pending request only). The archive step on approval reuses an `archive_enrollment()` helper extracted from the pre-existing direct admin-drop endpoint, so both paths archive identically.
- **Four new notification types**: admin gets notified on submission; the teacher gets notified of the outcome either way (approved/rejected); the student is only notified if actually removed (approval) — not while pending, and not on rejection, since nothing changes for them in that case.
- **No data cascade** — approval only flips `Enrollment.is_archived`/`deleted_at`, matching the existing admin-drop endpoint's behavior today. Submissions/points/grades for that section are untouched.
- **Frontend**: `RosterPanel.jsx` gets a "Request unenroll" button per row (with a required-reason inline form) that becomes "Cancel request" once pending; `AdminInbox.jsx` gets a new "Unenroll requests" category following the exact class-request branch template; `NotificationBell.jsx` gets route resolvers + Go-button support for all four new types.

Built on top of #56 (the `notify()` helper this depends on) — should merge after it, or this diff will show #56's commits too.

## Test plan
- [x] Full backend flow verified via curl against the running dev DB: create → admin notified → approve → student notified + roster updated + teacher notified; reject → only teacher notified; duplicate-pending-request guard (409); teacher cancel
- [x] Ran both new alembic migrations (table creation + 4 enum values) against the dev DB
- [x] Full UI flow verified in-browser: teacher requests removal from the roster with a reason, sees "Cancel request" afterward; admin sees it in the new "Unenroll requests" tab with reason/teacher/date, approves via the existing confirm-dialog pattern; roster updates live; notification bell "Go" button verified for admin, teacher (approved + rejected), and student (removed) — all navigate correctly
- [x] Manual review recommended on the `archive_enrollment()` extraction and the notification-routing choices, since this touches an existing endpoint's internals

author: segmentree
body:
An arcade football game styled after pixel-art soccer games like Pixel Cup Soccer.

## What's here

A playable 8-a-side match — goals, goal kicks, corners, throw-ins, two halves — with charge-and-release shooting, context passing, lofted balls, sprint/stamina, slide tackles and player switching.

## How the look works

The whole scene renders into a small buffer (~480x270) that CSS upscales with `image-rendering: pixelated`, so geometry, sprites and HUD all land on one pixel grid. Nothing is lit: every material is a flat `MeshBasicMaterial`, with shading painted into the textures.

**No image assets ship with the game.** Every texture is drawn pixel by pixel onto a 2D canvas at authoring size and uploaded with `NearestFilter`:

- `src/sprites.js` — player atlas (6 frames x 8 facings, generated per kit and per player so skin, hair and shirt number vary), ball, blob shadows, crowd, netting
- `src/field.js` — pitch texture with mown bands and every marking baked into one canvas, plus goals and terraces
- `src/font.js` — a hand-drawn 5x7 pixel font, authored on the grid so it stays legible at 1x

## Camera

A TV broadcast camera: straight across the pitch from the main stand, goals left and right, mown bands running vertically. The elevation is steep enough to read everyone's position without looking at the tops of heads. It fills the entire viewport at any aspect ratio — the pixel size is locked to a whole number of screen pixels and the internal buffer is sized to the window's aspect, so there are no bars and no uneven pixels.

## Some details worth calling out

- **Shooting** follows the direction you are running. Aim assist only engages when the player is already pointed within ~35 degrees of goal, and never pulls the shot more than 60% of the way over.
- **Player switching** picks whoever can actually reach the ball. While someone is dribbling that is simply the nearest player; once the ball has been struck, the real ball physics are run forward to find where it will come to rest and the pick is made against that. The predictor and the live ball share one `integrateBall()` so they cannot disagree.
- **Manual mode** (`I`) turns the AI off entirely so you can drive players by hand; the camera follows your player rather than the ball, since the ball is usually stationary then.

## Verification

- Production build passes; no console errors.
- Full 90-minute AI-vs-AI matches run clean end to end, with sane scorelines and restarts firing correctly.
- Ball-rest prediction checked against actually simulating five different strikes: exact match.
- Player-selection ranking brute-forced against 1288 ball positions across both teams: no wrong picks, and the keeper is never selected outside his own area.
- Layout verified at 1024x768, 1280x720, 1440x900 and 1600x900.

body:
## Summary

The library half of the 2026-07-26 mesh-gradients assessment session:

- **Delaunay gradient unlock**: `stop_gradient` on the qhull tables `pure_callback` input in `_jax_delaunay_tables`. With the visibility walk running point location, barycentric weights, dual areas and split points in-graph, the callback returns only int32 connectivity tables (piecewise-constant in the vertices), so `jax.grad` now returns the exact almost-everywhere derivative. Values bit-identical (jax_likelihood delaunay regression literal unchanged); FD-certified by the new `autolens_workspace_test/scripts/imaging/jax_grad/delaunay.py`. The autodifferentiability framing (piecewise-smooth, ReLU-network sense) is in the `Delaunay` class docstring.
- **Kernel-scheme linear algebra**: SPD `inv_via_cholesky` for `ExponentialKernel`/`GaussianKernel` (round-off-identical); `jitter` kwarg on the four kernel schemes (`None` default → historical 1e-8, byte-identical, af.Model prior counts unchanged); and — gated behind the existing `Settings.log_det_method="slogdet"` opt-in (default off) — the analytically exact `pixels·log(coeff) − log det C` evidence log-det from a single Cholesky of the kernel covariance (new `AbstractRegularization.log_det_regularization_matrix_term_from` hook; measured effect on the KNN Matérn fiducial: LL shift −1.1e-9, i.e. pure round-off, with the term now finite at any regularization coefficient).
- **xp-ports**: `ExponentialKernel` (xp threaded + NaN-safe `sqrt(d²+1e-20)` distances) and `BrightnessZeroth` (`pixel_signals_from` now threads `xp`) — both previously raised `TracerArrayConversionError` under `jax.grad`; the latter fix makes `AdaptSplitZeroth` FD-certified on the KNN meshes (8.2e-8).
- **Gradient-support docstrings** across all regularization schemes and the three mesh families, recording the regularization × mesh sweep findings where users compose models.

## Validation

- Full `test_autoarray` suite green (six new tests: kernel log-det shortcut identities, jitter byte-identity, inversion gating).
- JAX validation via the sibling-branch `autolens_workspace_test` jax_grad scripts (`pixelization.py`, new `knn.py`, `regularization.py`, `delaunay.py`) — merge that PR alongside this one; its smoke CI checks out same-named library branches.

body:
Tier 1, item 1. Closes a removal candidate that's been sitting in CLAUDE.md since Phase 5.

`AppendCompletion` opened by returning early if the last recorded step was already a completion. Phase 5 flagged it as unreachable and mutation testing confirmed no test covered it — but it was left in place rather than removed on suspicion.

## It is unreachable, and the callers prove it

- `AppendCompletion` has **exactly one caller**, `ProcessUntilDecision`, which `return`s immediately after calling it — so it cannot append twice in one pass.
- `ProcessUntilDecision` has **two callers**, and both create the step list *empty on the line before* they call (`List<WatchtowerCombatStepResult> automaticSteps = [];`).

So the list is always empty when the guard reads it, and `steps.Count > 0` can never hold. That's a proof from the call graph, not an inference from coverage.

Removed, with a comment recording why it doesn't need to be there — so the next reader doesn't add it back defensively.

- Debug build: 0 warnings
- Full suite: 1893 passed, 0 failed — both frozen combat transcripts unchanged
- Release build: clean

body:
## Why

Every GitHub merge commit is authored by `GitHub <noreply@github.com>` — set server-side, unchangeable afterwards — so any tooling that checks commit attribution flags them. Squash/rebase merges keep every commit on `main` attributed to whoever wrote it.

## Why this is not fixed retroactively

All three published release tags point at merge commits:

| Tag | Commit | |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.8.0` | `fa48614` | Merge PR #16 |
| `v0.9.0` | `3fb1e6f` | Merge PR #19 |
| `v0.10.0` | `f7b0cdd` | Merge PR #24 |

Those are the tags CI built the **published PyPI artifacts** from. Rewriting history to remove the merge commits would orphan all three released versions from `main`'s history — trading a working release lineage for a cosmetic label. Documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md` so the reasoning survives.

## Action for you

Enable **Settings → General → Pull Requests → Allow squash merging** and untick *Allow merge commits* to enforce it at the repo level. I'll use squash from here regardless — including for this PR.

author: mitetenov
body:
Разделяет CI на две последовательные джобы: `test` → `build`.

## Что меняется

Раньше тесты и Docker-сборка были шагами одной джобы `build`. Теперь:

- **`test`** — запускается на каждом событии, включая PR. Это и есть гейт для мерджа.
- **`build`** — `needs: test`, и `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'` переехал с отдельных шагов на уровень джобы. На PR она теперь пропускается целиком, а не выполняет checkout и тесты впустую.

Побочный эффект: на PR больше не поднимаются QEMU, Buildx и логин в Docker Hub.

## Версия из pom без Maven

`mvn help:evaluate` ради одной строки — 2.65 с локально. Прямой XML-парсинг даёт то же самое за 0.06 с, и сборочной джобе больше вообще не нужен JDK.

## Цена разделения

Замерил по реальным прогонам этого репозитория. Разбивка последнего полного прогона на master (262 с):

| Шаг | Время |
|---|---|
| Set up job + Checkout + JDK | 7 с |
| Run tests | 27 с |
| Extract version | 2 с |
| QEMU + Buildx + Login | 11 с |
| **Build and push** | **206 с** (79%) |

Дублируется только фиксированный оверхед: второй `Set up job` + `Checkout` (~2–3 с) и вторая аллокация раннера (~5–10 с). Кэш Maven и кэш buildx живут в хранилище GitHub, а не в джобе, поэтому разделение их не рвёт.

**Ожидаемо: +10–15 с к ~260 с, то есть 4–6%.**

Скорости это не добавляет — 79% времени лежит в multi-arch сборке под QEMU. Разделение делается ради читаемости падений, возможности перезапустить одну джобу и задела под будущие параллельные джобы.

Проверено `actionlint` — замечаний нет.

## ⚠️ Требуется действие: защита ветки

Сейчас в branch protection на `master` требуется чек **`build`**. После этого PR джоба `build` на pull request'ах **не запускается**, поэтому гейтом она быть не может — требовать нужно **`test`**.

Я не смог применить это сам: смена настроек репозитория заблокирована. Команда:

```bash
gh api -X PUT repos/mitetenov/SupportAiBot/branches/master/protection --input - <<'JSON'
{"required_status_checks":{"strict":true,"checks":[{"context":"test","app_id":15368}]},"enforce_admins":true,"required_pull_request_reviews":{"dismiss_stale_reviews":false,"require_code_owner_reviews":false,"required_approving_review_count":0,"require_last_push_approval":false},"restrictions":null,"required_linear_history":false,"allow_force_pushes":false,"allow_deletions":false,"block_creations":false,"required_conversation_resolution":false,"lock_branch":false,"allow_fork_syncing":false}
JSON
```

Меняется только список required checks: `["build"]` → `["test"]`. Все остальные настройки (strict, enforce_admins, запрет force-push и удаления, 0 обязательных аппрувов) переданы в том же виде, в каком они сейчас.

author: roosheel
body:
## What & why

The map's route polylines (156 runs) lived inline in `src/data.js` — a **2.9 MB** module imported statically, so every visitor downloaded a single **1.73 MB JS chunk (447 KB gzip)** before first paint. This was the biggest performance problem flagged in review.

## Changes

- **Route geometry → `src/routes.json`** (keyed by run id). `data.js` now holds metadata only: **2.9 MB → 71 KB**. `scripts/sync-strava.mjs` writes both files going forward, so future syncs stay split.
- **Journal fetches `routes.json` via dynamic `import()`** (its own async chunk) and reads geometry through a `routeOf()` helper. Markers, the start pin, and stats degrade gracefully until the data lands.
- **Lazy-load the Journal** (Leaflet + react-leaflet, the heaviest deps) with `React.lazy` + `Suspense`, so they're no longer in the critical bundle.

## Result

| Chunk (gzip) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Initial JS (critical path) | **447 KB** | **121 KB** |
| Leaflet + map (lazy) | — | 50 KB |
| Route geometry (lazy) | — | 268 KB |

Initial load is **73% smaller**; Leaflet and route data now load only when the Journal mounts, and `routes.json` caches independently of code.

## Verification

- `npm ci && npm run build` — clean.
- Loaded the production build in a browser: the Journal map renders all **156 route polylines**, the "route pts" stat reads correctly from the lazily-loaded data, and there are no new console errors (only a pre-existing `favicon.ico` 404).

Scoped to the #1 review finding only. The Instagram dual-source and sync-script shell-escaping items are untouched — happy to follow up on those separately.

author: adamsalisbury
body:
## What
Adds a `UnixSocketTransport`/`UnixSocketTransportListener` pair (Linux/macOS) and a `NamedPipeTransport`/`NamedPipeTransportListener` pair (Windows) implementing `ITransport`/`ITransportListener`, for fast, local, same-host inter-process communication without a loopback TCP port.

## Why
When a hub and its clients share one host — a sidecar or multi-process desktop/daemon layout — a loopback TCP socket pays for the full network stack and opens a port unnecessarily. Unix domain sockets and named pipes avoid both.

## Key Changes
- Factored the length-prefixed message framing out of `TcpTransport` into a new internal `StreamFramer` helper (`Transport/Framing/StreamFramer.cs`), so it is shared rather than duplicated — `TcpTransport` itself is refactored to delegate to it with no change to its public behaviour or exception messages.
- Added `UnixSocketTransport`/`UnixSocketTransportListener` using a raw `Socket` with `UnixDomainSocketEndPoint`, framed via `StreamFramer`. The listener deletes a stale socket file before binding and on disposal, and mirrors `TcpTransportListener`'s lock-guarded idempotent-dispose contract.
- Added `NamedPipeTransport`/`NamedPipeTransportListener` using `NamedPipeClientStream`/`NamedPipeServerStream`, also framed via `StreamFramer`. Both throw `PlatformNotSupportedException` on any operating system other than Windows.
- Added loopback, listener-lifecycle, and end-to-end (register/send/broadcast/group) test coverage for the Unix socket transport, and constructor-validation/platform-guard coverage for the named-pipe transport (its happy path can only be exercised on Windows; CI runs on Linux).
- Updated `README.md`: new namespaces, architecture table rows, a wire-protocol note on the shared framing helper, usage examples for both transports, and a security note on the filesystem-permission access-control model for local IPC.

Closes #20

author: maxugly
body:
**What:** 
Replaced `dev_alloc_skb` with `napi_alloc_skb` in the `sim_rx_dequeue` function and removed the manual `skb_reserve` call since `napi_alloc_skb` automatically handles `NET_IP_ALIGN`.

**Why:** 
The RX path operates in a NAPI polling context. `dev_alloc_skb` uses a generic slab allocator which can cause lock contention. `napi_alloc_skb` uses NAPI-specific per-CPU caches, providing faster sk_buff allocations during high-speed packet reception.

**Impact:** 
Significantly reduces CPU overhead and lock contention during network packet receiving, increasing RX throughput and reducing latency.

**Measurement:** 
Compare the `iperf3` RX bandwidth between `nata-a` and `nata-b` nodes using `scripts/nata-ns-up.sh` before and after the change, or check CPU utilization of softirqd under heavy RX load.

author: nursoda
body:
## What

Runs `tests/smoke/smoke.sh` on every pull request and every push to `main`, against **each Nextcloud version `appinfo/info.xml` declares support for**. The version list is read from `info.xml` by a preparation job, so the matrix cannot drift from what we claim. Currently that means two parallel jobs, 33 and 34, roughly five to six minutes each.

It adds a layer rather than replacing one: unit tests, psalm, cs and the lint workflows keep running as they do. What was missing so far is "does the app actually work inside a server" — that is what this covers. In CI it runs with `SLOW=1`, so unlike a quick local run it also verifies the *successful* resend after the cooldown.

## Why it is a separate pull request

It is not a documentation change, and this way its **first run happens where it belongs** — on itself.

Depends on #165, which adds `tests/smoke/`. The base is therefore that branch; GitHub retargets this pull request to `main` automatically once #165 is merged and its branch deleted. The diff here is the single workflow file.

## This workflow has never run

A workflow can only be proven by pushing it, so treat the first result here as the start of the iteration, not as a statement about the app. Most likely candidates if it comes back red: the krankerl download, PHP extensions the build needs, or the image pull timing. The file says so in its header as well, so nobody mistakes it later for something that was verified.

The package is built with **krankerl**, pinned to v0.14.0, because rebuilding its packaging rules inside the workflow would create a second source of truth about what actually ships. The cost of that choice is one third-party binary download per run; a sha256 next to it is worth adding once someone has established it.

author: paddione
body:
## Problem

Beide Flux-Bootstrap-SealedSecrets unter `flux/clusters/fleet/bootstrap/` trugen in `main` noch die Platzhalter aus der T002083-Bootstrap-PR:

```
.dockerconfigjson: AgD_dummy_encrypted_dockerconfigjson_placeholder_for_ghcr_auth
token:             AgD_dummy_encrypted_token_placeholder_for_flux_webhook
```

Live auf `fleet` scheiterte der Controller daran — der Unterstrich in `AgD_dummy` ist kein Base64-Zeichen, Byte 3 ist genau dieses `_`:

```
flux-webhook-token   illegal base64 data at input byte 3 (token)                 SYNCED=False
ghcr-auth            illegal base64 data at input byte 3 (.dockerconfigjson)     SYNCED=False
```

Zusätzlich fehlte `spec.template.metadata` (name + namespace), ohne den der Controller das Ziel-Secret nicht materialisieren kann.

Der Bug war **maskiert**: die Plain-Secrets existierten in `flux-system` und trugen bereits `ownerReferences` auf ihre SealedSecrets — sie waren also einmal aus echten Ciphertexten erzeugt worden, und die Platzhalter wurden erst später darüber appliziert. GHCR-Pull und Receiver-Webhook liefen dadurch normal. Latent war der Bootstrap aber nicht mehr aus git reproduzierbar: ein frisch aufgesetzter `fleet`-Cluster bekommt beide Secrets nicht, womit der Pull der OCI-Artefakte und der Flux-Webhook ausfallen — im Widerspruch zum pull-based-GitOps-Anspruch aus T002083.

## Fix

Beide Werte aus den bestehenden Live-Secrets neu gesealt, Plaintext nie materialisiert (`kubectl … -o yaml | kubeseal`, kein `echo`, keine Zwischendatei). Cert `environments/certs/fleet-mentolder.pem`, SHA256-Fingerprint verifiziert identisch zum Live-Controller-Key in `kube-system`. Secret-Typen erhalten (`kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` bzw. `Opaque`), `spec.template.metadata` ergänzt. Header-Kommentar dokumentiert den Regenerier-Befehl und die Cert-Bindung.

## Tests

Drei fail-closed BATS-Tests in `tests/spec/workspace-deploy.bats`:

1. **Kein `AgD_dummy`-Platzhalter** unter `flux/clusters/fleet/bootstrap/`.
2. **`spec.template.metadata.name` + `.namespace` Pflicht.** Parst mit PyYAML statt `grep`: ein SealedSecret hat *zwei* `metadata`-Blöcke (`metadata` und `spec.template.metadata`), ein flaches `grep` zählt beide und würde fälschlich "vorhanden" melden.
3. **Repo-weiter Copy-Paste-Guard.** Derselbe Ciphertext unter abweichender `(namespace, name)`-Identität ist ein Fehler, weil strict scope ihn an genau eine Identität bindet — er kann dann für höchstens eine entschlüsseln, der Rest bleibt still kaputt. Ausnahme für `namespace-wide`/`cluster-wide`-Annotationen (aktuell sind alle 25 SealedSecrets strict, die Ausnahme ist Vorsorge). Die 6 brand-übergreifenden Secrets bleiben korrekt grün, weil sie dieselbe Identität teilen.

Guard-Wirksamkeit nicht nur behauptet, sondern belegt: gegen die künstlich injizierte Fehlkonstellation verifiziert **rot** (benennt beide Fundstellen), nach dem Zurücksetzen wieder grün.

## Verifikation

| Gate | Ergebnis |
|---|---|
| `tests/spec/workspace-deploy.bats` | 71/71 grün |
| `task test:openspec` | 11/11 grün |
| `task quality:check` | 0 blocking |
| `task freshness:check` | exit 0 |
| Live `kubectl -n flux-system get sealedsecrets` | beide **`SYNCED=True`**, keine Fehlermeldung |
| Ziel-Secrets nach Apply | Typen und Keys unverändert |
| `OCIRepository fleet-manifests` | `READY=True` — `ghcr-auth` funktioniert weiter |

`task test:changed` bricht lokal an den Playwright-E2E-Tests ab (`CRON_SECRET` ist nur in CI gesetzt, T001453). Ausgelöst wird die E2E-Auswahl vom *generierten* `website/src/data/openspec-status.json`, das `^website/(src|…)/` in `Taskfile.yml:824` matcht — eine Fehlauswahl für diesen Change. E2E ist kein Required-Check (T000722).

## Nicht Teil dieser PR

Zwei Punkte aus derselben Analyse haben sich als **Nicht-Bugs** erwiesen und bleiben unangetastet: `RIGGER_HOST_IP` fehlt legitim in `environments/fleet-*.yaml` (`schema.yaml:400` ist `required: false` mit dokumentiertem Default, `flux-render-artifact.sh:63` setzt ihn), und die Sealed-Secret-Kollision der 6 geteilten Secrets ist durch getrennte Unterordner + zwei Kustomizations gelöst (beide `Ready=True`).

Die SSOT-Integration der Bootstrap-Secrets über `environments/schema.yaml` + `env:seal` läuft als **T002254** — sie braucht Secret-Typ-Support in `scripts/lib/seal-extra-namespaces.sh:87` (dort hart `type: Opaque`) und ändert den Secret-Pfad aller Envs, gehört also in eine eigenständig reviewbare PR.

Closes T002251

body:
## Summary

Top of the 3-PR stack (#1113 → #1107 → this). Small and focused: **one derived endpoint, one hook, one card, 6 tests** — the "clearest single win" named in `docs/MDX_SURFACE_COVERAGE_FINDING.md`.

Every `/api/mdx/qms` endpoint was already consumed — by `client/src/concept2cure/quality/*`, a **different application** from the MDX device shell. A device team working a 510(k) could not see whether its suppliers were qualified, whether required training was current, or which audit findings threatened readiness without leaving for another app. That gap matters more under QMSR (effective 2026-02-02), whose inspections reach management reviews and supplier/internal audit records.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Change Summary

**`GET /api/mdx/qms/readiness`** — a read-only aggregate over the five tables the existing `/qms/*` CRUD already owns (`qms_documents`, `qms_suppliers`, `qms_training_records`, `qms_internal_audits`, `qms_nonconforming_products`). No new writable surface.

**Quality system card on the MDX program home**, rendered through `DataGate` (from #1107), with an attention count summing only conditions that threaten readiness: overdue document reviews, unapproved critical suppliers, overdue supplier audits, expired training, open major audit findings, undispositioned NC product.

### The honesty properties, because they are the point

- **Every block carries `available`.** A tenant whose QMS tables are not migrated renders *"not tracked here yet"*, never zeroed counts. A zero from a system that is not running reads as an all-clear — the silent-fixture failure mode this stack removed, arriving through SQL instead of JSX. Blocks degrade independently on 42P01; all five absent is still a 200.
- **Org-scoped, and the card says so.** The QMS does not run per submission (21 CFR 820 / QMSR), so labelling org-wide counts with the selected programme's name would be the header-vs-panel mismatch #1107 fixed elsewhere.
- **No invented metrics.** Training reports lapsed acknowledgments, not a fabricated "compliance %" — the tables cannot say who *should* have trained on what.

author: dallascrilley
body:
Closes the one MEDIUM from the independent verification of #86.

## The gap

The verification pass confirmed the loop is closed, but flagged that `senderIsBot` fails **open**: it returned `false` whenever `sender` was missing, null, or not an object, so a review delivery with no readable sender still woke an agent. GitHub always names a sender, so an unnameable one on a review event is ambiguous — and ambiguity must not wake a runaway-cost path.

## The fix

Inverted the helper to `isHumanSender`, which requires a readable, non-bot sender. The guard now reads "wake only for a sender that reads as human" rather than "block known bots", which is the property actually wanted. A sender fails the check when `sender.type` is `Bot`, when the login ends in `[bot]`, or when there is no readable sender at all.

Issue and pull-request events are untouched.

## Two fixtures were hiding behind the fail-open

`github-webhook.spec.ts` (coalesce burst) and `webhook.post.spec.ts` (route-level coalesce) both omitted `sender` entirely and only passed because the old guard failed open. Both now name a human sender, which is also what GitHub actually sends. Worth noting: the fail-closed change is what surfaced these as unrealistic.

## Verification

Each branch confirmed covered by inverting it and re-running the spec — three probes, three failures:

author: jdwillmsen
body:
Closes the detection half of JDWLABS-209. This is a **read-only detection change** — no rollout behaviour is altered and nothing about Vault's `updateStrategy` changes.

## Why

On 2026-07-26 the Vault chart went `0.30.1 → 0.34.0`, carrying image `1.20.1 → 2.0.3`. ArgoCD applied it and immediately reported Synced + Healthy. The pod served **1.20.1 for the next 47 minutes**. During the subsequent restart `vault-0` was sealed and not Ready for ~68 seconds, and a health sample taken inside that window still read `49/49 Synced+Healthy`.

Three blind spots lined up, and each one independently returns green:

1. `updateStrategy: OnDelete` — ArgoCD's StatefulSet health check treats it as healthy unconditionally, so `currentRevision != updateRevision` never surfaces.
2. `.spec.updateStrategy` sits in the tenant `ignoreDifferences`, so a git diff will not show it either.
3. `platformctl`'s `vault-pod` check was phase-based: it asserted `pod platform-vault-0: Running`. A sealed Vault satisfies that.

The failure mode is not that Vault broke — it self-recovered via the auto-unseal CronJob. It is that the tooling could not distinguish a healthy Vault from a sealed one, nor tell you a major-version upgrade had been applied but not adopted. Vault gates secret access for the whole platform, so it is the worst component to be blind on.

## Changes

**`vault-pod` now asserts readiness, not phase.** Readiness *is* the seal signal: the chart's readiness probe runs `vault status`, whose exit code encodes seal state (`0` unsealed, `2` sealed), so a sealed Vault is Running-but-not-Ready.

Reading the pod condition rather than calling `/v1/sys/health` is deliberate — it keeps the check dependency-free, needing no route to Vault and no token, only the API server already in use. Severity is graded for the raft migration landing in JDWLABS-25: all Ready passes, none Ready fails, and a partially-ready set **warns**, because a quorum of unsealed members still serves reads.

**New `statefulset-revisions` check** compares `.status.currentRevision` against `.status.updateRevision` across every StatefulSet in the cluster. A skew warns rather than fails: nothing is broken, the applied change simply is not running yet. Both revisions empty is treated as unsettled (mid-creation), not skewed.

## Verified against the live cluster, not just fixtures

The skew this ticket describes is still present, which makes it a real demonstration target rather than a synthetic one:

```
$ platformctl cluster status
Layer 1 — Operators
  ✓  vault-pod                 1/1 pods Ready (unsealed)
  ⚠  statefulset-revisions     1/8 pending roll: vault/platform-vault [OnDelete] 65d6fbffd6→556744bc94

⚠ 20/21 checks passing, 1 warning(s) — cluster degraded
```

Before this change the same cluster reported `✓ 20/20 checks passing — cluster healthy`.

Structured output carries it too:

```json
{"phase":"cluster-status","layer":1,"group":"Operators","name":"statefulset-revisions","status":"warn",
 "message":"1/8 pending roll: vault/platform-vault [OnDelete] 65d6fbffd6→556744bc94"}
{"phase":"cluster-status","name":"summary","status":"warn","message":"20/21 passing, 0 failing, 1 warning(s)"}
```

## Tests

13 tests in `internal/cluster`, and per the ticket's DoD they demonstrate the checks **failing against genuinely bad state**, not merely passing against good:

- sealed Vault (Running, not Ready) → `fail`, message names the sealed case
- unsealed → `pass`; 2-of-3 ready → `warn` naming the unready member; CrashLoopBackOff → `fail`
- OnDelete skew → `warn` carrying namespace, name, strategy and both revision hashes, while a settled StatefulSet beside it is not reported
- unsettled (both revisions empty) → `pass`, so a StatefulSet mid-creation is not misreported
- empty cluster → `pass` with an explicit message rather than a blank one

```
go build ./...           clean
go test ./...            ok — all 10 packages
yamllint tenants/ bootstrap/   clean
```

`golangci-lint` could not run locally — the installed binary rejects the repo config format (`unsupported version of the configuration`). That is a local toolchain mismatch, not a code issue; relying on CI's pinned version.

## Docs

`docs/OPERATIONS.md` gains a note under Vault lifecycle explaining that `vault-pod` asserts readiness because readiness is the seal signal, plus a troubleshooting row for `statefulset-revisions` warning `pending roll` — including that adopting an OnDelete change means deleting pods deliberately, one at a time, and that Vault will seal after each delete until the CronJob catches up.

## Deliberately not in this PR

The ticket's third deliverable — *does Vault stay on `OnDelete` or move to `RollingUpdate` now that it is single-replica?* — is left open. It is coupled to JDWLABS-25, which makes Vault a 3-replica raft cluster; deciding it now against a single-replica topology would answer the wrong question. Recommend it be settled as part of that migration.

Also worth a follow-up, out of scope here: `cluster status` exits `0` and prints `Status: SUCCESS` even when the summary reads "cluster degraded". That is arguably the same class of bug this ticket is about, but changing exit-code semantics could break existing CI callers, so it should be decided rather than slipped in.

author: kindacoolhamster
body:
Documentation accuracy pass ahead of the `v0.1.0` tag. The trigger was the root README still calling the core image *distroless* when the default base is `cgr.dev/chainguard/static`; auditing the rest turned up two defects the docs were papering over.

## Wrong facts
| Where | Was | Is |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | core image "~22 MB static **distroless** binary" | Chainguard static base; size dropped (it was already stale) |
| `README.md` | LVM "host-local block volumes" | shared-VG — the plugin reports `NodeLocal=false`, and STATUS.md already said shared-VG |
| `README.md` | package table listed 2 of 5 plugin binaries | all five, plus `kubectl-bard` and `conformance` |
| `docs/quickstart.md` | localpath "~300-line" Python | 237 lines |
| `charts/.../README.md` | native profiles "(ceph-rbd, cephfs)" | iscsi has one too (documented 90 lines below in the same file) |
| `charts/.../values.yaml` | "harmless with the default **root** core" | the default core is **non-root** (65532) |
| `charts/.../Chart.yaml` | backend config is always user-supplied | native profiles render it; only credentials are always yours |

## Defects found while verifying claims
- **`docs/hardened-images.md`'s "complete runtime-dependency contract" was materially incomplete** — it omitted the `ceph` binary from *both* Ceph rows (CephFS's entire control plane is `ceph fs subvolume …`), omitted every expand/reclaim binary (`resize2fs`/`xfs_growfs`/`btrfs`/`fstrim`), and had **no iscsi row**. Rebuilt from the production (non-test) exec call sites.
- **CephFS `mounter: nfs` could not work.** It is chart-exposed and implemented (`internal/cephfsplugin/cephfsplugin.go` runs `mount -t nfs`), but `Dockerfile.plugin-cephfs` shipped no NFS client, so it failed at NodeStage. Added `nfs-common` and verified `mount.nfs` is present in the built image. The mounter is still unproven against a live NFS gateway and is now documented as untested.
- **The CI chart-render test proved nothing for ceph-rbd.** It enabled the plugin with no `instances`, which emits no ceph container, ConfigMap or BackendCluster at all — so it passed vacuously. Now renders with an instance and asserts both appear.
- **`make images` built 5 of the 7 images** the release workflow publishes (no iscsi, no localpath).

## Things v0.1.0 itself would have invalidated
- Both install docs justified the `--version` pin with *"every published chart version is currently a pre-release"* — false the moment `0.1.0` publishes. Pin kept; the reasoning now says what is actually true (reproducibility, and that an unpinned install silently resolves to the latest **stable** rather than erroring).
- **`Chart.yaml`'s dev placeholder was `0.1.0`** — the exact version about to ship. After tagging, a source-tree `helm install ./charts/bard-csi` would have quietly pulled released `0.1.0` images instead of failing loudly, and drifted as `main` advanced. Moved to `0.0.0-dev`.
- `RELEASING.md` expected `/releases/latest` to 404 for an RC; after the first stable release it returns that release instead.
- `deploy/` and `deploy/examples/` reference `:dev` tags that are **not published** (verified 404 anonymously) with no doc saying so, while the README told readers to `kubectl apply -f deploy/`.

## Release prerequisite
Bumps the documented install version to `0.1.0` (required — the release workflow gate fails the cut otherwise) and **extends `hack/check-doc-versions.sh` to cover `README.md`**, which now carries an install command: a pin outside the gate is exactly how the last one went stale.

## Verification
- `go build`/`go vet` clean, `gofmt` clean, **16/16 packages pass**
- `helm lint` clean; the new CI assertions replayed locally (sidecar + BackendCluster both render)
- `deploy/quickstart/values.yaml` still renders — it enables localpath with **no** `instances`, so the low-level escape hatch is load-bearing and must keep working
- `hack/check-doc-versions.sh v0.1.0` passes, and a deliberately mismatched README pin correctly fails it
- `Dockerfile.plugin-cephfs` rebuilt; `mount.nfs`, `mount.ceph`, `ceph`, `ceph-fuse` all confirmed present in the image

## Not done — needs a decision
`helm install --set plugins.ceph-rbd.enabled=true` (with no `instances`) renders a **silently backend-less driver**: no sidecar, no BackendCluster, no config, no error, and NOTES.txt still reports it as enabled. The chart has a `_validate.tpl` precedent for failing incoherent configs. A guard would need to accept the low-level path (`instances` omitted + explicit `controller`/`node` wiring) — which the quickstart itself relies on. Left as a follow-up rather than slipping a chart behaviour change into a docs PR.

author: shulaoda
body:
## Problem

In bundled dev (`experimental.bundledDev`), editing a worker source leaves the page running the old worker. The request for the new worker file returns `200` with `text/html` (the SPA fallback), so the browser cannot parse it as a module worker and only reports an `error` event with an undefined message. The network panel looks fine, so this is easy to miss.

Affects both `new Worker(new URL('./w.js', import.meta.url))` and `import Worker from './w.js?worker'`, and a worker spawned from inside another worker.

It only reproduces when the importing module is an HMR boundary. Without one the edit escalates to a full reload, which rebuilds and emits the worker. React Fast Refresh makes self-accepting importers the norm, so real apps sit on the failing path.

## Cause

`vite:worker` splits the work across two phases:

- `load` resolves the final worker URL and writes it into the module
- `generateBundle` hands the worker bytes to the bundler

An HMR patch is generated without a generate phase, so only the first half runs. Worker filenames carry a content hash, so an edited worker gets a new filename that was never emitted.

`vite:asset` avoids this by calling `emitFile` during `load`, before deriving the URL from it.

## Related Issues

Part of the Full Bundle Mode plugin coverage work (rolldown/rolldown#10469).

author: kristerhedfors
body:
Two commits, both about what the header terminal icon (`#termbtn`) does.

## 1. The switch always responds, and it shows the boot — feedback #38

> *"terminal button does not work, I don't get to see what happens in terminal"*

The button was fine; the pane was empty and the switch refused to move for that reason.

`showTerminalIcon` un-hides the icon the moment the sandbox knob is on — at first paint, from the cached knob, **before the VM boots** — because its presence is the "Linux is starting" signal (2026-07-14 directive). But the click handler opened with `if (!hasBackdropContent()) return;`, and content only exists once the VM prints. A cold boot is **24 s bare and up to ~80 s with a /src seed** (`docs/SANDBOX-PERFORMANCE.md`), so for most of the icon's visible life every tap did nothing at all — no body class, no layer, no feedback — on a control already styled as live (`.mode-bg`, accent outline).

The chat log behind the report (`chat_logs` #675) had `client_diag {coi:true, sab:true, bl:true, ran:1}` and a real `ls -la /` at exit 0, which is what ruled the sandbox itself out.

- **The handler always cycles.** Content gate gone from the click path; `setLayerMode` calls `ensureLayer()` + `render()` so there is a pane to bring forward.
- **The boot ticker feeds the pane.** `startBootQuips`'s tick drives the same progress line into both the chat activity label and the new `feedStatus()`. The `_bootOnMessage` check moved from an early `return` to an `if`, so a bare **pre-warm** boot — the auto-start-on-open path, no activity sink, exactly when a user meets a fresh icon — still feeds the pane. `stopBootQuips` clears it, covering ready / failed / timed-out / torn-down in one place. **The load-bearing sink guard is untouched:** `_bootOnMessage` is still never nulled there.
- **An empty pane says so.** `composePaneLines` stacks output → live prompt tail → status, falling back to `EMPTY_PANE_LINE` instead of a black void. `hasPaneContent` counts a boot in flight as content; `hideTerminalIcon` clears the status first so a knob-off still hides.

## 2. The icon owns the graph too — all permutations

Orchestrator's backdrop axis is `graph`, so it stands in front of **both** the rotating wireframe workflow graph and the terminal layer — but the graph mounted unconditionally with the mode and only the terminal was switchable. Per owner directive the one icon now walks every combination:

| mode | terminal | graph | body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `both` | faint backdrop | shown | — |
| `terminal` | forward (black field) | off | `term-fg` |
| `convo` | faint backdrop | off | — |
| `graph` | not shown | shown | `term-hidden` |
| `hidden` | not shown | off | `term-hidden` |

Non-graph modes keep the original three-cycle byte for byte. `terminal` has no graph variant on purpose: the forward pane is `rgba(10,13,18,.93)` over the whole viewport, so a graph behind it would be a state nobody can see.

- **The pairs decompose; the CSS never grew a case.** `terminalLayerOf` maps all five modes onto the same three terminal states that `body.term-fg`/`term-hidden`, `applyOpacity` and every gesture guard already read. `graphShownIn` is the other half.
- **The graph arrives as a HOOK, never an import.** `mode-backdrop.js` hands `setGraphLayer` a `{show, hide}` pair for a graph mode and `null` for every other; the view state decides what is mounted. **This direction is load-bearing:** `agent-backdrop.js` is in `isPublicAsset` because the Se/cure module graph imports it and `graph-backdrop.js` is not, so importing the graph into the switch would 401 the whole `/cure` tier — the recurring public-graph failure class. Checked with an import-closure walk of `/cure/drc.js`: 47 modules, all public, neither graph module in the closure.
- **A mode change keeps the user's choice.** `forGraphAvailability` re-homes the current mode into the cycle now in force: gaining a graph shows it (`convo`→`both`, `hidden`→`graph`), since the mode's background used to mount unconditionally and someone who hid the *terminal* said nothing about a graph they had not met; losing one drops that half.
- The icon also appears for a graph alone, so a graph mode with the sandbox off can still put its backdrop away.

## Verification

- `npm test` — **3454 pass, 0 fail** (324 suites), including the regenerated-artifact freshness checks.
- `npm run typecheck` — clean, both tsconfigs.
- **Browser-verified** in headless Chromium against the real `index.html` + `app.css`, since this is DOM glue with no Node test. Reproduced the original defect first (tap before content → `body.className` unchanged, `#dr-agent-backdrop` never built), then confirmed: empty pane → boot progress → live output; the three-cycle unchanged without a graph; all five states reachable with one; every distinguishable (terminal, graph) pair visited; no graph canvas left behind on the way out.

author: exoridus
body:
## Problem

Whenever a resample context is active, libswresample held already-captured audio in its internal filter delay and nothing flushed it at end-of-stream. The context was freed with that audio still inside, so the audio track ended short of the video:

- non-default output sample rate or channel count: ~10 ms
- engaged A/V clock slaving on the default 48 kHz path: sub-ms to a few ms (filter-length order)

## Fix

`OutputFormatAudioSrc::DrainResampler()` flushes the context with `swr_convert(ctx, out, max_out, nullptr, 0)`, looped until it produces nothing and sized from `swr_get_delay`. It works unchanged with a compensation armed (clock slaving re-arms one before every convert) and returns 0 on the passthrough and rematrix-only paths, which buffer nothing.

The audio worker calls it after the capture loop and before `source_->Shutdown()` frees the context, feeding the recovered frames to the encoder as an ordinary buffer so PTS continues from the accumulated frame counter. The encoder EOS flush and the mux finalize still run afterwards, unchanged and undoubled.

The AAC encoder's own converter is drained the same way at the head of `Flush()`, before the trailing partial frame is zero-padded. Its configured same-rate interleaved-to-planar conversion carries no delay today, so that part is a no-op in practice; it keeps the FIFO the single source of truth at EOS if the conversion ever gains a rate change. The whole-frame encode loop is now shared between `FeedFloat32` and `Flush` instead of duplicated.

## Behavior change

Only that the audio track now ends complete. The duration difference to video shrinks by the previously lost tail. The passthrough fast path is untouched and still byte-identical.

## Tests

- `OutputFormatAudioSrc.Drain_RateConversion_RecoversFullInputDuration`: 1.000 s of 48 kHz input resampled to 44.1 kHz yields 44100 output frames within 1 sample, and the pre-drain total is measurably short.
- `OutputFormatAudioSrc.Drain_CompensationEngaged_RecoversTailAtSetRate`: the drain flushes a compensating identity context and does not fall below the input duration.
- `OutputFormatAudioSrc.Drain_Passthrough_ProducesNothing` and `Drain_RematrixOnly_ProducesNothing`: the fast paths are unchanged and need no drain.
- `AudioThreadSourceAgnosticTest.AudioThread_ResampledTrack_DrainsResamplerTailAtStop`: end-to-end through the worker at 44.1 kHz PCM, verifying the drain sits at the right point in the stop chain.

Full Debug build plus complete ctest: 254/254 passing.

`KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md` loses the entry that documented the tail loss.


## Accepted edge case

If the recording is stopped while the source is in the degraded (device-loss) state, the drain flushes the roughly 10 ms of pre-outage audio it still held to the very end of the timeline, i.e. behind the silence that filled the outage. Reviewed and accepted as a rare corner: the alternative is discarding real captured audio, and the misplacement is bounded by the filter delay.

If the bounded flush loop is ever exhausted with the context still producing, the frames left behind are logged at Warn (`audio.resampler_drain`) with the track id, the iteration bound and the drained count, rather than disappearing silently.

author: redberet
body:
CVE-2026-11332 is an argument injection in `ansible-galaxy role install` that leads to arbitrary code execution, CVSS 7.8. The advisory patches the 2.18 line at `2.18.18rc1`, and the pin was `2.18.7`.

Dependabot raised the alert on 2026-07-19 but never opened a pull request for it, so the high severity finding sat open while the medium pytest one was fixed a minute later.

`2.18.18` keeps the same minor series rather than moving to 2.19, so the playbooks that drive the AlmaLinux fleet see a patch-level change and not a behavior change.

The lab does not call `ansible-galaxy` anywhere, so the vulnerable path was not reachable through the documented workflow. The dependency is still present in the environment the lab tells operators to build, which is reason enough to patch it.

The pin resolves (`pip install --dry-run` exits 0) and `pytest` passes 10 of 10.

author: halildeu
body:
## Boş liste bir hata değil, bir sessizlikti

Sağlama betiği permission-service yetkisinde duruyordu. O yetki **"bu hesap ürünü kullanabilir mi"** sorusunu cevaplıyor. **"Hangi davaları görebilir"** ayrı bir olgu — OpenFGA'da tutuluyor ve yetkinin dayandığı sayısal kimlikle değil, **Keycloak subject'iyle** anahtarlanıyor:

```
check(user:<kc-subject>, case_viewer, ethics_product:<orgId>)
```

Tuple yoksa `listCases` her davayı teker teker eliyor ve personel listesi **HTTP 200 + `[]`** dönüyor.

Adım eklenmeden önceki ölçüm:

```
org …0003'teki ethics_cases   : 21
GET /api/v1/ethics/cases      : 200 []
herhangi bir log'da hata      : yok
```

Boş dizi, "bu org'da dava yok" ile ayırt edilemez. Bu yüzden sorun bir kimlik doğrulama sorunu gibi görünüp arka arkaya birkaç düzeltmenin arkasında saklandı.

Adım eklendikten sonra:

```
GET /api/v1/ethics/cases      : 200, 21 dava
```

## Kayda değer iki ayrıntı

**ethics-service kendi OpenFGA store'unu kullanıyor** (`01KXYKEB…`), paylaşımlı platform store'unu değil. `ethics_product` / `ethics_case` tipleri yalnız orada var. Paylaşımlı store'u okuyunca sıfır tane görünüyor ve bu "model hiç kurulmamış" gibi okunuyor — bu yanlış teşhise bir tur harcandı.

**Doğrulama türetilmiş ilişkiyi sınıyor.** Yazılan `triager` ve `handler`; sunucunun sorduğu `case_viewer`. Bir ilişkiyi yazmak, sunucunun baktığı ilişkiye sahip olmakla aynı olgu değil — bu yüzden kontrol yazdıklarımı değil, çözülmüş sonucu okuyor.

## Negatif taraf da kilitlendi

Sentetik yönetici org …0001'de `case_viewer` tutmamalı. Orada **gerçek insanların gerçek ihbarları** var; sentetik bir hesabın onları okuyabilmesi test-verisi meselesi değil, gizlilik ihlalidir. Betik bunu fail-closed doğruluyor:

```
  case_viewer on own product  -> True
  case_viewer on the LIVE org -> False
```

## Hiç geçemeyecek olan kapı

Yetki kapısı `p["userId"] == p["subscriberId"]` karşılaştırıyordu — bir **dize** ile bir **sayı**; Python'da her zaman `False`. Sunucu `userId.equals(subscriberId.toString())` soruyor. Betik, doğru sağlanmış bir hücre için `FATAL` raporluyordu. Artık sunucunun sorduğu karşılaştırma yapılıyor.

## Boundary declaration (ADR-0011 §2.3)

This PR includes:

- [ ] credential-read
- [ ] credential-write
- [x] state-mutation (test cluster)
- [ ] state-mutation (production)
- [ ] boundary-cross
- [ ] user-communication
- [ ] none of the above (Codex consensus only)

User-approval evidence: N/A — test kümesi sağlama betiği; prod dokunulmadı. Yazılan tuple'lar yalnız sentetik org …0003'e; canlı org …0001 sınırı fail-closed doğrulanıyor.

author: milyin
body:
Stage T of #187 — closes #190, and **closes #136**. Targets `boundary-planning` (#202), not `main`.

One interned graph describing what the *source Rust type says*, owned by an explicit milestone. Stages 1 (#192) and 3 (#193) both consume it; without this stage neither owns it and both would grow a private copy of the same traversal — the precise failure #187 exists to prevent.

## What landed

`api/core/semantic.rs` — `SemanticShape` interned in a `ShapeGraph`:

| Node | Carries |
|---|---|
| `Leaf(TypeKey)` | a type this tier does not decompose — a statement about *the graph's knowledge*, not about the type |
| `Product { key, fields }` | a struct |
| `Choice { key, variants }` | an enum — **every** enum, unit-only included |
| `Optional(SemanticUse)` | an `Option` layer |
| `Sequence { kind, elem }` | `Vec` / `[T]` / `Cow<'_, [T]>` |

**Every child edge is use-qualified.** `SemanticUse { shape, source }` with `SourceUse = Value | SharedRef | ExclusiveRef` is what makes `Vec<&T>` expressible — container held by value, elements shared-borrowed — which a root-only crossing context cannot say, having one slot for a qualifier and two things to qualify. There is no unqualified `ShapeId` in a node, so a traversal cannot silently lose the distinction.

`FieldUse` retains `syn::Member` plus a separate `diagnostic_name` that nothing may key on; `VariantUse` retains the source `syn::Ident` independent of destination-language naming. Degrading either to a string would rebuild #186's textual-access problem one tier lower, which is the opposite of the point.

`SumSpec` **becomes the `Choice` constructor** rather than a parallel description: declaration-order tags, `syn::Member` addressing and the nested-prefix leaf names are now computed in exactly one place. `EnumShape` survives as a classifier *over* a choice (`SemanticShape::enum_shape`), not a second modelling of one.

## Cycles are represented, never cut

The id is reserved **before** children are built, so a recursive occurrence finds it in the intern map and becomes a back-edge. There is no stopping-rule hook: where a cycle may be cut is Tier 1 policy, and a hook here would be the same policy leak the tier boundary exists to prevent. `is_recursive` is a query over the finished graph, not a knob.

## Two decisions the issue left open

Both resolved toward the tier boundary, and both are stated in the module docs because they look like omissions otherwise:

- **`Shape<N>` survives as a derived view**, not a second model. `ShapeGraph::wrapper_projection` derives the layer stack onto the existing `Shape`; `N` — the null representation — stays a wire fact for Tier 1. The engines that fold over layers keep their algebra and stop deriving the stack themselves.
- **`Box<T>` is transparent, `Result<T, E>` is an ordinary `Choice`.** A `Box` is heap indirection — a representation fact, and what makes `Option<Box<Node>>` a legal recursion rather than an infinitely-sized type. A `Result` is a two-alternative sum at the source; that both adapters route it to an error channel is Tier 1's decision, and modelling it as an opaque leaf would hide `T` and `E` from the tier whose job is structure.

## On #136

Closed **structurally**, by delivering its first suggested fix: interning keys on the full `TypeKey`, never a bare ident.

What is deliberately *not* done is correcting the bare-ident cycle stack in `jni/emit/flat_input.rs` pointwise — Stage 3 deletes `FlatLeaf` outright, and touching emission here would break this stage's byte-identical exit.

What is deliberately *not claimed* is end-to-end coverage of #136's collision. The source namespace is flat and `check_no_duplicate` rejects duplicate idents across kinds, so two distinct declared types sharing a short name cannot reach the capture pipeline at all — #136 says as much itself. The test is scoped as a unit test on the graph, with generic instantiations (`Vec<Vec<u8>>` vs `Vec<u8>`) as the reachable form of the same distinction, and its doc comment says so rather than overselling it.

## Exit

- **Must not move — all generated artifacts.** ✅ `examples/regen-check.sh` byte-identical. This stage adds a tier; it does not reroute emission, and nothing outside `api/core` changed.
- **Asserted — no adapter policy is reachable from Tier 0.** ✅ A module-boundary test over the module's own text: adapter modules, JVM vocabulary (`jlong`, `JNIEnv`, `descriptor`, `Kotlin`), C ABI vocabulary (`c_char`, `repr(C)`, `MaybeUninit`) and delivery/wire vocabulary are all rejected, and imports are checked to stay inside `core`. Rust's module system cannot express this — `semantic.rs` could import `api::lang` and still compile — so the check is textual, which is crude but is the only form that can actually fail. **Verified it does fail** on an injected `jlong`.
- **Asserted — cycles are tested here, not assumed.** ✅ All three the issue names:
  - self-recursion (`Node { children: Vec<Node> }`) interns finitely, with the back-edge asserted to be **exactly** the `Node` `ShapeId` and the graph asserted at 3 nodes — not inferred from "it terminated";
  - mutual recursion through legal indirection (`A { bs: Vec<B> }` / `B { as_: Vec<A> }`) yields two nodes and two back-edges, both checked structurally;
  - the defensive full-`TypeKey` interning invariant, scoped as described above.

  Plus: a back-edge keeps its use qualifier (`Vec<&Node>` stays `SharedRef`), and a recursive `Choice` terminates through a variant payload.

19 tests total, covering every node kind, all three `SourceUse` values, all three `SequenceKind`s, the uniform `children()` accessor, and the `Shape` projection.

## Verification

```
cargo test --all --all-features             ok (425 lib tests)
cargo clippy --all-targets … -D warnings    ok
cargo fmt --check                           ok
examples/regen-check.sh                     PASS (byte-identical)
```

## Note for reviewers

The module carries `#![allow(dead_code)]`. That is the same gap `SumSpec` has carried since #146, for the same reason and with the same expiry: this tier lands before either adapter reads it, and the allow goes away with the first adapter that plans over a shape. If you'd rather it be gated some other way, say so — it is one line.

author: panoplied
body:
Fixes #10

`test-filter` calls `testCollection.enableTest(fullTitle, browserId)` for every entry of the input file. When `browserId` is missing in the test collection of the current run, testplane crashes while reading tests:

```
      TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'findIndex')
          at TestCollection.#findTestIndex (testplane/src/test-collection)
          at TestCollection.enableTest
          at @testplane/test-filter/lib/index.js:33
```

This happens both for a mistyped browser in the input file (#10) and when a single input file is shared by several runs with different browser sets (e.g. per-platform CI jobs, like the one where we currently get this issue in the internal autounskip CI-flow for fiji 🙃).

The fix checks each entry's `browserId` against `testCollection.getBrowsers()` and skips entries whose browser is not present.

Test is added also.

author: echo-storm
body:
## Summary

SillyTavern does not copy `chat_metadata` into a new checkpoint/branch chat — it builds a fresh `{ main_chat: <parent chat id> }` object instead (confirmed by reading ST core's `bookmarks.js`, `createNewBookmark`). So `lastExtractedIndex` always started at -1 on a checkpoint even though the copied messages already had memories extracted from them in the parent chat, silently forcing a full re-extraction unless the user manually clicked "Mark as Fully Extracted."

On `CHAT_CHANGED`, if the current chat has no extraction history yet and its metadata carries a `main_chat` pointer, this fetches the parent chat's `lastExtractedIndex` (`fetchChatMessages()` already existed for batch extraction and works here unchanged) and inherits it, clamped to the current chat's own message count in case the checkpoint was made earlier in the parent's history than its current extraction progress. Also guarded against a chat-switch race while the inherit fetch is in flight (same class of fix as the reentrancy-races PR).

Scoped to 1:1 chats — `fetchChatMessages()` reads via `this_chid`/character avatar and doesn't resolve group checkpoint files, so group chats are unaffected (same scoping precedent as the hide-extracted-messages feature).

## Now Verified

## Testing

Syntax-checked, full unit suite passing (178/178). No live checkpoint test performed (see above).

author: benmarte
body:
## Summary

- Implements the `develop-run` coding-contract engine (`actions/develop-run/`) with the **engine-owns-everything** decision: for both adapters, the engine owns git identity, branch naming (`swarm/issue-N`), spec-file commit, PR creation, PR verification via `gh api`, and the `swarm:develop → swarm:qa` transition. Adapters only edit the working tree.
- Ships `headless.sh` adapter wrapping any coding CLI via `ADAPTER_CMD` env, and documents the `claude-code-action` wrapper pattern (SHA-pinned step in `develop.yml` before the engine step).
- Adds `workflows/develop.yml` (`workflow_call`) with concurrency, per-job permissions, timeout, dry-run threading, and a conditional `claude-code-action` step + always-run engine step.
- 29 new unit + integration tests in `tests/develop-run.bats`; 11 structural tests added to `tests/workflows.bats` for `develop.yml`. Uses real git with a `file://` bare remote for push testing and PATH-stubbed `gh` for API call assertions.

## Key decision: engine-owns-everything

Both adapters follow the same model: the engine performs all GitHub state mutations (git push, `gh pr create`, `gh api` verify, label transition). The adapter is a pure working-tree editor. This prevents the adapter from faking PR creation and ensures the PR body always contains `Closes #N`, adapter name, and model.

For `claude-code-action` specifically: the action runs as a conditional step in `develop.yml` before the engine; the engine then skips its own git/push/PR steps and only verifies the PR exists and transitions the issue.

## Test types added

- **Unit:** input validation (issue number, adapter allowlist, ADAPTER_CMD guard), dry-run logging, headless.sh adapter guards (ADAPTER_CMD, SPEC_FILE, binary existence, exit propagation)
- **Integration:** end-to-end headless path through the engine with real git + file:// bare remote (branch creation, spec file commit, adapter output commit, push, PR body assertions, PR verify, transition); no-diff path → bump-attempts; PR verify failure → bump-attempts

E2E (full swarm-testbed run): tracked in issue #12 — not part of this PR.

Closes #7

author: hweeks
body:
Gets the extension to the point where installing it is one click and needs nothing else on the machine except Claude Code itself.

**The binary travels with the extension.** The release workflow already cross-compiled `acy` into each platform `.vsix`; nothing verified it. CI now asserts every platform package contains an executable `extension/bin/acy` and that the `universal` package contains none, and the extension chmods the bundled binary at launch — VS Code's install path has historically dropped the execute bit — aborting with an actionable message instead of opening a terminal that dies on EACCES.

**The extension looks for `claude` before it needs it.** New vscode-free `src/claude.ts` resolves the CLI through `.acy.json` `claudeBin` → the `acy.defaults.claudeBin` setting → `PATH` → the usual install directories. A GUI-launched VS Code inherits the login environment rather than a shell's, so `claude` is routinely off `PATH` even when it works fine in a terminal; when it is found there, its directory is prepended to the terminal's `PATH`, because acy is spawned as the shell and inherits that environment verbatim. Missing entirely, you get a warning at startup and a confirmation before launch instead of a run that dies on its first turn.

This also fixes a live bug: the manifest declared no `activationEvents`, so `activate()` never ran in a fresh window and the `$(check-all) acy` status-bar item the README advertises never appeared until a command was invoked from the palette.

**Releases publish to the Marketplace.** A `publish-marketplace` job pulls the `.vsix` assets back off the GitHub Release — so what the Marketplace serves is byte-identical to what the Release page offers — and publishes every target in one `vsce publish --packagePath` call. A missing `VSCE_PAT` skips with a notice rather than failing the release.

**WTFPL.** The repo had no license, which is why packaging carried `--skip-license`. It no longer does.

Verified: 24 extension tests, lint, typecheck, and packaging (now without `--skip-license`, with `extension/LICENSE.txt` confirmed inside the package); `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go test ./...`; `actionlint` on the workflow. The publish itself cannot be verified until a real release runs — `vsce verify-pat hweeks` passes, so the publisher and token are good.

author: alexberardi
body:
## What

One-line change to the `ChatGPTOpenAI` native-tools system prompt: add a concrete one-shot example so the model answers **"what time is it"** by calling `get_current_time` with no arguments, instead of replying *"Hey, what location should I check the time for?"*.

## Why

The nightly **behavior corpus** (`jarvis-integration-tests`, real `gpt-4.1-nano` through CC's native tool-calling path) has been failing exactly one utterance:

```
'what time is it': no tool call (stop_reason='complete',
assistant_message='Hey, what location should I check the time for?')
1 failed, 29 passed
```

It regressed when the warm household persona (#83, 7/24) landed. `get_current_time`'s `location` is **optional** ("Omit for local time"), and "what time is it" is the only corpus utterance that leaves an optional parameter unspecified. The folksy voice tips nano into a chatty clarifying question on that one edge. The shared rules + `build_personality_reminder` already say *never ask for a defaultable optional param* — nano ignores the abstract rule, so this gives it a concrete example.

#86 fixed the analogous deferral on the **text-embedded** local-provider path (29→30). This is the native-provider (nano) counterpart, scoped to `ChatGPTOpenAI` only.

## Validation

- In isolation (nano, temp 0 and 0.4, full corpus tool list): with the example present, `what time is it → get_current_time {}`, `in Tokyo → {location: "Tokyo"}`, `set a 10 minute timer → set_timer`, small talk → `<not_for_me/>` — nothing regresses.
- The exact CI failure only reproduces inside the fully-warmed CC prompt (persona + injected context), which the behavior corpus is purpose-built to exercise — so the **ground-truth check is a behavior-corpus dispatch** after this merges and `:dev` rebuilds.

body:
The HACS action validates the *head* repository, so on a PR from a fork it checks the fork:

    ::INFO:: Repository: bharvey88/ha-air-quality-card@fix/card-owned-graph-hover
    ##[error] <Plugin bharvey88/ha-air-quality-card> Repository structure for fix/card-owned-graph-hover is not compliant
    ##[error] Repository bharvey88/ha-air-quality-card not loaded properly in HACS.

Since #57 the bundle isn't tracked and `hacs.json` sets `hide_default_branch: true`, so a fork with no releases can't be structurally compliant. Every fork PR gets a red check: #74 fails this way, and so did #63 from a different fork, with the same two errors. #53 and #54, both before #57, passed.

Gating the job on the head repo keeps the check running where it can pass (pushes to `main` and same-repo PRs) and drops it to "skipped" on fork PRs.

One caveat, and it is the opposite of what you might expect: a job skipped by a job-level `if:` reports a `skipped` conclusion, which GitHub counts as **success** for a required status check. So if HACS Action is ever made required, fork PRs would pass it vacuously rather than block on it. `main` currently has no required status checks (`gh api repos/firstof9/ha-air-quality-card/rules/branches/main` returns only `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`), so this is a note for later, not a problem today. The pending-forever behaviour is what happens with workflow-level path filters, which this doesn't use.

body:
## What changed

- Mark Pages read-model `workflow_run` skips as expected when the upstream runtime maintenance was not schedule-triggered.
- Filter only completed `workflow_run` + `skipped` records from Pages runner-health evaluation.
- Keep scheduled, push, manual, failed, stalled, and genuinely skipped operational runs visible.
- Document the expected skip next to the Pages workflow guard.

## Why

The resilient cadence intentionally listens to all `Run runtime offline maintenance` completions, then runs only when the upstream maintenance event was `schedule`. A deploy-triggered maintenance completion therefore creates a one-second skipped Pages run. The health evaluator treated that expected control-flow skip as degraded, even though the previous Pages success remained fresh.

## Validation

- Regression test confirms an expected workflow-run skip is ignored.
- Regression test confirms a scheduled skip remains degraded.
- Existing fresh, running, failed, stalled, stale, rendering, and issue-lock contracts remain covered.

## Operational effect

The workflow-file change triggers a real Pages rebuild on merge, allowing the new MINUTE_DB schema from #345 to execute through the production read-model path.

body:
Samlar pauslandningens sista tre commits: länkgrinds-spåret, verktygs-passet, och §6-passet med ett kritiskt fynd på köpet.

## Kritiskt: `code-role-discipline.md` når aldrig en session

Verifierat mot disk i tre oberoende kontroller:

1. `find` över **samtliga** plugin-cachar ger **noll** träffar — pluginet distribuerar bara `README.md` + `skills/`
2. Hub-`CLAUDE.md` importerar den inte (ingen `@`-syntax) — den refereras enbart i prosa
3. Plugin-manifestet nämner inte `templates/`

**Konsekvens:** §1–§5 — Code-loopen, transparens-rapport-formatet, STOPPA-grindarna — har **inte varit i kontext** under denna session. ADR-042:s konstruktion är bruten i praktiken: konstitutionen bär principen, templaten bär stegen, men stegen levereras aldrig. Filen har underhållits v1.0 → v1.3 utan att läsas.

Frågan gäller **hela filen**, inte bara §6, och bör avgöras innan mer skrivs in i en artefakt som ingen läser.

## Verktygs-passet: tre av fyra egenbyggen var motiverade

| Egenbygget | Dom |
|---|---|
| Hermetiska mockar | **BYT** → `msw` + `@msw/playwright` |
| `check-docs.sh` | BEHÅLL — inget verktyg ger tri-state grön/röd/**skippad** |
| `ci-wait.sh` | BEHÅLL — `gh run watch` fäller på topp-nivån; `gh pr checks --watch` är **fail-open** på `CANCELLED`/`SKIPPED` |
| Två `changed-files`-listor | BEHÅLL men **laga** — vår `ci.yml` sitter redan på GitHubs säkra rad |

**Fälla vi hade gått i:** MSW:s `skipAssetRequests` är `true` som default och släpper igenom Google Fonts tyst — 86,4 % av vår mätta restrafik.

**Premiss-korrigering:** Ghost är ingen Playwright-precedent (Vitest Browser Mode + service worker). Formen stämmer, verktyget inte.

## §6-passet: håller i sak, fel lager

§6.2 sammanfaller nästan ord för ord med Anthropics egen brief-struktur — oberoende konvergens. Men instruktionsfiler är *"context, not enforced configuration"*, och mätdata visar **~0 % efterlevnad av skriven processregel mot 75 % när verktyget faktiskt togs bort**.

**Två rättelser krävs:** "läs aldrig transkriptet" saknar precedens, och "det finns ingen löpande insyn" är **faktiskt fel** för vår harness.

**Allvarligast saknade mönstret:** agentrapporten som obetrodd indata. Denna sessions harness flaggade exakt det på passets egen rapport.

**Ärlig motevidens:** enda faktorstudien av filstorlek finner ingen detekterbar effekt — "håll filen kort" är konsensus utan kontrollerat stöd.

## Länkgrinden

19 undantag, **19 externa, 0 interna**, 2 borttagna rader någonsin. Grinden har aldrig fällt på en intern länk. Föreslagen uppdelning gör 17 av 19 onödiga.

`check:docs` 8/8 grönt.

**What**:
Removed `setData` from `components/rowscroll/rowscroll.js` observer in favor of inline computed data (`listLength: list.length`) in WXML. Wrapped the `setData` in `components/courselist/courselist.js` observer with a strict equality check (`if (this.data.listLength !== newLength)`).

**Why**:
Setting derived states (like array lengths) directly in observers using `setData` triggers redundant secondary render cycles on every data update, even when the derived state hasn't changed.

**Impact**:
Reduces unnecessary secondary render cycles for lists during data hydration/updates, improving scroll performance and UI responsiveness.

**Measurement**:
Monitor component render durations and count of render cycles per update in the WeChat Developer Tools performance panel.

author: roxorloops1337
body:
From a real seven-minute match, wave 18 — the log that landed last change:

```
445374  t 12396  stalled     waiting on the other player at tick 12396
445542  t 12396  PEER GONE   the relay says the other player's socket closed
```

That same log also showed **the resync working in production**: a drift at tick 4650 detected, 7,288 bytes shipped, resumed one millisecond later, and the match ran another 7,745 ticks. And 413s of wall clock produced 6:53 of match, so the background clock is holding real-time pace.

What was left was the socket.

## A dead socket is no longer the end

The relay already held everything needed — the room keeps its seed, and a side is released on close and reclaimed *by name* rather than by counting, so a returning player gets their own hold rather than their opponent's. The only missing piece was that nobody was told a rejoin happened.

`start` can't just be sent again: it would put the player who **never left** back on the first tick and throw away the match they're still holding. So a room that's already playing announces a **rejoin** instead, and says which of the two is which — *returning* or *staying*. That decision belongs in the relay, because from inside a browser "I have a match and you do not" is exactly what a returning player can't work out.

The one that stayed hands the board over — the same snapshot the resync uses, which is why this is a small change. The one returning holds still until it arrives, because a freshly started match sits on tick zero and simulating it would be inventing a game that never happened.

A rejoin is **not** a drift and doesn't spend the resync budget. Different failures — a match that reconnects six times hasn't drifted once. The authority differs too: on a drift the host wins because both are live and something must break the tie; on a rejoin there's no tie, so seat must not decide it.

## Two things the browser test found

**A socket doesn't reliably announce its own death.** Killing one from under the page, the close event took **nine seconds** to arrive — and until it did, the match sat reading "waiting for the other player". Patience, for a peer it could no longer reach. A stall over four seconds with a socket that isn't OPEN now counts as a dropped link.

**`send()` on a closing socket doesn't throw** — it logs and discards, so the `try/catch` around it did nothing. Every publish after the drop printed *"WebSocket is already in CLOSING or CLOSED state"*. Guarded on `readyState`.

Reconnection backs off 0.5s → 8s over six tries, then gives up and says so.

## Verified in two real browsers

Socket killed from under the page:

```
P1 tick=247 peerLost=true | P2 link=true retry=1
                                    ← 4.5s later
awaiting board  from the player who stayed
sync in         adopted the other machine's board at tick 247
resume          from tick 247

both at tick 431 on hash 4185748368, 11 shared ticks, 0 differing
still playing (431 → 581), no console errors
```

Before the dead-socket detection the same test took **eleven seconds and printed four console errors**.

## ⚠️ Requires a relay redeploy

The `rejoin` message comes from the Worker, so the client half does nothing until `npx wrangler deploy` is run again from `ironbridge-relay/`.

Nothing breaks meanwhile — an old relay simply never sends `rejoin`, which is exactly today's behaviour.

`npm run check` green: **1230** ironbridge assertions, **48** relay (was 1212 / 39), exit 0.

author: kachkaev
body:
This PR fixes an artifact in the "Lines by language" chart: with age shading off it was drawn from tokei, which counts every file it recognizes — lockfiles, minified bundles, generated data — while with shading on it came from `git blame`, which only covers scannable source files. A repo whose largest `.json` or `.yaml` file is a lockfile therefore showed a big band that vanished the moment the toggle was ticked, and the totals disagreed in both directions.

The `languages` collector now counts lines itself over exactly the file set `survival` blames, using the blob cache `directives` and `todo-comments` already share. Verified on a 90-commit repo: at all 12 survival sample points, both modes report identical totals for every language.

Along the way: no more external `tokei` dependency and no worktree checkout, the collector samples every commit rather than monthly, and the extension → language map — previously duplicated between the dashboard and tokei's own naming — is a single map in the CLI that both views are labelled from.

body:
## ARCADE.2A — Wire authenticated Gamehouse portal & 3D cabinet inspection behind a flag

Integrates the already-merged Gamehouse venue shell (#404) and PropViewer3D (#403)
into the live world **behind the fail-closed, globally-OFF `citylife-arcade-3d-v1`
flag**. No gameplay, iframe, score persistence, PAT, KCO, public leaderboard, or
production deployment. This PR **never enables a production flag**.

### Acceptance
- ✅ Only an **authenticated, entitled `CITYLIFE_PLAYER`** (JWT `userId` + role) can
  see and enter the Gamehouse from the governed commercial plot **when the per-user/
  cohort flag is enabled**. Signed-out and non-entitled users cannot enter.
- ✅ Fail-closed: OFF / killed / 401 / 403 / timeout / malformed / network error all
  deny; the entitlement is memory-only and re-evaluated per identity (never bleeds
  across a session switch).
- ✅ **Latest-wins entitlement resolution.** Overlapping checks (identity change,
  on-entry, bounded interval, tab refocus) are sequenced by a shared gate so a stale
  earlier `enabled` can never land after a newer OFF/killed/denied/failed/aborted
  result. Every non-enabled winner **actively closes** the open venue, not just the
  render guard — a revoked venue cannot be re-opened by a late stale positive.
- ✅ A cabinet interaction opens the **isolated** `PropViewer3D` (rotate / zoom / pan
  / reset) and **closes cleanly with no duplicate render loop or leaked resources**.
- ✅ **OFF remains the global default.** Existing world coordinates and governed
  commercial-plot ownership preserved (portal wiring is read-only against the
  `kooker_gamehouse` plot).

### Changes
- `src/colony/entitlement/arcadeGamehouse.ts` — the fail-closed availability gate.
- `src/colony/entitlement/arcadeEntitlementGate.ts` — **NEW** pure latest-wins
  sequencer (single source of truth for out-of-order entitlement results).
- `src/colony/spatial/gamehousePortal.ts` — read-only wiring of the venue to the
  governed `kooker_gamehouse` commercial plot.
- `src/colony/ui/GamehouseOverlay.tsx` — the streamed venue + cabinet interaction.
- `src/colony/ui/ColonyApp.tsx` — flag-gated entry, both entitlement effects routed
  through the shared latest-wins gate (identity-scoped, memory-only fetch).

### Migration boundary (deliberate)
Worlds hydrated from a durable layout persisted **before** this feature are **not**
backfilled with the venue — an intentional decision (the flag is globally OFF, so an
un-migrated world is behaviourally identical for every user today; a backfill mutates
persisted spatial layouts and belongs in its own reviewed slice). Locked by an
exclusion test and tracked in `docs/arcade-2a-migration-boundary.md`.

### Evidence
- **Focused tests:** `arcadeGamehouseAccess` (authorization matrix),
  `arcadeEntitlementGate` (**deterministic out-of-order / latest-wins matrix**),
  `gamehousePortal` + `gamehousePortalRuntime` (deterministic metadata, ownership
  preserved, live inverse enter/exit, **migration-exclusion lock**),
  `gamehouseOverlay` (mounted open/close/repeated-open/cleanup + feature-OFF).
- **Full suite:** `npm test` → **217 files, 1833 tests passed**.
- **Typecheck:** `tsc --noEmit` clean. **Build:** `vite build` clean.
- **SYNTHETIC component evidence (NOT authenticated UAT):**
  `evidence/arcade-2a-synthetic/` (desktop 1280×800 + narrow 390×844), captured by
  `scripts/arcade-2a-screens-synthetic.mjs`. These **fabricate the session and stub
  the entitlement endpoint** — they prove the client gate + render/interaction wiring
  only. `?skipauth=1` / injected sessions are **not** authenticated proof.
- **Real authenticated UAT (operator-gated, pending):** the harness
  `scripts/arcade-2a-authenticated-uat.mjs` (fabricates nothing, stubs nothing;
  consumes a real disposable-player JWT and lets the real backend decide entitlement)
  and the runbook `docs/arcade-2a-authenticated-uat.md`. Capturing it needs an
  ephemeral non-production kooker backend + a disposable account with the scoped flag
  granted/killed — see the runbook. It is left as an explicit reviewer/operator gate.
