author: danolog
body:
## Co to jest

Trwały nośnik decyzji **„diagnoza otworzyła studentowi moduł X"**. Wiersz per student × moduł, **wyłącznie dla modułów faktycznie otwartych**, z **pełnym werdyktem**: `concept_slug`, `level`, `threshold` obowiązujący w chwili zapisu, `reason`, `support_mode`, `blocking_hole_slug`, odniesienie do sesji diagnozy.

Migracja `0045` addytywna, zastosowana **wyłącznie lokalnie** — prod NEON nietknięty (idzie z L6 razem z `0044`). Flaga `FLAG_PLACEMENT_DIAGNOSTIC` domyślnie **OFF**: deploy ≠ release, zero wierszy, student nic nie widzi.

**Dlaczego pełny werdykt, nie lista slugów** (wymóg produktowy): to jedyny nośnik miernika, na którym Sophia zweryfikuje próg ≥3, a **danych nie da się odtworzyć wstecz** — `result_json` tej samej sesji będzie później przeliczany inną mapą tagów i innym progiem.

## Bramka RODO/RLS przed implementacją uratowała prawo do usunięcia danych

Odruchowym ruchem przy tabeli „tylko do dopisywania" jest skopiowanie istniejącego wzorca z dziennika audytowego (`BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE`). **Złamałoby to art. 17 RODO:** wyzwalacz odpala się także przy kasowaniu **kaskadowym**, więc `DELETE FROM students` kończyłby się wyjątkiem i **konta studenta nie dałoby się usunąć**. Różnica: dziennik audytowy nie ma rodzica kasującego kaskadą, a ta tabela ma.

Mutacja M4 potwierdza: wariant z `DELETE` daje **19 z 19 testów czerwonych** — nie da się nawet posprzątać wierszy.

## Rozbieżność Ryan/Max — Ryan wycofał własny wariant w całości

Jego `CHECK` kształtu wymagał, by gałąź `carried_untagged` miała **puste** pole trybu wsparcia. Sophia w v0.3 — opublikowanej **po** bramce — rozstrzygnęła, że taki moduł dostaje `'full'`, a `null` przestaje być stanem osiągalnym.

Leo dowiódł wykonaniem, że skutek literalnego przeniesienia byłby cięższy, niż zakładaliśmy: zapis idzie **jednym wielowierszowym `INSERT`-em**, więc jeden nielegalny wiersz unieważnia **całą partię** — razem z legalnymi. Błąd `23514` przechodzi obok bezpiecznika (łapie tylko `23505`) i ląduje w `.catch(logError)`: **HTTP 200, wynik diagnozy dostarczony, zero odblokowań, cisza wobec studenta.**

Ryan: *„mój wariant był wadą konstrukcyjną — pomieszałem prowenienicję z leczeniem"*. Zawężenie Maxa egzekwuje jego intencję **mocniej**: dyskryminanta `(concept_slug, level)` jest całkowita i rozłączna, a `NOT NULL` obejmie też przyszłe gałęzie.

## Bramka Leo — GO po czterech notach, wszystkie wprowadzone

**N1 — strażnik produkcyjny deny-faculty.** To najpoważniejsze znalezisko przeglądu. Leo nadał wykładowcy `SELECT` na tabeli placementu: testy integracyjne **3 z 19 czerwonych**, ale **`k3-validate` — narzędzie walidujące PRODUKCJĘ — zielone**. Tabela wpadła między dwie listy: `TENANT_TABLES` (nie sprawdza ani jednego grantu) i lista DENY-both (której ta tabela nie jest, bo student ma odczyt).

Waga: **„skutek nie opuszcza ścieżki nauki" to warunek nośny oceny art. 22 RODO.** Naprawione testem 12b wzorem istniejącego 12a. Dowód mutacyjny w obie strony — i Max odtworzył też stan sprzed naprawy, gdzie ten sam grant dawał `✅ K3 WALIDACJA ZIELONA`.

**N2** — usunięte `?? "full"`: jedyna cicha ścieżka do wpisania trybu wsparcia, którego reguła nie policzyła. Teraz rzuca z nazwą modułu, wzorem sprzecznego `reason` dwie linie wyżej.
**N3** — test regresyjny zawężenia (`carried_untagged` + `fading` → odrzucone). Mutacja `CHECK`-a daje **dokładnie jeden** czerwony test.
**N4** — log zadziałania bezpiecznika: połknięcie `23505` było nieodróżnialne od uczciwego „nic nowego".

## Warunki

| | |
|---|---|
| **W-1** niezmienność | ✅ `BEFORE UPDATE` + `UNIQUE` + `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; testy: `UPDATE`→wyjątek, druga diagnoza→wiersz identyczny, **`DELETE FROM students` udaje się** |
| **W-2** klasyfikacja k3 | ✅ 28/28 tabel |
| **W-3** deny-faculty | ✅ test + strażnik produkcyjny (N1) |
| **W-4** szczelność haka | ✅ zapis po transakcji, best-effort, flaga ostatnim zwierającym warunkiem; inwariant flag-OFF **na konstrukcji**, nie na atrapie |
| **C1** bariera uuid/slug | ✅ awaria była **bezobjawowa** — wszystkie moduły dostawały „brak pomiaru", nieodróżnialnie od uczciwego braku |
| **C6** źródło nazwy kompetencji | ✅ ta sama kolumna, która karmi plan diagnozy |
| **C2** wyczerpujące porównanie | ✅ objęło `blockingHoleSlug` i `supportMode` |

```
build 0 · lint 623 pliki, 1 warning zastany · unit 1911/1911
integration 53 pliki / 340 testów · k3-validate 48 PASS, ✅ ZIELONE
```

## Do L4 (nie w tym PR)

Dokument Sophii **v0.4** dołączony, z trzema rozstrzygnięciami:
- **§6c → W-6:** moduł już zaliczony egzaminem — **pomijamy**, student nie widzi o nim nic. Dziś wiersz produkowałby komunikat „diagnoza otworzyła ci moduł X" skierowany do osoby, która **sama zdała go na ≈90%**.
- **P-1:** zdarzenie w `audit_log` przy **każdym** policzeniu placementu, także zerowym — same zdarzenia „zero odblokowań" **nie mają mianownika**. Plus poziom na koncepcie blokującym: ściana poziomów 2 znaczy „nasze pytanie jest za trudne", nie „próg za wysoki".
- **W-7 (nowe):** reguła **nie wie o zaliczeniach**, więc student, który zdał moduł egzaminem, a potem wypadł słabo na tym koncepcie w diagnozie, dostaje **dziurę na module, który ma zaliczony**. Słaby instrument unieważnia mocny — odwrotność zasady, na której stoi cała rama.

Carry-forward Leo: **L3-C1** (`NOT NULL` na `support_mode` bez pokrycia — mutacja przeżyła 28/28), **L3-C2** (`CHECK` nie wiąże trybu wsparcia z parą poziom/próg na gałęzi z własnym pomiarem — dryf miernika, wiersz jest append-only), **L3-C3** (sprzężenie flag z oceny art. 22 żyje **wyłącznie w prozie** — rejestr flag nie ma mechanizmu zależności), **L3-C4** (strażnik wariantu wyzwalacza w k3).

Znaleziska Maxa: listy w `k3-validate` są utrzymywane ręcznie, więc następna tabela tej klasy znów wpadnie między nie (twardy fix: wyprowadzić k3 z macierzy RLS jako **danych**, nie prozy); `k3-validate` **nie mówi, którą bazę zwalidował**.

author: mateuseap
body:
The initial mobile responsiveness pass had three regressions: the desktop stage collapsed because .stage was accidentally removed from the CSS, the play/pause hit detection used a stale totalMove that was last updated during pointerMove instead of measuring the actual end-to-end distance at pointerUp (noisy touch input that reports phantom movement between pointerDown and the first pointerMove falsely suppressed every tap), and the volume slider and mode buttons were hidden behind display:none on narrow viewports with no way to access them.

#### Changes made
- Restored .stage definition and reverted .device-stage to the original width:min(520px,80vw) and height:420px so desktop layout is identical to before the regression.
- Added .device-stage responsive sizing (85vw, aspect-ratio, max-height:60vh) inside the 640px media query only, so mobile gets proportional scaling while desktop stays untouched.
- Fixed play/pause on mobile: onPointerUp computes tapDist from pointerDown to pointerUp coordinates instead of relying on the stale totalMove variable. Combined with the pointercancel handler from the first pass, this gives double coverage for mobile pointer interruptions.
- Added overscroll-behavior:none to body so mobile browsers do not intercept touch gestures as pull-to-refresh.
- Volume slider is no longer hidden on mobile; mode buttons (shuffle/repeat) appear as a horizontal row below the stage instead of being hidden.

#### Test plan
- pnpm test passes: 14 client tests + 10 server tests
- pnpm build succeeds
- Desktop (1440x900): stage renders at 520x420, mode card on left, reset button on right, layout identical to before
- Chrome DevTools 375x667: CD boombox fits, play/pause works via tap on both MP3 center button and CD play-pause button, volume slider visible, shuffle/repeat buttons visible below stage

body:
The ladder existed to chase watertightness, and the evidence says that is not what this tool needs: `Hub_Socket` has **362 open edges and renders cleanly at 1.5× zoom** — the defects are sub-pixel. The diff renderer matches faces by stable `FACE_ID` rather than geometrically, so mesh cracks do not affect it either.

Watertightness would matter for a volumetric diff, a trustworthy mass delta, or STL export. None of those is what is being built, so these tests come out rather than standing as an invitation to keep optimising off the critical path.

#39 retains the diagnosis and the OCCT reference pipeline (`FixOrientation` → `FixPeriodicDegenerated` → `FixMissingSeam` → `FixAddNaturalBound`), so this is recoverable if a volumetric diff is ever wanted.

91 tests pass.

author: katolikov
body:
## Problem

The pipeline/weight/autotune cache reached disk only from `~Session()`. An Android app never destroys its ViewModels on Back or Home and registers no lifecycle hook, so a process killed while a multi-GB model was resident discarded the entire cold-load sweep and repaid it on every subsequent load.

Measured before the fix: after a completed encoder load no cache file existed even 300 s later; freeing the session produced a 57.7 MB file instantly.

## Fix

`Session::flushNewCacheWork()` runs at the end of `createFromVxm`, `create` and `prepareShapes`. The Vulkan gate writes only when the session produced new content -- the weight cache is dirty, or the driver's pipeline blob grew since the last save. Weight-dirty alone is not enough: a model whose weights all take the flat upload path leaves that cache clean while still paying for every pipeline compile. A warm load with nothing new costs one size query and no encode.

Supporting pieces: `vk::PipelineCache::currentBytes()` (size-only half of the two-call idiom) and `WeightCache::markSaved()`, which finally gives the previously unused `dirty()` a consumer.

## Cache-path resolution

- `Runtime::load` no longer discards a caller-set `Config::cacheFile`. Order is now: argument, then that field, then `<model>.cache` beside the model.
- `Config::cacheDir` is removed. No engine code read it, which is what made `--cache DIR` an inert flag. `run_io` and `classify` now resolve it through `Runtime::cacheFileIn`, and `saveCaches` creates missing parent directories.
- The splat load drops `Config::dumpTensors`. It fed a pose-readback fallback that cannot trigger: `camera_poses` is a declared output, and the second pattern matched no tensor in any bucket. A paired A/B confirmed it was not a performance cost either.

## Verification

Two devices, all three app modes. The cache lands at load, survives `am force-stop` with no teardown, and a warm load logs `Saved cache` zero times.

| mode | written at load | survives kill | warm load |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3D splat encoder | 60 490 527 B | yes | 2.3 s |
| chat (1B int4) | 365 998 B | yes | 2.85 s |
| VLM (2.2B int4) | 6 571 716 B | yes | -- |

Encoder outputs are byte-identical to v1.5.0 on the same device with seeded inputs -- all eight of `means`, `covariances`, `scales`, `rotations`, `harmonics`, `opacities`, `camera_poses`, `intrinsic_pred`. 418 host tests pass.

## Summary

Keep the natural-proportion fixed masonry Gallery, but stop older unresolved covers from dominating the opening screen.

- Rank Gallery works by image readiness first

The public opening wall should show the strongest available material while the historical cover backlog is repaired gradually. This does not delete or conceal records from the archive; it changes only Gallery presentation priority.

- **Review:** By commit
- **Merge strategy:** Merge (no squash)

## Description

Refactors the nightly, release, and optional-wheel workflows to build core and opNav-enabled wheels concurrently across macOS, Linux x86_64, Linux ARM64, and Windows.

A reusable wheel-building action now configures `sccache`, restores an isolated Conan cache, and handles the path and ownership differences between native runners and Linux `cibuildwheel` containers. Built wheels are transferred as short-lived artifacts to downstream jobs, where the optional distributions are assembled and tested before publishing can proceed.

The commits are organized as follows:

1. Parallelize and cache the wheel builds.
2. Add the corresponding release-note snippet.

## Verification

- Successfully ran the complete [Test Optional Wheels workflow](https://github.com/AVSLab/basilisk/actions/runs/30221063362).
- All core and opNav wheel builds completed on macOS, Linux x86_64, Linux ARM64, and Windows.
- All four downstream optional-wheel installation tests passed.
- The warm-cache workflow completed in approximately 16.5 minutes, compared with approximately 99 minutes for the previous sequential workflow.
- Repository pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.

No product test files were added or modified because this change only restructures CI execution. The existing optional-wheel installation test provides end-to-end validation of the generated distributions.

The nightly and publishing workflows were not dispatched because they can publish external artifacts. They use the same reusable build action and build/package topology exercised by the test workflow.

## Documentation

Added a release-note snippet describing the parallel wheel builds and compiler/Conan caching.

No user-facing installation documentation was invalidated because the generated wheel contents and supported platforms remain unchanged.

## Future work

Monitor GitHub Actions cache usage and eviction rates. A dedicated remote `sccache` backend or additional cache capacity may be considered separately if repository cache pressure affects hit rates.

author: michael-herwig
body:
Pushing the bazelisk mirror to GHCR failed on `windows/amd64` for every version:

```
416 REQUESTED_RANGE_NOT_SATISFIABLE: the request body is too large and exceeds
the maximum permissible limit of 4.00MiB
```

Four platforms published; only the Windows bundle crosses 4 MiB. This blocks most of the 42-mirror fleet, not just the pilot — any artifact over 4 MiB on GHCR hits it.

## The root cause is not what it looks like

ocx was **already chunking**. The vendored `rust-oci-client` fork implements streamed `PATCH` + `Content-Range` end to end and ocx already called it. The defect was `ClientBuilder` overriding `push_chunk_size` to **16 MiB — 4× GHCR's cap** — so every "chunk" was a single oversized request. No new upload machinery was needed.

## Two commits

**`bb4013ee`** sets the chunk size under the cap, as a named constant carrying GHCR's limit as its stated reason, and adds a guard that honours the registry's reported `Range` so a short-accepting registry cannot leave the client committing a blob the registry only partially stored. The guard half lives in the fork: **ocx-sh/rust-oci-client#2**.

**`b8f173a0`** stops an oversized blob falling back into the bug it just hit. Without it, any disagreement over the `Range` header raised a spec violation, the retry tripped the same guard, and the fallback pushed the whole >4 MiB body in one monolithic `PUT` — 416 again, reached through a new door. Above the cap the error now propagates (exit 69) with its reason logged and source chain intact, so the failure is diagnosable instead of self-inflicted. **Under-cap blobs still fall back deliberately**: that PUT can succeed, it is atomic, and it is the only escape for a registry with no chunked upload at all.

## Verification

`task verify --force`, true exit code **0**: 3499 unit tests run / 3499 passed, 8 skipped; acceptance 1794 passed, 42 skipped, 3 xfailed, 2 xpassed.

Every behaviour change is mutation-proved — mutation applied, named test watched to fail, restored, watched to pass. Four mutations in total, covering the chunk-size constant, the `Content-Range` header, the server-offset guard, and the fallback threshold. Both integrity tests are driven through `NativeTransport::push_blob`, the production path, not the fork's stream API directly — an earlier version asserted at the wrong layer, where the invariant its name claimed was in fact false for the shipped code.

## Two things to know before merging

1. **The submodule pointer moves.** `external/rust-oci-client` points at `f83e9e06`, pushed and proposed as ocx-sh/rust-oci-client#2. If that PR is re-signed or squashed, its sha changes and this gitlink needs bumping to match.
2. **Both commits are unsigned.** This environment has no passphrase-free signing path (no `ssh-agent`, no askpass). The parent repo's recent history is uniformly unsigned so these are consistent here; the fork's history is signed, which makes `f83e9e06` the outlier there.

Not yet proven against live GHCR — the fleet fix goes live only once this lands and the mirror re-runs. The five `windows/amd64` pairs are still absent from `ghcr.io/ocx-contrib/bazelbuild/bazelisk`.

author: philipyaz
body:
Closes philipyaz/cos-ops#3

## What changed and why

A real `vault query` answered a legitimate knowledge question and made two confident, wrong
claims about the board (a false absence — "no separate board case yet" when two closed cases
exist — and stale case ids presented as "the board context"). The mechanism: wiki pages carry
board case ids by reference only (`cases:` frontmatter + a `**Board:** CASE-N` body line),
unfollowable by design — the vault session has no board access at all. Nothing stopped an
otherwise-in-scope answer from asserting board state on that stale basis, and nothing told the
**caller** to distrust such a claim.

This is a **prose-only guardrail on both sides of the boundary** — no state, no API, no MCP
change, no new setup step:

1. **`second-brain-query/SKILL.md`** (vault-side) — new "Board claims inside an in-scope answer"
   section: never assert board contents (including inferred absence), cite `cases:` refs as-of
   the page's `updated:` date, never present case ids as current/complete board context. Mirrored
   identically into `vault/example-vault/` (committed template) and `vault/philip-vault/` (the live
   vault — gitignored, local-only, applied by direct copy to guarantee byte-identity).
2. **`vault-operations/SKILL.md`** (caller-side, per Philip's amendment on the issue — this is the
   skill he actually drives vault work through) — new "Reading a query answer — board claims are
   not facts" section: a query answer is knowledge-as-recorded, not board state; any board claim
   must be verified against the `board` MCP (`get_case`, `search`) before being repeated or acted
   on.
3. **`tests/run.sh` step [3]** — new HARD sub-check **3c** grep-asserting the five guardrail
   phrases in every vault's `second-brain-query/SKILL.md` and in `vault-operations`, wherever it
   lives (repo root today, `board/.claude/skills/` after cos-ops#1 lands). The pre-existing WARN
   sub-checks were relabelled `2a/2b` → `3a/3b` (comment-only; logic/semantics untouched) to avoid
   colliding with cos-ops#1's new top-level `[2b]` banner.
4. **Docs** — `docs/architecture/vault-agent.md` §"The knowledge-only boundary" gets a third bullet
   naming this enforcement layer; `docs/reference/deep-features.md`'s enforcement-layer enumeration
   gets a matching clause so the two pages don't diverge.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `/vault-operations` carries the knowledge-as-recorded / verify-against-`board`-MCP /
      as-of-`updated:`-date rule — `.claude/skills/vault-operations/SKILL.md`, new section
      "Reading a query answer — board claims are not facts".

      `mkdocs build --strict` passes (exit 0).

## Verifier output

**Demonstration order (mandatory per the issue): FAIL first, then PASS.**

1. With sub-check 3c added but the skills unedited: `bash tests/run.sh` step [3] printed **10**
   `FAIL: ... is missing the guardrail phrase: ...` lines (3 for example-vault's query skill, 3 for
   philip-vault's, 4 for vault-operations) and the suite ended `RESULT: FAIL (failed:
   vault-board-guardrail)`.
2. After the prose edits: `OK: board-assertion guardrail present in every query skill +
   vault-operations.` and the suite returned to its pre-change verdict.

Full suite (`bash tests/run.sh`) on this machine ends `RESULT: FAIL (failed: gen-roles)` — this is
a **pre-existing, unrelated, local-environment failure** (`join-blob refuses with no hub URL /
COS_HUB_PUBLIC_URL`, in the hermetic gen-roles manifest-contract check). I confirmed it fails
identically with this branch's changes stashed out against `main`, so it is not introduced by this
PR. CI (which doesn't carry this machine's local config) is unaffected.

Also run and green:
- `(cd board && npx --no-install tsc --noEmit)` — clean.
- `(cd board && npm run lint)` — 0 errors, 42 pre-existing warnings in files this PR does not
  touch.
- `uvx --with-requirements docs/requirements.txt mkdocs build --strict` — exit 0.
- `node scripts/pack-skills.mjs --check` — 14 bundles up to date (unaffected; vault-operations
  isn't bundled from its current repo-root location).

## Deviations from the plan

None. Implemented as written, including the architect's five adopted divergences already folded
into the plan text before I started (the one real defect — a pinned phrase split across a line
wrap in an earlier draft — was already corrected in the plan I read).

## Known gap, not fixed here (flagged by the plan and the architect)

**cos-ops#1 (PR #71) is still open and touches the same file.** Until it lands, `vault-operations`
stays at repo root with no skill-bundle, so **Claude Code** picks up this guardrail immediately
(it reads `.claude/skills/` live), but **Claude Cowork Desktop** only sees it once Philip re-runs
the manual zip-and-upload flow in `setup-vault`'s "Load the `vault-operations` skill in Cowork"
step — its existing Cowork copy predates this change and is now stale. Not fixed here because the
issue's scope is prose + the test gate, and re-uploading a Cowork skill isn't something this PR can
do on Philip's behalf.

## Decision candidate

No Cos surface may treat a vault `cases:` reference as current board state — a query answer is
knowledge-as-recorded, the board is the sole authority, and the rule is pinned on both sides of the
boundary (producing skill and calling skill) by a hard fixed-string gate, not by convention.

author: usirin
body:
The `gh-phoenix` shim rewrites `gh pr edit` / `gh issue edit` into a REST `PATCH`, and that rewrite used to ignore the caller's `-R` / `--repo` flag: `gh pr edit -R other/repo 5 --title x` became `PATCH repos/<resolved>/issues/5`, so the edit landed on a repository the caller never named, with no error and nothing on stderr. This PR makes the flag decide the target.

The shim now reads `-R` / `--repo` and uses it as the PATCH repo, and says so on stderr. A flag that is present but unusable — a value that is not `owner/name`, or no value at all — blocks with a message naming the flag and the value, instead of quietly falling back. That was the last silent-retarget path left in this shim; the neighbouring one (an unresolved repo defaulting to a hardcoded literal) was fixed in #4294.

Fixes #4301

## What changed

`packages/pipeline-cli/src/tools/gh-phoenix/router.ts`

- New `readRepoFlag` reads `-R` / `--repo` in every form real `gh` accepts: `--repo value`, `--repo=value`, `-R value`, `-R=value`, and the attached shorthand `-Rowner/name`. It returns three states — absent, named, unusable — so a present-but-unusable flag cannot degrade into "absent" and silently reuse the resolved repo.
- `routeEdit` builds its REST path from the flagged repo when one is named, else the resolved one. Both the `apiArgv` target and every hint that quotes a `repos/...` path use that effective repo.
- A named `-R` also supplies a target when resolution found none, so `-R` no longer has to lose a race with the #4270 refusal.
- The `rewrite` reason names the retarget (`..., targeting \`-R other/repo\`.`), which is the shim's own observability channel — the caller sees which repository the PATCH is aimed at.
- An unusable value returns a `block` whose `reason` quotes the flag and the value and whose `hint` says it is refusing rather than PATCHing the repository the shim resolved.
- The `owner/name` shape check is now the exported `isRepoSlug`, so the flag and the resolver validate one shape.

`packages/pipeline-cli/src/tools/gh-phoenix/resolve.ts`

- Drops its local `REPO_RE` and consumes `isRepoSlug` from the router. The pure core owns the shape; the IO seam imports it (never the reverse).

`packages/pipeline-cli/src/tools/gh-phoenix/router.unit.test.ts`

- Nine cases for the `-R` path: `pr edit` and `issue edit`, `--flag value` and `--flag=value` and the attached shorthand, each asserting the resolved repo is *not* the PATCH target; the unresolved-repo case; the malformed value; the valueless flag; and a case pinning that `--title` / `--milestone` / `--add-project` handling is unchanged alongside `-R`.
- Two regression cases pinning the already-correct behaviour: `-R` still reaches real `gh` verbatim on a `passthrough` route, and survives a `routeView` `--json` rewrite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `routeEdit` reads `-R` and `--repo` in both `--flag value` and `--flag=value` forms (plus `-Rowner/name`).
- [x] `gh pr edit -R other/repo <N> --title x` PATCHes `repos/other/repo/issues/<N>` — never the resolved repo silently.
- [x] The same holds for `gh issue edit`.
- [x] Refuse shape not chosen (honor was), but the one refusal this adds — an unusable `-R` value — names the flag and its value in `reason`.
- [x] `router.unit.test.ts` covers `-R` for both verbs, in both flag forms, asserting the resolved repo is not the PATCH target.
- [x] Regression tests pin `-R` reaching real `gh` untouched on `passthrough` and through a `routeView` rewrite.
- [x] No behaviour change to `--body-file` / `--body` / `--title` / `--milestone` / `--add-project` / `--remove-project`.

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run src/tools/gh-phoenix` in `packages/pipeline-cli` — 95 passed.
- `pnpm typecheck` — 29/29 tasks successful.
- `pnpm lint:worktree` — exit 0 (two pre-existing `useOptionalChain` warnings on untouched lines).
- `pipeline-cli cp-classify classify` — `not-control-plane [path-clear-no-content-source]`.

author: ltphongssvn
body:
docs(context): record CF beacon vs React 19 hydration 418 lesson

The production-only React 418 saga (PR 273 no-transform, PR 283 beacon
removal) shipped without a context/ lesson file, so the reasoning lived
only in commit bodies and chat history. Both fixes are on develop and
verified: proxy.ts passThroughNoTransform merges no-transform into the
two HTML pass-throughs, and no self-hosted beacon remains in the root
layout.

Records the two distinct root causes and why the first fix was not
enough: Cloudflare RUM auto-injects beacon.min.js as the last body child
at the edge for browser user agents only, which React 19 throws on where
18 warned; and the earlier attempt to render that beacon ourselves in
head traded the injected duplicate for a manual beacon posting to a
cross-origin endpoint that 404s and is CORS-blocked, delivering zero
analytics while still perturbing the tree. Removing it entirely was the
root fix, because a CDN-proxied domain already gets edge analytics with
no client script.

Also captures the Next.js trap: the root layout calls cookies(), marking
every route dynamic, so Next stamps its own Cache-Control that overrides
next.config headers() -- only proxy.ts response headers win.

Documentation only: no source, test or config changes.

Documentation-only reconciliation of the assembled Journey runtime prompt so every loaded file reflects the **approved, frozen clinician model**. Prompt `.md` files plus two regression-test assertion updates. **No code-behaviour change** — the paired implementation (gates, optional sharing, anchor conditions, progression logic) is the next, separate phase.

## The approved model applied

- **Formulation model** (one primary, evolving) replaces "working hypothesis"; evaluate-new-info-first; provisional-observations-not-conclusions.
- **Bounded, capability-based assessment** replaces "hold everything until a fully confirmed picture."
- **Sharing a formulation aloud is optional and clinically determined** (not mandatory); the state-report checklist is framed as mechanical bookkeeping that records, it does not dictate clinical choices.
- **Route discipline / intervention-failure** handling.
- **Personal Anchor = conditional identity-restoration intervention** (Shared Core §6), and — per the owner's universal rule — **not a general stabiliser**: it is never triggered merely by distress/rising intensity/destabilisation/close, and never a mandatory preliminary step.
